project.name: tsu-stack
project.description: TypeScript full-stack monorepo: TanStack Start + Hono + oRPC + Drizzle + Better Auth

nodes.name: apps/server/Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Multi-stage Dockerfile for the Hono+oRPC server app, building on node:25-bookworm-slim with a Vite Plus installer stage, a builder stage that runs unit tests and builds the server filter, and a production stage that runs the compiled node entrypoint as a non-root user with a /health/live healthcheck on port 5000.
nodes.languageNotes: Four named stages (base, installer, builder, production) chained via FROM --inherit. Uses ARG/ENV for build-time secrets, USER for non-root runtime, HEALTHCHECK with wget to derive the path from VITE_SERVER_URL, and a shell-form CMD that pins 0.0.0.0.

nodes.name: server
nodes.summary: Container image for the server app. Production stage copies apps/server/.output to /app/.output (plus packages/db/migrations for runtime migrations) and runs /app/.output/index.mjs as the `server` user on PORT 5000, with a healthcheck hitting /health/live on VITE_SERVER_URL.

nodes.name: apps/web/Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Multi-stage Dockerfile for the TanStack Start web app, building on node:25-bookworm-slim with a Vite Plus installer stage, a builder stage that runs unit tests then applies Drizzle migrations (vp run db:migrate) before building the web filter, and a production stage that runs the compiled node server as a non-root user with a /_api/health/live healthcheck on port 3000.
nodes.languageNotes: Four named stages (base, installer, builder, production). Unlike the server Dockerfile, the builder also runs database migrations so the TanStack Start prerender step can query the schema. Production entrypoint is /app/.output/server/index.mjs (TanStack Start Node adapter), exposed on 0.0.0.0:3000 with a healthcheck against /_api/health/live.

nodes.name: web
nodes.summary: Container image for the web app. Production stage copies apps/web/.output to /app/.output and runs /app/.output/server/index.mjs as the `web` user on PORT 3000, with a healthcheck hitting /_api/health/live on VITE_WEB_URL.

nodes.name: .github/workflows/ci.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions CI pipeline with two jobs (check and build) triggered on push to main and on pull request open/synchronize/reopen. Uses the voidzero-dev/setup-vp@v1 action to install Node 24 with caching, then runs `vp install` and `vp check` for type/lint verification, and `vp run build` for the production build. The build job materializes packages/env/.env from job-level env (vars and secrets) using `printf '%q'` to safely quote values, then runs `vp run build`; concurrency is grouped per workflow+ref and cancels in-progress runs.
nodes.languageNotes: Five top-level YAML keys: name, on (push to main, pull_request opened/synchronize/reopened), permissions (contents: read), concurrency (per workflow+ref, cancel-in-progress), jobs (check + build). The build job uses a multi-line shell step with `: > packages/env/.env` to truncate before printf, and quotes env values with `printf '%q\n'` so values containing `$` or other shell metacharacters stay safe. GitHub Actions secret names use `GH_` aliases for OAuth credentials (the GITHUB_ prefix is reserved for internal tokens) and are re-exposed under their expected names inside the step env.

nodes.name: CI
nodes.summary: Continuous integration pipeline for the tsu-stack monorepo. Triggers on push to main and PR events, cancels superseded runs, and runs two sequential jobs: `check` (vp install + vp check) and `build` (vp install + write packages/env/.env from secrets/vars + vp run build). The build job feeds DATABASE_URL, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, GitHub OAuth credentials (under GH_* aliases), and Vite/Source env into the env file so the web build can load them via dotenvx.

jobs.name: build
steps: write packages/env/.env from job env (printf %q quoting)

nodes.name: .agents/api-fetching-patterns.md
nodes.summary: Authoritative guide for TanStack Query code in apps/web slices. Defines file-naming (get-*.query.ts / *.mutation.ts), slice-local placement (pages/<slice>/api/), and the standard module shape (query keys object, query options factory, hook wrapper, optional result type). Specifies that route files import option factories from the slice barrel and preload them in `beforeLoad` via `ensureQueryData`; caching lives in React Query, not the router cache, and `defaultPreloadStaleTime: 0` is intentional.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown with 9 H2 sections (Goals, File Naming, Placement, Query Module Shape, Mutation Module Shape, Route Integration, Component Usage, Naming Rules). Code samples use TypeScript and reference the orpc client via `@tsu-stack/api/client/tanstack-start/orpc` plus `@tanstack/react-query`. Cross-references core.md for shared enum import from packages/core.

nodes.name: .agents/auth.md
nodes.summary: Source of truth for Better Auth integration. Documents the server/client split (Hono routes /auth/*, nanostore-based authClient, $getUser server function), the auth user query (5 min staleTime, 10 min gcTime, refetchOnWindowFocus 'always'), route groups (pathless __protected/ and (guest)/ layouts), two middleware sensitivity levels (authMiddleware vs freshAuthMiddleware), and the three-layer schema extension rule (auth config + Drizzle schema + client inference with inferAdditionalFields). Calls out that auth.schema.ts is auto-generated by the Better Auth CLI and must be composed with hand-written relations.ts via spreading both into a single drizzle() relations config.
nodes.languageNotes: 11 sections (Architecture, Query Pattern, Route Guards with Protected/Guest H3 subsections, Middleware, Schema Extension with auto-generated and composing relations H3 subsections, Gotchas). Includes a markdown table comparing authMiddleware vs freshAuthMiddleware.

nodes.name: .agents/environment-variables.md
nodes.summary: Authoritative env-var policy. All vars live in packages/env/.env (validated by Zod via @t3-oss/env-core) and split into three scoped objects (ENV_SERVER, ENV_WEB_ISOMORPHIC, ENV_WEB_SERVER). Client exposure is restricted to VITE_ prefixes; server-only secrets must never reach the client. Adding/updating a var requires touching six places: packages/env/src, docker-compose.yaml, Dockerfile, .env.example, .github/README.md, and optionally apps/web/vite.config.ts. Documents build-time vs runtime required via the runtimeRequired(schema) helper, IS_BUILD=true handling, Worker bindings (GITHUB_CACHE_KV, GITHUB_SIGNAL_RELAY) living in wrangler.jsonc, and Neon serverless WebSocket driver constraints (no -pooler hostname, db created/closed per request inside runWithDb).
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown with H2 sections (Single Source Of Truth, Three Scoped Objects with a markdown table, Client Exposure Rule, When Adding/Updating Env Vars as a numbered 6-item list, Gotchas). No code samples; describes policy in prose and bullet lists.

nodes.name: .agents/logging.md
nodes.summary: Defines the use of evlog through @tsu-stack/logger as the only logger facade; do not install or import evlog directly. The default rule is to not add application logs during normal work unless explicitly asked or the flow is audit/security/high-risk. Specifies when to log (after outcome, not before), level semantics (INFO=completed business outcome, DEBUG=investigation only, WARN/ERROR=call to action), wide-event structure (event + data in fields, not string-interpolated messages), and post-emit warnings (a logger is sealed after emit()). Covers global Hono onError + parseError pattern, structured createError helper, Better Auth identity integration via the request-scoped logger (Hono: c.get('log'), TanStack Start/oRPC: passed through context), sensitive-data redaction (no secrets/tokens/headers/raw bodies), request logging sampling, and client-logging rarity. Bootstrap packages like @tsu-stack/env may use small console.debug statements.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown with 14 H2 sections (Default Rule, When To Log, Levels, Structure, Post-Emit Warnings, Error Handling, Identity And Better Auth, Sensitive Data, Request Logging, Client Logging, Bootstrap Console). Multiple TypeScript code samples showing the wide-event createLogger + emit, onError parseError pattern, and createError helper. Cross-references Better Auth and request middleware.

nodes.name: .agents/media-storage.md
nodes.summary: Prescriptive guide for the first S3-compatible media storage implementation in this repo (not yet shipped). Defines the generic media_asset schema with purposes (avatar/document/image/archive) and statuses (pending_upload, uploaded_orphaned, linked), UUID-based keys, default direct browser-to-storage uploads via files-sdk (MinIO adapter), synchronized hard delete as the default lifecycle, and the proposed package split (packages/core/src/media-asset/, packages/db/src/schema/media-asset.schema.ts, packages/api/src/lib/storage/). Includes the upload contract (discriminated union PUT/POST), the request-contract / upload-in-browser / complete / link flow, URL derivation rules (do not persist publicUrl on media_asset; resolve at read time from files.url(key)), preferred env names (MINIO_*), and a permission/policy checklist.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown with 17 H2 sections (Goals, First Implementation Rule, Recommended Library, Default Package Shape, Implementation Order, Generic Media Asset Shape, URL Derivation, Upload Contracts, Upload Flow Defaults with H3 Request A Contract / Upload In The Browser / Complete The Upload / Link To The Owning Row subsections, Delete Lifecycle with H3 Synchronized Hard Delete / Async Delete With Retry / Soft Delete Or Retention Window subsections, Environment Variables, Permission And Policy Checklist, Change Rules). nodes.name: .agents/orpc.md
nodes.summary: Repo-specific oRPC patterns: use publicProcedure/protectedProcedure from packages/api/src/lib/procedures/factory.ts, add .route({ description, method }), declare input/output Zod schemas explicitly, and prefer repo-native return shapes. Errors use .errors(...) with errors.MY_ERROR() throws (typed data, status, no sensitive data); ORPCError is allowed for interop. Handlers receive context.logger (request-scoped evlog) — do not log routine reads, do not duplicate middleware/global error logs; one wide terminal event for a genuinely durable outcome. Router folder shape: packages/api/src/routers/<slice>/{index.ts,queries.ts}; promote helpers into lib/ only on real reuse. Client error handling uses isDefinedError from @orpc/client and switches on error.code (not message), reading error.data only for typed errors.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown with 9 H2 sections (Goals, Server Route Shape, Errors, Logging, Router Conventions, Router Folder Shape, Shared Contracts, Client Error Handling, Practical Rules). Multiple TypeScript code samples for procedure shape, errors definition, wide-event handler, and isDefinedError-based client mutation onError.

nodes.name: .agents/seo.md
nodes.summary: Authoritative guide for TanStack Start route `head()` SEO using `@tsu-stack/seo`. Package boundaries: keep packages/seo isolated from packages/env, pass app-specific values from the consuming app, prefer #@/ absolute imports, export only what the app uses. App pattern: define one typed site config with `satisfies TanStackStartSeoSite`, wrap generateTanStackStartSeo in an app helper like generateAppSeo, inject repo-specific locale defaults in the app wrapper. Route pattern: use route head() per TanStack Start docs, pass canonicalPath and locale from route params, use loaderData for dynamic titles/descriptions, set robots noindex for dashboards/auth/editors. Limitations: package does not generate robots.txt/sitemap.xml, does not fetch data, does not infer locale.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown with 7 H2 sections (Package Boundaries, App Pattern, Route Pattern, Root Route, Titles And Images, JSON-LD, Limitations). No code samples; describes policy and pattern in prose.

nodes.name: .agents/tanstack-patterns.md
nodes.summary: Repo-specific TanStack Router/Start patterns. Documents the FSD layer mapping (routes=app, pages, widgets, features, entities, shared — imports only go downward), the standard segment structure (index.ts barrel, ui/, lib/, utils/, types/, hooks/, stores/, api/), and route hierarchy ((github-layout) for marketing+guest auth, (guest) pathless under it for sign-in/create-an-account, __protected/ as auth guard directly under root so the dashboard does not inherit the public navbar/footer). Route file rules: thin, import page component, wire beforeLoad with ensureQueryData using exported query option factories; caching lives in React Query (defaultPreloadStaleTime: 0 is intentional), not the router cache.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown with 7 H2 sections (Routing with FSD Layers/Segment Structure/Route Hierarchy/Adding a Route H3 subsections, Route Files Stay Thin, React Query Preloading, Gotchas). Includes a markdown table of FSD layers and a text-block segment structure tree.

nodes.name: .agents/testing.md
nodes.summary: Authoritative testing policy. Core rule: assume no tests unless explicitly requested; never auto-add tests to feature work; respect unit (src/**/__tests__/*.test.ts) and e2e (__e2e__/**/*.spec.ts) location conventions. Vite+/Vitest setup rule: when tests are explicitly requested and the package has no Vite+ testing config, add a root vite.config.ts (do not create vitest.config.ts) and put Vitest config inside via `defineConfig({ test: { include: [...] } })`. Canonical commands are `vp run test:unit:run` and `vp run test:e2e:run`. When tests are explicitly requested, generate behavior-driven tests (happy paths, edge cases, pathological inputs, regression-prone cases, contract invariants) with table-driven tests, public-contract testing, fixtures/builders, and regression tests for bug fixes.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown with 4 H2 sections (Core Policy, Test Commands, Test Locations, Vite+/Vitest Setup Rule, When Tests Are Explicitly Requested). Includes a small TypeScript code sample for the default vite.config.ts test block. Cites https://viteplus.dev/guide/test as the source of truth.

nodes.name: .agents/typescript.md
nodes.summary: Repo-wide TypeScript conventions. Shared schema pattern: small domain module with constants.ts, types.ts, utils.ts, index.ts. Schema placement: keep schemas close to the owning slice/package; for app-local code default to types/thing.type.ts; promote to packages/core when consumed across package boundaries. Module resolution: nodenext with allowImportingTsExtensions; cross-package via @tsu-stack/<package>/<subpath>; intra-package via #@/ alias. lib/ vs utils/: lib holds business logic/integrations/API clients, utils holds pure stateless helpers. Linting uses Oxlint with eslint-disable compatible comments; import sorting is auto-enforced by Oxfmt in the order builtins -> external -> @tsu-stack/* -> @/pages -> @/widgets -> @/features -> @/entities -> @/shared -> relative -> styles.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown with 6 H2 sections (Shared Schema Pattern, Schema Placement, Module Resolution, `lib/` vs `utils/` with a markdown table, Linting (Oxlint), Import Sorting (auto-enforced by Oxfmt)). Code samples for the ThingSchema + inferred Thing pattern and oxlint disable comments.

nodes.name: .agents/ui.md
nodes.summary: Source of truth for app UI composition, extraction decisions, and packages/ui boundaries. Default sources: prefer @tsu-stack/ui/components/* primitives, then app wrappers in apps/web/src/shared/ui, lucide-react for icons, @tsu-stack/ui/lib/utils cn(...) for class composition. Build page UI in pages/, composite sections in widgets/ and features/, app-level primitives in shared/ui; keep route files thin. Extraction rule: only extract to packages/ui when the component is reusable, app-agnostic, and the shared package can own styling/a11y. packages/ui must not import from apps/*, TanStack Router, or app env modules. Dependency injection: accept linkComponent?: React.ElementType (default 'a') and imageComponent?: React.ElementType (default shared image primitive). Repo uses shadcn with base-maia style, neutral base color, CSS variables, and Lucide icons.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown with 9 H2 sections (Goals, Default Sources, App Composition, Extraction Rule, Shared Package Boundaries, Dependency Injection, Decision Rule with a TypeScript CardProps sample, shadcn Usage, Images And Links, Do And Don't). Describes policy in prose and bullet lists with a small TypeScript reference pattern.

nodes.name: .agents/vite-plus.md
nodes.summary: Intro to Vite Plus (Vite+) as the all-in-one CLI replacing pnpm/npm/yarn and bundling Oxlint, Oxfmt, Vitest, and staging hooks into a single defineConfig in the root vite.config.ts. CLI mapping table (pnpm -> vp, pnpx -> vpx, pnpm run <script> -> vp run <script>, pnpm --filter <pkg> <script> -> vp run --filter <pkg> <script>, etc.). Key behaviors: `vp run -r <script>` runs recursively across packages, `vp check` runs lint+typecheck, `vp check --fix` adds format, `vp config` sets up Vite Plus hooks on prepare. The root vite.config.ts holds staged hooks ('*': 'vp check --fix'), Vitest config, Oxfmt ignore/import-sort config, and Oxlint config with FSD/query/react-hooks plugins. Mental model: vp is the only CLI needed; never install pnpm/npm/yarn directly for standard development.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown with 5 H2 sections (What It Is, CLI Mapping with a markdown table, Key Behaviors, Root vite.config.ts, Mental Model). No code samples; describes CLI surface in a table and bullets.

nodes.name: .agents/workflow.md
nodes.summary: Repo workflow: essential commands table (`vp run dev`, `vp check`, `vp run -w fix`, `vp run build`). Validation timing: prefer narrow package-local `vp check` first; use `vp run -w fix` only after substantial code/config work or before handoff. Do not run -w fix for markdown-only edits; staged files auto-check on git commit. Completion claims: do not report work complete until the relevant edits/commands have run and output has been checked. Fallow is auxiliary cleanup only, not default validation. Database schema changes: edit packages/db/src/schema/, run `vp run db:generate`, check DATABASE_URL (Neon-backed; stop and warn if it points at prod/main), run `vp run db:migrate`. `vp run db:setup` is first-time dev setup only, wrapping vpx neon-new@latest. Commits use Conventional Commits (commitlint) with auto `vp check --fix` via hooks.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown with 8 H2 sections (Essential Commands with a markdown table, Validation Timing, Completion Claims, Auxiliary Static Analysis, Feature Workflows, Database Schema Changes, Other Commands with a markdown table, UI Components And shadcn, Testing, Commits). nodes.name: portal-props
nodes.summary: Documents the optional `portalProps` forwarding pattern that composed coss primitives expose on their `*Popup` and toast-provider surfaces. `portalProps` is spread onto the internal Base UI `Portal`, enabling `keepMounted`, `container` (stacking contexts, micro-frontends, shadow DOM), and any other `Portal.Props` passthrough. nodes.name: docker-compose.coolify

nodes.name: 0001-identity-refresh-hybrid-auto-write
nodes.summary: ADR-0001 — Identity refresh uses a hybrid auto-write policy with a ratcheting confidence threshold. The GitHub-webhook / workflow-run triggered `refreshIdentityWorkflow` calls `identityRepository.writeFacet(..., source='github')` for high-confidence diffs, but uncertain writes are held back as proposals in `portfolio_identity_proposals`. The threshold starts permissive (auto-write everything) and ratchets up over time as false positives accumulate — keeping the agent visibly working without a daily approval ritual, while preserving a single-knob safety valve for LLM errors.
nodes.languageNotes: Short, single-paragraph ADR — no Context/Decision/Consequences sections. References `refreshIdentityWorkflow`, `identityRepository.writeFacet`, and `portfolio_identity_proposals` as the concrete artifacts.

nodes.name: 0003-voice-is-not-a-facet
nodes.summary: ADR-0003 — Voice is a peer of identity, not a facet. The agent's writing-style rules (tone, dos, don'ts) live in `packages/core/src/voice/schema.ts` and `packages/ai/src/agents/prompt-fragments.ts` instead of as a `portfolio_identity_facets` row. Voice is consumed only by the agent's `instructions` string — it is not displayed on the public site, not exposed to the dashboard identity view, and not part of the audit trail. Without the split, `portfolio_identity_revisions` would conflate 'Salah rewrote his bio' with 'the agent was told to sound more casual' as indistinguishable timeline events.
nodes.languageNotes: Single-block rationale. No Context/Decision/Consequences headers. References both packages/core/src/voice/schema.ts and packages/ai/src/agents/prompt-fragments.ts as the split, and contrasts the voice validation shape (freeform tone + lists) with identity's structured {short, long} bio.

nodes.name: 0005-idempotency-delivery-id-and-unique-index
nodes.summary: ADR-0005 — Idempotency uses two layers for the GitHub webhook handler. Layer 1 (cheap, O(1)): the `X-GitHub-Delivery` ID is written to `GITHUB_CACHE_KV` with a 7-day TTL and the workflow is skipped on a hit. Layer 2 (defense in depth): the `portfolio_identity_revisions` table has a unique index on `(facet_key, source, source_ref)` when `source_ref IS NOT NULL` so a missed cache TTL or a parallel manual edit still fails at the database.
nodes.languageNotes: Single-block ADR. Names the two invariants and lists the failure mode of removing either layer (cost of duplicate webhooks or two revisions for the same key).

nodes.name: 0011-signal-vs-namespace-invalidation
nodes.summary: ADR-0011 — Revalidation signals and cache namespaces are two parallel mechanisms for GitHub cache staleness, both written by webhooks and admin paths. Signals (`github_revalidation_signal`) are time-relative per-topic events keyed by `signal_key` with `updated_at`; namespaces (`github_cache_namespace`) are monotonic per-group version counters keyed by `namespace`. Staleness rules differ: a cached row with `fetchedAt < signal.updatedAt` is stale, a row whose `namespaceVersion !== currentVersion` is stale forever. Webhooks write to both; `refreshInstallationAccess` uses signals only; `clearViewerCache` writes 4 signal + 9 namespace keys with no overlap. The ADR documents the transactional fix wrapping both writes in a `getDb().transaction(...)` block and the switch from `new Date()` to `now()` (database transaction-start time) in the SET clause.
nodes.languageNotes: Full Context/Decision/Consequences structure (this one uses a custom `## The transactional fix` and `## now() over new Date()` subsection). References handle-github-webhook.ts:67-71 and packages/api/src/routers/github/index.ts:123-152. Considered-options section explains why signals and namespaces were not collapsed into one table.

sections.heading: # 0011 — Revalidation signals and cache namespaces are different invariants about the same event

nodes.name: 0012-signal-relay-durable-hibernation
nodes.summary: ADR-0012 — The `GitHubSignalRelay` Durable Object moves from an in-memory `Map<WebSocket, Set<string>>` (which lost every connected client on isolate restart, forcing a 20s polling fallback in apps/web/src/shared/lib/use-github-signal-stream.ts:455-498) to the Cloudflare WebSocket Hibernation API. The class now extends `DurableObject<Env>` from `cloudflare:workers`, calls `this.ctx.acceptWebSocket(server)` on connect, stores per-socket subscriptions via `server.serializeAttachment({ keys: [...] })`, and implements the runtime-supplied `webSocketMessage` / `webSocketClose` / `webSocketError` handlers. Per-socket state survives hibernation; idle clients no longer keep the isolate alive. The `web_socket_auto_reply_to_close` compat flag is auto-enabled on compatibility_date >= 2026-04-07. ADR also notes the v1 `new_sqlite_classes` migration in apps/server/wrangler.jsonc:61-66 is no longer needed.
nodes.languageNotes: Full Context/Decision/Consequences structure (uses `## Cost and behaviour` and `## Considered options` subsections). Direct file references include apps/server/src/github-signal-relay.ts:19, apps/web/src/shared/lib/use-github-signal-stream.ts:455-498, and apps/server/wrangler.jsonc:61-66.

sections.heading: # 0012 — Signal relay uses the Durable Object WebSocket Hibernation API

nodes.name: 0013-portfolio-entry-table
nodes.summary: ADR-0013 — Replace the scattered `enable_ai` boolean on `experience`, `project`, and `stack` with a dedicated `portfolio_entry` join table keyed on `(type, entity_id)`. Single `portfolio.toggle` oRPC route owns the write, single `portfolio.list` oRPC route serves the read for both the public site and the agent. Schema: `portfolio_entry` has id PK, type (`experience | project | stack | contact` pgEnum), entity_id (text), timestamps; each entity carries a nullable `portfolio_entry_id` FK with cascade delete. The `portfolio.list` route accepts an RSQL-style `filter` parsed in `packages/api/src/lib/rsql.ts` (with default = every opted-in row) and a `paginated` flag for cursor pagination. The migration backfills from `enable_ai = true` rows in one step, then drops the columns in a second step to keep the data move and the schema change reviewable.
nodes.languageNotes: Full Context/Decision/Consequences structure. References packages/api/src/lib/rsql.ts, `portfolio.toggle`, and `portfolio.list` oRPC routes. Notes the contact table also gains a `portfolio_entry_id` even though it never had `enable_ai` — the FK exists for the first toggle.

sections.heading: # Portfolio entry table for per-item visibility

nodes.name: 0014-portfolio-sync-in-entity-repos
nodes.summary: ADR-0014 — Portfolio-entry sync lives inside the entity repositories, not the route handlers. Supersedes part of ADR-0013's prediction that forms would call `portfolio.toggle` separately — in practice the entity create/update forms send `includedInPortfolio` as part of the entity payload, which caused two concrete failures: (1) portfolio_entry create never set the entity's `portfolioEntryId` FK so responses showed `includedInPortfolio: false`; (2) portfolio_entry delete happened after entity re-fetch so responses showed `includedInPortfolio: true` after the entry was removed. Fix: `experienceRepository`, `projectRepository`, `stackRepository` each gain an optional `includedInPortfolio?: boolean` options-bag param on `create()` / `update()`. The portfolio_entry create/delete runs inside the same Drizzle transaction as the entity write, the FK is set on create, the entity is re-fetched with `tx.query.*` for the response. `portfolio.toggle` stays as-is (a different entry point). Contacts are unchanged (composite key).
nodes.languageNotes: Full Context/Decision/Consequences structure. Explicitly notes the partial-supersession of ADR-0013 — the dedicated join table insight is unchanged, only the form-submit write path is added. References `tx.query.*` (Drizzle relational query API) and explains why the cross-table responsibility belongs in the repo.

sections.heading: # Portfolio-entry sync lives inside entity repositories

nodes.name: 0015-pdfnative-pdf-generation
nodes.summary: ADR-0015 — Replace `@react-pdf/renderer` with `pdfnative` + `pdfnative-react` for resume PDF generation. The motivating gap: @react-pdf cannot produce tagged PDFs (no `/StructTreeRoot`), the foundation for screen-reader accessibility and reliable ATS text extraction. pdfnative is the only library scoring on all four axes (tagged PDF/PDF-A, Cloudflare Workers compat, zero runtime dependencies, declarative React model). Decision: install pdfnative + pdfnative-react, rewrite `apps/web/src/server/resume-pdf.tsx` to pdfnative-react components maintaining the same A4 single-column layout, enable `tagged: true` on `<Document>` for PDF/A-2b, register custom Geist fonts via `fontEntries`, switch from `renderToBuffer()` (Node Buffer) to `renderToBytes()` (Uint8Array) for R2 compatibility, and remove @react-pdf from the workspace catalog. Layout translation notes document the contact-row (`<Text>` with ' · ' separator since pdfnative-react has no flexbox) and section grouping (use atomic `<Heading>` / `<Paragraph>` / `<List>` instead of `<View>`).
nodes.languageNotes: Full Context/Decision/Consequences structure with a Considered options table comparing pdfnative, @imprint-pdf/react, keep @react-pdf, and PDFKit-direct. References apps/web/src/server/resume-pdf.tsx as the file to rewrite, and notes the supply-chain/API-stability risk given pdfnative v1.4.0 (Apr 2026) and pdfnative-react v0.2.0 (Jun 2026) are young.

sections.heading: # pdfnative for tagged, ATS-safe resume PDFs

nodes.name: 0016-hono-resume-generation
nodes.summary: ADR-0016 — Move resume PDF generation from the TanStack Start web worker to the Hono server worker, using `pdfnative` core's `buildDocumentPDFBytes()` directly instead of `pdfnative-react`'s `renderToBytes()`. ADR-0015 chose pdfnative + pdfnative-react, but kept the renderer in apps/web (TanStack Start), where every generation made three hops (web → server for data → render in web → R2) and pulled React's reconciler into the Worker bundle just to serialize a JSX tree to JSON `DocumentParams`. Decision: add `resume.generate` as an oRPC protectedProcedure on the existing `resumeRouter` in `packages/api/src/routers/resume.router.ts`, rewrite the resume template as a plain TypeScript module producing `DocumentParams` JSON, add an `r2_buckets` `MEDIA_BUCKET` binding to the server worker's wrangler.jsonc, thread the binding through the oRPC context, simplify the web `POST /api/resume/generate/` route to delegate, and move R2 cleanup into the server's `resume.delete` procedure. Server bundle gains ~200KB (pdfnative core), web bundle loses pdfnative + pdfnative-react + react-reconciler weight.
nodes.languageNotes: Full Context/Decision/Consequences structure. Builds directly on ADR-0015 — the v1 work and the ADR-0015 table are referenced as upstream context. References packages/api/src/routers/resume.router.ts, the oRPC context, and the server wrangler.jsonc (R2 binding surface increase).

sections.heading: # Move resume generation to Hono server with pdfnative core

nodes.name: 2026-06-30-r2-files-sdk-integration
nodes.summary: Implementation plan that replaces the broken UploadThing integration with a Cloudflare R2 + `files-sdk` direct-upload flow. The browser asks the worker for a presigned PUT contract, uploads directly to R2 via the S3-compatible API, and uses the returned public URL as the form value — the worker never sees upload bytes. 10 tasks cover R2 bucket provisioning, env schema (R2_ACCOUNT_ID/ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET_ACCESS_KEY/BUCKET/PUBLIC_BASE_URL in packages/env/src/web/env.server.ts:18), local .dev.vars, pnpm-workspace.yaml dependency swap (drop uploadthing + @uploadthing/react; add files-sdk ^2.0.0), the storage client in packages/api/src/lib/storage/index.ts (Files + r2() adapter from files-sdk/r2), the files-sdk gateway mounted in apps/web/src/routes/api/files/index.ts with Better Auth (keyPrefix = `${userId}/`), the shadcn UploadProgress component install, the rewrite of apps/web/src/shared/form/image-field.tsx (useFiles + UploadProgress), the deletion of the old uploadthing files, and end-to-end verification. Rollback path uses `git revert --no-commit HEAD~9..HEAD`.
nodes.languageNotes: Standard superpowers plan format with Goal / Architecture / Tech Stack header, File Structure table, then Task 1–10. Each task has Files, numbered Steps with `pnpm --filter` and `git commit` commands. The Architecture paragraph names the key invariant: worker never proxies bytes. Step 6 has the `keyPrefix` authorization contract explained in a follow-on Notes block.

nodes.name: 2026-07-07-multi-select-batch-actions
nodes.summary: Implementation plan that adds checkbox-based multi-select with batch delete and add-to-portfolio actions to the experiences, projects, and stacks pages. Extends the shared `createItemsUIStore` (apps/web/src/widgets/items-page/lib/) with `selectedIds: Record<string, boolean> | null` plus `toggleSelect` / `selectAll` / `clearSelection` actions (cleared on tab or filter change), threads `isBatchSelected` + `onToggleSelect` through `ListItem` and a Checkbox overlay through `StackItem`, adds a `batch?: BatchConfig` prop to `HeaderActions` (renders coss `Group` + `GroupSeparator` with Trash2Icon / BookmarkPlusIcon / CheckIcon / X buttons plus a coss `AlertDialog` for destructive confirmation), and wires each page to pass `orpcClient` (from @tsu-stack/api/client/tanstack-start/orpc) batch calls. Tasks 6/7/8 are parallel: same pattern across the three pages, swapping the entity client (`orpcClient.experiences.delete` / `orpcClient.projects.delete` / `orpcClient.stacks.delete`) and the portfolio toggle `type` (`"experience"` / `"project"` / `"stack"`). The existing `await onRevokeAll?.()` error in packages/ui/components/auth-session-manager.tsx:327 is explicitly called out as pre-existing and unrelated.

Step 5 in Task 6 calls out a deliberate bypass of TanStack Query mutations: `Promise.allSettled(ids.map((id) => orpcClient.experiences.delete({ id })))` because the mutation cache would dedupe concurrent identical calls.

nodes.name: 2026-07-09-agent-infrastructure
nodes.summary: Implementation plan that wires the web app through the server's auth-aware oRPC pipeline to the Mastra agent Worker, using AI SDK streaming for chat. Pipeline: web → `orpcQueryClient` → server (Hono + oRPC + Auth) → service binding (prod) or `AGENT_WORKER_URL` (dev) → agent Worker. 11 tasks cover: (1) adding `OrpcContextAgentWorker` to packages/core/src/orpc-context/index.ts:81-91; (2) creating a shared `createAgentWorker()` factory in packages/api/src/lib/agent/worker.ts that prefers `AGENT_WORKER` (Cloudflare Fetcher) and falls back to `AGENT_WORKER_URL` (uses `@ts-expect-error` for the `duplex: "half"` forwarding of streaming bodies); (3) adding `AGENT_WORKER_URL: z.string().url().optional()` to packages/env/src/server/env.ts and documenting it in packages/env/.env.example; (4) wiring the `services[]` binding (`devhub-agent` service) + env var in apps/server/wrangler.jsonc and wrangler.dev.jsonc plus the `AGENT_WORKER: Fetcher` type in apps/server/worker-configuration.d.ts; (5–6) plumbing `agentWorker` through both the Hono and SSR oRPC context builders; (7) adding `ai` and `@ai-sdk/react` to the workspace catalog (Mastra's peerDep requires `ai >= 5.0.76`); (8) creating packages/api/src/routers/agent.router.ts with `chat` (`POST /agents/:agentId/generate`) and `chatStream` (`POST /agents/:agentId/stream/ui` — NOT `/stream`, which returns Mastra's own chunk format; `useChat` expects AI SDK `UIMessageChunk`); (9) the web client transport in apps/web/src/features/agent/api/agent-chat.client.ts using `useChat` + `eventIteratorToUnproxiedDataStream` from `@orpc/client`; (10) the route at apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/playground/agent/index.tsx with noindex SEO; (11) end-to-end verification of token-by-token streaming. Plan explicitly notes that `@mastra/client-js`, `@orpc/ai-sdk`, `ai`, and `@ai-sdk/react` are NOT installed and that the SSE-encoded `UIMessageChunk` is piped through unchanged using `streamToEventIterator` from `@orpc/server` (verified in `@orpc/shared@1.14.6` d.ts).
nodes.languageNotes: Plan opens with a 16-line 'Type & Path Notes' section that documents the precise Mastra route paths (`/agents/:agentId/stream/ui` for AI SDK UIMessage stream, NOT `/stream`), import alias conventions (`@/` in apps/web, `#@/` in packages/api, `@tsu-stack/<pkg>/` cross-package), Cloudflare `Fetcher.fetch(Request | string)` signature, and the fact that streaming bytes can be piped through oRPC's `streamToEventIterator(upstream.body)` without format conversion. Each task has Files, numbered Steps, typecheck, and a `git commit` line.

nodes.name: packages/env/.env.example
nodes.summary: Single source of truth for env var documentation in the monorepo. Loaded by every consumer (apps/web dev/preview/start, apps/server dev) via `pnpm dotenvx run -f ../../packages/env/.env -- ...`. Grouped into four sections: Shared (VITE_SERVER_URL, VITE_WEB_URL, DATABASE_URL, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, GITHUB_CLIENT_ID, GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET — all required), Web (VITE_IMGPROXY_URL — optional), Server (ENABLE_OPEN_API_DOCS, GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET, RESEND_API_KEY, EMAIL_FROM, OPENCODE_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, OLLAMA_BASE_URL, EMBEDDING_MODEL, AGENT_WORKER_URL — most optional, OPENCODE/OPENAI/OLLAMA are the LLM/embedding key trio), and Build (SOURCE_COMMIT). 17 total variables with explicit `✅ required` / `⚙️ optional` / `✅ required at runtime` markings. nodes.name: packages/seo/README.md
nodes.summary: README for @tsu-stack/seo — SEO helpers for TanStack Start route `head()` objects. Documents the deliberately small public API: `generateTanStackStartSeo({ site, alternates?, title?, description?, images?, openGraphType?, robots?, scripts?, includeDocumentMeta? })` returns a TanStack-Start-compatible head object containing title (via `titleTemplate`), description, Open Graph tags, Twitter card tags, canonical links, alternate locale links, robots + googlebot meta, optional application/ld+json script tags, and (when `includeDocumentMeta: true` is passed on the root route only) charset + viewport + application-name + x-dns-prefetch-control. Setup pattern: define a `TanStackStartSeoSite` config in the consuming app, then wrap `generateTanStackStartSeo` in an app-specific `generateAppSeo` that injects the app's `i18n.baseLocale` + `i18n.locales`. Common use cases section covers: root route (includeDocumentMeta: true), static page (canonicalPath + locale), dynamic page (loaderData + params), noindex routes (auth, dashboard, search), and JSON-LD pass-through. Limitations section explicitly states the package does NOT configure sitemap.xml / robots.txt / prerendering / SSR / favicon / preload / non-SEO links, does NOT inspect route params or loader data (caller must pass them in), and does NOT generate JSON-LD objects (caller must serialize). Title template behavior applies to document title, og:title, and twitter:title only.
nodes.languageNotes: Standard monorepo-package README — Public API → What It Generates → Basic Setup → Common Use Cases → Title Template Behavior → Limitations → Recommended Integration Pattern. Code blocks are TypeScript. The site-config example uses a `satisfies TanStackStartSeoSite` clause (not `as`) so the inferred type is preserved. The Limitations section is unusually thorough — six explicit boundaries the package will not cross, so consumers know what they need to wire in the app shell.

nodes.name: packages/seo/package.json

One script: `test:unit: vp test`.

The `test:unit` script is the only script; the package has no build step (consumed as `.ts` directly via the source export, like all other @tsu-stack/* packages in this monorepo).

nodes.name: packages/ui/package.json
nodes.summary: Workspace package manifest for @tsu-stack/ui — the shared UI primitives + coss/Base-UI component library consumed by apps/web. ESM, subpath imports `#@/*` → `./*.ts` (root-level files), and three exports: `./*` → `./*.ts` (root files like lib/utils), `./styles/globals.css` (the main CSS entry), and `./components/*` → `./components/*` (every coss/Base-UI primitive + custom component like auth-session-manager). One script: `ui: vpx shadcn@latest` — wires the shadcn CLI to the coss/Base-UI registry. Dependencies: @base-ui/react (the unstyled primitives layer), @fontsource-variable/inter (the Inter Variable font), @lonik/oh-image (the optimized image primitive), @shikijs/langs ^4.3.0, @tanstack/react-router (for typed Link/useNavigate in primitives), the full @tiptap/* suite (Link/Placeholder/Typography/PM/React/StarterKit — used by RichTextField), class-variance-authority + clsx + tailwind-merge (variant API), cmdk (command palette), date-fns, files-sdk (R2 upload hook for ImageField), geist (the Geist Variable font family), lucide-react (icons), motion (Framer Motion successor), next-themes (theme switching), radix-ui (compatibility re-exports), react-day-picker ^10.0.1 (CalendarDropdown), react-resizable-panels, shiki ^4.3.0 (code highlighting), sonner (toasts), std-env (runtime detection), tw-animate-css (animation utility classes for Tailwind 4), and vaul ^1.1.2 (drawer primitive). Dev deps: @tsu-stack/tsconfig, @types/node, @types/react, @types/react-dom, tailwindcss, typescript. Peer deps: react / react-dom (catalog-pinned).
nodes.languageNotes: The `ui` script wires the shadcn CLI to vpx (Vite Plus) and is how the team runs coss/Base-UI codegen. The three exports shape is what lets apps/web do `import { Button } from "@tsu-stack/ui/components/button"` and `import "@tsu-stack/ui/styles/globals.css"` (the CSS file is exported as a separate subpath).

nodes.name: packages/ui/tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: TypeScript config for @tsu-stack/ui. Extends @tsu-stack/tsconfig/tsconfig.base.json, sets the in-package path alias `@tsu-stack/ui/*` to `./*` (so a component at `components/button.tsx` resolves as `@tsu-stack/ui/components/button`), and explicitly includes two files outside the package root: `../../apps/web/src/shared/ui/icon-picker.tsx` and `../../apps/web/src/shared/form/calendar-dropdown.tsx` — both files live in apps/web but need to be type-checked against the UI package's surface (the UI components they compose are resolved via the path alias). Excludes `node_modules`.
nodes.languageNotes: The cross-package include is unusual — it's the only tsconfig in the monorepo that pulls in files from another package. It works around a tsconfig-include boundary issue when the UI compiler encounters icon-picker.tsx and calendar-dropdown.tsx (which were originally in apps/web but depend on UI primitives).

nodes.name: packages/ui/styles/animations.css
nodes.summary: Tiny animation keyframes module in @tsu-stack/ui. Defines a single `spinner-leaf-fade` @keyframes (opacity 0 → 1 → 0) inside a Tailwind 4 `@theme inline` block, then surfaces it as the utility class `animate-spinner-leaf-fade` (800ms linear infinite) inside `@layer utilities`. This is the spinner-leaf animation the coss `Spinner` primitive uses.
nodes.languageNotes: Two-block structure: `@theme inline { @keyframes ... }` declares the keyframes (so Tailwind 4 picks them up), then `@layer utilities { .animate-... }` exposes the animation utility. The 0% / 50% / 100% opacity ramp is the only easing in the file.

nodes.name: packages/ui/styles/base-theme.css
nodes.summary: Backward-compatibility alias layer for the @tsu-stack/ui theme. The coss theme (in shadcn.css) uses Tailwind's standard neutral-* palette; this file re-exposes the older `base-*` / `surface-*` / `night-*` / `light` / `white-4` token names by mapping each to its neutral-* equivalent. All 16 tokens are declared inside a single Tailwind 4 `@theme inline` block so they become utility classes (`bg-surface-1`, `text-night`, etc.) — the comment explicitly says existing code using base-* / gray-* continues to work.
nodes.languageNotes: Single `@theme inline` block, no `dark` override here — dark-mode colors flow through the standard `neutral-*` palette and the base-theme aliases inherit them via `var(--color-neutral-N)`. The `white-4` alias uses the coss `--alpha()` helper so it must be loaded after shadcn.css.

nodes.name: packages/ui/styles/globals.css
nodes.summary: Main CSS entry for @tsu-stack/ui — the single import target for apps/web (`@import "@tsu-stack/ui/styles/globals.css"` in apps/web/src/shared/styles/app.css). Top-level cascade: tailwindcss + tw-animate-css + animations + shadcn + base-theme + scrollbar + prose. The `@source "../**/*.{ts,tsx}"` directive tells Tailwind 4 to scan all UI package source for class names (so coss primitives + their consumers are picked up). `@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *))` activates the coss dark-mode selector. The `@layer base` block adds: prefers-reduced-motion media query that disables all animations/transitions, a universal border + outline reset, iOS Safari touch-action: manipulation, forced-color-adjust: none, color-scheme: light dark, font-feature-settings for Inter-style glyph variants, antialiased font smoothing, iOS tap-highlight removal, text-rendering: optimizeLegibility, overscroll-behavior: none, body bg/text, and `a { cursor: pointer }`. A `.shiki` / `.shiki span` block sets dual-theme Shiki colors (light + dark). A `@utility container` redefines Tailwind's container with the bespoke width ladder the design system uses (640 / viewport-32px / 1280-vw-414px / min(vw-710px, 1536px)). A final `@theme inline` block adds the `--text-xss` (0.7rem) and `--text-xsss` (0.6rem) micro-typography tokens that shadcn.css does not provide.
nodes.languageNotes: Critical ordering: tailwindcss + tw-animate-css imports first, then animations, shadcn (coss theme), base-theme (which depends on neutral-*), scrollbar, prose. The `@custom-variant dark` declaration must come after the tailwindcss import. The container @utility is unusual — it shadows Tailwind's built-in container with the project's bespoke width breakpoints.

nodes.name: packages/ui/styles/prose.css
nodes.summary: Tailwind 4 port of the `prose` typography utility (adapted from gridatek/tailwind-typography). The `@theme` block declares 23 `--tw-prose-*` theme variables (body, headings, lead, links, bold, counters, bullets, hr, quotes, quote-borders, captions, kbd, kbd-shadows, code, code-bg, pre-code, pre-bg, th-borders, td-borders) plus the 19 `--tw-prose-invert-*` light-mode counterparts. Body / headings / kbd use the warm-neutral `var(--color-white)` / `var(--color-black)` / `var(--color-base-N)` palette, and the code/pre backgrounds use `oklch(from var(--color-base-700) l c h / 0.5)` to derive a 50%-opacity tint from the same color. The `@utility prose` block then styles paragraphs (with `:where([class~="not-prose"])` opt-outs for nested non-prose content), lead text, links (hover underline), list-check checkboxes (`accent-color: var(--color-success)`), bold, ordered/unordered lists with all type=A/a/A s/a s/I/i variants, list markers, table styles, headings (h1–h6), blockquote with the `--tw-prose-quote-borders` left border, kbd (`box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px var(--tw-prose-kbd-shadows)`), code (inline + block), lead, hr, and the image rule. The full prose selector is gated with `:not(:where([class~="not-prose"], [class~="not-prose"] *))` so any element inside a `.not-prose` container is exempt.
nodes.languageNotes: Largest CSS file in the package. Every selector is a `:where(...)` so the `not-prose` opt-out is the same `:where` selector. `oklch(from var(--color-base-700) l c h / 0.5)` is Tailwind 4 / modern CSS relative-color syntax — it derives a half-opacity version of the same color without needing a separate token. List `type=A s` / `type=a s` / `type=I s` / `type=i s` are HTML's `<ol type="A s">` style — A/a with start attribute, I/i with start attribute.

nodes.name: packages/ui/styles/scrollbar.css
nodes.summary: Custom scrollbar styling for @tsu-stack/ui. Defines `--scrollbar-width: 6px` and `--scrollbar-thumb: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-foreground) 20%, transparent)` on `:root` inside `@layer base`. The custom scrollbar is applied via `*::-webkit-scrollbar` only inside `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` (so non-touch devices get the thin style, touch devices get the platform default). Sets the same on the standard `*` selector with `scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: var(--scrollbar-thumb) transparent`. A second `:root:has(.disable-scroll)` rule disables global scrolling (used by full-screen dialogs). A `@utility no-scrollbar` block provides a `scrollbar-width: none` utility that also hides the webkit scrollbar.
nodes.languageNotes: The two media-query clauses `hover: hover` and `pointer: fine` together are the canonical way to detect devices with hover-capable pointers (mouse / trackpad) — touch devices get the platform's default scrollbar. The `.disable-scroll` opt-out uses `:has(...)` (modern browsers only) and is a cleaner pattern than toggling `overflow: hidden` on body manually.
mediaQueries: @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) — webkit + firefox scrollbar rules

nodes.name: packages/ui/styles/shadcn.css
nodes.summary: Core coss/Base-UI theme layer for @tsu-stack/ui — declares the design tokens consumed by every primitive. The `@theme inline` block has two parts: (1) 6 @keyframes (`accordion-down` / `accordion-up` that read `var(--radix-accordion-content-height, var(--accordion-panel-height, auto))`, `skeleton`, `caret-blink`, `toast-success-odd/even`, `toast-error-odd/even`) plus 5 animation properties (`--animate-skeleton`, `--animate-caret-blink`, and 4 toast animations); (2) the full color-token surface (--font-heading / --font-sans / --font-mono, --color-sidebar-* / --color-code-highlight / --color-code / --color-chart-1..5 / --color-secondary-foreground / --color-secondary / --color-ring / --color-primary / --color-popover-foreground / --color-popover / --color-muted / --color-input / --color-foreground / --color-destructive / --color-card / --color-border / --color-background / --color-accent) and the radius scale (--radius-sm/md/lg/xl/2xl/3xl/4xl as multiples of --radius). Then 12 `@custom-variant` rules (data-open, data-closed, data-checked, data-unchecked, data-selected, data-disabled, data-active, data-horizontal, data-vertical, aria-invalid, data-destructive, data-invalid) — each gates `@slot` on either `data-state="X"` or the data-X attribute. The `:root` block declares light-mode values (40+ variables: destructive, info, success, warning, accent, background, border, card, foreground, input, muted, popover, primary, ring, secondary, chart-1..5, code, code-foreground, code-highlight, radius, sidebar-*). The `.dark` block declares the dark-mode counterparts (mirrors the same set). The `@layer base` block applies `border-border outline-ring/50` to `*`, `bg-background text-foreground` to `body`, sets `font-family: var(--font-mono)` on code/kbd/samp/pre, and sets `html` to `font-mono font-sans` (the dual-fonts rule is unusual — both classes applied, with the latter winning).
nodes.languageNotes: Largest and most complex stylesheet in the package. The two `@theme inline` content blocks (keyframes + tokens) and 12 `@custom-variant` rules are the coss-specific surface; the `:root` + `.dark` blocks are the shadcn-shaped light/dark color surface; the `@layer base` block applies the global resets. The `html { @apply font-mono font-sans }` rule is a shadcn-style scaffold — the second class wins so html defaults to sans, but JetBrains Mono-style font-feature-settings are available via the explicit font-mono declarations on `code/kbd/samp/pre`.

nodes.name: .agents/skills/coss-particles/SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Index of all 484 coss UI particles across 52 component types. Documents the JSON URL pattern `https://coss.com/ui/r/p-<name>-<N>.json` used to fetch each particle's source, the particle file location `apps/ui/registry/default/particles/`, and the generator script `node apps/ui/scripts/generate-particle-index.cjs`. The body is a per-component H3 catalog with counts (e.g. button 40, autocomplete 15, input-group 28, slider 23, select 23, calendar 24) followed by per-particle description + URL entries for each component type, used as a lookup table when picking a copy-paste-ready UI pattern built on coss primitives.
nodes.languageNotes: One H1, six H2 sections (How to use, JSON URL pattern, Source code, Updating, Component types, plus a trailing exhaustive per-particle catalog), with H3 sections per component type and 1-2 line entries per particle (description + coss.com JSON URL).

nodes.name: .agents/skills/coss/SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Authoritative skill for coss UI components (Base UI + shadcn-style developer experience). Frontmatter specifies Tailwind v4 + @base-ui/react requirements. Defines usage workflow (identify intent -> consult component-registry -> select from coss docs -> check particles -> write minimal code -> self-check a11y), 5 agent-output principles (prefer primitives, composition over reinvention, follow coss naming exactly, accessibility, Tailwind v4 conventions), 6 critical usage rules (no invented APIs, trigger/popup hierarchy, a11y labels, primitive guides, full manual install deps, prefer styled exports over *Primitive), 4 rule references (styling, forms, composition, migration + portal-props), and 7 high-risk primitives flagged for extra care (dialog, menu, context-menu, select, form, input-group, toast).
nodes.languageNotes: YAML frontmatter (name, description, compatibility, license, metadata.author) + 11 H2 sections (What this skill is for, Source of truth, Out of scope, Principles, Critical usage rules, Component discovery, Usage workflow, Installation reference, Primitive Guidance, Output Checklist, plus a Resources appendix referencing the four rules/* and component-registry.md, portal-props.md, and 54 primitives/*).

nodes.name: .agents/skills/mastra/scripts/provider-registry.mjs
nodes.summary: Standalone Node CLI that loads the installed `@mastra/core` provider-registry.json (walks up to 10 dirs to find node_modules) and lists providers + their model names sorted newest-first. Exposes three modes: `--list` (all providers with name + model count), `--provider <name>` (model list for a given provider), `--help` (usage). Version sorting is done by `extractVersion` (regex-based numeric-segment parser that strips param-count suffixes like 8b/70B, filters date-like segments >=2020, and skips MM-DD-looking tail patterns) feeding `compareVersionsDesc` (tuple-wise numeric compare with name tiebreaker).
nodes.languageNotes: ESM script with shebang. 5 functions: findRegistryPath (walks up looking for the registry json), loadRegistry (reads + parses with friendly error), extractVersion (model-name version parser), compareVersionsDesc (sort comparator), listProviders, listModels, printUsage. CLI dispatch is a flat `args.includes('--list')` / `args.indexOf('--provider')` ladder at the bottom.

nodes.name: .agents/skills/mastra/SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Mastra framework skill (v2.0.0). Pre-loads the `provider-registry.mjs` helper and 8 references covering create-mastra, core-concepts, embedded-docs, remote-docs, model-selection, common-errors, migration-guide, mastra-api. Core message: never trust internal knowledge — Mastra evolves rapidly, always verify against embedded docs in node_modules first, then installed source, then remote https://mastra.ai/llms.txt. Requires ES2022 modules (CommonJS will fail). Models must use the `provider/model-name` format and the provider-registry script must be run first to verify keys/names. Mastra Studio runs via `npm run dev` on http://localhost:4111; the `mastra api` CLI inspects or calls resources on local / Mastra platform / remote servers.
nodes.languageNotes: YAML frontmatter (name, description, license, metadata with author/version/repository) + 11 H2 sections (Critical: do not trust internal knowledge, Prerequisites, Resources as a 3-column markdown table, Priority order, Core concepts, Mastra Studio, Mastra API CLI, Critical requirements, When you see errors, Development workflow, plus a Resources appendix linking 8 reference files).

nodes.name: .agents/skills/neon-postgres/SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Comprehensive Neon Serverless Postgres skill. Two ways to fetch docs as markdown (append `.md` to URL or send Accept: text/markdown), and a single index at https://neon.com/docs/llms.txt. Documents self-driving setup via `npx -y neonctl@latest init --agent <name>` (supports 11 agent names: cursor, copilot, claude, claude-desktop, codex, opencode, cline, gemini-cli, goose, zed), the 6-step setup flow (select org/project, get DATABASE_URL, pick connection method, optional Neon Auth, optional ORM, schema), connection methods (serverless driver for @neondatabase/serverless, Neon JS SDK for auth+data), 4 developer tools (CLI Init, VSCode extension, MCP server, neonctl), Neon Admin API (REST + TypeScript SDK + Python SDK), Neon Auth overview, plus branching (copy-on-write, isolated compute), autoscaling, scale-to-zero (default 5min idle, cold start ~hundreds of ms), instant restore, read replicas, connection pooling via PgBouncer (add -pooler to hostname), IP allow lists, and logical replication.
nodes.languageNotes: YAML frontmatter with multi-line description that lists 14 trigger phrases. 20+ H2 sections (What Is Neon, Getting Started with H3 sub-flows Check Status Quo / Self-Driving Setup / Setup Flow, Connection Methods & Drivers, Developer Tools, Neon Admin API, Neon Auth, Branching, Autoscaling, Scale to Zero, Instant Restore, Read Replicas, Connection Pooling, IP Allow Lists, Logical Replication). Markdown tables for docs index and tool URLs. Inline shell commands for setup, install, and CLI workflows.

nodes.name: .agents/summaries/github-repo-page-port.md
nodes.summary: Current-state summary for the public GitHub repo experience (replaces the earlier drifted task log). Confirms the public repo routes live under apps/web/src/routes/{-$locale}/(github-layout)/, the public GitHub shell lives in apps/web/src/widgets/layout/, GithubRepoPage uses SidePanelPortal from @/widgets/layout for activity cards, branch comparison is the read-only branch-comparison-banner, and data flows packages/github -> packages/api/src/routers/github -> page-local query files. nodes.languageNotes: Short status document. 4 H2 sections (Status, What Exists Now, Current Constraints, Known Gaps) plus a 'Important Files' bullet list of 9 paths. No code samples; one absolute path reference to vite.config.ts.

nodes.name: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md
nodes.summary: GitHub Issue template for bug reports. YAML frontmatter (name: Bug report, about, title, labels: bug, assignees). 5 H2 sections (Bug Description, How to Reproduce, Expected Behavior, Screenshots, Platform/OS, Additional Context) plus commented-out 'Would I like to work on this?' section. The Platform/OS section has a Desktop subsection (OS/Browser/Version placeholders) and a Smartphone subsection (Device/OS/Browser/Version placeholders).
nodes.languageNotes: Standard GitHub issue form with YAML frontmatter at top defining labels: bug. Uses italic prompts and a 1-2-3-4 numbered list inside How to Reproduce. The Smartphone subsection duplicates the Desktop fields with device-specific labels.

nodes.name: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md
nodes.summary: GitHub Issue template for feature requests. YAML frontmatter (name: Feature request, about, title, labels: enhancement). 4 H2 sections (Problem with 'Is your feature request related to a problem?' italic prompt, Possible Solution, Alternative Solutions, Additional Context or Screenshots) plus commented-out 'Would I like to work on this?' section. Mirrors the bug_report template structure but reframes for new functionality.
nodes.languageNotes: Same shape as bug_report.md but the frontmatter label is enhancement instead of bug, and the section prompts are solution-oriented rather than reproduction-oriented.

nodes.name: .node-version
nodes.summary: Single-line Node.js version pin: `25.8.2`. Consumed by tools that honour .node-version (rtx/mise/asdf and the Voidzero setup-vp GitHub Action) to install the matching runtime for the workspace. Aligns with the `node:25-bookworm-slim` base image used by apps/server/Dockerfile and apps/web/Dockerfile and the Node 24 baseline used in CI (setup-vp installs Node 24 for the runner, but apps target Node 25).
nodes.languageNotes: Plain text, single line, no newline at end (the file is exactly the version string).

nodes.name: .ua/.understandignore
nodes.summary: Stock .understandignore template for the file-analyzer skill. Documents the syntax (.gitignore-style globs, # comments, ! negation, trailing / for dirs), lists built-in defaults (node_modules/, .git/, dist/, build/, obj/, *.lock, *.min.js), and ships an entire library of uncommented examples covering logs, .env files, .pnpm-store, dist-ssr, IDE folders (.vscode/* with !.vscode/extensions.json + !.vscode/settings.json negated), OS files, test file patterns (JS/TS .test.*/.spec.*/.snap, .NET *Tests.cs, Java *Test.java / *IT.java / *Spec.kt, Go *_test.go, C++ *_test.cc/_unittest.cc/_benchmark.cc), and suggested uncomments for docs/ and scripts/. All examples are commented out — the file is a starting template, not an active ignore list.
nodes.languageNotes: Plain text with comment lines starting with `#`. No active patterns — everything is commented out (so the default behavior applies). The structure is: header comment block explaining syntax, then three labelled sections (From .gitignore, Detected directories, Test file patterns) each containing commented-out examples.

nodes.name: .ua/config.json
nodes.summary: Configuration for the file-analyzer skill. Single key `outputLanguage: "en"` instructs the analyzer agent to emit all human-readable text (summaries, tags, descriptions) in English regardless of the repo's primary language. Located next to `.understandignore` in the `.ua/` scratch directory.
nodes.languageNotes: Single-key JSON object. No trailing newline visible. The key name `outputLanguage` matches the `Language directive` field used in the analyze-files prompts.

nodes.name: .vite-hooks/commit-msg
nodes.summary: Git commit-msg hook. Runs `commitlint --edit "$1"` against the staged commit message, enforcing the Conventional Commits ruleset configured at the workspace root. Wired in via the Vite Plus hook installer so the hook lives in `.vite-hooks/` rather than `.git/hooks/` (keeping it tracked in git).
nodes.languageNotes: Plain shell one-liner. No shebang line, no newline (the file is exactly the command). The `commitlint` binary is expected to be on PATH (provided by the workspace devDependencies).

nodes.name: .vite-hooks/pre-commit
nodes.summary: Git pre-commit hook. Runs `vp staged` to invoke the Vite Plus staged-changes pipeline (oxlint --fix, oxfmt --write, typecheck, tests for the changed packages) against the staged diff. Tracked in `.vite-hooks/` rather than `.git/hooks/` so the hook config is version-controlled.
nodes.languageNotes: Plain shell one-liner. No shebang line, no trailing newline.

nodes.name: .zed/settings.json
nodes.summary: Zed editor settings for the workspace. Configures the oxlint LSP with `run: onType`, safe-fix kind, type-aware, and `unusedDisableDirectives: deny`, and the oxfmt LSP with `fmt.configPath: ./vite.config.ts` and `run: onSave`. Per-language overrides: JavaScript/TypeScript/Vue.js all disable Prettier, enable `format_on_save: on`, and route formatting through the oxfmt LSP. JavaScript additionally binds code actions to `source.fixAll.oxc` so all oxc fixes apply on save.
nodes.languageNotes: JSON object with two top-level keys: `lsp` (oxlint + oxfmt initialization_options) and `languages` (per-language formatter bindings). No comments allowed in JSON, so all intent is encoded in key names.

nodes.name: apps/package.json
nodes.summary: Minimal monorepo sub-workspace root manifest. Single key `type: "module"` makes every apps/* package implicitly ESM. No dependencies, no scripts, no exports — the file exists only to set the module mode for nested apps that pnpm-workspace.yaml picks up under `apps/*`.
nodes.languageNotes: Single-key JSON, no name/version. The `type: module` field propagates to every package below apps/ so they can use ESM syntax and .js extensions by default.

nodes.name: apps/agent/src/mastra/agents/weather-agent.ts
nodes.summary: Defines `weatherAgent`, a Mastra Agent (id `weather-agent`) that uses `openai/gpt-5-mini`, wires the `weatherTool` from `#@/mastra/tools/weather-tool`, attaches 3 scorers (toolCallAppropriateness at ratio 1, completeness at ratio 1, translation at ratio 1) from `#@/mastra/scorers/weather-scorer`, and instantiates `new Memory()`. The instructions prompt frames the agent as a weather assistant that always asks for a location, translates non-English city names, prefers the most relevant part of multi-part locations, and returns temperature/humidity/wind/precipitation details. Registered in apps/agent/src/mastra/index.ts as the `weatherAgent` export of the Mastra instance.
nodes.languageNotes: TypeScript module with two relative imports via the #@/* path alias and one zod-free definition. The instructions string uses a 7-bullet guidance list. Scorers are wired with sampling `{ type: 'ratio', rate: 1 }`.

nodes.name: apps/agent/src/mastra/index.ts
nodes.summary: Central Mastra instance for the apps/agent worker. Constructs `mastra = new Mastra({...})` with a `CloudflareDeployer` (name `devhub-agent`, custom_domain routes for `${VITE_WEB_URL}/agent*`, plus placeholder D1 + KV bindings), one workflow (`weatherWorkflow`), one agent (`weatherAgent`), three scorers, a `MastraCompositeStore` (LibSQLStore default + DuckDBStore for observability), a `PinoLogger` at info level, and an `Observability` config with `MastraStorageExporter` + `MastraPlatformExporter` exports and a `SensitiveDataFilter` span output processor. VITE_WEB_URL is sourced from `@tsu-stack/env/web/env.isomorphic`.
nodes.languageNotes: Top-level await for `new DuckDBStore().getStore('observability')` inside the composite-store `domains` field. Uses #@/* path alias for local imports. The D1 and KV bindings use placeholder ids (`d1-database-id`, `kv-namespace-id`) — they would need to be filled in before deploy.

nodes.name: apps/agent/src/mastra/scorers/weather-scorer.ts
nodes.summary: Three Mastra scorers for the weather agent. `toolCallAppropriatenessScorer` wraps `createToolCallAccuracyScorerCode({ expectedTool: 'weatherTool', strictMode: false })`. `completenessScorer` is the prebuilt `createCompletenessScorer()`. `translationScorer` is a custom LLM-judged scorer (id `translation-quality-scorer`) that pre-processes run input/output, analyzes whether a non-English location was correctly translated (output schema has nonEnglish/translated/confidence/explanation), generates a 0..1 score (1 if not applicable, 0.7+0.3*confidence if translated, 0 otherwise), and emits a reason string. Exported both as individual scorers and as a `scorers` object.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of fluent builder API: `createScorer({...}).preprocess(...).analyze({ outputSchema, createPrompt }).generateScore(...).generateReason(...)`. Uses `getAssistantMessageFromRunOutput` / `getUserMessageFromRunInput` helpers from `@mastra/evals/scorers/utils`. The analyze prompt embeds `${results.preprocessStepResult.userText}` and `assistantText` inside a multi-line string.

nodes.name: apps/agent/src/mastra/tools/weather-tool.ts
nodes.summary: Defines `weatherTool = createTool({ id: 'get-weather', ... })` that takes a `location` string and returns temperature/feelsLike/humidity/windSpeed/windGust/conditions/location. The internal `getWeather` async function geocodes the location via the Open-Meteo geocoding API, fetches the weather forecast, and maps the WMO weather code to a human-readable condition via `getWeatherCondition`. `getWeatherCondition` is a 30-entry lookup table mapping WMO weather codes 0..99 to descriptive strings (clear sky -> thunderstorm with heavy hail).
nodes.languageNotes: Two internal types (`GeocodingResponse`, `WeatherResponse`) declared as types. `getWeatherCondition` is a pure function (no side effects). Tool execute uses `await getWeather(inputData.location)` directly.

nodes.name: apps/agent/src/mastra/workflows/weather-workflow.ts
nodes.summary: Two-step Mastra workflow `weatherWorkflow` (id `weather-workflow`). Step 1 `fetchWeather` takes a `city` string, geocodes via Open-Meteo, fetches the hourly forecast, and returns a `forecastSchema` (date, maxTemp, minTemp, precipitationChance, condition, location). Step 2 `planActivities` takes the forecast, fetches the `weatherAgent` from `mastra.getAgent('weatherAgent')`, streams a structured prompt asking the agent to suggest day-specific activities with morning/afternoon/indoor-alternative/special-considerations sections, accumulates the streamed text into `activitiesText`, and returns `{ activities }`. Workflow is built via `createWorkflow({...}).then(fetchWeather).then(planActivities)` and committed via `weatherWorkflow.commit()`.
nodes.languageNotes: Duplicates the `getWeatherCondition` lookup table from weather-tool.ts (a smaller 20-entry version). Uses `for await (const chunk of response.textStream)` to accumulate streamed agent output. The planActivities prompt is ~40 lines of structured instructions with emoji section headers and exact formatting requirements.

nodes.name: apps/server/src/app.ts
nodes.summary: Main Hono application for the @tsu-stack/server worker. Constructs `app = new Hono<AppEnv>().basePath(serverBaseUrl.pathname)`, applies CORS scoped to the configured VITE_WEB_URL, the honoLoggerMiddleware (with `**/health/**` and `**/_logs/ingest` excluded), and the client-side log ingestion endpoint. Registers explicit routes BEFORE the catch-all `/*` middleware: a root health-check (returns 200 with name+status+timestamp), a WebSocket upgrade at `/api/ws/github-signals` that forwards to the GITHUB_SIGNAL_RELAY Durable Object, the `/auth/reference` redirect, the Better Auth openapi schema generator, the Better Auth catch-all `/auth/*` (intentionally outside `runWithDb` since the HTTP drizzle singleton is stateless), and the `/webhooks/github` POST (intentionally inside `runWithDb` so handleGitHubWebhook's repositories have a live connection). Exports `app`, `openApiHandler` (with SmartCoercionPlugin, OpenAPIReferencePlugin configured for /docs, RethrowHandlerPlugin) and `rpcHandler`.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of Hono middleware ordering: routes registered before the catch-all `/*` short-circuit. Comments explicitly explain why auth uses the http singleton while webhooks need runWithDb. The `/*` middleware builds the per-request db, calls createContext, then runs the rpcHandler -> openApiHandler fallback chain. Imports `#@/shared/lib/logger` for the side-effect of initLogger.

nodes.name: apps/server/src/github-signal-relay.ts
nodes.summary: Cloudflare Durable Object class `GitHubSignalRelay` that fans out GitHub signal keys to subscribed WebSocket clients. Two routes: POST `/broadcast` (JSON body `{ signalKeys: string[] }` sends a JSON `{ type: 'signals', keys }` payload to every accepted WebSocket whose serialized attachment has any matching key; closes failing sockets) and `/connect` (requires `Upgrade: websocket` header, otherwise 426; on upgrade calls `ctx.acceptWebSocket(server)` and returns the client side of a `WebSocketPair`). The `webSocketMessage` handler accepts `{ type: 'subscribe', keys: string[] }` and overwrites the per-socket attachment; malformed JSON is silently ignored. `webSocketClose` and `webSocketError` close the socket cleanly. Type guard `isSubscribeMessage` does runtime shape validation.
nodes.languageNotes: Standard Cloudflare Durable Object pattern: class with constructor(state, env), `fetch`, plus the four lifecycle methods (`webSocketMessage`, `webSocketClose`, `webSocketError`, and the implicit `webSocketError`). Attachment per-WS holds a `SocketState = { keys: string[] }` so the broadcast loop can filter subscribers.

nodes.name: apps/server/src/index.ts
nodes.summary: Re-export of the Hono `app` from `./app`. Single line: `export { app } from './app';`. The package's `main` field in package.json points at this file, so the server worker entry is `app.fetch` (Hono's standard Cloudflare Workers handler).
nodes.languageNotes: One-line re-export. No logic.

nodes.name: apps/server/src/shared/lib/logger.ts
nodes.summary: Side-effect module that initializes the server-side logger at import time. Calls `initLogger({ env: { environment: ENV_SERVER.NODE_ENV, service: LOG_SERVICES.SERVER, version: ENV_SERVER.WORKERS_CI_COMMIT_SHA } })` and is imported by app.ts (`import '#@/shared/lib/logger'`) so the logger is always up before the first request lands.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure side-effect module. No exports. Uses #@/* path alias (implied by the import map in package.json).

nodes.name: apps/server/src/worker.ts
nodes.summary: Cloudflare Workers default-export handler. Imports `app` from `#@/app` and the `GitHubSignalRelay` Durable Object from `#@/github-signal-relay`. Exports a default object with `fetch(request, env, executionContext)`: routes the WebSocket upgrade at `${VITE_SERVER_URL}/api/ws/github-signals` to the `global` instance of the GitHubSignalRelay DO via `stub.fetch('https://internal/connect', request)`, otherwise delegates to `app.fetch`. Also re-exports `GitHubSignalRelay` so Wrangler's `new_classes` migration can register it.
nodes.languageNotes: Default-export pattern required by the Workers runtime. The GITHUB_SIGNAL_RELAY id-from-name lookup is `idFromName('global')` (a single shared instance rather than per-key instances). The `https://internal/connect` URL is the internal handshake protocol consumed by github-signal-relay.ts's handleConnect.

nodes.name: apps/server/vite.config.ts
nodes.summary: Vite Plus config for the @tsu-stack/server Cloudflare Worker. Three big lifts beyond a normal Vite config: (1) a custom `stubNodeBuiltinsPlugin` that resolves bare `path`/`os`/`url` to the `node:`-prefixed forms (Workers `nodejs_compat` provides these) and stubs `fs`, `http`, `https`, `stream`, `child_process`, `cluster`, `worker_threads`, `dgram`, `net`, `tls`, `dns`, `querystring` with a `Proxy` + named exports (sync fs ops, fs/promises, child_process, stream, http, net, tls, dns, cluster, worker_threads, dgram, querystring, crypto `= undefined`); (2) a `REQUIRE_POLYFILL_BANNER` injected via `rollupOptions.output.banner` so rolldown's `__require` calls in inlined CJS (gray-matter, probe-image-size, needle, stream-parser, lodash.merge, typescript) get a no-op global `require` instead of throwing a 10021 validation error; (3) the `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` `cloudflare({ inspectorPort: false, configPath: process.env.IS_BUILD === 'true' ? 'wrangler.jsonc' : 'wrangler.dev.jsonc' })` so `vp build` (with `cross-env IS_BUILD=true vp build`) uses the production wrangler and `wrangler dev` uses the dev config. Also sets `server.cors: false` so Hono's CORS middleware owns preflight, and `server.port` derived from VITE_SERVER_URL (default 5000).
nodes.languageNotes: The single-largest config in the repo. Uses an inline `defineConfig({ run: { tasks: { build: { command: 'cross-env IS_BUILD=true vp build' } } }, build: { rollupOptions: { external: [...], output: { banner: REQUIRE_POLYFILL_BANNER } } }, ssr: { noExternal: [...] }, plugins: [stubNodeBuiltinsPlugin(), cloudflare({...})], server: { cors: false, port: devServerPort } })`. The stub plugin's `load()` for STUB_MODULE_ID returns a ~200-line string of no-op exports — comment explains that Workers has no fs/child_process/etc. and these only need to satisfy module load, not runtime calls.

nodes.name: apps/server/worker-configuration.d.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated Cloudflare Workers env type definition emitted by `wrangler types --config wrangler.dev.jsonc` (the `cf-typegen` package.json script). The bulk of the file is a deeply-nested `interface Cloudflare.Env` declaring the typed shape of every binding the server worker reads at runtime: vars (VITE_SERVER_URL, VITE_WEB_URL, AGENT_WORKER_URL, etc.), the `Cloudflare.Env` is a single object with one key per binding. Includes the typed interface for the GitHubSignalRelay Durable Object class. The file is regenerated whenever the wrangler config changes, so it should not be hand-edited.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure types — no runtime code, no exports. The single `Cloudflare.Env` interface is ~14000 lines because it inlines the full shape of every binding (KV, R2, Durable Objects, service bindings, vars, secrets). The `cf-typegen` script in apps/server/package.json is what regenerates it.

nodes.name: apps/web/public/manifest.json

Identifies the app as 'TanStack App' / 'Create TanStack App Sample' with three icons (favicon.ico at 64/32/24/16 sizes, logo192.png, logo512.png), start_url '.', display 'standalone', theme_color '#0c0a09' (warm-neutral dark), and background_color '#ffffff'. Served from /manifest.json by the TanStack Start static handler.
