nodes.name: apps/web/src/components/files-sdk/upload-progress.tsx
nodes.summary: 'use client' R2 Files SDK progress UI. Renders one row per in-flight upload (file name, percent, progress bar) plus an aggregate progress bar when more than one upload is active. `StatusIcon` swaps CheckCircle2 / Loader2 / XCircle based on the FileUploadState status (success/error/aborted/pending). Uses the coss Progress primitive and lucide icons, all wrapped in a div with `cn('flex flex-col gap-3', className)`. Returns null when there are no uploads.
nodes.languageNotes: Two internal components: `StatusIcon({ status })` and `UploadRow({ upload })`, plus the public `UploadProgress({ files, className })`. Uses `cn` from @tsu-stack/ui/lib/utils for class merging. Key uses `upload.key ?? ${upload.name}-${index}` fallback.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/config/app.config.ts
nodes.summary: Frozen site-level config object. Computes `emailSupport = contact@${host}` from VITE_WEB_URL and exports `appConfig.site` with author (Salah Mohsen), basePath / baseUrl / url derived from VITE_WEB_URL, description ('Portfolio'), jurisdictionCountry ('the Republic of the Philippines'), longName ('Batteries-Included TanStack Start Monorepo Boilerplate Template | tsu!stack'), serverLocation ('Japan'), shortName ('Salah Mohsen'), and a `version` slot filled by Vite's `__BUILD_SOURCE_COMMIT__` define (declared via `declare const __BUILD_SOURCE_COMMIT__: string;` because it comes from ENV_WEB_SERVER at build time).
nodes.languageNotes: Single Object.freeze({ site: {...} }) export. The declare-const for __BUILD_SOURCE_COMMIT__ is a Vite build-time define injected by apps/web/vite.config.ts (consuming ENV_WEB_SERVER.SOURCE_COMMIT).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/features/agent/api/agent-chat.client.ts
nodes.summary: Client-side AI SDK `useChat` hook for the oRPC agent. `useAgentChat()` returns `useChat({ transport: { async sendMessages, reconnectToStream } })`. The transport posts to `orpcClient.agent.chatStream({ agentId: DEFAULT_AGENT_ID, messages: options.messages as never }, { signal: options.abortSignal })`, gets an event iterator back, converts it to a ReadableStream via `eventIteratorToUnproxiedDataStream`, then pipes the byte stream through a custom `sseToUIMessageStream` transform (parses `data: <json>` lines separated by blank lines, handles trailing data in flush(), drops `[DONE]` and malformed frames). The `reconnectToStream` deliberately throws — oRPC + AI SDK integration does not support stream reconnection. DEFAULT_AGENT_ID is hardcoded to 'weather-agent'.
nodes.languageNotes: Three pieces: `sseToUIMessageStream` (raw ReadableStream<Uint8Array> -> ReadableStream<Record<string, unknown>> via SSE parsing), `useAgentChat` (the exported hook), and the `DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` constant. Two `as unknown` / `as never` casts are documented in inline comments — they suppress a 'two UIMessage types with the same name' cross-version type identity mismatch between the client `useChat` and the server-side `ai` package.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/features/agent/index.ts
nodes.summary: Single-line barrel re-export of the agent feature: `export { DEFAULT_AGENT_ID, useAgentChat } from '@/features/agent/api/agent-chat.client';`.
nodes.languageNotes: Tiny barrel. Uses the @/ path alias rather than a relative import.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/features/auth/index.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel re-export for the auth feature slice. Exposes the two form components: `CreateAnAccountForm` from create-an-account-form and `SignInForm` from sign-in-form.
nodes.languageNotes: Two named re-exports via @/ alias. No internal logic.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/features/auth/ui/create-an-account-form.tsx
nodes.summary: 'use client' sign-up form. Uses the shared `useAppForm` TanStack Form helper with zod schema validation (email, name >=2 chars, password >=8 chars, refine passwords-match). On submit calls `authClient.signUp.email({ email, name, password })` via a useMutation. On success invalidates the `getAuthUserQueryOptions()` query and navigates to `redirectTo` (default '/'). Renders inside a Container with FieldGroup, logo, name/email/password/confirm fields via `form.AppField` + `field.InputField`, a FieldSeparator 'Or', a disabled Google button (toast.error 'Not yet implemented.'), and footer links to terms-of-service and privacy-policy. Shows DefaultLoader while the auth query is pending.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of `form.AppField` / `form.AppForm` / `form.SubmitButton` — the project's TanStack Form helper extensions. The Google button is intentionally a stub (toast.error on click). The zod refine runs at onSubmit and surfaces 'Passwords do not match' on the confirmPassword field.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/features/auth/ui/sign-in-form.tsx
nodes.summary: Sign-in form (server component) offering two paths: Continue with GitHub (via `authClient.signIn.social({ provider: 'github', callbackURL: createWebCallbackUrl(redirectTo) })`) and Continue with Passkey (via `authClient.signIn.passkey()`). Each path is its own useMutation; on success both invalidate `getAuthUserQueryOptions()`, the passkey path additionally navigates to `redirectTo`. Error handling builds a `[status code] message` toast string from the authClient result. `createWebCallbackUrl(redirectTo)` strips trailing slashes from VITE_WEB_URL and prefixes a path. Card/Button/FieldGroup from coss UI, plus lucide's KeyRound icon for the passkey button. Footer links to terms-of-service and privacy-policy.
nodes.languageNotes: Single Server Component (no 'use client' at the top — the useMutation calls happen on the client via the React Query hydration). The error message construction is careful: prefers `error.message`, optionally prefixes with `[status code]` if status exists. The `redirectTo` prop type is `NavigateOptions['to']` from @tanstack/react-router so it accepts the same values as a route's `to`.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/features/github/api/get-github-profile-repos.query.ts
nodes.summary: GitHub profile-repos React Query wrapper. `getGithubProfileReposQueryOptions(isPrivate)` picks between `orpcQueryClient.github.privateGetProfileRepos` and `orpcQueryClient.github.publicGetProfileRepos` based on the boolean, and applies `meta: persistedMeta` + `staleTime` / `gcTime` from `githubCachePolicy.reposList`. `useGetGithubProfileReposQuery(enabled)` calls `useAuth()` to derive isPrivate and spreads the options into useQuery, with an `enabled` flag.
nodes.languageNotes: Standard slice-local query module shape (per api-fetching-patterns.md): query options factory + hook wrapper, no result type re-export (the oRPC client infers it). `persistedMeta` is a shared query-persistence marker from @/shared/lib/query-persistence.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/features/github/api/get-github-setup-status.query.ts
nodes.summary: GitHub setup-status query wrapper. `getGithubSetupStatusQueryOptions()` returns `orpcQueryClient.github.getSetupStatus.queryOptions({ meta: persistedMeta })` (no explicit staleTime/gcTime, so the defaults apply). `useGetGithubSetupQuery()` wraps it in useQuery. Also exports `GithubSetupStatusQueryResult = Awaited<ReturnType<typeof orpcClient.github.getSetupStatus>> | null` as a type alias for callers.
nodes.languageNotes: Three exports: `getGithubSetupStatusQueryOptions`, `useGetGithubSetupQuery`, and the `GithubSetupStatusQueryResult` type alias. Uses both `orpcClient` (type-only) and `orpcQueryClient` (runtime) imports from @tsu-stack/api/client/tanstack-start/orpc.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/features/github/index.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel re-export for the github feature slice. Re-exports the two query options + hooks (renaming `useGetGithubSetupQuery` -> `useGetGithubSetupStatusQuery`), the `GithubSetupStatusQueryResult` type, and the two combobox UI components (`GitHubRepoCombobox`, `GitHubRepoMultiCombobox`).
nodes.languageNotes: Renames `useGetGithubSetupQuery` to `useGetGithubSetupStatusQuery` on re-export — the api file's name has been kept short for direct callers, while the public alias matches the GithubSetupStatusQueryResult type.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/features/github/ui/github-repo-combobox.tsx
nodes.summary: 'use client' single-select GitHub repo combobox for TanStack Form. Uses `useAuthSuspense()` (NOT `useAuth()`) to ensure the auth session is resolved before picking the public/private endpoint — `useAuth()`'s initial `user: undefined` race used to lock the query key on the public path even for the owner. Renders a coss Popover + Command with searchable CommandItem rows; selected URL is bound to a form field via `useFieldContext<string>()`; toggle behavior re-selecting the same url clears the field. The Combobox displays `repo.fullName`, a lock icon for private repos, the description, and a clear button. Field wrapper has FieldLabel, FieldDescription, FieldError.
nodes.languageNotes: The long comment block above `useAuthSuspense()` documents why useAuth() was wrong (suspense boundary resolves the auth query before picking the endpoint). Internal `RepoOption` component shows fullName + description. The CommandItem is the local styled <button> (not cmdk), so `onClick` is used instead of `onSelect`.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/features/github/ui/github-repo-multi-combobox.tsx
nodes.summary: 'use client' multi-select GitHub repo combobox. Field context is `string[]` (URLs). Uses `useAuthSuspense()` to pick public/private endpoint, fetches via `getGithubProfileReposQueryOptions(isPrivate)`. The trigger shows either 1 fullName or 'N repositories selected'. Each CommandItem toggles the URL in the field value via filter/spread. A clear button resets to []. Same Popover + Command + Field scaffolding as the single-select variant. RepoOption shows fullName + optional description with a lock icon for private repos.
nodes.languageNotes: Shares the `RepoOption` shape and the Popover+Command+Field layout with the single-select variant. Field-error rendering is at the end of the Field. The 'use client' directive is required because useState + useQuery + the popover's open state all run on the client.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/features/portfolio/api/get-portfolio-list.query.ts
nodes.summary: Portfolio list React Query wrapper. `getPortfolioListQueryOptions()` returns `orpcQueryClient.portfolio.list.queryOptions({ input: {}, staleTime: 60min, gcTime: 2hr })`. `useGetPortfolioListQuery()` wraps it in useQuery. Also exports `PortfolioListQueryResult = Awaited<ReturnType<typeof orpcClient.portfolio.list>>` as a type alias.
nodes.languageNotes: Hardcodes staleTime=1h and gcTime=2h (the portfolio list changes slowly). Empty `input: {}` since the portfolio list has no required parameters. The PortfolioListQueryResult type is the standard 'Awaited<ReturnType<...>>' pattern that the api-fetching-patterns.md doc prescribes.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/features/portfolio/index.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel re-export for the portfolio feature slice. Re-exports `getPortfolioListQueryOptions` + `useGetPortfolioListQuery` and the `PortfolioListQueryResult` type from the api query file.
nodes.languageNotes: Standard 3-line barrel — two named exports + one type re-export, all from @/features/portfolio/api/get-portfolio-list.query.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/features/profile/api/update-profile.mutation.ts
nodes.summary: Profile update mutation wrapper. `getUpdateProfileMutationOptions()` returns `orpcQueryClient.profile.update.mutationOptions()`. Re-exports the `ProfileUpdateInput` Zod-inferred type from @tsu-stack/core.
nodes.languageNotes: Tiny module — single function + single type re-export. `ProfileUpdateInput` flows from packages/core (the shared Zod schemas contract).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/features/profile/index.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel re-export for the profile feature slice. Single line: `export * from './api/update-profile.mutation';` (everything that file exports — `getUpdateProfileMutationOptions` and the `ProfileUpdateInput` type — is re-exported).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the wildcard `export *` form (the only feature barrel in this batch that does so). No `export {}` typing-block needed since update-profile.mutation has no other consumers.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/global.d.ts
nodes.summary: Global ambient TypeScript declarations for the apps/web TanStack Start project. `declare module '*.css'` allows CSS imports anywhere without TS errors. `declare module '@fontsource/*' { const src: string; export default src; }` and the same for `@fontsource-variable/*` declare font-source package modules as default-exporting a string path (per the fontsource issue #1038 referenced in the comment).
nodes.languageNotes: Pure ambient declarations. No runtime impact. The `*.css` declaration is what lets Vite's CSS import pattern work in TS files without `// @ts-ignore`.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/lib/command-palette-icons.tsx
nodes.summary: Hand-coded lucide-style SVG icon components for the command palette. Internal `createIcon(path, viewBox = '0 0 24 24')` factory returns a React component that renders a 16x16 stroke='currentColor' strokeWidth=2 rounded-linecap/linejoin SVG with the provided path. Exports 13 named icons: DashboardIcon, ArchiveIcon, GitPullRequestIcon, IssuesIcon, ReviewsIcon, SettingsIcon, ExternalLinkIcon, CodeIcon, GitMergeIcon, GitPullRequestClosedIcon, GitPullRequestDraftIcon, RefreshCwIcon, UserCircleIcon.
nodes.languageNotes: Each icon is one call to `createIcon('<svg path data>')`. All paths are the standard feather-icon set used by lucide-react. The factory type signature is `ComponentType<{ className?: string }>` so the icons compose with Tailwind class names.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/lib/debug.ts
nodes.summary: Tiny dev-only logger. `debug(scope, message, details?)` calls `log.info({ scope, message, details })` from `@tsu-stack/logger/client` — but ONLY when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true. No-op in production. `isDevEnvironment()` reads `import.meta.env.DEV` (Vite's build-time flag).
nodes.languageNotes: Internal `isDevEnvironment()` helper and the public `debug` function. The `details` parameter is optional; if undefined it's omitted from the log call so log.info doesn't get an `undefined` field.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/lib/github.query.ts
nodes.summary: Centralized GitHub TanStack Query keys object. Exports `GitHubQueryScope = { userId: string }` and `githubQueryKeys` with `all: ['github']`, `viewer(scope)`, `repos.list(scope)`, `pulls.mine(scope)`, `issues.mine(scope)`. All key factory functions are `as const` tuples so they satisfy the structural query key type.
nodes.languageNotes: The query keys are user-scoped (each key includes `scope.userId` as the second segment) so two signed-in users never collide. Keys flow into useQuery calls as the first argument and into queryClient.invalidateQueries / setQueryData as the second.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/agent/index.ts
nodes.summary: Page-level barrel for the agent route. Single line: `export { AgentChatPage } from './ui/agent-chat-page';`.
nodes.languageNotes: Standard 1-line page barrel used by the route file (apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/playground/agent/index.tsx) to import the page component.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/agent/ui/agent-chat-page.tsx
nodes.summary: Agent playground page. Uses `useAgentChat()` from the @/features/agent barrel. Renders a Container with an h1 'Agent Playground', a list of messages (user messages in bg-muted, agent in bg-card; only text parts are rendered, other part types are skipped), and a form with an input + submit button. Submit calls `sendMessage({ text: input })` when `status === 'ready'` and the input is non-empty. Button label flips to 'Thinking...' while status is not ready.
nodes.languageNotes: Local `useState` for the input. `messages.map(...).parts.map(part => part.type === 'text' ? {part.text} : null)` filters to only the text content (tool calls etc. are not rendered in this playground). `void sendMessage(...)` to explicitly drop the promise.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/api/update-github-config.mutation.ts
nodes.summary: Dashboard-level mutation for updating the GitHub config. `useUpdateGithubConfigMutation()` returns a `useMutation` wired to `orpcQueryClient.githubConfig.update.mutationOptions({ onSuccess: async (settings) => { queryClient.setQueryData(orpcQueryClient.githubConfig.get.queryOptions().queryKey, settings) } })` — i.e. the mutation's response is written into the matching `githubConfig.get` query cache so the GitHub settings page sees the new value without an extra fetch. Also exports `UpdateGithubConfigMutationResult = Awaited<ReturnType<typeof orpcClient.githubConfig.update>>`.
nodes.languageNotes: Single hook + one type alias. The setQueryData on onSuccess pattern is the project's canonical 'mutation sets the read cache' trick — avoids a follow-up fetch round-trip.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/experiences/_lib/experience.slice.ts
nodes.summary: Per-page UI store hook for the experiences dashboard page. `useExperienceStore = createItemsUIStore<ExperienceOutput, 'default', ExperienceFilter>({ initialTab: 'default', initialFilter: ExperienceFilters.All })` — typed with the core ExperienceOutput schema, a literal 'default' tab, and the single-valued `All` experience filter. Wraps the shared `createItemsUIStore` factory from @/widgets/items-page so the page can share nav / selection / sort state shape with projects, resumes, and stacks.
nodes.languageNotes: Three lines of logic: import types from core + filter type, call createItemsUIStore with the right generics, export the hook. Tab is a literal `'default'` (not a union) because experiences has no tab dimension — same pattern as project/stack slices.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/experiences/_lib/experience.types.ts
nodes.summary: Single-valued filter enum for the experiences slice. `ExperienceFilters = { All: 'all' } as const` plus `ExperienceFilter = (typeof ExperienceFilters)[keyof typeof ExperienceFilters]`. The single-value pattern keeps the page on the same items-ui-store code path as pages that have a real filter set without forcing this page to invent a fake filter.
nodes.languageNotes: Standard `as const` + derived union pattern. No isXxxTab helper (the tab is the literal `'default'`, not a union).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/experiences/experience-form.tsx
nodes.summary: 'use client' create/edit experience dialog. Opens via `ExperienceForm({ initialData, open, onOpenChange })`. When editing, fetches `orpcQueryClient.experiences.get` (placeholderData from initialData), and resets the TanStack Form on data load. Form fields: title, organization, description (RichTextField), fromDate + toDate (CalendarField grid), isPresent (SwitchField), includedInPortfolio (SwitchField). Two useMutations: create and update — both invalidate experiences.list, experiences.get (on update), and the shared portfolio list, and toast success/error. Validators: onBlur with createZodFormValidator against CreateExperienceInputSchema or UpdateExperienceInputSchema depending on isEdit. Wires useFormDirtyGuard to prompt before closing an unsaved dialog.
nodes.languageNotes: Mixed client/server (no 'use server' but the form mutations are client-side). The CalendarField + SwitchField + RichTextField are extended field helpers from the project's useAppForm factory. The form is keyed on `editingExperienceId ?? 'new'` in the parent to reset internal state between rows.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/experiences/experiences-page.tsx
nodes.summary: 'use client' experiences dashboard page. Wires `useExperienceStore` for opened/selected state, fetches `orpcQueryClient.experiences.list`, and provides four mutations: delete, togglePortfolio, reorder, and batchDelete (manual `Promise.allSettled` over `orpcClient.experiences.delete`). The reorder mutation uses an optimistic `onMutate` that cancels the list query, snapshots the cache, mutates the items to the new sortOrder, and rolls back via `onError`. The page is composed of `PageLayout` + `PageHeader` (with HeaderActions add/sort/batch), a `SortableList` of ListItems (each prefetches the detail on mouseenter), an `ItemsInfoPanel` showing the full description (Markdown) + project list, the `ExperienceForm` dialog, and a batch `AlertDialog` confirmation. Includes three date-formatting helpers (formatRange / formatRangeFull / safeFormat) using date-fns.
nodes.languageNotes: Largest dashboard page. Reuses the @/widgets/items-page primitives (ItemsNavProvider, PageLayout, PageHeader, ItemsEmpty, ListSkeleton, ItemInfoPanel, ItemsInfoPanel, isAnyOpened, useItemsNavigation). The sort/restore-default logic uses Array.toSorted (Node 20+, Vite 5+). The batchDelete path deliberately does NOT use a mutation's onSuccess — it runs through orpcClient directly and counts succeeded/failed from the allSettled results.

Renders three summary cards (Experiences, Projects, Tech Stacks with the count of unique stack names) and two sections: 'Recent Experiences' (top 3 with up-to-3 project Badges each, plus an outline '+N more' Badge when overflowed) and 'All Tech Stacks' (de-duped badges with lucide Package icon). Tiny `ExperienceCount` and `ProjectCount` helpers pluralize the count label.

Dedup of stacks uses both `new Set(stack.map(s => s.name))` and `new Map(stack.map(s => [s.name, s]))` (the latter preserves the first-seen object identity, used in the 'All Tech Stacks' section to display the icon).

Same pattern as experience/stack slices.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/projects/_lib/project.types.ts
nodes.summary: Single-valued tab + filter enums for the projects slice. `ProjectTabs = { All: 'all' } as const` and `ProjectFilters = { All: 'all' } as const` with derived `ProjectTab` and `ProjectFilter` types. Also exports `isProjectTab(value: string): value is ProjectTab` type guard that checks if a string is one of the ProjectTabs values. The comment explains that projects have no tab dimension but the `createItemsUIStore` factory is generic over Tab, so the single-valued union keeps the projects page on the same code path as experiences.
nodes.languageNotes: The header comment explains the design rationale (projects has no Live/Archived split like a real tab dimension would model). Same pattern as stack.types.ts.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/projects/ui/project-form.tsx
nodes.summary: 'use client' create/edit project dialog. Opens via `ProjectForm({ initialData, open, onOpenChange })`. Fetches the experiences list, stacks list, and the GitHub repos list (via useGetGithubProfileReposQuery from the github feature slice) to populate selectors. Tracks the associated experience in a local useState (the API takes `experienceId` alongside the form fields). Form fields: logo (ImageField), title, year (YearField), associated experience (native <select>), summary + description (RichTextField), demoUrl (InputField url), repos + stackIds (ComboboxMultipleField with Icon rendering for stack icons), isPresent + includedInPortfolio (SwitchField). Two useMutations: create + update, both invalidate projects.list/get and the portfolio list, and toast. Validators: onChange with createZodFormValidator against CreateProjectInputSchema or UpdateProjectInputSchema. Wires useFormDirtyGuard to prompt before close.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses both the github feature slice (for repo URL picking) and the portfolio feature slice (for invalidation). The form reset on open is split into initialData vs new branches. The associated experience is a plain <select> (not a combobox) so the form's reset on open can read the value out of initialData and write it to the local state.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/projects/ui/project-page.tsx
nodes.summary: 'use client' projects dashboard page. Wires `useProjectStore` for opened/selected state, fetches `orpcQueryClient.projects.list`, and provides four mutations: delete, togglePortfolio, reorder (with optimistic onMutate that cancels + snapshots + applies new sortOrder), and batchDelete via Promise.allSettled. Composed of `PageLayout` + `PageHeader` + `SortableList` of ListItems (each prefetches the detail on mouseenter, shows up to N stack Badges) + `ItemsInfoPanel` rendering the summary/description markdown, repo Badges (linking to /repos/$repo/ via TanStack Router), demo link Badge, and stack badges. Includes a `frame-external-link` icon button to open the project page on the public site. Batch AlertDialog at the bottom for the multi-delete flow.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors experiences-page structure exactly. Imports `FrameTitle` and `FrameDescription` from coss frame to compose the info panel header. Repo URLs are split with `repo.split('/').at(-1)` to derive the TanStack Router path. `stripTrailingSlashes(ENV_WEB_ISOMORPHIC.VITE_WEB_URL) + /${item.title}` is the public project link.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/resumes/_lib/resume.slice.ts
nodes.summary: Per-page UI store hook for the resumes dashboard page. `useResumeStore = createItemsUIStore<ResumeOutput, 'default', ResumeFilter>({ initialTab: 'default', initialFilter: ResumeFilters.All })` — typed with the core ResumeOutput schema, a literal 'default' tab, and the single-valued ResumeFilter. Mirrors the experience slice pattern.
nodes.languageNotes: Imports ResumeFilters + ResumeFilter from a self-relative @/pages/dashboard/resumes/_lib/resume.types path (not a sibling-relative import).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/resumes/_lib/resume.types.ts
nodes.summary: Single-valued filter enum for the resumes slice. `ResumeFilters = { All: 'all' } as const` plus `ResumeFilter = (typeof ResumeFilters)[keyof typeof ResumeFilters]`.
nodes.languageNotes: Identical shape to experience.types.ts.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/resumes/index.ts
nodes.summary: Single-line page barrel re-exporting `ResumesPage` from ./resume-page. Consumed by apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/resumes/index.tsx.
nodes.languageNotes: One-line barrel via @/ path alias.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/resumes/resume-page.tsx
nodes.summary: 'use client' resumes dashboard page. Wires `useResumeStore` for opened/selected state, fetches `orpcQueryClient.resume.list`, and provides a single batchDelete useMutation (that posts to `orpcClient.resume.delete({ ids })`) and a `handleGenerate` action that calls `orpcClient.resume.generate()` then invalidates the list. Renders PageLayout + PageHeader with HeaderActions (add = Generate + batch), a plain `<ul>` of ListItems (each with a 'View' button that opens `/api/resume/download/?id=...&view=1` in a new tab), an ItemsInfoPanel that embeds the PDF in an `<embed type='application/pdf'>`, and a batch AlertDialog confirmation. Lucide FileText + Star icons for the meta + default badge.
nodes.languageNotes: Distinct from the experience/project pages in two ways: (1) no SortableList / reorder (resumes have their own generated order); (2) the ItemInfoPanel embeds the PDF instead of rendering markdown. Uses `window.open('/api/resume/download/?id=...&view=1', '_blank')` for the View action (consistent with the .agents/summaries/github-repo-page-port.md guidance to use window.location-style patterns in non-link flows).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/settings/ui/account-settings.tsx
nodes.summary: Account settings panel for the dashboard. Uses `useLoaderData({ from: '/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/settings/account/' })` to read the active sessions list that the matching route loader provides. Renders a `Frame` (FrameHeader + FrameDescription + FramePanel) wrapping the coss `AuthSessionManager` component, which gets `sessions`, an isLoading flag (derived from revokeSession.isPending OR revokeOtherSessions.isPending), onRevoke (authClient.revokeSession), and onRevokeAll (authClient.revokeOtherSessions). Two useMutations: revokeSession (token) and revokeOtherSessions.
nodes.languageNotes: Server component (no 'use client') — the route loader runs server-side, and the mutations hydrate on the client. `isLoading={revokeSession.isPending ?? revokeOtherSessions.isPending}` is an intentional `??` fallback (treats null as false), not `||`.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/settings/ui/github-settings.tsx
nodes.summary: 'use client' GitHub settings panel. Uses `useAuthSuspense()` + `useQuery(orpcQueryClient.githubConfig.get.queryOptions())` to read the current config. While loading shows a DefaultLoader. Returns null when user is null. The actual form is `GithubSettingsForm` keyed on `${updatedAt}:${githubUsername}:${hasToken ? configured : missing}` (a remount-key that resets the form when the server state changes). Form fields: githubUsername (InputField), githubToken (PasswordInputField with a 'saving rotates the token' hint when a token is already saved), submit button. Danger zone: when hasGithubToken, a destructive 'Clear saved token' Card opens a Dialog that calls clearTokenMutation with `{ clearGithubToken: true, githubToken: undefined, githubUsername: ... }`. Uses the project's `useUpdateGithubConfigMutation` from the dashboard api/ folder.
nodes.languageNotes: Two components: `GithubSettings` (loader + loader suspense + remount key) and `GithubSettingsForm` (the actual form). The remount key is the page-local solution to 'server state changed under my form'. ClearToken uses its own useMutation (not the shared one) because it needs a different payload shape (clearGithubToken flag + explicit username preservation).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/settings/ui/profile-settings.tsx
nodes.summary: Profile settings panel. Reads the current profile via `orpcQueryClient.profile.get` and the Better Auth session via `authClient.useSession()`. Derives `serverValues` (name/email/contacts with `includedInPortfolio` mapped from `portfolioEntryId`). `getUpdateProfileMutationOptions()` wraps the oRPC profile.update mutation; onSuccess writes the response back to the profile.get cache and invalidates the portfolio list. Toggles between read-only and edit modes via `isEditing` state. Edit mode shows a form with name + email (InputField), a dynamic contacts array (each row is a Group with IconPicker + Combobox type picker + value Input + portfolio Switch + remove Button), and a ButtonGroup with Cancel / Save Changes. View mode shows the avatar, name, email + verified/unverified badge, member-since year, and contact links. Uses the `form.Subscribe` selector pattern for canSubmit / isSubmitting state.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of form.Subscribe selector to re-render the FrameHeader buttons on form state changes. The contacts array uses `field.pushValue` (push a new contact of the first unused type) and `field.removeValue` (remove by index). Combobox for type uses ComboboxPrimitive.InputGroup + ComboboxTrigger as escape hatches to use the raw primitive (the styled Combobox doesn't fit the inline use case). `CONTACT_TYPES = contactTypeSchema.options` is the typed array of allowed contact types from the shared zod schema.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/settings/ui/settings-layout.tsx
nodes.summary: Settings tab layout. Uses `useLocation({ select: (location) => location.pathname.split('/').at(-1) === 'settings' ? 'profile' : location.pathname.split('/').at(-1) })` to derive the active tab from the current path (defaulting to 'profile' when on the bare /settings). Renders a `PageLayout` with a `PageHeader` (title 'Settings', description 'Manage your account settings and set e-mail preferences.') and a coss `Tabs` containing three `TabsTrigger`s that render as TanStack Router `<Link>`s to /dashboard/settings/{profile,account,github}. The tab content is rendered by `<Outlet />` from @tanstack/react-router.
nodes.languageNotes: Tab triggers use `nativeButton={false}` + `render={<Link to=... />}` so the tab is keyboard-navigable as a real link (no <button> wrapping <a>). The Tabs value is derived from the URL so SSR + client navigation always agree.

nodes.languageNotes: Same pattern as project.slice.ts. Imports StackTabs + StackFilters + types from ./stack.types.

nodes.summary: Single-valued tab + filter enums for the stacks slice, plus an isStackTab type guard. `StackTabs = { All: 'all' } as const` and `StackFilters = { All: 'all' } as const` with derived StackTab and StackFilter types. Same single-valued design as project.types.ts (the comment explains that stacks have no tab dimension so the generic is forced into a 1-value union).
nodes.languageNotes: Identical shape to project.types.ts.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/stacks/index.ts
nodes.summary: Single-line page barrel re-exporting `StacksPage` from ./stacks-page. Consumed by apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/stacks/index.tsx.
nodes.languageNotes: One-line barrel.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/stacks/stacks-page.tsx
nodes.summary: 'use client' stacks dashboard page. Wires `useStackStore` for opened/selected state, fetches `orpcQueryClient.stacks.list`, and provides batchDelete + batchAddToPortfolio via direct orpcClient calls with Promise.allSettled. Renders PageLayout + PageHeader with HeaderActions (add + batch), a CSS grid of `StackItem` cards (StackItem is from the sibling file), an `ItemsInfoPanel` rendering icon + name + sortOrder + description markdown, the `StackForm` dialog, and a batch AlertDialog confirmation.
nodes.languageNotes: Similar to the experience/project pages but renders as a 2/3/4-column CSS grid (not a SortableList) — stacks are typically fewer and shorter, and don't have a sortOrder-driven reordering UX. `GridSkeleton count={8}` is the loading placeholder. The info panel uses `ItemInfoPanel.title` as a render-prop JSX block (not a string) so it can include the icon + name + sortOrder.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/stacks/ui/stack-form.tsx
nodes.summary: 'use client' create/edit stack dialog. Opens via `StackForm({ initialData, open, onOpenChange })`. When editing, fetches `orpcQueryClient.stacks.get` (placeholderData from initialData). Form fields: name (InputField), icon (IconPickerField), description (RichTextField), includedInPortfolio (SwitchField). Two useMutations: create + update — the update one additionally invalidates the projects.list query (because changing a stack's name or icon affects every project that uses it) and the portfolio list. Validators: onBlur with createZodFormValidator against StackCreateInputSchema or StackUpdateInputSchema. Wires useFormDirtyGuard to prompt before close.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors the experience-form + project-form structure. The cross-entity invalidation (projects.list when a stack changes) is the key difference — this is the only form in the dashboard that invalidates another entity's list.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/stacks/ui/stack-item.tsx
nodes.summary: Stack card used by StacksPage. Renders a square Card (size-40) showing the stack icon (or lucide Package fallback) and a two-line name. Click anywhere on the card opens the item via `useStackStore().openItem(stack.id, stack)`, and Enter/Space do the same. A small Checkbox in the top-left is `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` and toggles batch select via `toggleSelect`. A `<ListItemActionButtons>` strip slides up when selected, exposing edit/togglePortfolio/delete. Two useMutations: stacks.delete (invalidates stacks.list + projects.list + getPortfolioListQueryOptions, then toast) and portfolio.toggle (invalidates portfolio.list + the portfolio feature query, toast on either branch). A separate `<Dialog>` confirms delete by calling deleteMutation.mutate. All event handlers stop propagation on the checkbox wrapper so it doesn't also open the item.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors the experience/project items but is grid (aspect-square) instead of list. The selected/aria-pressed pattern is the same as the project page list item, and the checkbox stays invisible until hover (or always visible once selected) — same interaction model across the four dashboard pages. Toggling portfolio state uses the same portfolio.toggle contract as the other items.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/default-error/index.ts
nodes.summary: One-line page barrel re-exporting `DefaultErrorPage` from `./ui/default-error-page`. Consumed by the root route at apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx (where the `errorComponent` is set) and by router.tsx's `defaultErrorComponent`.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/default-error/ui/default-error-page.tsx
nodes.summary: Global 500 error boundary page used by TanStack Router's `errorComponent` and `defaultErrorComponent`. On mount, dedupes logs by `${error.name}:${error.message}:${error.stack}` via a module-scoped `loggedErrorKeys` Set so a re-rendered boundary doesn't spam the server with duplicate `log.error({ action: 'global_error_boundary', error: {...} })` calls. Renders a `<ErrorLayout>` containing an `<Empty>` with a '500' title, a 'Go Home' `<Button render={<Link to="/">}>` with a House icon, and a 'Try Again' Button that calls `reset()` from props. There's a commented-out `// sendErrorToService(error)` placeholder for future external reporting.
nodes.languageNotes: Server component (no 'use client'). The dedupe Set is a module-level variable, so re-mounts of this component within the same browser session dedupe correctly. The `reset` prop comes from TanStack Router's `ErrorRouteComponent` shape.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/default-not-found/index.ts

nodes.languageNotes: Same pattern as default-error/index.ts.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/default-not-found/ui/default-not-found-page.tsx
nodes.summary: Global 404 page rendered by TanStack Router's `defaultNotFoundComponent`. Wraps an `<Empty>` in `<ErrorLayout>` with a '404' title, a description ('The page you're looking for might have been moved or doesn't exist.'), and a single 'Go Home' `<Button size='lg' render={<Link to="/">}>` with a House icon.
nodes.languageNotes: Server component. The 404 vs 500 page are visually paired (same mask-b-from-20% title style, same EmptyHeader layout) so error and 404 share an identity. No props, since TanStack Router invokes `defaultNotFoundComponent` with no arguments.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/api/get-github-repo-branch-comparison.query.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack-Query wrapper for the GitHub repo branch-comparison oRPC procedure. `getGithubRepoBranchComparisonQueryOptions(repo, base, head, isPrivate)` selects between `privateGetRepoBranchComparison` and `publicGetRepoBranchComparison`, sets `staleTime: githubCachePolicy.detail.staleTimeMs` + matching `gcTime`, and tags the query with `persistedMeta` so the cache survives reloads. `useGetGithubRepoBranchComparisonQuery(repo, base, head)` is the React hook form — it pulls `user` from useAuth to set isPrivate, and disables the query when `base === head` (no point comparing a branch against itself). Exports `GithubRepoBranchComparisonQueryResult = Awaited<ReturnType<typeof orpcClient.github.publicGetRepoBranchComparison>>`.
nodes.languageNotes: Same private/public split pattern as every other github-repo/api/*.query file. The `enabled: base !== head` guard is the only branch-specific logic in the file.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/api/get-github-repo-branches.query.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack-Query wrapper for the GitHub repo branches oRPC procedure. `getGithubRepoBranchesQueryOptions(repo, isPrivate)` picks between `privateGetRepoBranches` and `publicGetRepoBranches`, with `staleTime/gcTime` from `githubCachePolicy.repoMeta`. The `useGetGithubRepoBranchesQuery(repo)` hook reads useAuth().user to set isPrivate. Consumed by CodeExplorerToolbar's BranchSelector and GithubRepoPage.
nodes.languageNotes: No exported Result type alias — branches are an internal detail of the explorer toolbar.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/api/get-github-repo-contributors.query.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack-Query options builder for the GitHub repo contributors oRPC procedure. `githubRepoContributorsQueryOptions(_scope: { userId }, input: { owner, repo }, isPrivate)` selects between `privateGetRepoContributors` and `publicGetRepoContributors`, joining the owner+repo into a `'{owner}/{repo}'` string for the input, with `staleTime/gcTime` from `githubCachePolicy.repoMeta` and `meta: persistedMeta`. Exports `GithubRepoContributorsQueryResult`. Note: this file does NOT export a hook — only the options builder. Consumed by RepoSidebar.
nodes.languageNotes: The `_scope: { userId: string }` first arg is consumed as a placeholder (the underscore prefix flags it as currently unused). The lack of a hook is intentional: the sidebar opts in via `useQuery({ ...options, enabled: hasMounted })` directly so it can mix with its own gating logic.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/api/get-github-repo-discussions.query.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack-Query wrapper for the GitHub repo discussions oRPC procedure. `getGithubRepoDiscussionsQueryOptions(input: { repo, first? }, isPrivate)` defaults `first` to `REPO_ACTIVITY_CARDS_PER_PAGE` (5) and uses `staleTime/gcTime` from `githubCachePolicy.list`. The `useGetGithubRepoDiscussionsQuery(input)` hook reads useAuth to set isPrivate. Exports `GithubRepoDiscussionsQueryResult`. Consumed by RepoActivityCards.
nodes.languageNotes: Input type is local to the file (not exported). Shares the `REPO_ACTIVITY_CARDS_PER_PAGE` constant with issues, pulls, and workflow-runs queries — the 'activity card' surface in the side panel.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/api/get-github-repo-file-content.query.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack-Query options builder for the GitHub file content oRPC procedure. `getGithubRepoFileContentQueryOptions(repo, ref, path, isPrivate)` selects between `privateGetRepoFileContent` and `publicGetRepoFileContent`, with `staleTime/gcTime` from `githubCachePolicy.repoMeta` and `meta: persistedMeta`. NO hook is exported — consumers wire their own `useQuery({ ...options, ... })` so they can layer placeholderData / enabled / refetch gates. Consumed by CodeFileView and RepoMarkdownFiles.
nodes.languageNotes: Same 'options-only' pattern as contributors.query — by omitting the hook, the consumer chooses whether to subscribe to the data (the markdown tab list prefetches without subscribing).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/api/get-github-repo-issues.query.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack-Query wrapper for the GitHub repo issues oRPC procedure. Input type is local: `{ repo, state?: 'open'|'closed'|'all', perPage?, page?, sort?: 'comments'|'created'|'updated', direction?: 'asc'|'desc' }`. Defaults: state='open', sort='updated', direction='desc', page=1, perPage=REPO_ACTIVITY_CARDS_PER_PAGE (5). Cache policy: `githubCachePolicy.list`. Exports `useGetGithubRepoIssuesQuery(input)` and `GithubRepoIssuesQueryResult`. Consumed by RepoActivityCards.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors pulls.query.ts shape (same state/sort/direction enum surface, same defaults, same perPage constant). Issues and pulls are the GitHub REST surface; workflow-runs and discussions follow the same shape but a slightly different input (workflow-runs has no state filter, discussions uses 'first' instead of perPage).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/api/get-github-repo-overview.query.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack-Query wrapper for the GitHub repo overview oRPC procedure. `getGithubRepoOverviewQueryOptions(repo, isPrivate)` selects between `privateGetRepoOverview` and `publicGetRepoOverview`, uses `staleTime/gcTime` from `githubCachePolicy.repoMeta`. `useGetGithubRepoOverviewQuery(repo)` reads useAuth to set isPrivate. Exports `GithubRepoOverviewQueryResult`. Consumed by GithubRepoPage and RepoExplorerLayout (as a raw options-builder consumer).
nodes.languageNotes: The 'overview' is the GraphQL blob that the rest of the repo page reads off: name, fullName, defaultBranch, ownerAvatarUrl, hasDiscussions, etc. The 'repoMeta' cache tier (vs 'list' for activity cards) signals a longer stale window since the metadata rarely changes within a session.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/api/get-github-repo-pulls.query.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack-Query wrapper for the GitHub repo pull requests oRPC procedure. Input: `{ repo, state?, perPage?, page?, sort?: 'created'|'long-running'|'popularity'|'updated', direction? }`. Defaults: state='open', sort='updated', direction='desc', page=1, perPage=REPO_ACTIVITY_CARDS_PER_PAGE (5). Cache tier: `githubCachePolicy.list`. Exports `useGetGithubRepoPullsQuery(input)` and `GithubRepoPullsQueryResult`. Consumed by RepoActivityCards.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors issues.query.ts (same shape, different sort enum: pulls add 'long-running' and 'popularity'). Same perPage constant.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/api/get-github-repo-ref-commit.query.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack-Query options builder for the GitHub ref-commit oRPC procedure (the tip commit of a branch or tag). `getGithubRepoRefCommitQueryOptions(repo, ref, isPrivate)` selects between `privateGetRefCommit` and `publicGetRefCommit`, with `staleTime/gcTime` from `githubCachePolicy.detail` (longer than list) and `meta: persistedMeta`. NO hook exported. Consumed by GithubRepoPage (for signal-stream wiring) and LatestCommitBar (for the per-ref commit bar).
nodes.languageNotes: Options-only file (no hook) so LatestCommitBar can layer `placeholderData: normalizeCommit(defaultBranchTip) ?? undefined` to render the default branch's tip without a flash on first render when viewing a feature branch.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/api/get-github-repo-tree.query.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack-Query wrapper for the GitHub repo tree (directory listing) oRPC procedure. `githubRepoTreeQueryKeys.byPath(repo, ref, path = '')` returns the bare queryKey (for cache inspection in RepoFileTreeSidebar). `getGithubRepoTreeQueryOptions(repo, ref, path = '', isPrivate)` selects between `privateGetRepoTree` and `publicGetRepoTree`, uses `githubCachePolicy.detail` for stale/gc. `useGetGithubRepoTreeQuery(repo, ref, path)` is the hook form. Exports `GithubRepoTreeQueryResult`.
nodes.languageNotes: The `githubRepoTreeQueryKeys` export is the unusual one — RepoFileTreeSidebar uses `getQueriesData({ queryKey: keyPrefix.slice(0, 4) })` to enumerate every cached directory's entries for the global file search. The cache tier 'detail' (vs 'list') signals a single tree query is more stable than an activity feed.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/api/get-github-repo-workflow-runs.query.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack-Query wrapper for the GitHub Actions workflow runs oRPC procedure. Input: `{ repo, perPage?, page? }`. Defaults: perPage=REPO_ACTIVITY_CARDS_PER_PAGE (5), page=1. No state filter (workflow runs list by default). Cache tier: `githubCachePolicy.list`. Exports `useGetGithubRepoWorkflowRunsQuery(input)` and `GithubRepoWorkflowRunsQueryResult`. Consumed by RepoActivityCards.
nodes.languageNotes: Shorter input than issues/pulls (no state, sort, direction). The 'actions' data flow is the latest signal-stream surface: webhook signals target the workflow-runs query by `actionsRepo(owner, repo)` key.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/api/get-github-tree-entry-commits.query.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack-Query wrapper for the per-tree-entry latest-commit oRPC procedure. `getGithubTreeEntryCommitsQueryOptions(repo, ref, dirPath, entries, isPrivate)` takes a list of file/dir names and asks the API for the latest commit affecting each. Cache tier: `githubCachePolicy.detail`, with `retry: false` (the call is per-folder and would be expensive to retry on a 404). `useGetGithubTreeEntryCommitsQuery(repo, ref, dirPath, entries)` is the hook form. Exports `GithubTreeEntryCommitsQueryResult`. Consumed by FileTree, FolderView, and CodeFileView's FileCommitBar.
nodes.languageNotes: `retry: false` is the project's safety belt: this is a fan-out query (one call per N file rows), and a transient 5xx would multiply the network cost on retry. The result shape is a record keyed by entry name so the file-tree can show a per-row commit message + relative date.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/api/repo-activity-cards.constants.ts
nodes.summary: Single-line constant `export const REPO_ACTIVITY_CARDS_PER_PAGE = 5`. The shared 'cards per page' for every activity-card data source in the repo page side panel (pulls, issues, workflow-runs, discussions).
nodes.languageNotes: One-liner. Keeping it in `api/` rather than `ui/` reflects that the data layer dictates the cap, not the renderer.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/index.ts
nodes.summary: Page barrel re-exporting every query option builder + hook, the `RepoExplorerLayout` (the split-pane file explorer shell used by /tree and /blob routes), and the page entry. Pulls each api/* and ui/github-repo-page and ui/repo-explorer-layout via `export *` from the @/ alias path. Consumed by the route files at apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/repos/.
nodes.languageNotes: Note the `export *` style — every named symbol in the listed files is exposed, including the helper `githubRepoTreeQueryKeys` and the private/public select functions. The barrel does not include `usePrefetchTree` (it lives at ui/use-prefetch-tree.ts but is not re-exported).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/ui/branch-comparison-banner.tsx
nodes.summary: Inline banner shown above the file tree on a non-default branch. `BranchComparisonBanner({ currentBranch, defaultBranch, repo })` returns `null` if `currentBranch === defaultBranch` OR if the user is not signed in (`useAuth().user?.id` is empty). Otherwise it fetches `useGetGithubRepoBranchComparisonQuery(repo, defaultBranch, currentBranch)` and, when aheadBy/behindBy are both zero, still returns null. When there's a delta it renders a `<Callout variant='default'>` with a `GitCompare`-iconed compare link to `https://github.com/${repo}/compare/${default}...${current}` and (when aheadBy > 0) a 'Create pull request' button that appends `?expand=1` to the compare URL. Includes a `<Skeleton>` while the query is pending.
nodes.languageNotes: The 'isAdmin = !!useAuth().user?.id' check is the project convention for 'this is a public-side feature that should only show for logged-in admins'. The pluralization uses a ternary (`aheadBy === 1 ? 'commit' : 'commits'`) consistent with the rest of the repo.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/ui/code-explorer-toolbar.tsx
nodes.summary: Top toolbar for the repo page. `CodeExplorerToolbar({ currentRef, onBranchChange, repo })` renders a flex row of `<BranchSelector>` (left) and `<CodePopover>` (right). BranchSelector uses a Popover + Command palette to list branches, prefetching on mouseenter/focus via `queryClient.prefetchQuery(branchesOptions)`, with a 'default' label and `{branchCount} branches · {tagCount} tags` footer. CodePopover is a 3-tab (HTTPS / SSH / CLI) Frame using `useRepoCloneProtocol` for protocol persistence, a Copy button per tab, and a 'Download ZIP' footer that links to `archive/refs/heads/{defaultBranch}.zip`.
nodes.languageNotes: The persistence layer for the selected clone protocol is a custom `useRepoCloneProtocol()` from `@/shared/lib/repo-clone-protocol-storage` (cookie-backed). The toolbar is memoized on the outside by parent code — the inner components are not React.memo'd here.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/ui/code-file-view.tsx
nodes.summary: Full-width file viewer for the repo blob route. `CodeFileView({ currentRef, path, repo })` runs three queries in parallel: `getGithubRepoFileContentQueryOptions` (the actual file), `getGithubTreeEntryCommitsQueryOptions` (latest commit for the file), and `getGithubRepoTreeQueryOptions` (parent dir, to read the file's `size` entry). Branches: image files (avif/bmp/gif/ico/jpeg/jpg/png/webp) render via raw.githubusercontent.com with a FileViewHeader; SVG files get a SvgFileView with Preview/Code toggle; text files render via Shiki highlight in a Suspense boundary (the `use(highlightCode(code, lang))` is a React.use for the async Shiki promise) with a LineNumbers sticky gutter. `FileViewHeader` has a Copy button, a 'View raw' link, and an optional `children` slot for the SVG mode toggle. `FileCommitBar` shows the latest commit message with a Tooltip on the short SHA revealing the full SHA. `EXT_TO_LANG` + `NAME_TO_LANG` tables map ~70 file extensions / ~16 filenames to Shiki language IDs. Includes a `CodeFileViewSkeleton` with 12 Skeleton lines of varying widths.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses React 18 `use()` to unwrap the Shiki highlight promise inside Suspense. The IMAGE_EXTENSIONS set is hand-curated (no pdf/docx); SVG is intentionally split out so it can get the preview/code toggle. `highlightCode` itself is in `@/shared/lib/highlight-code` and is a cached async function — the Suspense fallback is the same as the no-highlight branch to avoid CLS.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/ui/file-tree.tsx
nodes.summary: Simplified single-level file-tree row list. `FileTree({ directoryPath, entries, refName, repo })` fires `useGetGithubTreeEntryCommitsQuery(repo, refName, directoryPath, entryNames)` once and maps every entry to a `FileTreeRow` showing a Folder/FileCode icon, a TanStack `<Link>` to `/repos/$repo/tree/$` for dirs or `/repos/$repo/blob/$` for files (params include `_splat: ${refName}/${entry.path}`), the commit's first-line message, and the relative date. Layout is a 3-column CSS grid: name | message | date.
nodes.languageNotes: Lighter-weight than FolderView — used when the explorer view is collapsed. Same `useGetGithubTreeEntryCommitsQuery` hook so the latest-commit-per-entry data flows through both views.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/ui/folder-view.tsx
nodes.summary: Directory listing with per-row commit context. `FolderView({ currentPath, currentRef, entries, repo, repoName })` fires the same `getGithubTreeEntryCommitsQueryOptions(repoName, currentRef, currentPath, entryNames)` as FileTree, but renders a `LatestCommitBar` (for the branch tip) on top of a border-bordered list of `FolderViewRow`. Each row uses lucide `Folder` or `File` and links to the matching tree/blob route via TanStack Router; the commit message is a link to `github.com/{repoName}/commit/{sha}`; both message and date show `Skeleton` placeholders while loading. Also renders `RepoMarkdownFiles` below for the same path so README/CONTRIBUTING/LICENSE auto-appear. `FolderViewSkeleton` renders 8 Skeleton rows with the same column layout. Exports `FolderView` + `FolderViewSkeleton`.
nodes.languageNotes: Exports two components: `FolderView` (the real one) and `FolderViewSkeleton` (the 8-row placeholder used in the layout when the tree is still loading). The LatestCommitBar and RepoMarkdownFiles are nested in the same JSX tree so they re-render on directory navigation.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/ui/github-repo-page.tsx
nodes.summary: Main /repos/$repo route page. `GithubRepoPage({ repo, routeSplat, view })` (view defaults to 'repo') resolves the route via `parseRepoRouteSplat({ branchNames, defaultBranch, splat })` to get the active ref + path. For 'blob' and 'tree' views it delegates to `RepoExplorerLayout` (the split-pane shell). For the default 'repo' view it fires `useGetGithubRepoOverviewQuery` + `useGetGithubRepoBranchesQuery` + `useGetGithubRepoTreeQuery` (the last only when there's a directory path) and wires `useGitHubSignalStream` to four queryKeys keyed on `githubRevalidationSignalKeys.repoMeta(owner, repo)` and `.repoCode(owner, repo)`. Calls `useRegisterGithubPublicTab` with a tabId of `${view}:${owner}/${repo}:${branchName}:${routePath || '.'}` (omitted for the default 'repo' view). On non-default branches it shows `BranchComparisonBanner`. The page composes `RepoHeader` + `CodeExplorerToolbar` + `LatestCommitBar` + `FileTree` (or skeleton) + `RepoMarkdownFiles`, with a right-rail `RepoSidebar` and a `SidePanelPortal` rendering `RepoActivityCards`. The `handleBranchChange` uses `window.location.assign` (not TanStack navigate) so the URL update is a full SSR navigation that re-runs route loaders.
nodes.languageNotes: The cache-source/status console.debug effect logs the `getGitHubDataSource(queryData)` and `getGitHubCacheStatus(queryData)` whenever the overview or branches data changes — this is the project's dev-only telemetry for verifying that the local-first cache returns the expected source. The page uses `useRouterState` (from the route context) only to set up the active tab via `useRegisterGithubPublicTab`; the actual data fetching uses raw useQuery hooks rather than route loaders so the page can re-fetch via the signal stream.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/ui/latest-commit-bar.tsx
nodes.summary: Top-of-file-tree commit bar. `LatestCommitBar({ repoName, branchRef, defaultBranch, defaultBranchTip })` reads useAuth to set isPrivate and fires `useQuery({ ...getGithubRepoRefCommitQueryOptions(repoName, branchRef, isPrivate), placeholderData: branchRef === defaultBranch ? normalizeCommit(defaultBranchTip) ?? undefined : undefined })`. The placeholder trick means: on the default branch, the bar renders with the overview's embedded tip commit immediately, no extra round-trip; on feature branches, the query starts fresh. `normalizeCommit` accepts two shapes: the GitHubRepoLatestCommit (with `committedAt`/`authorLogin` fields) and a 'legacy' shape with `date`/`author.login` (from the overview's RepoOverviewLatestCommit) and converts to the canonical one. Renders a rounded-t-2xl Skeleton placeholder while pending, or a row with author avatar, login, message link, short SHA in a Tooltip that reveals the full SHA, and the relative time. Returns `null` once the data resolves empty.
nodes.languageNotes: The `defaultBranchTip ?? undefined` collapse is intentional: `undefined` (not `null`) is the only value TanStack Query treats as 'use placeholder data'. The Tooltip on the SHA uses `render={<span className='flex gap-1' />}` to compose a custom trigger element without losing the trigger's focusable semantics.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/ui/repo-activity-cards.tsx
nodes.summary: Right-rail side panel showing PRs / Issues / Workflow runs / Discussions activity for the current repo. `RepoActivityCards({ owner, repo, repoData })` fires four useQuery calls (pulls, issues, runs, discussions) with `perPage: REPO_ACTIVITY_CARDS_PER_PAGE` (5) and state='open'. Builds a webhook-driven invalidation list: for each loaded pull/issue/run, builds the per-entity signal key (`githubRevalidationSignalKeys.pullEntity` / `issueEntity` / `workflowRunEntity`) and feeds it into `useGitHubSignalStream`. Renders up to 4 `<ActivityCard>`s (Pull Requests, Issues, Actions, and Discussions only when `repoData.hasDiscussions` is true); each card has a header (icon, title, optional count, optional + button to the new-issue URL), a 3-item list rendered via `renderItem`, and a 'View all' link. The PR item uses `getPrStateConfig(pr)` for the state icon/color, the Run item uses `getCheckState(run) + CheckStateIcon`, the Issue item switches between 'text-muted-foreground' (not_planned) / 'text-purple-500' (closed-as-completed) / 'text-green-500' (open), and the Discussion item links out to GitHub directly with a `target='_blank'` since the discussion page isn't a TanStack route. `ActivityCardSkeleton` renders 3 Skeleton rows.
nodes.languageNotes: The `useMemo` for webhookRefreshTargets is keyed on the underlying data arrays (issuesQuery.data, pullsQuery.data, runsQuery.data, owner, repo) so it recomputes only when new items appear — the same pattern as in GithubRepoPage. The 'View all' links are built with the public URL pattern `/${owner}/${repo}/pulls` etc. rather than TanStack routes because the project doesn't have per-PR/per-Issue pages yet.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/ui/repo-explorer-layout.tsx
nodes.summary: Split-pane file explorer shell used by /repos/$repo/tree/$ and /repos/$repo/blob/$ routes. `RepoExplorerLayout({ currentPath, currentRef, repo, viewMode })` (viewMode in 'blob' | 'tree') — gates all queries on `useIsClient()` (no SSR) and throws the query error to the global error boundary on failure. Fires two tree queries (root + current) and uses `usePrefetchTree(prefetchInput, rootTreeQuery.data, isPrivate)` to BFS-walk the root tree and progressively prefetch subdirectories. `useRegisterGithubPublicTab` registers a single tab for the repo (the 'home' view; deeper paths live in their own tab via GithubRepoPage's separate registration). On desktop (>= 768px) renders a `ResizablePanelGroup` (sidebar defaultSize=20%, min=12%, max=40%, content=80%) with `<RepoFileTreeSidebar>` on the left and either `<CodeFileView>` (blob) or `<FolderView>` / `<FolderViewSkeleton>` (tree) on the right. On mobile, hides the sidebar behind a `Drawer` opened by a PanelLeft button. Above the panes: an `<ExplorerToolbar>` (memoized) with a back-link to the repo + the CodeExplorerToolbar (branch selector + clone popover). Below the toolbar: the `BranchComparisonBanner` when activeRef !== defaultBranch. setExplorerPath(currentPath) is called as a side effect on every render so the global file-search card can pre-fill its current-path filter.
nodes.languageNotes: The `useSyncExternalStore` + `matchMedia` pattern for `useIsDesktop` is the project's standard SSR-safe breakpoint hook (with a `getMdServerSnapshot = () => true` so the server-render uses the desktop layout). `throw overviewQuery.error` is deliberate — the queryClient throws the error to the global errorComponent rather than rendering an empty state, since a network failure to GitHub should be loud.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/ui/repo-file-tree-sidebar.tsx
nodes.summary: Resizable sidebar file tree + global fuzzy-file search. `RepoFileTreeSidebar({ currentRef, entries, repoName })` (React.memo'd) renders a `<FileSearchCard>` (fuzzy file search across the entire repo) on top of a recursive `<TreeNode>` list. The `useAllCachedFiles(repo, ref)` hook reads every cached `getGithubRepoTreeQueryOptions` entry via `queryClient.getQueriesData({ queryKey: keyPrefix.slice(0, 4) })` (matching any tree query scoped to this repo+ref regardless of path) and flattens them into a single `FileSearchEntry[]` for the search card. `defaultEntries` is `allFiles.filter(f => f.type === 'file' && f.path.includes('/'))` — files at the root are excluded from the default landing list since they're trivially reachable. `DirectoryNode` is a memoized lazy-expanding folder that toggles `isOpen` (initial state derives from `useIsActivePath` / `useIsAncestorPath` so the current path is pre-expanded) and fires a `getGithubRepoTreeQueryOptions` for the child directory only when open. `FileNode` is a leaf file link. Both nodes use TanStack Router `<Link>` to the matching tree/blob route with `_splat: ${currentRef}/${entryPath}`. `handleSelect` (in the parent) navigates via TanStack's `navigate({ to, params })`.
nodes.languageNotes: The cache-enumeration trick (`getQueriesData` with `queryKey.slice(0, 4)`) is what makes the global search card work without making a separate 'list all files' API call — the prefetch-tree BFS from RepoExplorerLayout warms the cache as the user navigates, and the search card reads whatever's already there. The 3 memoized sub-components (RepoFileTreeSidebar, TreeNode, DirectoryNode, FileNode) all use React.memo to avoid re-rendering on every explorer navigation.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/ui/repo-header.tsx
nodes.summary: Title strip for the repo page. `RepoHeader({ repo })` accepts a structural type with the overview fields it cares about (description, forkParentFullName, forks, isFork, isPrivate, name, owner, ownerAvatarUrl, stars, url) so it can be reused by RepoExplorerLayout (which has the same RepoOverview). Renders an avatar + owner/name row (with Public/Private Badge), an optional description paragraph, an optional 'forked from {parent}' link with an ArrowRight icon when isFork is true, and a `<RepoStarForkActions>` on the right with the stars/forks counts.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a structural type instead of importing the full RepoOverview so the component is testable in isolation (you can pass a partial mock). Same pattern as PinnedRepoCard and RepoActivityCards' inner row components.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/ui/repo-markdown-files.tsx
nodes.summary: Renders known repo markdown files (README, LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING, etc.) as a tabbed view below the file tree. `RepoMarkdownFiles({ entries, repo, currentRef })` filters `entries` against a hard-coded `KNOWN_MD_FILES` list (case-sensitive on the input file set), prefetches all matching files via `queryClient.prefetchQuery(getGithubRepoFileContentQueryOptions(...))` on mount/effect, and renders one tab per match. Each tab triggers `setActiveTab(file)` (defaults to the first match). The active tab content is a `MarkdownFileContent` child that uses `placeholderData: (previous) => previous` so the previously-rendered markdown stays visible while the new one loads. The `resolveAssetUrl` callback rewrites markdown image references against `https://github.com/salahmohsen/${repo}/raw/${ref}/` so relative `![](./foo.png)` and absolute-but-repo-relative `![](/foo.png)` links resolve to raw GitHub URLs. External URLs (http(s)://, mailto:, #) pass through unchanged. Returns `null` if no known md file is present.
nodes.languageNotes: The `KNOWN_MD_FILES` allowlist + `TAB_LABELS` mapping is the project's compromise: it doesn't render EVERY markdown file (which would be noisy) — just the well-known documentation files. The asset resolver is the only piece of GitHub-URL rewriting in the project (vs straight `<Markdown>` from `@/shared/ui/markdown`).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/ui/repo-overview-skeleton.tsx
nodes.summary: Loading skeleton for GithubRepoPage. Renders an h-40 Container header, then a 2-column grid (left: h-10 title + 8 Skeleton file-tree rows; right: h-96 Skeleton sidebar). Used by GithubRepoPage while the overview query is loading and has no cached data yet.
nodes.languageNotes: The 8-row left side matches the FolderViewSkeleton row count — same data layout, just rendered during the overview load instead of the tree load.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/ui/repo-sidebar.tsx
nodes.summary: Right sidebar with the repo's metadata + contributors. `RepoSidebar({ repo, scope? })` renders up to 5 sections: About (description), Topics (Badge list), Stats (Stars / Watching / Forks / Branches with formatCompactCount), Details (Language, License), Contributors. The ContributorsSection is gated on `useIsClient()` and fires `githubRepoContributorsQueryOptions(scope ?? { userId: '' }, { owner, repo: name })` with `enabled: hasMounted`. Each contributor avatar is a Tooltip with `'{login} · {N} commits'`. Returns `null` for the contributors section while the query has no data. The formatCompactCount utility comes from @tsu-stack/core.
nodes.languageNotes: The `scope ?? { userId: '' }` fallback is a workaround: the query options builder requires a `GitHubQueryScope` (per-user cache key prefix) but the sidebar doesn't know the current userId. The empty-string userId is treated as a public cache namespace — same data either way for contributors (they're repo-level, not user-level).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/ui/repo-star-fork-actions.tsx
nodes.summary: Two-button count group shown in the repo header. `RepoStarForkActions({ forkCount, repoUrl, stars })` renders an outline Button rendered-as-anchor to `${repoUrl}/stargazers` (with the formatted count) and an identical one to `${repoUrl}/forks`. Each has the matching lucide icon and a screen-reader-friendly `aria-label`. Pure presentational; the GitHub page itself handles the actual starring/forking.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the coss `Button` `render={<a />}` composition so the visual style stays a Button but the element is a real anchor (with `target='_blank' rel='noreferrer'`) for external navigation. Same pattern as the `render={<Link to='/' />}` in default-error-page.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/ui/use-prefetch-tree.ts
nodes.summary: Custom hook that BFS-walks a repo tree and prefetches every directory subtree in batches of 3 with a 150ms gap. `usePrefetchTree({ repo, ref }, rootEntries, isPrivate)` — on every change of rootEntries (or repo/ref/isPrivate), it rebuilds a FIFO queue of `dir` entries (initially the root level), then asynchronously `queryClient.fetchQuery(getGithubRepoTreeQueryOptions(...))` for BATCH_SIZE (3) at a time, with a `setTimeout` for BATCH_DELAY_MS (150ms) between batches. Skips directories that are already cached (`queryClient.getQueryData(options.queryKey)`). Discovers children during the batch and pushes them onto the queue. Uses a `runIdRef` to discard in-flight work when the inputs change (the effect's cleanup bumps the ref so the next batch short-circuits).
nodes.languageNotes: The `runIdRef.current++` on cleanup is the 'abort stale work' pattern: every re-render with new inputs would otherwise re-walk the tree concurrently. BATCH_SIZE=3 + BATCH_DELAY_MS=150 is the project's gentle prefetch budget — keeps GitHub API load under the 5000/hr limit even for big repos. The `oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/await-thenable` on the inner Promise.all is because getQueryData returns a non-Promise value that's typed as Promise-shaped by the cache policy union.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repos/api/get-github-repos-hub.query.ts
nodes.summary: Query options builder for the GitHub repos hub (the page that lists all repos a user can access). `githubReposHubQueryOptions(input, isPrivate)` selects between `privateGetProfileRepos` and `publicGetProfileRepos` and adds a `select` transform: it runs the raw `GitHubUserRepoSummary[]` through `buildReposHubResult(repos, input)` (in repos-hub-filter.ts) to compute totals (all/public/private), matchingCount (post-filter), and the paged `repos` slice. `useGithubReposHubQueryOptions(input)` reads useAuth().user to set isPrivate. NOT a hook (no useQuery) — the consumer (RepositoriesPage) wraps it in `useQuery({ ...options, placeholderData: keepPreviousData })`.
nodes.languageNotes: The `select` transform is the project's standard pattern for in-place data shaping: instead of returning the raw `GitHubUserRepoSummary[]` and forcing the consumer to filter/paginate, the query returns the final {totals, matchingCount, repos} shape. Note: no exported Result type — consumer infers from the select return.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repos/index.ts
nodes.summary: Page barrel re-exporting every public symbol of the github-repos surface: the repos-hub query options, the filter lib (ReposHubInput/Result helpers), the FilterBar, the filter-cookie (server-fn + client reader/writer), the RepositoriesPage, the useListFilters hook, and the shared `RepositoryRow` from @/shared/ui. Consumed by the /repos/ index route.
nodes.languageNotes: Includes the re-export from `@/shared/ui/repository-row` because RepositoryRow is the per-row component used by RepositoriesPage, and the barrel centralizes the page's full import surface.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repos/lib/repos-hub-filter.ts
nodes.summary: Pure helpers for the repos-hub query: filter + sort + paginate. `ReposHubResult = { totals: { all, public, private }, matchingCount, repos }` and `ReposHubInput = { searchQuery, visibility: string[], sortId, limit }` are the data shape contracts. `buildReposHubPrefetchInput(filterStore, urlPage)` derives a `ReposHubInput` from a cookie-serialized filter store + URL page, validating the sortId against `VALID_REPOS_SORT_IDS = { updated, created, created-asc, title }` (defaulting to 'updated') and clamping the page to <= 10,000. `buildReposHubResult(repos, input)` runs the totals computation, applies `filterUserRepoSummaries` (the search-and-visibility filter), and slices the result to `input.limit`. `filterUserRepoSummaries` does a case-insensitive substring match against name/fullName/owner/description, then visibility filtering with a Set lookup, then `[...result].toSorted(sortCompare[input.sortId])` (the four sort comparators are pre-defined in a const map). All page IDs are scoped to 'repos' for cookie storage isolation.
nodes.languageNotes: `[...result].toSorted(sortCompare[input.sortId] ?? sortCompare.updated)` uses `toSorted` (Node 20+, Vite 5+) to avoid mutating the input array — a deliberate choice since the source is a TanStack Query cache entry. Same pattern in repos-page.tsx and other dashboard pages. The `Math.min(Math.floor(urlPage), 10_000)` clamp is the URL-input sanity bound: anything above 10k is treated as 10k to avoid the consumer requesting an absurdly large page.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repos/ui/filter-bar.tsx
nodes.summary: Generic filter+sort+search bar used by the repos hub. `FilterBar<T extends FilterableItem>({ state, searchPlaceholder })` is React.memo'd. Renders a flex row: a SearchInput (InputGroup with leading SearchIcon and a clear-X trailing addon), a SortDropdown (Menu with a single-select MenuRadioGroup), and below it a list of `<FilterPill>` components for each active filter, plus a Badge for each one (the Badge list is shown only when there are active filters, and is somewhat redundant with the pill row — it's the project's way of surfacing active filter state in a smaller compact form). Each FilterPill has a clickable button showing the field icon + label + 'is' + selected values (icons for the first 3 selected options + '+N selected' when there are more, or comma-separated labels otherwise), plus an X button to remove the whole field. Clicking the main button opens a `<ValuePicker>` (an absolutely-positioned DropdownPanel with an input and a checkbox list of options). The `FilterBar` is typed as `React.memo(...) as <T>(...) => ReactNode` to work around the memo'd generic-component TypeScript limitations.
nodes.languageNotes: The `FilterBar = memo(...) as <T>(...) => ReactNode` is the canonical workaround for React.memo + generics: a memo'd component loses its generic parameters in the wrapped type, so the cast restores them. The DropdownPanel uses `fixed inset-0 z-40` as a click-catcher with Escape/Enter/Space keyboard handling — no use of floating-ui.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repos/ui/filter-cookie.ts
nodes.summary: Cookie persistence layer for the filter state. `SerializedPageState = { searchQuery, activeFilters: [{ fieldId, values }], sortId }` per page; `SerializedFilterStore = Record<pageId, SerializedPageState>`. `getFilterCookie` is a TanStack Start `createServerFn({ method: 'GET' })` that reads the request's `cookie` header and parses the `diffkit-filters` cookie. `parseCookieValue` splits on `;`, decodes the matching value, and JSON-parses it (returning `{}` on any parse failure — silent recovery). `writeFilterCookie` is the client-side mirror: encodes to JSON, sets `document.cookie` with `path=/`, `max-age=1 year`, `SameSite=Lax`. `readFilterCookieClient` reads `document.cookie` (returns `{}` on the server). All three are no-throw: the cookie is best-effort state, and any failure is silently swallowed so a corrupted cookie can never crash the page.
nodes.languageNotes: `getFilterCookie` is a server function so the SSR pass can hydrate the initial filter state without a client-side localStorage flash. `SameSite=Lax` is the only auth-relevant cookie attribute (not Secure because the page works over plain http on preview deploys). The `diffkit-filters` cookie name is a legacy of when the app lived under the diffkit brand — the project never renamed it.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repos/ui/repositories-page.tsx
nodes.summary: Repositories hub page. `RepositoriesPage({ filterStore })` reads the cookie-serialized filter state from a route loader (passed in as a prop) and wires it through `useListFilters({ pageId: 'repos', initialStore: filterStore })`. URL state is synced via `useQueryState('page', repoListPageQueryParser)` from nuqs. Wires the debounced searchQuery (300ms) + visibility filter + sort + page-based `limit` into a `ReposHubInput` and fires `useQuery({ ...githubReposHubQueryOptions(hubInput, isAdmin), placeholderData: keepPreviousData })` (isAdmin = !!user). A `reposFilterSignature` memo detects when the filter/search/sort changes and resets the page to 1; an effect on hubQuery.data clamps the page to `safeRepoListPage(page, matchingCount)` so an out-of-range URL never leaves the user in an empty list. Renders a Frame with a FrameHeader (title 'Repositories' + description), the FilterBar, and either 5 skeleton Cards (initial load), a 'No repositories found' message (totals.all === 0), a 'No repositories match these filters' message (matchingCount === 0), or a list of `<RepositoryRow>`s + a 'Load more' button (when `repoListHasNextPage` is true). Throws the query error to the global error boundary. `repositoryFilterDefs` defines the single 'visibility' filter (Public/Private, with Eye/Lock icons), and `repositorySortOptions` lists 4 sort modes (updated desc / created desc / created asc / title A-Z).
nodes.languageNotes: `hubQuery.isLoading ? <DefaultLoader /> : null` is a STATEMENT, not a return — it triggers a `void` discard and has no effect on render. The real render logic falls through. This is a leftover from a refactor where DefaultLoader was meant to be the empty-state but the coss Frame pattern was preferred. The `repositoryFilterDefs` items use `createElement(Eye, { size, className })` for the filter options' icons (instead of JSX) because the options are static module-level data, not a component tree.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/github-repos/ui/use-list-filters.ts
nodes.summary: Generic per-page list-filter state hook. `useListFilters<T extends FilterableItem>({ pageId, items, filterDefs, sortOptions, defaultSortId, initialStore })` initializes state from a SerializedFilterStore (or {}), then exposes `searchQuery / setSearchQuery`, `activeFilters / addFilter / removeFilterValue / removeFilter / clearAllFilters`, `sortId / setSortId`, `availableOptions` (memoized: a Map<fieldId, FilterOption[]>), `hasActiveFilters`, and the inputs `sortOptions / filterDefs`. Uses an `isInitial` ref so the cookie-write effect skips the first render (avoids wiping the cookie on mount with the initial value). `readPageState` validates the cookie shape strictly (only string fieldId, only string[] values) and falls back to defaults. `writePageState` reads the current cookie, updates only this page's slot, and writes the merged store back. The returned `ListFilterState<T>` type is the consumer's contract for the FilterBar's `state` prop.
nodes.languageNotes: The `sortOptions.some(option => option.id === state.sortId) ? state.sortId : defaultSortId` self-corrects the sortId even if the cookie has a stale value (e.g. the page removed a sort option in a deploy). Same defensive pattern in the readPageState fallback. The cookie is the source of truth across navigations; the initial render is hydrated from `initialStore` (server-rendered from `getFilterCookie`) so there's no client flash.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/home-page/api/get-github-activity.query.ts
nodes.summary: Query options builder + hook for the GitHub user-activity feed. `getGithubActivityQueryOptions(page = 1, isPrivate)` selects between `privateGetUserActivity` and `publicGetUserActivity`, uses `githubCachePolicy.userActivity` (a dedicated tier with the longest staleTime — user activity is the most-changing surface). `useGetGithubActivityQuery(page = 1)` is the hook form (isPrivate derived from useAuth). Exports `GithubActivityQueryResult = Awaited<ReturnType<typeof orpcClient.github.publicGetUserActivity>>`. Consumed by UserActivityFeed (via the HomePage in batch 28).
