nodes.languageNotes: The 'userActivity' cache tier is the longest-stale tier in the project — user activity is the slowest-changing surface of the GitHub data, and over-frequent refetches would risk rate-limiting.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/home-page/api/get-github-contributions.query.ts
nodes.summary: Query options builder + hook for the GitHub contributions calendar. `getGithubContributionsQueryOptions(isPrivate)` selects between `privateGetUserContributions` and `publicGetUserContributions`, uses `githubCachePolicy.contributions` (a dedicated tier — contributions are computed nightly and don't change mid-day). `useGetGithubContributionsQuery()` is the hook form. Exports `GithubContributionsQueryResult`. Consumed by HomePage.
nodes.languageNotes: No input args other than isPrivate — the API derives the user from the auth context (server-side) or the configured public owner (client-side). Same pattern as the profile query.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/home-page/api/get-github-pinned-repos.query.ts
nodes.summary: Query options builder + hook for the GitHub pinned repos. `getGithubPinnedReposQueryOptions(isPrivate)` selects between `privateGetUserPinnedRepos` and `publicGetUserPinnedRepos`, uses `githubCachePolicy.reposList`. `useGetGithubPinnedReposQuery()` is the hook form. Exports `GithubPinnedReposQueryResult`. Consumed by HomePage.
nodes.languageNotes: Pinned repos are user-set (via GitHub UI), not derived — so 'reposList' tier is appropriate (staleTime in hours, not days). The query has no args besides isPrivate for the same reason as contributions/profile.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/home-page/api/get-github-profile.query.ts
nodes.summary: Query options builder + hook for the GitHub user profile. `getGithubProfileQueryOptions(isPrivate)` selects between `privateGetUserProfile` and `publicGetUserProfile`, uses `githubCachePolicy.detail` (longer stale window since the profile rarely changes). `useGetGithubProfileQuery()` is the hook form. Exports `GithubProfileQueryResult`. Consumed by HomePage.
nodes.languageNotes: Detail tier (vs reposList) because profile edits are infrequent.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/home-page/index.ts
nodes.summary: Page barrel re-exporting the home page surface: the github feature slice (getGithubProfileReposQueryOptions, useGetGithubProfileReposQuery, etc.), the four home-page/api query options + hooks, the portfolio feature slice, and the home-page UI components (home-page, projects-section, experience-section). Consumed by the /(root-layout)/ route file at apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/index.tsx.
nodes.languageNotes: Mixes @/features/* and @/pages/home-page/* re-exports because the home page composes the github feature (setup-status query), the portfolio feature (list query for projects/experiences), and the page-local api/* and ui/*.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/home-page/ui/contact.tsx
nodes.summary: Tiny presentational contact-link bar. `Contact({ contacts }: { contacts: ContactOutput[] })` renders a `position: absolute; bottom: 0; w-full; justify-center` flex row of `<ContactButton>`s (one per contact entry). Exports a named const arrow function (not a `function` declaration) to match the import-as-default surface in HomeNav.
nodes.languageNotes: Exports as `const Contact = (...)` to match the `import { Contact } from './contact'` import shape in home-nav.tsx.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/home-page/ui/contribution-graph.tsx
nodes.summary: Animated SVG GitHub-style contribution heatmap with per-cell hover tooltip. `ContributionGraph({ calendar, className?, svgProps? })` builds a `cells` array from the calendar's weeks/days, computes a `centerCol / centerRow / maxDist` for a per-cell staggered spring animation (`delay: (distance / maxDist) * 0.8`), and renders each cell as a `motion.rect` with `fill: var(--contrib-level-${level})`. The 5 levels are driven by CSS vars set in a hoisted `CONTRIB_STYLES` string injected via `<style>` — light/dark variants for both 'green' and 'monochrome' themes (green is the default). On `mousemove`, projects the cursor to SVG coordinates via `createSVGPoint().matrixTransform(svg.getScreenCTM().inverse())`, derives the (col,row) cell, sets `activeCell`, and animates `mouseX` / `mouseY` motion values for tooltip positioning. The tooltip is portaled to `document.body` (so it escapes any container clip), rendered as a `motion.div` with `<NumberFlow>` for the count (so the number animates when switching cells), and a `popLayout` `<AnimatePresence>` for the month name cross-fade. A short-SHA-style ordinal-suffix helper (`1st`/`2nd`/`3rd`/`Nth`) drives the day display.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `useSyncExternalStore`-free approach with `mouseX`/`mouseY` motion values for tooltip positioning. The CSS variable injection (`<style>{CONTRIB_STYLES}</style>`) avoids prop-drilling color tokens. Wrapped in a `<ClientOnly>` boundary in HomePage because the `createPortal` call would crash during SSR. The default `preserveAspectRatio: 'xMidYMid meet'` lets the graph scale to its container; the home page overrides it to 'xMidYMid slice' for the hero header.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/home-page/ui/experience-section.tsx
nodes.summary: Public home-page experience timeline. `Experience()` is a top-level component: it reads `useGetPortfolioListQuery()` for the filtered experiences list and `useQuery(orpcQueryClient.resume.getDefault.queryOptions())` for the default resume download link. Renders an `<ol className='group/list'>` of `<ExperienceItem>` rows and, if a default resume exists, a 'Download Resume' link to `/api/resume/download/?id=${defaultResume.id}` (opens in new tab, noopener, noreferrer). `ExperienceItem` is a small structural subcomponent: it formats the date range (`formatDuration(fromDate, toDate, isPresent)` → e.g. 'Jan 2020 — current') and renders the title, organization, and HTML description in an 8-column grid (date | content). Uses Tailwind's `lg:group-hover:opacity-50` pattern to dim non-hovered items on hover, with `hover:lg:opacity-100!` to restore focus.
nodes.languageNotes: Two named exports (`Experience` + `ExperienceItem`) — same naming convention as `ProjectsSection` + `ProjectsItem`. The date formatter uses `toLocaleDateString('en-US', { timeZone: 'UTC' })` so the formatted date doesn't drift based on the viewer's local timezone. `formatDuration` returns just 'to' (e.g. 'current') if fromDate is null, which is unusual but handles the legacy 'employment without a start date' case.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/home-page/ui/github-setup-component.tsx
nodes.summary: Empty-state component for the home page when the GitHub config is missing or the data load failed. `GithubProfileUnavailableState()` renders a `<Container>` with an `<Empty>` showing a 'GitHub profile is temporarily unavailable' title, a description that tells the user to verify the configured username and token in the dashboard, and a 'Open GitHub config' Button (rendered as a TanStack Router `<Link to='/dashboard/settings/github' />`). Consumed by HomePage in three error/empty cases (unconfigured, isError, no profile data).
nodes.languageNotes: Exports as `GithubProfileUnavailableState` (long name, not just 'Empty' or 'Unavailable') because the home page renders this from a few different code paths and the explicit name is clearer at the call site than a generic 'Empty'.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/home-page/ui/home-nav.tsx
nodes.summary: Right-rail sticky in-page jump nav. `HomeNav()` reads `useGetPortfolioListQuery()` (for the contacts row at the bottom) and `useQuery(orpcQueryClient.resume.getDefault.queryOptions())` (for the optional 'Resume' link). Builds a `navItems` list: `['projects', 'experience', 'certificates']` as hash links, plus a `['Resume', '/api/resume/download?id=...']` tuple if a default resume exists. Each `<NavItem>` is a list item with an animated 8→16px underline that highlights when the matching section is intersecting (via `useIntersection` from the shared intersection provider). External links (tuples) render with `target='_blank' rel='noreferrer noopener'`. The 'contacts' row at the bottom of the nav is a `<Contact contacts={portfolioQuery.data.contacts} />`. Hidden on screens below `lg`.
nodes.languageNotes: The hash-derive `name.replace(/\s/g, '').toLowerCase()` strips whitespace (so 'Stack Overflow' becomes '#stackoverflow') to match the typical `id` convention in the page. The external-link check `typeof name !== 'string'` reuses the tuple-vs-string union as the discriminator — no separate boolean flag.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/home-page/ui/home-page.tsx
nodes.summary: Main / (home) route page. `HomePage()` reads the GitHub setup status (to derive `owner` and the isConfigured gate), the URL `?tab=` via `resolveGithubProfileTab` (returns a githubProfileTabs enum value), and four user-data queries: profile, contributions, pinnedRepos, profileRepos (only triggered if the active tab is 'repositories'). Wires `useGitHubSignalStream` against the four user-level signal keys (`ownerProfile`, `ownerContributions`, `ownerPinnedRepos`, `PublicOwnerRepos` / `PrivateOwnerRepos`). Returns the appropriate skeleton or `GithubProfileUnavailableState` at any of the four failure/loading gates. Renders a hero header (gradient background or the lazy-imported `<ContributionGraph>` wrapped in `<Suspense>` with a matching gradient fallback — requires `useIsClient()` because it uses `createPortal`), an Avatar (128px, fetchPriority=high, with sizes hint) overlapping the hero, an admin-only 'Edit GitHub profile' icon-button linking to github.com/settings/profile, the profile name + bio + a `<ProfileMetadata>` (Building / MapPin / Twitter handle, each as plain spans or external links), the pinned-repos grid (only when non-empty), the `<ProjectsSection>`, and the `<Experience>` section. Renders inside a `max-w-3xl` column with anchor IDs (#projects, #experience) for the HomeNav jump links. The `ContributionGraph` is a `React.lazy` chunk so its first render after hydration suspends without tripping the global errorComponent.
nodes.languageNotes: The lazy import + Suspense pattern is the project's standard way to ship a heavy client-only chart without hurting first-paint. `fetchPriority='high'` on the avatar is the React 19 hint to prioritize the LCP image. `useRouterState({ select: (state) => state.location })` is the canonical way to read the current location without subscribing to the whole router state. `useGetGithubProfileReposQuery(isRepositoriesTab)` is invoked unconditionally but the hook internally gates on the tab (it takes the enabled flag as its only arg, derived from isRepositoriesTab).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/home-page/ui/pinned-repo-card.tsx
nodes.summary: Small repo card shown in the home page's 'Pinned' section. `PinnedRepoCard({ repo })` accepts a structural subset (description, forks, isPrivate, language, languageColor, name, owner, stars) so it can be reused. Renders a TanStack `<Link to='/repos/$repo' params={{ repo: repo.name }}>` (a 144px-tall rounded card) with the repo name, a Private Badge (when isPrivate), a 2-line clamp description, and a bottom row with the language dot (colored from languageColor, fallback #6e7681), stars count, and forks count (each with formatCompactCount). The link target is the local /repos/$repo route, not the GitHub URL — clicking the card opens the in-app repo explorer.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses `formatCompactCount` (e.g. '1.2k' for 1234) on the stars/forks counts rather than the raw toLocaleString — matches the stats display in RepoSidebar. Structural typing pattern (same as RepoHeader) keeps the component decoupled from the full pinned-repos schema.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/home-page/ui/projects-section.tsx
nodes.summary: Public home-page projects timeline. `ProjectsSection()` reads `useGetPortfolioListQuery()` for the filtered projects list. Renders an `<ol className='group/list'>` of `<ProjectsItem>` rows. `ProjectsItem({ project })` is a structural-typed subcomponent that renders a circular logo (with `lg:group-hover:scale-125` and a saturate-0 → saturate-100 hover transition), a year + 'current' suffix, the title + an ExternalLink icon-button to `project.repos[0]` (when there are repos), the project description (raw HTML via dangerouslySetInnerHTML with the `[&_li]:mb-1 [&_ul]:list-disc [&_ul]:pl-4` Tailwind prose styles), and a wrap of `<StackBadge>`-like elements showing each project.stack's icon + uppercase name. Uses the same `group-hover:opacity-50` dimming pattern as ExperienceItem for hover focus.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors the ExperienceSection pattern: 2 named exports, 2 hooks in the parent (portfolioQuery), structural subcomponent type. The `lg:group-hover:bg-surface-1` chain on the logo is the project's hover-focus pattern — only the hovered row gets the surface background while others dim.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/home-page/ui/user-activity-feed.tsx
nodes.summary: Timeline of GitHub user activity events, grouped by month. `UserActivityFeed({ events }: { events: GithubActivityQueryResult })` returns a 'No recent activity' paragraph when empty, otherwise builds month-groups (`Map<month-label, events[]>`) sorted desc by `createdAt` and renders them as a left-rail timeline (a vertical gradient line via the `before:` pseudo-element). Each event is an `<ActivityEventRow>` with a circular icon (chosen by event.type via `getEventIcon`: PushEvent→GitCommitHorizontal, CreateEvent/DeleteEvent→GitBranch, PullRequestEvent/PullRequestReviewEvent→GitPullRequest, IssueCommentEvent/IssuesEvent→MessageSquare, WatchEvent→Star, ForkEvent→GitFork, default→Circle) and a description (via `getEventDescription`: 'Pushed N commits to {repo}', 'Opened PR {title} in {repo}', etc., all using the event's `repo` as a TanStack Link to `event.repo.url`). For PR/Issue events with detail, renders a small card (title + '#N · state'). For comments, renders a 2-line clamp. The relative time is `formatRelativeTime(...).replace(/ ago$/, '')` (drops the ' ago' suffix to save space). The `capitalize(value)` helper returns 'Updated' for null.
nodes.languageNotes: The `compactRelativeTime` helper exists solely to drop the ' ago' suffix — the rest of the app keeps the suffix, so this is a page-specific visual choice. `getEventDescription` uses a switch over `event.type` because GitHub's event taxonomy is a closed union (the type system would have caught missing cases). The PR detail card uses `render={<Link to={url} />}` composition so the visual is a card but the element is a real router link.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/playground/index.ts
nodes.summary: One-line page barrel re-exporting `PlaygroundPage` from `./ui/playground-page`. Consumed by the /playground/ route.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a relative import (./ui/playground-page) instead of the @/ alias because the import is in the same parent directory. The other pages use the @/ alias for consistency with the rest of the codebase.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/playground/ui/playground-page.tsx
nodes.summary: Internal /playground/ route — a smoke-test page for the project primitives. `PlaygroundPage()` fires `useQuery(orpcQueryClient.health.live.queryOptions())` to test the RPC connection (renders a green/red status dot based on `healthCheck.data && !healthCheck.isLoading`, with a 'Checking...' intermediate state gated on `isClient || healthCheck.isLoading`). Three sections: (1) 'Image Optimization' — a 256px-tall `<Image width=736 height=736 quality=20 priority placeholder='blur' src='/img/bg.jpg'>` (tests the wrapper Image component + blur placeholder + responsive srcset) with a Freepik attribution link; (2) 'Test RPC' — the health-check dot described above; (3) 'Test Error Handling' — three buttons: 'Throw Error' (calls `logger.debug('playground', 'Throwing test error...')` then throws a new Error to test the global error boundary, the dead-code after the throw is annotated with `oxlint-disable-next-line no-unreachable`), 'Show Toast' (toast.info), and 'Visit Privacy Policy' (rendered as a TanStack Link to /privacy-policy). `useLogger()` from the shared provider surfaces the logger interface.
nodes.languageNotes: The 'Throw Error' button is the canonical way to test the DefaultErrorPage boundary during dev. The `healthCheck.isLoading` intermediate state uses a `bg-destructive` (red) dot, then flips to `bg-success` (green) once data resolves — this matches the health router's actual shape (the live endpoint returns a 'live' status which the dot treats as 'connected').

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/privacy-policy/index.ts
nodes.summary: One-line page barrel re-exporting `PrivacyPolicyPage` from `./ui/privacy-policy-page`. Consumed by the /privacy-policy/ route.
nodes.languageNotes: Same pattern as the other 1-line page barrels. Uses the @/ alias.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/privacy-policy/ui/privacy-policy-page-content.mdx
nodes.summary: MDX content for the privacy policy page. Imports `appConfig` and exports 4 derived constants at the top: SITE_NAME (shortName), COMPANY_NAME (author), CONTACT_EMAIL (emailSupport), SERVER_LOCATION (serverLocation), plus an EFFECTIVE_DATE literal 'February 4, 2026'. The body is an 11-section privacy policy (Information We Collect, How We Use Your Information, Data Retention, Data Transfer, Sharing of Data, Your Rights (GDPR/CCPA), Security, Third-Party Links, Children's Privacy, Changes to This Policy, Contact). All brand-specific strings are interpolated from the exports so a config change propagates to the rendered page. The 'Contact' sections use `<a href={`mailto:${CONTACT_EMAIL}`}>` inline JSX to render the email link.
nodes.languageNotes: MDX is parsed by the framework's MDX pipeline (Vite + @mdx-js/rollup). The `export const` at the top of the file is the MDX mechanism for passing values to the consumer — PrivacyPolicyPage uses the Content component and that's it (it doesn't read the exports directly), but the exports are what allow the template to interpolate the values. `EFFECTIVE_DATE` is a hard-coded literal rather than computed from `new Date()` so the rendered date matches the actual legal revision.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/privacy-policy/ui/privacy-policy-page.tsx
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper for the privacy policy MDX content. `PrivacyPolicyPage()` renders a `<Container className='prose not-dark:prose-invert'>` with the imported MDX content. `prose` enables Tailwind Typography defaults; `not-dark:prose-invert` makes the prose use the inverted color palette in light mode (the app is dark-mode-by-default, so the light mode is the 'inverted' one).
nodes.languageNotes: Server component (no 'use client'). The MDX import is processed at build time. The Container comes from @tsu-stack/ui/components/container.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/terms-of-service/index.ts
nodes.summary: One-line page barrel re-exporting `TermsOfServicePage` from `./ui/terms-of-service-page`. Consumed by the /terms-of-service/ route.
nodes.languageNotes: Same pattern as privacy-policy/index.ts.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/terms-of-service/ui/terms-of-service-page/index.tsx
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper for the terms-of-service MDX content. `TermsOfServicePage()` renders a `<Container className='prose not-dark:prose-invert'>` with the imported MDX content from `./content.mdx`. Identical structure to PrivacyPolicyPage — the project uses a sub-folder `terms-of-service-page/` to co-locate the .tsx and .mdx file because the route path is more verbose than for privacy-policy.
nodes.languageNotes: Same MDX rendering pattern as PrivacyPolicyPage. The folder layout (terms-of-service-page/{index.tsx, content.mdx}) differs from privacy-policy ({privacy-policy-page.tsx, privacy-policy-page-content.mdx}) — the inconsistency is cosmetic and reflects different authors. Both produce the same output.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/pages/terms-of-service/ui/terms-of-service-page/content.mdx
nodes.summary: MDX content for the terms of service page. Imports `appConfig` and exports 5 derived constants: SITE_NAME, COMPANY_NAME, CONTACT_EMAIL, LEGAL_JURISDICTION_COUNTRY (jurisdictionCountry from appConfig), plus an EFFECTIVE_DATE literal 'March 2, 2026'. The body is a 10-section ToS (Use of the Service, Account Responsibilities, Intellectual Property, User Content, Termination, Disclaimers, Limitation of Liability, Governing Law, Changes to Terms, Contact). The 'Contact' section uses inline JSX `<a href={`mailto:${CONTACT_EMAIL}`}>` for the email link. Note: there's a small typo on the last line ('contact us at: contact us at:') that the project never cleaned up.
nodes.languageNotes: MDX with 4 config-derived exports + 1 literal effective date. The dual 'contact us at:' text in the last section is a real typo (it appears verbatim in the rendered page) — preserved here as the project hasn't touched the file since the original commit.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/router.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Router factory + browser log init. Calls `initLog({ batchedTransport: { drain: { credentials: 'include', endpoint: <server>/_logs/ingest }, pipeline: { batch: { intervalMs: 2000, size: 25 }, retry: { maxAttempts: 3 } } }, console: false, service: LOG_SERVICES.WEB_CLIENT })` to wire the client-side logger to the server's log ingestion endpoint. Exports `getRouter()` which: (1) creates a `queryClient` via `createAppQueryClient()`, (2) calls `createTanStackRouter({...})` with the routeTree, `defaultErrorComponent: (({ error }) => { throw error })` (intentionally re-throws to defer to the root route's errorComponent and avoid double-layout nesting — see TanStack router issue 1181), `defaultNotFoundComponent: DefaultNotFoundPage`, `defaultPendingComponent: () => <DefaultLoader ... />`, `defaultPreload: 'intent'`, `defaultPreloadStaleTime: 0`, `defaultStructuralSharing: true`, `context: { queryClient, user: null }`, `scrollRestoration: true`, and a `Wrap: ({ children }) => <AppQueryClientProvider><LoggerProvider>{children}</LoggerProvider></AppQueryClientProvider>` (so the QueryClient + Logger are available in every route). (3) Calls `setupRouterSsrQueryIntegration({ router, queryClient, handleRedirects: true, wrapQueryClient: false })` for the TanStack Query + SSR integration. (4) Declares a `Register` module augmentation so `Router` knows the custom `RouterAppContext` type.
nodes.languageNotes: The `defaultErrorComponent: (({ error }) => { throw error })` re-throw is the workaround for the TanStack Router error-boundary nesting bug (referenced in the comment with a link to GH issue 1181#issuecomment-2192468966). The `wrapQueryClient: false` flag tells the SSR integration to NOT wrap with its default QueryClientProvider because we already wrap with our own (AppQueryClientProvider, which adds persistence). The `Register` module augmentation is the standard way to teach TanStack Router's generics about the app's context type — without it, the createRouter call would need to be annotated with the context type at every callsite.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx
nodes.summary: Root route (matches every URL). Defines `RouterAppContext = { queryClient: QueryClient, user: AuthQueryResult }` and `Route = createRootRouteWithContext<RouterAppContext>()({ errorComponent: DefaultErrorPage, shellComponent: RootDocument, beforeLoad: async ({ context, preload }) => { if (!preload) void context.queryClient.prefetchQuery(getAuthUserQueryOptions()) }, head: () => ({...}) })`. The `beforeLoad` prefetches the auth user on the initial app load (skipped on preloads to avoid spamming the server). The `head()` returns links for the favicon, sitemap, geist variable + mono latin woff2 preloads, and the app stylesheet; plus the SEO meta from `generateAppSeo({ includeDocumentMeta: true })`. `RootDocument` is the HTML shell: `<html lang='en' suppressHydrationWarning>` with a `<head>` (HeadContent + a dev-only `<script type='module' src='/@vite-plugin-checker-runtime-entry' />` that connects the HMR client to vite-plugin-checker), a `<body>` wrapping the children with `ThemeProvider attribute='class' defaultTheme='dark' > TooltipProvider > ProgressProvider > NuqsAdapter` + a `Toaster richColors` (sonner) and the TanStackDevtools panel (Query / Router / Form / a11y) + `<Scripts />`.
nodes.languageNotes: The `if (!preload)` gate in beforeLoad is the key optimization: every link hover triggers a preload, and without this check the app would refetch the auth session on every link hover. The `suppressHydrationWarning` on both html and body is required because ThemeProvider toggles the `class` attribute client-side to apply the chosen theme, which would otherwise cause a React hydration mismatch warning. The dev-only vite-plugin-checker script is injected via `import.meta.env.DEV` so it's tree-shaken from production builds.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/experiences/index.tsx
nodes.summary: Route file for /dashboard/experiences. `Route = createFileRoute('/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/experiences/')({ component: ExperiencesPage, loader: async ({ context: { queryClient } }) => { void queryClient.prefetchQuery(orpcQueryClient.experiences.list.queryOptions()) } })`. Renders ExperiencesPage (re-exported from the page barrel) and prefetches the experiences list in the route loader so the SSR pass can stream the initial data.
nodes.languageNotes: No auth check here — the parent `/__protected/route.tsx` handles the auth gate (the path segment `__protected` is a convention for the project's auth-wrapping layout). `void queryClient.prefetchQuery(...)` discards the returned promise — the actual data flow goes through the page's useQuery, which reuses the prefetched cache entry.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/experiences/route.tsx
nodes.summary: Layout route for /dashboard/experiences. `Route = createFileRoute('/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/experiences')({ component: ExperiencesLayout })` and `ExperiencesLayout() = <Outlet />` — a pass-through layout. Exists so future experiences sub-routes (e.g. /dashboard/experiences/:id) can be added without restructuring the URL tree.
nodes.languageNotes: The pass-through Outlet pattern is the TanStack Router convention for declaring a layout route that doesn't wrap its own UI. Same pattern as /dashboard/resumes/route.tsx.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/index.tsx
nodes.summary: Route file for /dashboard (the dashboard home). `Route = createFileRoute('/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/')({ beforeLoad, loader, head, component: DashboardHomePage })`. `beforeLoad` calls `context.queryClient.ensureQueryData(githubConfig.get.queryOptions())` (awaited, since the dashboard home should redirect to /dashboard/settings/github if no config is present — `ensureQueryData` blocks until the data is in cache so the page can decide). `loader` prefetches experiences.list and projects.list (void-returned). `head()` returns the SEO meta via `generateAppSeo({ alternates: { canonicalPath: '/dashboard' }, description: 'Manage your resume content in {site.shortName}.', robots: { follow: false, index: false }, title: 'Dashboard' })` (noindex/nofollow since the dashboard is private). Renders DashboardHomePage.
nodes.languageNotes: `ensureQueryData` in beforeLoad is awaited (vs `void queryClient.prefetchQuery` in loader) because the home page needs the githubConfig data to render correctly — without it, the page would have to refetch in a useQuery and the first paint would flash. Same auth-gate convention as the other __protected routes.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/projects/index.tsx
nodes.summary: Route file for /dashboard/projects. Marked with `'use client';` at the top. Renders ProjectsPage and prefetches projects.list in the route loader. No beforeLoad, no head — the dashboard layout chain provides the noindex SEO meta implicitly.
nodes.languageNotes: The `'use client';` directive is the only project route that uses it explicitly — ProjectsPage likely uses a client-only API (the file includes `useRouterState` in the query-string sync). Same pattern as /dashboard/experiences except for the directive.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/resumes/index.tsx
nodes.summary: Route file for /dashboard/resumes. `Route = createFileRoute('/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/resumes/')({ component: ResumesPage, loader: async ({ context: { queryClient } }) => { void queryClient.prefetchQuery(orpcQueryClient.resume.list.queryOptions()) } })`. Renders ResumesPage and prefetches the resume list in the loader.
nodes.languageNotes: Same pattern as the other dashboard index routes.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/resumes/route.tsx
nodes.summary: Layout route for /dashboard/resumes. Pass-through Outlet that exists to allow future sub-routes (e.g. /dashboard/resumes/:id/preview) to mount under the resumes URL prefix without restructuring.
nodes.languageNotes: Identical to the experiences layout route.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/settings/account/index.tsx
nodes.summary: Route file for /dashboard/settings/account. Defines a local `ParsedUserAgent` type and a `parseUserAgent(ua)` helper that detects the OS (iOS / iPadOS / macOS / Windows / Android / Linux) via regex, the deviceType ('mobile' | 'tablet' | 'desktop' | 'unknown') via the same regex, the deviceName (e.g. 'iPhone', 'Mac', 'Windows PC', or the model extracted from the Android UA), and the browser (Edge / Firefox / Opera / Chrome / Safari) via the browser token in the UA. `Route = createFileRoute('/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/settings/account/')({ component: RouteComponent, loader: async () => { const listSessions = await authClient.listSessions(); const currentToken = (await authClient.getSession()).data?.session.token; return listSessions.data?.map(session => ({ isCurrent: session.token === currentToken, browser: parsed.browser, deviceName: parsed.deviceName, deviceType: parsed.deviceType, id: session.token, ipAddress: session.ipAddress ?? undefined, lastActive: session.updatedAt, os: parsed.os })) } })`. The loader returns the parsed session list (an array of shape consumed by AccountSettings) so the page doesn't have to refetch the same data. `RouteComponent() = <AccountSettings />`.
nodes.languageNotes: The route loader is awaited (not void) because the AccountSettings page reads its data via `useLoaderData({ from: '/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/settings/account/' })` — the loader's return value flows directly into the page. The parseUserAgent helper is local to the file rather than shared because the auth surface has only one consumer and the regex set is stable.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/settings/github/index.tsx
nodes.summary: Route file for /dashboard/settings/github. `Route = createFileRoute('/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/settings/github/')({ component: GithubSettings, loader: async ({ context }) => void context.queryClient.prefetchQuery(orpcQueryClient.githubConfig.get.queryOptions()) })`. Renders GithubSettings (re-exported from @/pages/dashboard) and prefetches the githubConfig in the loader.
nodes.languageNotes: Note: the `GithubSettings` import comes from `@/pages/dashboard` (the page barrel re-exports it). The page is at apps/web/src/pages/dashboard/settings/ui/github-settings.tsx — the barrel's 'mis-pointed' alias from batch 25's notes is still the case.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/settings/profile/index.tsx
nodes.summary: Route file for /dashboard/settings/profile. `Route = createFileRoute('/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/settings/profile/')({ component: RouteComponent, loader: async ({ context }) => { void context.queryClient.prefetchQuery(orpcQueryClient.profile.get.queryOptions()) } })`. Prefetches the current profile in the loader and renders `<ProfileSettings />` via the inner `RouteComponent` (kept as a local function rather than inlining, to match the project's other dashboard route files that wrap with a small component).
nodes.languageNotes: The wrap-in-`RouteComponent` is the same pattern as /settings/account/ — the file's actual render is one component call, but having a named local function gives a stable `component` reference for HMR. Same auth-gate via the parent __protected layout.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/settings/route.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Router layout route for the /dashboard/settings/* group. `Route = createFileRoute(...)({ component: SettingsLayout })` — the only job of this file is to mount the shared SettingsLayout (a sidebar + content shell) as the layout of the three settings sub-routes (account, profile, github). No loader, no beforeLoad, no head.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure pass-through route. SettingsLayout (imported from @/pages/dashboard/settings/ui/settings-layout) provides the chrome; child route files (account, profile, github) provide the Outlet content.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/stacks/index.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Router index route for /dashboard/stacks. `Route = createFileRoute(...)` declares a `loader` that void-prefetches `orpcQueryClient.portfolio.list` so the StacksPage (the admin CRUD page for the shared StackSelector vocabulary) lands with a warm cache. The component is StacksPage imported from the page barrel.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the oRPC query client (not the orpcClient) for prefetch — the loader pattern is `void queryClient.prefetchQuery(orpcQueryClient.<proc>.queryOptions())`. StacksPage is imported as a named import from @/pages/dashboard/stacks barrel.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/__protected/route.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Router layout route for the `__protected` pathless layout group (the auth-guarded shell that wraps /dashboard/* and the future /settings/* surfaces). `Route = createFileRoute('/(root-layout)/__protected')({ beforeLoad, component: RequiresAuthLayout })`. The `beforeLoad` calls `context.queryClient.ensureQueryData({ ...getAuthUserQueryOptions(), revalidateIfStale: true })` and `throw redirect({ to: '/sign-in', search: { redirect: location.href } })` if no user. On success it returns `{ user }` to the route context. The `RequiresAuthLayout` component runs the same auth query again as a useQuery (so child loaders can read context.user from the redirect-flow data) and uses a useEffect to redirect to /sign-in on a logged-out null result (gated by an `isGuestRoute(pathname)` early-return so the (guest)/sign-in subtree is allowed to render). Renders `<Outlet />`.
nodes.languageNotes: The `__protected` folder-name prefix is the TanStack Router file-based convention for pathless layout groups — it wraps its children in the auth guard without contributing a URL segment. The useEffect in RequiresAuthLayout is needed because the beforeLoad redirect only fires on route entry; a session-expiry-on-mount case needs the post-mount effect. `isGuestRoute` is a defensive predicate even though (guest) is technically a sibling layout (not a child of __protected).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/(guest)/sign-in/create-an-account/index.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Router index route for /sign-in/create-an-account. Defines `guestSearchSchema = z.object({ redirect: z.string().optional().catch(undefined) })` for the optional `?redirect=` post-login continuation URL, validates it with zodValidator, and uses `head: () => generateAppSeo({ ..., robots: { follow: false, index: false } })` to no-index the page. The component pulls `redirect` from `Route.useSearch()` and renders `<CreateAnAccountForm redirectTo={redirect as NavigateOptions['to']} />`.
nodes.languageNotes: The `redirectTo` is cast `as NavigateOptions['to']` because TanStack's typed-routes string literal union is too narrow for an unknown optional redirect URL — the cast is a known acceptable escape hatch for this validation-shape (the form's onSubmit redirects to it if provided, else to /). `robots: { follow: false, index: false }` makes the page invisible to crawlers.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/(guest)/sign-in/index.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Router index route for /sign-in. Mirrors the create-an-account route shape: same `guestSearchSchema` (optional `?redirect=` URL), zod-validated, noindexed head via `generateAppSeo({ ..., robots: { follow: false, index: false } })`. Renders `<SignInForm redirectTo={redirect as NavigateOptions['to']} />`.
nodes.languageNotes: SignInForm is from the @/features/auth barrel; the redirectTo cast is the same TanStack-typed-routes escape hatch used by the create-an-account sibling route.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/(guest)/sign-in/route.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Router layout route for the (guest)/sign-in pathless group. Renders a vertically-and-horizontally-centered flex container with `<Outlet />` so the /sign-in and /sign-in/create-an-account child routes both render in the same centered chrome.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure pass-through. The centered flex wrapper is the only chrome — no head() (the children set their own), no loader, no beforeLoad.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/index.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Router index route for / (the home page). `ssr: true` enables SSR for the home page. `beforeLoad: ({ context }) => context.queryClient.ensureQueryData(getGithubSetupStatusQueryOptions())` warms the setup-status cache up-front so the page can decide if it should prefetch GitHub user data. The loader reads the warmed setupStatus from the cache; if `isConfigured && owner` it triggers 4 parallel prefetches (profile, pinnedRepos, contributions, activity) and always prefetches the portfolio list. `head: () => generateAppSeo({ ..., description: appConfig.site.description })` uses the app-wide default description. Component `RootGithubProfilePage` simply renders `<HomePage />`.
nodes.languageNotes: The beforeLoad uses ensureQueryData (awaited, blocks the route) while the loader uses fire-and-forget void prefetchQuery — the difference is that setupStatus gates the rest of the loader so it must be ready, but the user-data prefetches can be backgrounded. `getQueryData` on the warmed query is how the loader reuses the beforeLoad's work without a second network call.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/playground/agent/index.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Router index route for /playground/agent. Sets a noindex head with `title: 'Agent Playground'` and a custom description, and renders `<AgentChatPage />` from the page barrel. No loader.
nodes.languageNotes: Single-component route, no data fetching — the AgentChatPage owns its own chat state and queries (it uses useAgentChat from the @/features/agent barrel).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/playground/index.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Router index route for /playground. Sets a noindex head with `title: 'Playground'` and a description that interpolates `appConfig.site.shortName`. Renders `<PlaygroundPage />` from the page barrel. No loader.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure head + render route. The page is an internal smoke-test surface (images, RPC health, toasts, error handling) so it's deliberately not indexed.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/privacy-policy/index.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Router index route for /privacy-policy. Sets a `generateAppSeo({ ..., title: 'Privacy Policy' })` head with the app's shortName in the description. Renders `<PrivacyPolicyPage />` from the page barrel. No loader.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors the terms-of-service route. The page itself renders an imported MDX default export inside a <Container className='prose not-dark:prose-invert'> (covered in batch 28).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/repos/$repo/blob/$.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Router file route for /repos/$repo/blob/* (the blob viewer). `ssr: true`. Component `GithubRepoBlobRoutePage` reads `{ _splat, repo }` from `Route.useParams()` and renders `<GithubRepoPage repo={repo} routeSplat={_splat} view='blob' />`.
nodes.languageNotes: The `$.tsx` is TanStack Router's splat-segment convention (catches the rest of the URL). The `view='blob'` prop tells GithubRepoPage to render the CodeFileView rather than the FolderView.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/repos/$repo/index.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Router index route for /repos/$repo (the repo home — repo overview, sidebar, branch-tip, etc.). `ssr: true`. Component `GithubRepoRoutePage` reads `{ repo }` from `Route.useParams()` and renders `<GithubRepoPage repo={repo} />` (no splat, no view prop → defaults to the home view).
nodes.languageNotes: Sibling of the blob/$.tsx and tree/$.tsx file routes. The layout (route.tsx at repos/$repo) provides the setup-status guard; this index route is the default child when no blob/ or tree/ sub-path is present.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/repos/$repo/route.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Router layout route for /repos/$repo. `RESERVED_NON_REPO_SEGMENTS = new Set(['.well-known', 'firebase-messaging-sw.js'])` — segments that look like a repo param but are actually service-worker / well-known paths. `beforeLoad` throws notFound() if `params.repo` is in the reserved set or if GitHub is not configured for an owner. `loader` void-prefetches `getGithubRepoOverviewQueryOptions(params.repo)` and `getGithubRepoBranchesQueryOptions(params.repo)`. Renders `<Outlet />`.
nodes.languageNotes: The reserved-set check is a defensive trap: e.g. /repos/firebase-messaging-sw.js would otherwise match the $repo param and try to fetch a repo called 'firebase-messaging-sw.js'. The set is closed (typed `as const`) so it's exhaustively checkable. beforeLoad uses `throw notFound()` (the TanStack Router helper) — notFound is the only one of the two guards that the route file actually has.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/repos/$repo/tree/$.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Router file route for /repos/$repo/tree/* (the file tree viewer). `ssr: true`. Component `GithubRepoTreeRoutePage` reads `{ _splat, repo }` from `Route.useParams()` and renders `<GithubRepoPage repo={repo} routeSplat={_splat} view='tree' />`.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirror image of the blob/$.tsx sibling. The `view='tree'` prop tells GithubRepoPage to render the FolderView / RepoFileTreeSidebar split-pane layout rather than the CodeFileView.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/repos/index.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Router index route for /repos (the repositories hub — filter + list of GitHub repos). `ssr: false` (client-only because the filter state is cookie-backed and the page is heavy). `validateSearch` accepts a `{ page?: number }` shape — coerces from a numeric or numeric-string URL param (returns the empty object for any unparseable input). Loader awaits the `getFilterCookie()` server-fn and `ensureQueryData(getGithubSetupStatusQueryOptions())`, computes `hubPrefetchInput` from the filter store + page, and only prefetches `githubReposHubQueryOptions(hubPrefetchInput)` if GitHub is configured. Returns `{ filterStore }` to the page via useLoaderData. `head: () => generateAppSeo({ ..., title: 'Repositories', robots: { follow: false, index: false } })`. Component destructures `filterStore` from `Route.useLoaderData()` and renders `<RepositoriesPage filterStore={filterStore} />`.
nodes.languageNotes: The custom validateSearch (rather than a zod-validator) is intentional: the only URL param is a positive integer page, and the manual coercion handles both `?page=2` and `?page=abc` (returns `{}` for the latter so the page defaults to 1). ssr: false + the cookie-backed filter state means the page is built around client-only data.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/route.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Router layout route for the (root-layout) pathless group. Loader void-prefetches `getPortfolioListQueryOptions()` so the chrome (RootLayout) and any child page can read the portfolio data from cache. Renders `<RootLayout><Outlet /></RootLayout>`.
nodes.languageNotes: RootLayout is from @/widgets/layout — the global chrome (top nav, footer, theme provider, etc.). Every page in the (root-layout) group (the home page, dashboard, repos, legal pages, playground) gets this shell.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/(root-layout)/terms-of-service/index.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Router index route for /terms-of-service. Sets a `generateAppSeo({ ..., title: 'Terms of Service' })` head with the app's shortName in the description. Renders `<TermsOfServicePage />` from the page barrel. No loader.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirror of the privacy-policy route. The page itself renders an imported MDX default export inside a <Container className='prose not-dark:prose-invert'> (covered in batch 28).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/[_]api/health/live.ts
nodes.summary: Server-only TanStack Router file route at /_api/health/live (the liveness probe — `[_]api` is a non-routable path prefix that the file-based router keeps out of the URL). The route declares `server: { handlers: { GET } }` and the GET handler returns a JSON body parsed through `HealthLiveOutputSchema` containing `buildSha` (ENV_WEB_SERVER.SOURCE_COMMIT), `environment` (NODE_ENV), `status: 'healthy'`, `timestamp` (ISO string), `uptimeMs` (Math.floor(process.uptime() * 1000)), and `url` (ENV_WEB_ISOMORPHIC.VITE_WEB_URL). The schema's `.parse` will throw a ZodError if any field is missing, which the server middleware converts to a 500 — that is the intended loud failure mode.
nodes.languageNotes: `[_]api` (the underscore prefix in brackets) is the TanStack Router file-based convention for an ignored URL segment — the segment exists in the file path so the file is matched, but it does not appear in the route path. The handler returns a Response.json so the TanStack Start server pipeline serializes the body. HealthLiveOutputSchema lives in @tsu-stack/core so the contract is shared with the server (Hono) for consistency.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/api/files/index.ts
nodes.summary: Server-only TanStack Router file route at /api/files. Forwards GET, POST, and PUT handlers to the `filesRouter` (a files-sdk createFilesRouter instance) imported from @/server/files-gateway. The files-router handles auth (Better Auth session check via `auth.api.getSession({ headers: req.headers })`), per-user keyPrefix scoping, and the actual upload/download pipeline against the MEDIA_BUCKET R2 binding.
nodes.languageNotes: Three verbs are intentionally forwarded (GET for download, POST for upload, PUT for chunked/multipart resume). The files-gateway wires ENV_WEB_SERVER.FILES_API_SECRET and the allowedOrigins CORS list (just VITE_WEB_URL). The createFilesRouter is a generic files-sdk factory — the route file is a thin TanStack-Start adapter that hands off the raw Request.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/api/resume/download/index.ts
nodes.summary: Server-only TanStack Router file route at /api/resume/download. The GET handler reads `?id=` from the URL; if present it calls `resumeRepository.findById(id)`, else `resumeRepository.findDefault()`. Both queries run inside `runWithDb(createDb(), ...)` (the @tsu-stack/db Cloudflare-D1 connection scope). On a hit, it streams the PDF from `env.MEDIA_BUCKET.get(resumeRow.r2Key)` (R2 binding) and returns it as a Response with `content-type: application/pdf`, `content-disposition: ${viewMode ? 'inline' : 'attachment'}; filename=...`, and `cache-control: public, max-age=3600`. 404 'Resume not found' / 'PDF not found' on the two failure modes.
nodes.languageNotes: `view` query param toggles inline vs attachment disposition (the viewer tab uses `?view=1`, the resume download button uses the default attachment). The pdf's Content-Disposition filename uses the resumeRow.filename column (set at upload time), not the slug. `runWithDb` is required because Cloudflare's D1 binding is request-scoped — without it, the repo call would have no live D1 connection.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/robots[.]txt.ts
nodes.summary:
Server-only TanStack Router file route at /robots.txt. The GET handler returns a `text/plain` Response with `User-agent: *
Allow: /
Sitemap: <ENV_WEB_ISOMORPHIC.VITE_WEB_URL + /sitemap.xml>
`. The Sitemap URL is built by `new URL('/sitemap.xml', VITE_WEB_URL).href` so it works for both localhost dev and production.
nodes.languageNotes: `robots[.]txt.ts` (the brackets-dot-escape) is TanStack Router's way of declaring a route whose path literally contains a `.` — otherwise the router would treat the `.` as a file-extension separator. The Sitemap reference must point to the same host as VITE_WEB_URL so Google picks it up.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routes/sitemap[.]xml.ts
nodes.summary: Server-only TanStack Router file route at /sitemap.xml. The GET handler walks the generated `routeTree` (from @/routeTree.gen) to extract every route's `{ id, fullPath }`, filters out API routes (`/_api/`), file routes (containing `.`), param routes (containing `$` or `:`), and underscored routes, dedupes by normalized URL, and emits a sitemap XML string with `<urlset>`, `<loc>`, `<lastmod>` (today, ISO date-only), `<changefreq>weekly</changefreq>`, `<priority>0.8</priority>`. Helpers: `escapeXml` for the 5 XML entities, `normalizeUrl` (strips trailing slashes, collapses double slashes, prepends basePath), `shouldIncludeInSitemap` (the filter predicate), `getRouteTreePaths` (recursive walker that handles an array-or-object children shape).
nodes.languageNotes: `preload: false` on the route so the sitemap isn't eagerly preloaded by the router. The regex set (BASE_PATH_REGEX, PATH_REGEX, DOUBLE_SLASH_REGEX, AMPERSAND_REGEX, etc.) is hoisted to module scope so they're compiled once. The `RouteTreeNode` type is a structural subset of the real routeTree — the handler is intentionally decoupled from the generated shape so changes to @tanstack/router don't break the sitemap. The black-list (ROUTE_BLACKLIST) is empty by design; the type `as const satisfies ReadonlyArray<string>` makes it explicit that the list is intended to be filled with exact route paths.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/routeTree.gen.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated route tree for apps/web, emitted by `tsr generate` from TanStack Router. The file imports every Route from every route file under src/routes (root, sitemap, robots, root-layout, __protected, api/files, terms-of-service, repos, privacy-policy, playground, _api/health/live, repos/$repo, sign-in (guest), api/resume/download, repos/$repo/index, playground/agent, __protected/dashboard/index, sign-in/index, __protected/dashboard/settings, __protected/dashboard/resumes, __protected/dashboard/experiences, __protected/dashboard/stacks, __protected/dashboard/resumes/index, __protected/dashboard/projects/index, __protected/dashboard/experiences/index, sign-in/create-an-account, repos/$repo/tree/$, repos/$repo/blob/$, __protected/dashboard/settings/profile, __protected/dashboard/settings/github, __protected/dashboard/settings/account) and then calls `.update({ id, path, getParentRoute: () => rootRouteImport })` to attach each one to its parent in the routing tree. The final exported `routeTree` is the assembled TanStack router state used by the createRouter call in src/router.tsx and by the sitemap walker.
nodes.languageNotes: Top-of-file: `/* eslint-disable */`, `// @ts-nocheck`, `// noinspection JSUnusedGlobalSymbols` — TanStack Router's generator output is intentionally untyped and un-linted. The 'do not modify' comment is the file's only documentation. Each Route is wrapped in `.update({...} as any)` to avoid type-check failures on the synthetic parent assignments.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/server.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack Start server entry point. Imports `@tanstack/react-start/server-entry` as the default `handler`, calls `initLogger({ env: { environment, service: LOG_SERVICES.WEB_SERVER, version: SOURCE_COMMIT }, sampling: { keep: [{ status: 400 }, { duration: 1000 }], rates: { info: 0 } } })` once at module load. Exports a default object with `async fetch(req: Request)` that creates a per-request `requestLog` via `createRequestLogger({ method, path })`, awaits the TanStack handler, emits `requestLog.emit({ status: response.status })` on success, and on caught errors calls `requestLog.error(error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error)))` then `requestLog.emit()` before re-throwing.
nodes.languageNotes: The sampling policy (`keep: [{ status: 400 }, { duration: 1000 }]` + `rates: { info: 0 }`) is a request-logger tuning: keep only 4xx+ status responses or requests that took ≥1s, and never sample info-level entries — the project's standard 'low-noise prod logger' baseline. The `LOG_SERVICES.WEB_SERVER` constant tags the service in structured logs so they're filterable downstream.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/server/files-gateway.ts
nodes.summary: Server-side files-router factory for apps/web. Imports `env` from `cloudflare:workers`, `FilesError` and `createFilesRouter` from files-sdk, `createFiles` from @tsu-stack/api/lib/storage (a thin wrapper over the R2 binding), `auth` from @tsu-stack/auth, and the ENV_WEB_ISOMORPHIC/ENV_WEB_SERVER env modules. Exports `filesRouter = createFilesRouter({ files: createFiles(env.MEDIA_BUCKET), secret: ENV_WEB_SERVER.FILES_API_SECRET, allowedOrigins: [ENV_WEB_ISOMORPHIC.VITE_WEB_URL], authorize: async ({ req }) => { const session = await auth.api.getSession({ headers: req.headers }); if (!session?.user) throw new FilesError('Unauthorized', 'sign in'); return { keyPrefix: \`${session.user.id}/\` }; } })`. The keyPrefix scopes every uploaded object to the user's ID so the files-sdk never has to think about authorization.
nodes.languageNotes: The `FilesError('Unauthorized', 'sign in')` second arg is the files-sdk error code (not a URL) — the client SDK renders it as a sign-in prompt. The `keyPrefix: \`${session.user.id}/\`` convention is the files-sdk's expected per-user object-key namespace. The allowedOrigins CORS list intentionally has only one entry (VITE_WEB_URL) — the API is not meant to be called from any other origin.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/form/calendar-field.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Form field binding for a single-date calendar picker. `CalendarField(props: CalendarFieldProps)` (props is `Omit<CalendarProps, 'mode'> & { label?, description?, classNames? }`) reads the typed field context as `useFieldContext<Date | undefined>()` and renders a Field+Label+Popover+CalendarDropdown combo. The PopoverTrigger is a Button outline (placeholder text 'Select Date' when no value, otherwise `new Date(value).toDateString()`). The CalendarDropdown is mode='single' (the `mode` prop is set internally so consumers can't pick range/multiple), bound to `field.state.value` / `field.handleChange`, and constrained to `startMonth: new Date(1995, 0)` / `endMonth: new Date(2030, 11)` for portfolio dates. `onDayBlur={field.handleBlur}`.
nodes.languageNotes: The `'mode'` Omit is critical: the underlying CalendarProps from coss is mode-typed, but this field only ever does single-mode, so the prop is locked. `classNames` is a per-slot override object (field / label / description / error).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/form/checkbox-field.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Form field binding for a boolean checkbox. `CheckboxField({ label?, description?, className? })` reads `useFieldContext<boolean>()` and renders a Field (flex-row with the coss Field primitives) with a hand-rolled `<input type='checkbox'>` (peer-styled with the coss focus/disabled ring), the optional label, the optional description, and the FieldError. `'use client'` directive at the top.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a raw `<input type='checkbox'>` rather than the coss Checkbox primitive because the coss one has a different value/change contract than TanStack Form's `field.state.value: boolean` / `field.handleChange(boolean)`. The peer-hocus-visible ring classes (`peer size-4 ... focus-visible:ring-ring/50`) match the coss Checkbox visual.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/form/combobox-field.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Form field binding for a single-select combobox. `ComboboxField({ label?, description?, placeholder?, emptyMessage?, items, classNames? })` reads `useFieldContext<string>()`, wraps a coss Combobox (value, onValueChange, items) with the coss Field+Label+ComboboxInput (showClear)+ComboboxContent+ComboboxEmpty+ComboboxList+ComboboxItem chrome. The items prop is the `ComboboxItemType[]` shape `{ value, label }`. The value bridge is `onValueChange: (val) => field.handleChange(val ?? '')` and `value: field.state.value || null` (ComboboxValue is nullable, the field stores a string).
nodes.languageNotes: The `|| null` coercion on value is the nullable-ComboboxValue contract: passing a string would render the wrong 'no value' state. `items` shape is intentionally a plain array (not a map) because the ComboboxList render-prop needs to render label + value, which is awkward in the coss items-as-map shape used by DropdownField.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/form/combobox-multiple-field.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Form field binding for a multi-select chip combobox. `ComboboxMultipleField({ label?, description?, placeholder?, emptyMessage?, items, classNames? })` reads `useFieldContext<string[]>()`. Items are `{ value, label, icon? }` (the icon shows in the chip and in the dropdown row). The coss Combobox is configured with `multiple`, `itemToStringValue: (item) => item.value`, and an onValueChange that maps the selected `ComboboxItemType[]` back to `string[]` (just the values). The selected values are derived by filtering the props.items array against the field's `string[]` value. The chip list (ComboboxChips+ComboboxValue render-prop) shows each selected item with its icon, label, and a `ComboboxChip aria-label={item.label}`. The search input (ComboboxChipsInput) hides its placeholder when at least one chip is selected. The popup is a ComboboxPopup+ComboboxEmpty+ComboboxList+ComboboxItem layout. Re-exports the `ComboboxItemType` type.
nodes.languageNotes: The `itemToStringValue` is the coss Combobox's hook for telling it what property of an item is the unique value (vs. the display label). Re-exporting the ComboboxItemType type is deliberate so consumers can type their `items` prop without re-declaring it.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/form/dropdown-field.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Form field binding for a single-select dropdown (the coss Select primitive variant). `DropdownField({ label?, description?, placeholder?, items, classNames? })` reads `useFieldContext<string>()`. Items are `{ value, label }[]`. The coss Select is given `items: itemsMap` (an Object.fromEntries(items.map(i => [i.value, i.label])) value→label map) plus an `itemToStringLabel` useCallback that looks up the label by value. The SelectTrigger+SelectValue+SelectPopup+SelectList+SelectItem chrome wraps the value. The value bridge is `onValueChange: (val) => field.handleChange(val ?? '')`.
nodes.languageNotes: The two `items`-shape choices are deliberate: the coss Select's `items` prop wants a Record<value, label> map (for quick lookup), but the coss SelectList wants an iterable (for rendering). The component builds both: `itemsMap` for the Select, `items` for the .map. `itemToStringLabel` is a useCallback with `[props.items]` dep so the coss Select doesn't re-compute the label on every render.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/form/form-contexts.ts
nodes.summary: Single-line wrapper around `createFormHookContexts()` from @tanstack/react-form. Exports `fieldContext`, `formContext`, `useFieldContext`, `useFormContext` — the four primitives every field and the SubmitButton in apps/web/src/shared/form/* bind to. The `form.ts` file uses the contexts as the `fieldContext` / `formContext` keys in the createFormHook call.
nodes.languageNotes: This file is the only place in the form surface that knows the contexts are module-scoped — every other form file just imports `useFieldContext` from here. Splitting the contexts out of `form.ts` lets the field components be imported without pulling in the full createFormHook wiring (which depends on every other field component).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/form/form.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack Form factory: `createFormHook({ fieldComponents: { CheckboxField, ComboboxField, ComboboxMultipleField, CalendarField, DropdownField, InputField, NumberFieldForm, PasswordInputField, RichTextField, YearField, InputGroupField, StackSelector, SwitchField, ImageField, IconPickerField }, fieldContext, formComponents: { SubmitButton }, formContext })`. Re-exports the typed hooks `useAppForm`, `withForm`, `withFieldGroup`, `extendForm`, `useTypedAppFormContext` — these are what every form-using page (auth, profile-settings, projects, experiences, etc.) consumes via `@/shared/form`'s barrel.
nodes.languageNotes: The factory is the single registration point for every field and form component — the coss primitives are wrapped once in field bindings, then the apps/web pages consume them via `useAppForm` (which has them strongly typed). `withFieldGroup` and `extendForm` are the pattern for sharing field-group logic across forms (e.g. a `withImageFieldGroup` HOC).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/form/icon-field.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Form field binding for the IconPicker primitive. `IconPickerField({ label?, description?, classNames? } & Omit<IconPickerProps, 'classNames'>)` reads `useFieldContext<string>()`. Renders a Field+Label+IconPicker (id=field.name, value=field.state.value ?? '', onValueChange=(icon) => field.handleChange(icon), onBlur=field.handleBlur) wrapped in FieldDescription+FieldError. `'use client'` directive.
nodes.languageNotes: The `Omit<IconPickerProps, 'classNames'>` is what allows the field to define its own classNames shape (per-slot override) without colliding with the IconPicker's own classNames. IconPicker is the Lucide-icon + custom icon search popover in @/shared/ui/icon-picker.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/form/image-field.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Form field binding for an image upload that goes through the files-sdk. `ImageField({ label?, description?, className? })` reads `useFieldContext<string>()` and watches the form store for `state.values[field.name]` (the current public URL) via `useStore`. Uses `useFiles({ endpoint: '/api/files' })` from files-sdk/react for upload + url-derivation. `handleFileChange`: gets the first selected File, sets `uploading=true`, calls `files.upload(file)` → `files.url(key)` → `field.handleChange(publicUrl)`; on error, swallows (the `files.error` message is rendered below); on finally, enforces a 400ms minimum loader-visible time (`MIN_LOADER_MS = 400`) so the spinner doesn't flash. `handleClear` resets the field to ''. Renders a 96×96 preview tile with a destructive X button when a value is set, a hidden `<input type='file' accept='image/*'>`, and an upload/replace button (Loader2 spinner when uploading).
nodes.languageNotes: The 400ms minimum loader (`MIN_LOADER_MS`) is a UX trick: a sub-400ms upload feels janky, so the loader is shown for at least that long even on instant returns. `files.error` is the files-sdk's sticky error state — it's rendered as a FieldError rather than thrown, so the field stays interactive after a failed upload.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/form/index.ts
nodes.summary: Public barrel for apps/web/src/shared/form. Re-exports the four TanStack Form contexts (useFieldContext, useFormContext, fieldContext, formContext) and the createFormHook factory outputs (useAppForm, withForm, withFieldGroup) — these are the two primary consumption points for form-using pages. Also re-exports the field bindings that are commonly used as form-level custom components: CheckboxField, ComboboxMultipleField, InputField, NumberFieldForm, PasswordInputField, RichTextField, StackSelector, SubmitButton, SwitchField, YearField.
nodes.languageNotes: CalendarField, ComboboxField, DropdownField, ImageField, IconPickerField, InputGroupField, and the StackSelector helper are imported directly from their files by their consumers (not from the barrel) — the barrel only re-exports the most-commonly-used fields to keep the type surface small.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/form/input-field.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Form field binding for a basic text/email/url/etc. input. `InputField({ label?, placeholder?, description?, type?, classNames? })` reads `useFieldContext<string>()` and renders a Field+Label+Input (id=field.name, onBlur=field.handleBlur, onChange=(e) => field.handleChange(e.target.value), type defaults to 'text', value defaults to '' if null/undefined). Wrapped in FieldDescription+FieldError. `'use client'`.
nodes.languageNotes: The `value ?? ''` coercion is required because TanStack Form's field value can be `undefined` for an un-set string field — passing undefined to a controlled <input> triggers a React warning.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/form/input-group-field.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Form field binding for an InputGroup (input with optional left/right addons). `InputGroupField({ label?, placeholder?, description?, type?, classNames?, children }: PropsWithChildren<InputFieldProps>)` reads `useFieldContext<string>()` and renders a Field+Label+InputGroup (with InputGroupInput as the controlled input) + any children (which become addons). The same value/onBlur/onChange bridge as InputField. `'use client'`.
nodes.languageNotes: The `PropsWithChildren<InputFieldProps>` re-uses the input-field's prop shape and adds the children prop. Children are placed inside the InputGroup after the InputGroupInput so they appear as the right-side addon (e.g. a 'show password' eye button for the password input group, or a 'clear' button for a search input).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/form/number-field.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Form field binding for the coss NumberField (the +/- button group primitive). `NumberFieldForm({ label?, description?, placeholder?, min?, max?, step?, size?, classNames? })` reads `useFieldContext<number>()`. Wraps a coss NumberField (min, max, name, size, step, onBlur, onValueChange) with a NumberFieldGroup+NumberFieldDecrement+NumberFieldInput+NumberFieldIncrement sub-tree. The onValueChange bridge: if null/undefined, field.handleChange(0); else field.handleChange(next). `value` is `value ?? 0` so an unset field starts at 0. `'use client'`.
nodes.languageNotes: The null-coercion (`next == null ? 0 : next`) is the coss NumberField's empty-input contract — it fires onValueChange(null) when the user clears the field, and the form always wants a number. The exported name is `NumberFieldForm` (not `NumberField`) to avoid colliding with the imported `NumberField` component from coss.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/form/password-input-field.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Form field binding for a password input. `PasswordInputField({ label?, placeholder?, description? })` reads `useFieldContext<string>()` and renders a Field+Label+PasswordInput (coss primitive with the built-in show/hide eye button). Same value/onBlur/onChange bridge as InputField but no classNames slot. `'use client'`.
nodes.languageNotes: No `type` prop — the coss PasswordInput is always type='password' and renders its own show/hide eye. The SignInForm and CreateAnAccountForm in apps/web/src/features/auth/ui use this field for the password input.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/form/rich-text-field.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Form field binding for the RichTextEditor (coss primitive). `RichTextField({ label?, description?, ...editorProps }: Omit<RichTextEditorProps, 'value' | 'onChange' | 'onBlur'>)` reads `useFieldContext<string>()` and renders a Field+Label+RichTextEditor (value=field.state.value ?? '', onChange=(html) => field.handleChange(html), onBlur=field.handleBlur, className='w-full', ...rest). Wrapped in FieldDescription+FieldError. No `'use client'` directive (RichTextEditor may be SSR-safe depending on its underlying editor).
nodes.languageNotes: The Omit<RichTextEditorProps, 'value' | 'onChange' | 'onBlur'> strips the three props the field binds itself; the rest of the editor's props (placeholder, theme, extensions, etc.) pass through. The output is an HTML string (the editor's contract).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/form/stack-selector.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Form field binding for selecting one-or-more Stacks (the shared vocabulary table). `StackSelector({ label?, description?, className? })` reads `useFieldContext<string[]>()`. Fires `useQuery(orpcQueryClient.stacks.list.queryOptions())` for the available stacks. Local state: `open` (Popover), `createOpen` (create-stack Dialog), `newName`, `newIcon` (create form fields). The Popover renders a Command palette (CommandInput+CommandList+CommandGroup with the stacks as CommandItems) plus a 'Create new stack' button that opens a Dialog with an inline name+icon form. `createMutation = useMutation(orpcQueryClient.stacks.create.mutationOptions({ onSuccess: (created) => { invalidate stacks.list + portfolio.list, field.handleChange([...selectedIds, created.id]), close dialog, clear inputs } }))`. `toggleStack` adds/removes the id from the field's array. Below the Popover, the selected stacks render as removable pill chips (× button on each). The CommandItem click uses native onClick (not onSelect) because the local CommandItem is a styled <button>, not the cmdk version. Helper `StackOption` shows the stack's icon + name in the dropdown row.
nodes.languageNotes: The 'use native onClick on the CommandItem' comment is the single explicit gotcha in the file — the coss CommandItem wraps cmdk but the local version is a plain button, so cmdk's onSelect is never fired. The `invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ...portfolio.list.queryKey({ input: {} }) })` call is what refreshes the project cards after a new stack is added (the project page reads portfolio.list with the same empty-input key).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/form/submit-button.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Form form-level component (registered as `formComponents.SubmitButton` in form.ts) that subscribes to `state.isSubmitting` and disables the underlying Button while a submission is in flight. `SubmitButton({ children, isLoading?, ...props })` reads `useFormContext()`, wraps the coss Button in `<form.Subscribe selector={(state) => [state.isSubmitting]}>{([isSubmitting]) => <Button type='submit' disabled={isLoading ?? isSubmitting} {...props}>{children}</Button>}</form.Subscribe>`. `'use client'`.
nodes.languageNotes: The SubmitButton lives in `formComponents` (not `fieldComponents`) because it subscribes to the form's overall state rather than a single field's state. `isLoading ?? isSubmitting` lets consumers pass an external isLoading (e.g. a parent mutation's pending state) that takes precedence over the form's own isSubmitting.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/form/switch-field.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Form field binding for a boolean Switch. `SwitchField({ label?, description?, classNames? })` reads `useFieldContext<boolean>()`. Renders a Field (flex-row with the switch on the left and an optional FieldContent+FieldLabel+FieldTitle+FieldDescription cluster on the right) + the coss Switch (id, name, checked, onCheckedChange, onBlur). The right-side content cluster only renders if label or description is set. `'use client'`.
nodes.languageNotes: FieldTitle (separate from FieldLabel) is used inside the FieldLabel so the label is clickable (the click goes to the FieldLabel htmlFor) and the title text has the bold/medium weight — the coss pattern is FieldLabel+FieldTitle for switch/checkbox right-side content. `classNames.input` is a slot for the switch's own styling so consumers can color/size the switch without touching the field row.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/form/year-field.tsx
nodes.summary: TanStack Form field binding for a year-only dropdown (no month/day). `YearField({ label?, classNames? })` reads `useFieldContext<number>()`. The year range is module-scoped: `YEAR_MIN = 1980` to `currentYear = new Date().getFullYear()`, pre-built as `yearLabels: { value, label }[]` and an `itemsMap: Record<string, string>` for the coss Select. Renders a Field+Label+Select (with itemToStringLabel: (val) => val) + SelectTrigger+SelectValue ('Select year' placeholder) + SelectPopup+SelectList with the yearLabels as SelectItems. The onValueChange bridge converts the string value back to a number: `field.handleChange(val ? Number(val) : currentYear)`. `'use client'`.
nodes.languageNotes: Building the items once at module load (rather than per-render) is what makes the year array cheap — the range is at most ~50 years, so re-deriving inside the component is fine, but the pattern is to pre-build the map at module scope. `itemToStringLabel: (val) => val` is a trivial identity lookup (year is its own label) — the callback is wrapped in useCallback with no deps because the function body is referentially stable.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/command-palette/open-state.ts
nodes.summary: Module-scoped external store for the command-palette open/close state. `let open = false; const listeners = new Set<() => void>(); function notify() { listeners.forEach((l) => l()); }`. Exports `isOpen(): boolean` (imperative read), `setCommandPaletteOpen(value: boolean)` (imperative write + notify), and `useCommandPaletteOpen()` (React `useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, isOpen, isOpen)` wrapper). Subscribe is the standard add/remove listener pair.
nodes.languageNotes: The `useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, isOpen, isOpen)` pattern (getServerSnapshot === getSnapshot) is the SSR-safe form of the hook — the server returns the current open state (default false), and the client reuses the same value to avoid hydration mismatch. The set/notify pattern is the standard `useSyncExternalStore` shape (no version tracking because the value is a primitive boolean).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/command-palette/registry.ts
nodes.summary: Module-scoped external store for registered command-palette commands. `let commands: CommandItem[] = []; const listeners = new Set<() => void>(); function emit() { ... }`. Exports `registerCommands(items: CommandItem[]): () => void` (adds to the array, emits, returns a deregister function that filters by id and emits), `getRegisteredCommands(): CommandItem[]` (imperative read), `subscribeCommands(listener: () => void): () => void` (subscribe/unsubscribe). At module load, registers 4 static nav commands: `nav:overview` (Go to Home, G+H, lucide HomeIcon), `nav:repos` (Go to Repositories, G+O, ArchiveIcon), `admin:projects` (Edit projects, G+P, ArchiveIcon), `nav:dashboard` (Go to Dashboard, G+D, SettingsIcon). Three more commands (nav:pulls PR, nav:issues, nav:reviews) are commented out as future toggles.
nodes.languageNotes: The static `registerCommands([...])` at module load is the project's pattern for code-split command registration: rather than importing the registry into a config file, the config IS the registry file, and features that need to add commands call `registerCommands([...])` from a useEffect. The shortcut convention is single-key (e.g. ['G', 'H']) — the use-command-palette hook wires each as a 2-step chord (G then H within 800ms).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/command-palette/types.ts
nodes.summary: Type definitions for the command palette. `CommandAction = { type: 'navigate'; to: string; params?: Record<string, string> } | { type: 'execute'; fn: () => void | Promise<void> }` — the discriminated union of actions a command can take. `CommandItemMeta = { repo?, comments?, updatedAt?, language?, stars? }` — extra row metadata. `CommandItem = { id, label, group, icon? (ComponentType<{className?: string}>), iconClassName?, keywords?, shortcut? (string[]), action, priority?, meta? }` — the full command shape consumed by useCommandItems + the CommandPalette renderer.
nodes.languageNotes: The `action` is a discriminated union by `type`, so consumers narrow with a switch (`if (cmd.action.type === 'navigate') ... else ...`). The `icon: ComponentType<{ className?: string }>` is the standard lucide icon shape — accepting a className is what allows the command palette to color icons by state (draft=muted, merged=purple, closed=red, open=green).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/command-palette/use-command-items.ts
nodes.summary: Hook that builds the full list of command-palette commands (static + dynamic). `useCommandItems(): CommandItem[]` reads `useQuery(getAuthUserQueryOptions())` for the user (used to scope the githubQueryKeys lookups), gets `staticCommands` via `useSyncExternalStore(subscribeCommands, getRegisteredCommands, getRegisteredCommands)`, and reads 4 queryClient caches via `getQueryData` (no refetch): repos (githubQueryKeys.repos.list), pulls (githubQueryKeys.pulls.mine), issues (githubQueryKeys.issues.mine), viewer (githubQueryKeys.viewer). Builds a `dynamicItems: CommandItem[]` starting with a 'Refresh data' action that calls `useRefreshGitHubData()` and conditionally appends: a 'Go to Profile' nav (if viewer), one item per repo (navigate to /{owner}/{name}), one item per pull (across authored/assigned/reviewRequested/mentioned/involved, deduped by id, with PR-state-colored icon and comments/updatedAt meta), one item per issue (across authored/assigned/mentioned, deduped by id, with state-colored icon). Sorts dynamic items desc by `meta.updatedAt`. Returns `[...staticCommands, ...dynamicItems]`.
nodes.languageNotes: Helpers `getPrIcon(pr)` and `getIssueIcon(issue)` map the closed/merged/draft + state-reason states to a `{ icon, iconClassName }` pair — the same color logic as pr-state.ts but inline. The dedupe Set is per-entity-type (separate `seen` Set for pulls vs issues) because the same PR can show up in multiple buckets. The `string[]` shortcut is the multi-step chord — the use-command-palette hook expands each string to `{ key }`.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/command-palette/use-command-palette.ts
nodes.summary: Hook that wires the command palette: open-state, the cmd-K (or ctrl-K) toggle, and per-command chord shortcuts. `useCommandPalette()` reads `useCommandPaletteOpen()` and `useRouter()`. Calls `useGlobalShortcuts([{ shortcut: { key: 'k', mod: true }, allowInEditable: true, onTrigger: () => setCommandPaletteOpen(!isOpen()) }, ...getRegisteredCommands().flatMap((cmd) => cmd.shortcut ? [{ shortcut: cmd.shortcut.map((key) => ({ key })), enabled: !open, onTrigger: () => { if (cmd.action.type === 'navigate') void router.navigate({ to: cmd.action.to }); else void cmd.action.fn(); } }] : [])])`. Returns `{ open, setOpen: setCommandPaletteOpen, close }` (close is a useCallback that calls setCommandPaletteOpen(false)).
nodes.languageNotes: `enabled: !open` on the chord shortcuts means the per-command chords are disabled while the palette is open (so typing the next chord key inside the search input doesn't accidentally navigate). The `flatMap` returns [] for commands without a shortcut — a clean way to skip them without a separate filter.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/command-palette/use-refresh-github-data.ts
nodes.summary: Hook that returns a single-flight callback for clearing the GitHub viewer cache. `useRefreshGitHubData()` uses `useRef<Promise<void> | null>(null)` to track an in-flight task. The returned `useCallback` is no-op-ish if a task is already in flight (returns the same promise); otherwise it calls `orpcClient.github.clearViewerCache()` and throws 'You need to be signed in to refresh data.' if `!result.ok`, then `window.location.reload()`.
