Catches and swallows errors on the ref's chain (`.catch(() => undefined)`) so a failed refresh doesn't leave a stuck ref, then `.finally(() => { inFlightRef.current = null })`.
nodes.languageNotes: The single-flight pattern (useRef of the in-flight promise) is what makes repeated clicks of 'Refresh data' a no-op while a reload is pending. `window.location.reload()` is used instead of `queryClient.invalidateQueries` because the GitHub API rate limit budget is process-scoped — a hard reload re-fetches from a clean slate.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/explorer-path-store.ts
nodes.summary: Lightweight external store for the current explorer path in the file tree sidebar. Module-scoped `let currentPath = ''; const listeners = new Set<() => void>(); function emit() { listeners.forEach(fn => fn()); }`. Exports `setExplorerPath(path: string)` (no-op if path === currentPath, else updates + emits), `getExplorerPath(): string` (imperative read), `useExplorerPath()` (returns the raw string via useSyncExternalStore — used by the file-search card to pre-fill the current-path filter), `useIsActivePath(entryPath: string)` (returns a boolean via useSyncExternalStore — the snapshot is a boolean primitive, so unchanged nodes skip re-render), and `useIsAncestorPath(entryPath: string)` (returns a boolean — `currentPath.startsWith(\`${entryPath}/\`)` — used to auto-expand ancestor directories).
nodes.languageNotes: The boolean snapshots for useIsActivePath and useIsAncestorPath are the project's pattern for fine-grained subscription in a tree of memoized nodes: because useSyncExternalStore compares snapshots by ===, navigating between files re-renders only the old-active and new-active nodes (and the ancestors whose startsWith result flipped). The server snapshot for useExplorerPath is '' (not undefined) to match the client's initial value and avoid hydration mismatch.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/format-relative-time.ts
nodes.summary: Tiny pure function that formats an ISO date string as a compact relative time. `formatRelativeTime(dateString: string | null): string` — returns 'Unknown' for null; otherwise computes `diffMs = Date.now() - new Date(dateString).getTime()`, rounds to `diffDays = max(1, round(diffMs / 86400000))`, and picks the largest unit that yields ≥1: 'Ny ago' (≥365d), 'Nmo ago' (≥30d), 'Nw ago' (≥7d), 'Nd ago' (otherwise). The min-1-day clamp prevents a same-day commit from showing '0d ago'.
nodes.languageNotes: No Intl.RelativeTimeFormat — the format is hand-rolled for the project's compact style ('2y ago' / '3mo ago' / '4w ago' / '5d ago'). The min-1-day round-up is the only non-obvious detail: `Math.max(1, Math.round(...))`.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/fuzzy-file-search.ts
nodes.summary: Tiny dependency-free fuzzy file search. Exports `FileSearchEntry = { name, path, type: 'dir' | 'file' | 'submodule' }`, `FileSearchResult = FileSearchEntry & { score: number }`, `scoreMatch(query, filePath): number` (the scoring algo), `getMatchIndices(query, text): Set<number>` (returns the positions in text that matched the query — used for highlight), and `searchFiles(query, entries, limit=50): FileSearchResult[]`. The scoring: case-insensitive subsequence match (returns -1 if not a subsequence), then base score from name/path containment (exact name = 1000, name starts with = +100, name contains = +50, path contains = +25), then +5 × max consecutive run length, then -2 × path depth, then -name length. The default limit is 50.
nodes.languageNotes: Two passes in scoreMatch: a fast fail pass that just checks subsequence (returns -1 early if not a match), then a scoring pass that only runs on a valid match. The consecutive-run bonus (+5 × maxRun) is what makes 'foo' match 'frontend/foo' feel snappier than 'f-o-o' against a long path. getMatchIndices is the highlight helper: returns the positions in the original-cased text where the query's characters matched, so consumers can render <mark> spans.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/github-access-modal-store.ts
nodes.summary: Module-scoped external store for the GitHub access modal prompt. `let prompt: GitHubAccessPrompt | null = null; const listeners = new Set<() => void>();`. Exports `openGitHubAccessPrompt(nextPrompt: GitHubAccessPrompt)` (sets + emits — annotated with a `fallow-ignore-next-line unused-export` comment because the only call site is the warning-store's checkPermissionWarning), `closeGitHubAccessPrompt()` (no-op if null, else sets to null + emits), and `useGitHubAccessPrompt()` (useSyncExternalStore with the prompt object as snapshot). The prompt type is `{ source: 'onboarding' | 'warning'; owner?, repo?, fallbackHref? }`.
nodes.languageNotes: The store is intentionally separate from warning-store.ts even though both surface 'GitHub access' issues — the modal is a one-shot, blocking dialog (waits for the user to grant access) while warnings are non-blocking toasts. `fallow-ignore-next-line` is the project's linter-suppression marker for intentionally-unused exports.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/github-repo-commit-sparkline.query.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack Query options builder + hook for the per-repo commit sparkline (the 7-day commit-activity SVG used in the repo overview card). `getGithubRepoCommitSparklineQueryOptions(repo: string)` calls `orpcQueryClient.github.publicGetRepoCommitSparkline.queryOptions({ input: { repo }, staleTime: githubCachePolicy.detail.staleTimeMs, gcTime: githubCachePolicy.detail.gcTimeMs, meta: persistedMeta })`. `useGetGithubRepoCommitSparklineQuery(repo)` is the `useQuery` wrapper. Re-exports `GithubRepoCommitSparklineQueryResult` (Awaited<ReturnType<typeof orpcClient.github.publicGetRepoCommitSparkline>>).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the 'public' orpc procedure (no auth required) so the sparkline works on the public-facing /repos page for unauthenticated viewers. `persistedMeta` is the shared meta flag from query-persistence.ts that opts the query into nuqs-style URL persistence — re-renders re-hydrate the cached value from the URL on the next navigation.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/highlight-code.ts
nodes.summary: Caching wrapper around the @tsu-stack/ui Shiki highlighter for code blocks in rendered markdown. `highlightCode(code: string, lang: string): Promise<string>` — the lang string is normalized via `FENCE_LANG_ALIASES` (shell/sh/console/zsh → shellscript, js → javascript, ts → typescript, yml → yaml, md → markdown), then checked against `shikiBundledLangSet` (if not present, falls back to 'text'). The function is memoized in `htmlCache: Map<key, Promise<string>>` where key is `lang:code` (full HTML output). Lang load is single-flighted: each lang is loaded once and added to `loadedLangs`; concurrent calls share the same `langLoadPromises` Map entry. The highlighter is module-scoped (`highlighterPromise: Promise<MarkdownHighlighter>`) — created via `createMarkdownHighlighter()` on the client, and stubbed to `new Promise<MarkdownHighlighter>(() => {})` on the server (intentionally never resolves so SSR blocks on the highlight, preventing unhighlighted flicker).
nodes.languageNotes: The server-side `new Promise<MarkdownHighlighter>(() => {})` is a 'never resolves' promise — it makes highlightCode hang forever on the server, which is intentional because Shiki is a heavy WASM bundle that shouldn't be loaded during SSR. Consumers must gate highlightCode with useIsClient or a Suspense boundary. The dual-cache (htmlCache for the full output, loadedLangs + langLoadPromises for the lang load) is what makes repeated renders of the same code block effectively free.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/parse-repo-route-splat.ts
nodes.summary: Pure function that splits a TanStack Router splat param (e.g. `main/src/index.ts`) into `{ path, ref }` (e.g. `{ path: 'src/index.ts', ref: 'main' }`). `parseRepoRouteSplat({ branchNames, defaultBranch, splat })`: if splat is empty or only `/`, returns `{ path: '', ref: defaultBranch }`. Otherwise normalizes the splat (strips leading + trailing slashes) and looks for the longest branch name that is either equal to the splat or a prefix of `splat/`. If a branch matches, returns `{ path: splat.slice(branchName.length).replace(/^\/+/, ''), ref: branchName }`. If no branch matches, returns `{ path: rest.join('/'), ref: firstSegment || defaultBranch }` (treating the first segment as the ref and the rest as the path).
nodes.languageNotes: The branch-names sort by descending length is the critical detail — a branch named 'feature/x' would otherwise be split out as ref='feature' path='x' by a naive `splat.split('/')`. The 'longest match wins' order ensures 'feature/x' is recognized as the ref and only the rest is treated as the path. The `if (!matchingBranch)` fallback handles non-branch refs (tags, SHAs) by treating the first segment as the ref — same shape, but the caller is responsible for not assuming it's a real branch.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/pr-state.ts
nodes.summary: PR-state → visual-config mapper. Exports `PrStateTone = 'open' | 'closed' | 'merged' | 'muted'`, `PrStateConfig = { icon: LucideIcon; color: string; label: string; tone: PrStateTone }`, and `getPrStateConfig(pr: { isDraft, state, isMerged?, mergedAt? }): PrStateConfig`. The order: isDraft → muted (gray, GitPullRequestDraftIcon, 'Draft'); isMerged || mergedAt || state === 'merged' → merged (purple, GitMergeIcon, 'Merged'); state === 'closed' → closed (red, GitPullRequestClosedIcon, 'Closed'); otherwise → open (green, GitPullRequestIcon, 'Open').
nodes.languageNotes: Same logic as the inline getPrIcon helper in use-command-items.ts (the command-palette's PR items), but lifted to a shared util so the repo activity cards, the PR list, and the command palette all see identical PR-state styling. The `isMerged` + `mergedAt` + `state === 'merged'` triple-check is because different GitHub API responses use different fields to signal merged (older responses only had mergedAt, newer ones also set state=merged for convenience).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/profile-tabs.ts
nodes.summary: Const + resolver for the GitHub profile-page tab. `githubProfileTabs = { overview: 'overview', repositories: 'repositories' } as const`, type `GithubProfileTab = (typeof githubProfileTabs)[keyof typeof githubProfileTabs]`, and `resolveGithubProfileTab(tab: string | null): GithubProfileTab` (returns 'repositories' if tab === 'repositories', else 'overview' — i.e. defaults to overview for any other input including null).
nodes.languageNotes: The `as const` makes the object readonly and the literals string-typed — `typeof githubProfileTabs` becomes the literal union 'overview' | 'repositories'. The resolver is a defensive default (any unknown input → 'overview') so a malformed URL never causes a tab render to fail.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/query-persistence.ts
nodes.summary: Query persistence helpers. Exports `persistedMeta = { persist: true } as const` (the meta flag that opts a query into URL persistence), `getGitHubDataSource(value: unknown): string | null` (reads `value.__meta.source` — the cache-source tag set by the oRPC server handler so consumers can tell whether a response came from cache, KV, or upstream), and `getGitHubCacheStatus(value: unknown): string | null` (reads `value.__meta.cacheStatus` — the cache hit/miss status returned alongside the data).
nodes.languageNotes: The `__meta` convention is set by the oRPC server when it returns GitHub data — every GitHub response has a `__meta` field with `source` and `cacheStatus`. Consumers use these helpers to render the 'cached' badge, the 'stale-while-revalidate' indicator, or the 'rate-limited, showing cached' fallback. Both helpers are defensive: they check `__meta` exists and is an object before reading nested properties, returning null on any unexpected shape.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/repo-clone-protocol-storage.ts
nodes.summary: LocalStorage-backed clone-protocol preference hook. `useRepoCloneProtocol()` returns `[protocol, setProtocol]` where protocol is `'cli' | 'https' | 'ssh'`. Initializes from `localStorage.getItem('portfolio-v2:github-clone-protocol')` (default 'https' for SSR or missing/invalid stored value). `updateProtocol(value: string)` validates (only 'cli' | 'https' | 'ssh' are accepted; anything else normalizes to 'https') and writes to localStorage on the client.
nodes.languageNotes: The lazy `useState<...>(() => ...)` initializer is what makes the localStorage read happen only on the client (and once per mount, not on every render). The `value: string` parameter is intentionally loose — the call site can pass any string from a UI element, and the function normalizes the bad cases to 'https'. No 'use client' directive at the top, but the hook is safe to use in client components only (the typeof window checks prevent SSR crashes).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/repo-list-utils.ts
nodes.summary: Pure functions for client-side repo-list pagination + nuqs URL-state parser. Exports `parseRepoListPage(page: string | null): number` (parses a URL page param, returns 1 for null/invalid/non-positive), `getRepoListPageCount(totalItems: number): number` (Math.max(1, ceil(totalItems / 12))), `clampRepoListPage(page, totalItems): number` (clamps page into [1, pageCount]), `sliceReposForPage<TItem>(repos, page): TItem[]` (slices the array by page, 12 per page), `repoListHasNextPage(page, totalItems): boolean` (page < pageCount), `githubRepoListPageSize = 12` (the named re-export of the PAGE_SIZE constant), `REPO_LIST_PAGE_SIZE = 30` (a second, larger page size used by the github-repos hub), `repoListPageQueryParser = parseAsInteger.withDefault(1).withOptions({ history: 'push' })` (the nuqs URL-state parser for the ?page= param), `maxRepoListPage(itemCount): number` (Math.max(1, ceil(itemCount / 30))), and `safeRepoListPage(page, itemCount): number` (clamps to [1, maxRepoListPage]).
nodes.languageNotes: Two page-size regimes coexist: the 12-item size is the legacy / repos-list pagination, the 30-item size is the github-repos hub pagination (the more recent design). The `as const` is implicit (the consts are typed as their literal values). `history: 'push'` on the nuqs parser means each page change pushes a new history entry (browser back navigates by page) rather than replacing in place.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/route-preload.ts
nodes.summary: Single-flight + dedupe wrapper around TanStack Router's `router.preloadRoute({ to })`. Module-scoped `completedRoutePreloads: Set<string>` (every successfully-preloaded 'to' value) and `inFlightRoutePreloads: Map<string, Promise<unknown>>` (in-flight preload tasks, deduped by 'to'). `preloadRouteOnce(router, to)`: returns `Promise.resolve()` if `to` is in completed, returns the in-flight task if one exists, otherwise starts a new task that calls `router.preloadRoute({ to })`, adds `to` to completed on success, and removes the in-flight entry in finally.
nodes.languageNotes: Module-scoped state means the dedupe is process-global — two components calling preloadRouteOnce('/repos', router) at the same time share the same Promise. The `Promise<unknown>` is intentional: preloadRoute's return type varies by router version, and consumers don't read the result anyway.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/seo.ts
nodes.summary: Project-specific SEO helper that wraps @tsu-stack/seo's `generateTanStackStartSeo` with the appConfig-derived site identity. Module-scoped `site: TanStackStartSeoSite` (sourced from appConfig: applicationName, baseUrl, defaultDescription, defaultImages, defaultTitle, siteName, titleTemplate — titleTemplate is `%s | ${appConfig.site.shortName}`). Exports `generateAppSeo(options: Omit<GenerateTanStackStartSeoParams, 'site'>)` that returns `generateTanStackStartSeo({ ...options, site })`.
nodes.languageNotes: Every route's head() calls generateAppSeo (with the route-specific title, description, robots, canonicalPath) — the helper is the single point where the appConfig-derived site identity is injected. The Omit<> strips 'site' from the consumer's call shape so they can't accidentally override the app-wide site identity. titleTemplate is the only brand-string format that's route-specific (the shortName suffix).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/tab-store.ts
nodes.summary: LocalStorage-backed tab store for the diffkit-style file-tab bar (one tab per opened PR/issue/review/repo/commit). `Tab` shape: `{ id, type: TabType ('pull' | 'issue' | 'review' | 'repo' | 'commit' | 'actions'), title, number?, url, repo, iconColor, avatarUrl?, additions?, deletions?, merged? }`. `TABS_STORAGE_KEY = 'diffkit:tabs'`. Module-scoped `let tabs: Tab[] = readStoredTabs()`. Type guards `isValidTabType` + `isValidTab` validate the parsed JSON shape; invalid stored data is silently removed. Exports `readStoredTabs(): Tab[]` (server-safe — returns [] on no window), `addTab(tab)` (updates if exists with any field change, else appends), `removeTab(id)`, `removeOtherTabs(id)` (filters to just that id), `removeTabsToRight(id)` (slices to keep only the tab and earlier), `isMergedTab(t)`, `removeMergedTabs()`, `reorderTabs(newOrder)`, and `useTabs()` (useSyncExternalStore with the tabs array as snapshot, empty array as the server snapshot).
nodes.languageNotes: The `satisfies Record<TabType, true>` on VALID_TAB_TYPES is what makes the type-guard exhaustive — adding a new TabType forces an update to the validator. `isMergedTab` is a derived helper (checks the merged flag OR the iconColor=='text-purple-500' for pull/review tabs). The server snapshot is a frozen `emptyTabs: Tab[]` constant so the reference is stable across renders — important for useSyncExternalStore to not trigger spurious updates on hydration.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/use-debounced-value.ts
nodes.summary: Generic debounced-value hook. `useDebouncedValue<T>(value: T, delayMs: number): [T, React.Dispatch<React.SetStateAction<T>>]` — returns the current debounced value (initialized to value, not undefined) + a setter that immediately updates the debounced value. Uses setTimeout in a useEffect with `value` and `delayMs` as deps; the cleanup clearTimeout is what makes the debounce work on rapid value changes.
nodes.languageNotes: The return tuple is `[T, Dispatch<SetStateAction<T>>]` — the second element is a real React setter (not a debounced setter), so consumers can call `setDebounced(next)` to bypass the debounce. The deps include delayMs but delayMs is typically a stable literal — including it is the right call for correctness but in practice it never re-fires.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/use-github-signal-stream.ts
nodes.summary: The GitHub signal-stream hook — opens a WebSocket subscription to the server's `/api/ws/github-signals` endpoint and a polling fallback (every 20s) for the same signal keys, then invalidates the relevant TanStack Query caches when a signal fires. `useGitHubSignalStream(targets: readonly GitHubSignalStreamTarget[])` merges the targets with `mergeTargetsWithMyGitHubLists` (which derives the user scope from the first target's queryKey and appends the standard pulls-mine + issues-mine targets), computes the deduped sorted `signalKeysKey`, the deduped `mergedTargetsIdentity` (used to reset the lastSeenTimestampsRef on change), opens a WebSocket via `useGitHubSignalStreamWebSocket` (reconnect on close with 3s delay, message handler parses the { type: 'signals', keys: string[] } payload, calls `invalidateTargets` to invalidate matching queryKeys, listens to visibilitychange + focus + online to trigger a one-shot catch-up via `orpcClient.github.getRevalidationSignals`), and runs `useGitHubSignalPoll` as a fallback (only enabled when the WebSocket is 'disconnected'). Helpers: `getGitHubDataFetchedAt` (reads `__meta.fetchedAt` from query data), `getGitHubSignalComparisonTimestamp` (prefers the data's fetchedAt over the query's dataUpdatedAt), `invalidateTargets` (skips queries with no data, no-data, or already-fetching state), `collectKeysToInvalidateAfterServerSync` (delta-tracks the server's `signals[].updatedAt` per (queryKey, signalKey) composite key in lastSeenTimestampsRef, returns only the keys that are strictly newer than the last seen). The WebSocket URL is built from `ENV_WEB_ISOMORPHIC.VITE_SERVER_URL` (swapping https→wss, http→ws, joining with /api/ws/github-signals).
nodes.languageNotes: The three-tier invalidation logic (WebSocket primary, poll fallback, visibility/focus/online catch-up) handles all the corner cases: WebSocket drops → poll takes over; WebSocket reconnects but a signal was missed during the gap → catch-up reconciles via the server's `getRevalidationSignals` REST call. The lastSeenTimestampsRef Map<compositeKey, number> is the per-(queryKey, signalKey) delta tracker — it's reset whenever the signalKeysKey or mergedTargetsIdentity changes. `mergeTargetsWithMyGitHubLists` auto-derives the userId scope from the first target's queryKey (`key[0] === 'github' && typeof key[1] === 'string'`) and adds the standard pulls-mine + issues-mine signal targets — every page that uses the hook gets the standard my-lists invalidation for free. The `// oxlint-disable-next-line react-hooks-js/set-state-in-effect` comments mark the early-return setState calls that the linter's strict mode would flag but are correct here (setStatus on initial mount and on no-WebSocket environment).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/use-global-shortcuts.ts
nodes.summary: Hook that registers global keyboard shortcuts (single-key or 2-step chord) on the window. `useGlobalShortcuts(shortcuts: ShortcutDefinition[])` — `ShortcutDefinition = { shortcut: ShortcutStep | ShortcutStep[], enabled?, allowInEditable?, preventDefault?, stopPropagation?, onTrigger }`, `ShortcutStep = { key?, code?, alt?, ctrl?, meta?, mod?, shift? }` (mod=true means meta or ctrl; mod=false means neither). The keydown handler (wrapped in useEffectEvent for stable reference): skips shortcuts with `enabled === false` or fired in an editable target unless `allowInEditable`; first checks single-step shortcuts; if none matches, accumulates the key into a 800ms-timeout'd sequence and checks for matching multi-step chords; if a chord prefix matches, stores the sequence and waits for the next key; otherwise resets. Cleans up the keydown listener + clears the sequence timer on unmount.
nodes.languageNotes: useEffectEvent (React 19) is what makes the keydown handler referentially stable without re-subscribing on every render — the handler reads the current shortcuts closure via the effectEvent wrapper, so the listener registration in useEffect can have an empty dep array. The 800ms sequence timeout (SEQUENCE_TIMEOUT_MS) is the standard vim/linear chord window. The mod/missing-mod branches: if mod is specified, the shortcut fires on meta OR ctrl; if mod is omitted, both meta and ctrl must explicitly match.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/use-has-mounted.ts
nodes.summary: Tiny mount-detection hook. `useHasMounted()` returns a boolean that flips to true on the first useEffect (initial render = false, post-mount = true). Used as an SSR guard around client-only side effects (e.g. gating useGitHubSignalStream, useIntersection, useFiles). The `// oxlint-disable-next-line react-hooks-js/set-state-in-effect` comment silences the strict-mode lint that would flag the setState-in-effect pattern.
nodes.languageNotes: The setState-in-effect is the canonical SSR pattern: initial render (SSR) returns false, client hydration returns false, then the useEffect fires and sets it to true. The whole 'is this on the client yet?' question is answered by this single hook — no window checks in every consumer.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/use-media-query.ts
nodes.summary: Tiny useMediaQuery hook. `useMediaQuery(query: string): boolean` — initial value is false (SSR safe), useEffect creates a MediaQueryList from `window.matchMedia(query)`, sets the initial value from `mq.matches`, subscribes to 'change' (calls setMatches on each change), and removes the listener on cleanup. Re-subscribes when `query` changes.
nodes.languageNotes: The `// oxlint-disable-next-line react-hooks-js/set-state-in-effect` comment is the same setState-in-effect suppression used in use-has-mounted. Initial value of false means the SSR render and the first client render always agree (no hydration mismatch) — the actual matchMedia check happens after mount.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/use-refresh-on-return.ts
nodes.summary: Hook that refreshes the GitHub installation-access cache + invalidates all GitHub queries + the router when the tab becomes visible again after being hidden (the 'user returned from the GitHub install page' use case). `useRefreshOnReturn({ enabled = true } = {})` returns a `refresh` callback (useCallback wrapping `orpcClient.github.refreshInstallationAccess()` + `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: githubQueryKeys.all })` + `router.invalidate()`). A useEffect attaches a visibilitychange listener that flips wasHiddenRef on hidden→visible transitions and calls refresh. The early-return on `!enabled` makes the hook a no-op in contexts that don't need the auto-refresh.
nodes.languageNotes: The wasHiddenRef pattern (only refresh on a real hidden→visible transition, not on every visibilitychange to visible) prevents duplicate work — if the user clicks the GitHub link, the tab hides, the user grants access, comes back, the tab shows, and the refresh fires exactly once. The `finally` block in refresh ensures the invalidation runs even if the oRPC call throws (so the user sees at least the local refresh).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/use-register-github-public-tab.ts
nodes.summary: Hook that registers (or refreshes) a tab in the diffkit tab-bar for a public GitHub page (repo/PR/issue/review). `useRegisterGithubPublicTab(tab)` — `tab` is either null (no-op) or `{ tabId?, iconColor? } & Omit<Tab, 'id' | 'iconColor'> & { type: TabType }`. A useEffect (deps: [tab]) calls `addTab` with `id = tab.tabId ?? \`${tab.type}:${tab.repo}\``, `iconColor = tab.iconColor ?? TAB_ICON_COLORS[tab.type] ?? 'text-muted-foreground'`. `TAB_ICON_COLORS` provides default colors per TabType: repo=blue, pull/issue=green.
nodes.languageNotes: The deps include `tab` (the object reference), which means a new object on every parent render triggers the effect. For consumers that pass a stable object, the effect runs only when the underlying tab actually changes (because addTab's idempotency check returns early when nothing changed). The id convention `\`${type}:${repo}\`` makes the tab stable across navigations that re-derive the same object.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/warning-store.ts
nodes.summary: Module-scoped external store for non-blocking warnings (the diffkit-style 'you need to configure access' toast). Types: `WarningAction = { kind: 'link', label, href } | { kind: 'github-access', label, href?, owner?, repo? }`, `WarningSeverity = 'warning' | 'error'`, `Warning = { id, message, severity?, dismissible?, action? }`. Exports `addWarning(warning)` (no-op if id is already in the list — idempotent), `removeWarning(id)`, `useWarnings()` (useSyncExternalStore with the warnings array as snapshot), `surfaceForbiddenOrgWarnings(orgs)` (one warning per org, id `forbidden-org:${org}`, kind: 'github-access' → 'Configure access'), `surfaceTimeoutWarning(timedOut)` (adds/removes the `github-api-timeout` error-severity warning), and `checkPermissionWarning(result, repo)` (parses the result.error string for 'Insufficient permissions' or 'OAuth App access restrictions' and surfaces a permission warning for the repo with a 'Configure access' action).
nodes.languageNotes: Three surfacing helpers exist to keep the warning-store API focused (just add/remove/useWarnings) while letting feature code declare their warnings with one line: surfaceForbiddenOrgWarnings(orgs) for the GitHub user-forbidden-org list, surfaceTimeoutWarning(timedOut) for the /api/ws/github-signals timeout flag, checkPermissionWarning(result, repo) for the per-repo oRPC response. The `fallow-ignore-next-line unused-export` markers identify the surfacing helpers as deliberately-tolerant unused exports (they're called from feature code that may not always be loaded).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/lib/zod-form-validator.ts
nodes.summary: Adapter that turns a Zod schema into a TanStack Form onChange validator. `createZodFormValidator<T extends z.ZodTypeAny>(schema: T): ({ value }) => { fields: Record<string, Array<{ message: string }>> } | undefined` — returns undefined on success, or a `{ fields: { [path0]: [{ message }] } }` object on failure where path0 is the first segment of the issue's path. The adapter shape matches TanStack Form's `onChange` validator contract.
nodes.languageNotes: The flat-fields shape (one error per first-path-segment, not the full nested path) matches what the field bindings expect from the `state.fieldMeta[fieldName].errors` shape — a single field with the same name gets an array of {message}s, which the FieldError primitive renders as a list.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/providers/intersection.provider.jsx
nodes.summary: Tiny IntersectionObserver-state React context (the only .jsx file in this batch — JS, not TS, to keep the surface zero-deps). Creates `IntersectionContext` via `createContext()`, exports `IntersectionProvider({ children })` (holds two state slices: `sectionIntersectedName: string` defaulting to '#about' and `isIntersecting: boolean` defaulting to false) and `useIntersection()` (returns `useContext(IntersectionContext)` — typed as the implicit any since it's JS).
nodes.languageNotes: The state is held in the provider (so any descendant can update the active section), not in a hook — the project pattern for the right-rail in-page jump nav (HomeNav in pages/home-page) to highlight the active section. The .jsx extension is deliberate to keep this file dependency-free (no tsconfig, no types) — it's a primitive that anything can import.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/providers/logger.provider.tsx
nodes.summary: Logger context provider that bridges the Better Auth session to the @tsu-stack/logger client identity. `LoggerProvider({ children })` is a client component: it reads `useAuth()`, and inside a useEffect, calls `setIdentity({ user: { id: user.id } })` when authenticated or `setIdentity({ user: { id: 'anonymous' } })` when not, with a cleanup that calls `clearIdentity()` on unmount or user change. The provider value is `{ logger: log }` from @tsu-stack/logger/client. `useLogger()` is the consumer hook — it reads the context, falls back to the raw `log` singleton (with a `log.warn('logger-provider', 'Called outside of LoggerProvider')` warning) when the context is null, and returns the typed `log` function. The shape `LoggerContextValue = { logger: typeof log }` keeps the surface tightly typed to the logger's exported API.
nodes.languageNotes: The 'called outside of provider' fallback returns the singleton (not throws) so hooks can be safely used in shared utilities without forcing every consumer to be wrapped — the warn() call surfaces misuses in development without breaking production. `typeof log` is the pattern for keeping the consumer's type in lockstep with the upstream logger API; if the logger adds a method, it propagates here automatically. The cleanup-then-setIdentity pattern is important: re-running the effect on user change clears the prior identity before the new one is set, so the logger's internal user-bound state never gets stale entries from a previous session.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/providers/progress.provider.tsx
nodes.summary: Wraps @bprogress/react to bind the top-of-page progress bar to TanStack Router navigation. `PROGRESS_DELAY_MS = 175` is the threshold before showing the bar (so fast navigations don't flash it). `ProgressBarSubscriber` is a renderless component: inside a useEffect it subscribes to two router events — `onBeforeLoad` (only when `pathChanged`) arms a setTimeout that calls `start()` if the router is still loading after 175ms, and `onResolved` cancels the timeout and calls `stop()`. The timeout + an `isNavigatingRef` guard ensure the bar only shows for genuinely slow navigations. Cleanup unsubscribes both, clears the timeout, and calls stop(). `ProgressProvider({ children })` is the public wrapper — it renders `<RawProgressProvider color='var(--color-primary)' options={{ showSpinner: false }}>` with the subscriber mounted as a child, and accepts standard ReactNode children.
nodes.languageNotes: The 175ms delay is the magic number — it absorbs SPA navigations (where the new route's loader is essentially cached) and only shows the bar when there's actual loading. The isNavigatingRef + the `router.state.isLoading` check inside the setTimeout together prevent the bar from sticking on if the navigation finished between when the timer was armed and when it fired. `onBeforeLoad` (rather than onLoad) is the right hook because by the time onLoad fires the navigation is already done. The two refs (timeoutRef + isNavigatingRef) form a small state machine inside the effect closure — using refs rather than state avoids the effect re-firing on every state change.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/providers/query-client.provider.tsx
nodes.summary: The TanStack QueryClient factory + persistence layer for the web app. The persistence subsystem selectively dehydrates GitHub queries to localStorage and rehydrates them on next page load, with two persist modes — `true` (always save) and `'tab'` (save only while the underlying tab is open). Constants: `GITHUB_QUERY_CACHE_STORAGE_KEY = 'diffkit:github-query-cache:v1'`, `GITHUB_QUERY_CACHE_MAX_AGE_MS = githubCachePolicy.viewer.gcTimeMs` (so the localStorage copy is at most as fresh as the in-memory gc). Types: `PersistedGitHubQueryCache = { version: 1; persistedAt: number; clientState: unknown }`, `PersistBehavior = true | 'tab'`, `PersistableGitHubQuery = { state: { data?, status }; meta?; queryKey: readonly unknown[] }`. Six type-guard helpers (`isPullQueryKeyInput`, `isIssueQueryKeyInput`, `isRepoQueryKeyInput`, `isRepoCommitQueryKeyInput`) validate the input shape of each query's queryKey[4] entry. `matchesTabQuery(queryKey, tab)` decides whether a given GitHub query belongs to a given Tab (PR review/detail/comments/status, review workspace except `files` patches — explicitly excluded with a comment about localStorage quota + 3k-file PRs, reviewThreads, fileSummaries), commit tabs (matched by SHA via `tab.url.match(/\/commit\/([0-9a-f]+)/i)`), repo overview, or issue page/detail/comments. `shouldPersistGitHubQuery(query)` gates persistence on `state.status === 'success'`, `queryKey[0] === 'github'`, `state.data != null`, and the meta.persist flag. `pruneClosedTabQueries(queryClient, tabs)` removes `persist: 'tab'` queries whose tab has been closed. `pruneNullGitHubQueries(queryClient)` removes any GitHub query whose data is null. `usePruneClosedTabQueries(queryClient)` is a hook that watches `useTabs()` and re-runs prune on tab change. `restorePersistedGitHubQueryCache(queryClient)` reads localStorage on mount, rejects expired or wrong-version entries, calls `hydrate(queryClient, persistedState.clientState)`, and prunes nulls. `persistGitHubQueryCache(queryClient)` subscribes to `queryClient.getQueryCache()`, debounces writes by 250ms, and adds a `beforeunload` handler to flush synchronously. `GitHubQueryPersistence({ queryClient })` is the renderless component that mounts the effect. `createAppQueryClient()` constructs the QueryClient with `retry: 1`, `networkMode: 'online'`, and immediately runs the restore pass. `AppQueryClientProvider({ children, queryClient })` is the public wrapper — `<QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}><GitHubQueryPersistence queryClient={queryClient} />{children}</QueryClientProvider>`.
nodes.languageNotes: The exclude-patches comment is the key design note: review-workspace persistence deliberately skips the `files` resourceName because dehydrating a 3k-file patch into localStorage would blow the quota and cost serialization time on every cache write. The commit-tab SHA extraction via regex on tab.url is the workaround for commits not having a `number` field like PRs/issues do. `usePruneClosedTabQueries` uses a tabsRef to skip the effect on the first render (when tabs are first read from localStorage and may equal the prior ref value) — the effect only fires on actual change. The 250ms debounce + beforeunload flush together give 'save on quit' semantics without paying a write cost on every cache mutation. `retry: 1` is a conservative default for the SSR client; pair with networkMode: 'online' so failed queries don't retry in a flaky network while the tab is being rehydrated. The `as PersistBehavior | undefined` cast on `query.meta?.persist` is necessary because the meta type is `Record<string, unknown>` and we want to type-narrow only when the value is one of the two literals.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/check-state-icon.tsx
nodes.summary: Visual + classifier for CI check run states (GitHub Actions `status` + `conclusion` fields). `type CheckState = 'success' | 'failure' | 'pending' | 'waiting' | 'skipped' | 'expected'`. `getCheckStateColor(state)` returns a Tailwind text class — green-500, red-500, yellow-500, or muted-foreground. `getCheckState({ status, conclusion })` maps a GitHub check run payload to a CheckState: 'expected' if status is 'expected', 'waiting' for queued/waiting/pending status, 'pending' for non-completed or null-conclusion, 'success' for success/neutral, 'skipped' for skipped/stale, 'failure' otherwise. `CheckStateIcon({ state })` renders a 3.5x3.5 wrapper with the appropriate icon — green check (success), red X (failure), small bordered dot (skipped), hollow ring SVG (waiting), filled yellow dot (expected), animated yellow spinner (pending).
nodes.languageNotes: The 'expected' state is a special-case for GitHub's 'expected' status (used for required-but-not-yet-run checks) — it gets its own visual treatment so required-but-pending isn't confused with optional-and-pending. The pending state uses an inline SVG spinner rather than the lucide Loader spinner to keep the size and strokeWidth tightly controlled (3.5x3.5, strokeWidth=2). Note that the 'pending' SVG has opacity=0.25 on the base ring vs opacity=0.35 for the 'waiting' ring — the visual distinction is subtle but tells the user that the check hasn't even started yet vs it's queued.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/contact-button.tsx
nodes.summary: Single 9x9 anchor button for a portfolio contact entry. `ContactButton({ contact, propsIcon })` — `contact: ContactOutput` (from @tsu-stack/core) provides `value` (the href), `icon` (the icon name resolved via the @/shared/ui/icon bridge), and `type` (used as the aria-label). Renders an `<a>` with `target='_blank'`, `rel='noopener noreferrer'`, the standard hover-accent transition, and the Icon component as its child. `propsIcon?: IconBaseProps` is forwarded to the Icon component for size/colour overrides.
nodes.languageNotes: Renders as an `<a>` not a `<button>` because contact links are navigation, not form submission. `aria-label={contact.type}` is the canonical screen-reader-only label (e.g. 'github', 'email') — visible-tooltip labels are not present so the label is the only identifier. The 9x9 aspect-square + flex centering is the consistent icon-button size used in the public sidebar.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/container.tsx
nodes.summary: Single-line re-export of `Container` from @tsu-stack/ui/components/container. The local file exists so that app-level imports can use the `@/shared/ui/container` alias (consistent with the shared/ui barrel pattern) without depending directly on the cross-package ui path.
nodes.languageNotes: No local logic — the re-export is the file's entire purpose. This pattern lets the apps/web/src/shared/ui/* surface have a consistent internal-import path while delegating the actual implementation to packages/ui.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/default-loader.tsx
nodes.summary: Wrapper that picks the right size/proportions for the @tsu-stack/ui DotmSquare18 loader. `DefaultLoader({ className })` renders `<DotmSquare18 className={cn('min-w-full py-16', className)} size={28} dotSize={4} speed={1.2} />`. The `min-w-full py-16` base classes give the loader a full-width strip with vertical breathing room — typically used as a centered loading state for full-page sections.
nodes.languageNotes: The size=28 / dotSize=4 / speed=1.2 triple is the page-level preset — smaller variants live in the ui package for inline use. `cn()` is the @tsu-stack/ui utils shim for clsx + tailwind-merge, used here to let callers append additional classes without the typical clsx + tailwind-merge ceremony.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/error-layout.tsx
nodes.summary: Full-viewport min-h-screen flex column with a center-aligned main grid. `ErrorLayout({ children })` renders a `<div className='flex min-h-screen flex-col'>` with a `<main className='relative -top-(--navbar-height) grid flex-1 place-items-center pt-(--navbar-height)'>` inside. The `-top-(--navbar-height)` + `pt-(--navbar-height)` combo visually centers the content under the navbar (pulls it up by the navbar height and re-pads the same amount so the layout doesn't shift). Used as the wrapper for error boundaries (404, 500, etc.).
nodes.languageNotes: The CSS variable trick (`--navbar-height`) is the project's pattern for nav-height-aware layouts — the variable is set in the global stylesheet to the actual navbar height, so layouts can reference it without hardcoding pixels. `-top-` + `pt-` of the same value is the centering-under-fixed-navbar idiom: it visually pulls the main area up by the navbar height (so the visible content starts where the main scroll area would start), and the matching `pt-` keeps the document flow correct so the page is still scrollable. `grid place-items-center` is the cleanest way to center a single child both axes.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/file-search-card.tsx
nodes.summary: Command-palette-style fuzzy file search card. `FileSearchCard({ activePath, defaultEntries, entries, onSelect, placeholder='Search files...', shortcutKey='f' })` is a memoized component (use React.memo). State: `query` (controlled input), `deferredQuery` (useDeferredValue for non-blocking search), `focused` (input focus), `activeIndex` (currently-highlighted result). The card has a compact collapsed state (icon + input + kbd hint) and an expanded state (with the result list sliding down). `isExpanded = focused || query.length > 0`; `hasResults = deferredQuery.trim().length > 0`. Search: `searchResults = useMemo(() => searchFiles(deferredQuery, entries), ...)`; when no query, `computedDefaults` shows up to 5 file-type entries from `defaultEntries ?? entries.filter(type === 'file').slice(0,5)`, each with score=0. Keyboard: ArrowUp/ArrowDown cycles the active index (wraps around), Enter triggers `handleSelect(visibleResults[activeIndex])`, Escape blurs and clears. Click-outside: a `pointerdown` document listener collapses the card when the click is outside `cardRef`. Global shortcut: pressing `/` or the configured `shortcutKey` (default 'f') focuses the input — but only when no INPUT/TEXTAREA is focused and no modifier is held. Animation: shared-layout `motion.span` on the search icon (layoutId='sidebar-search-icon') animates the icon between collapsed and expanded positions. The result list uses motion's height-auto animation, and each result is rendered as a `SearchResultRow` (also memoized) that shows the file/folder icon, the name (with query-highlighted spans), the parent dir (if any), an `isHighlighted` background, and an `activePath` background when the result is the current path. `HighlightedText` splits the text into runs of matched/unmatched characters and wraps the matched runs in a `text-foreground` span for visual highlight (consumes the `indices: Set<number>` from fuzzy-file-search's `getMatchIndices`). When the result list is empty AND there's a query, the empty state shows 'No files found'.
nodes.languageNotes: `useDeferredValue` is the key for keeping typing snappy while the search runs on the deferred (slightly-stale) value — this lets React flush the keystroke to the input immediately and search in the background. The `setState in effect` warning (line 96) is suppressed with `oxlint-disable-next-line react-hooks-js/set-state-in-effect` because resetting `activeIndex` to 0 on every new query is the intended UX (don't carry the highlight from the previous query's result). The shortcut-key effect's two listeners (pointerdown for click-outside, keydown for shortcut) are both gated on `isExpanded` to avoid registering global listeners when the card is fully collapsed. The `motion.span` with `layoutId='sidebar-search-icon'` participates in a shared layout — when the card transitions between collapsed and expanded, the icon slides smoothly between the two positions rather than fading in/out. `aria-busy` is not used here (this isn't a loading state — it has data); the card uses `aria-live='polite'` indirectly via the result rows being focusable. The defaultEntries prop with score=0 trick lets the parent pass pre-scored entries (e.g. recent files) without going through `searchFiles` for the empty-query state.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/form-dirty-guard.tsx
nodes.summary: Hook that gates a form's close action behind an unsaved-changes confirmation dialog. `useFormDirtyGuard(form: AnyFormApi, onClose?: () => void)` — reads `form.store` with `useSelector` for the boolean `state.isDirty && state.isTouched`, mirrors it into an `isDirtyRef` via useEffect, and exposes `handleCloseAttempt` (open the dialog if dirty, else call onClose) and `confirmClose` (close the dialog and call onClose). Returns `{ alertDialog, handleCloseAttempt }` — `alertDialog` is the full Radix AlertDialog JSX (sr-only-friendly with explicit Cancel/Discard actions) that the consumer mounts once at the bottom of the form. Tracks the showAlert boolean in local useState.
nodes.languageNotes: The `isDirty && isTouched` check is the project's 'real dirtiness' definition — `isTouched` means the user has actually interacted with the form, so a freshly-opened form with prefilled values doesn't trigger the dialog. The `isDirtyRef` mirror is critical: useCallback's `handleCloseAttempt` needs to read the latest dirty value, but if it depended on `isDirty` directly the callback identity would change on every keystroke (and the consumer's `onClick={handleCloseAttempt}` would re-render). The ref+effect pattern is the standard 'latest-value-in-stable-callback' trick. `as const` on the return value preserves the tuple/object type and the readonly modifier on the return type. `AnyFormApi` accepts any TanStack form instance so the same hook works across every form in the app.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/header-actions.tsx
nodes.summary: Tri-mode page header actions — single add button, sort edit mode, or multi-select batch actions. `HeaderActions({ add, batch, sort })` renders one of three layouts based on the props: (1) when `sort.isSort` is true, shows a Group with Save / Restore default / Cancel buttons; (2) when `batch.selectedCount > 0`, shows a Group with a destructive Delete (with the count) and an optional Add-to-portfolio, plus a 'Select all (N)' or 'Deselect all' button; (3) otherwise shows the optional Reorder (sort start) button and the Add button. Loading states are surfaced via Button's `loading` prop (Delete, Add-to-portfolio, Save). Uses lucide icons (ArrowUpDown, BookmarkPlus, Check, Plus, RotateCcw, Trash2, X) and the @tsu-stack/ui Group/GroupSeparator primitive for the split-button look.
nodes.languageNotes: The tri-mode branching uses `sort.isSort` first (highest priority — sort mode overrides everything), then `batch && batch.selectedCount > 0` (batch mode suppresses the add/sort buttons to avoid accidental action), and the default state shows the standard add/sort entry-points. The 'Select all' → 'Deselect all' toggle is a small UX choice: when every item is selected the button flips to 'Deselect all' so the user can clear without the Cmd+A dance. `GroupSeparator` (from @tsu-stack/ui) is the visual divider in a split button group — it's not a `<hr>`, it's a styled separator that respects the group's border radius. `Group` itself is a `role='group'` div for accessibility. `sort: { isSortPending }` is a separate flag from the regular `loading` because the save mutation has its own pending state that may be unrelated to the regular add mutation.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/icon-picker.tsx
nodes.summary: Virtualized category-aware icon picker backed by the icons-data.ts catalogue. `IconPicker` is a React.forwardRef wrapping a Popover trigger. Props: `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `open/defaultOpen/onOpenChange`, `searchable=true`, `searchPlaceholder='Search for an icon...'`, `triggerPlaceholder='Select an icon'`, `iconsList` (override), `categorized=true`, `modal=false`. Internally: `useIconsData()` lazy-loads the 4896-line iconsData via dynamic `import('./icons-data')` (the dynamic import is the key — without it, every page that renders the picker would pay the full icon catalogue cost in the initial bundle). `useDebouncedValue('', 100)` debounces the search input. Fuse.js (threshold 0.3, ignoreLocation, includeScore) is the fuzzy search — keys are `name`, `tags`, `categories`. `categorizedIcons` groups by category (Map keyed by category name; uncategorized land in 'Other'), sorted alphabetically by name. `virtualItems` flattens the categories into a single array of `{ type: 'category' | 'row', ... }` items so @tanstack/react-virtual can virtualize across them. `categoryIndices` is a Record<categoryName, virtualItemIndex> for the click-to-jump buttons. `useVirtualizer` with estimateSize 25 (category headers) / 40 (rows), gap 10, overscan 5. Renders a tooltip-wrapped button per icon. A 240px rootMargin IntersectionObserver would be more efficient but this version uses a simple parentRef-based scroller. A ResizeObserver on parentRef re-measures the virtualizer when the popover first opens. `renderVirtualContent()` produces the absolutely-positioned translated virtualItems. Skeleton: `IconsColumnSkeleton` shows 40 skeleton tiles for the loading state. `handleOpenChange` resets the search and runs the virtualizer measure on next tick (setTimeout 1ms — inside the popover open animation frame). `handleIconClick` updates value + closes the popover. `scrollToCategory` jumps to a category header by index. `useEffect` on `isPopoverVisible` re-measures the virtualizer (the parentRef is null until the popover mounts, so the first measure happens post-open).
nodes.languageNotes: The dynamic `import('./icons-data')` is the single most important perf decision in this file — iconsData is 4896 lines (~80KB) and the picker is rarely used on every page. The hook's `isMounted` guard prevents setIcons after unmount during the import resolution. The `virtualItems` flattening (category headers + 5-icon rows interleaved) is what lets the virtualizer treat them as one scrollable list. `categoryIndices` is computed by iterating `virtualItems` and recording the index whenever a 'category' item is found, then the popover's category-jump buttons call `virtualizer.scrollToIndex(categoryIndices[name], { align: 'start', behavior: 'smooth' })`. The `useIconsData` + dynamic import is decoupled from the props.iconsList override — if the caller passes iconsList, the picker uses it directly and skips the dynamic load (useful for testing with a tiny fixture). The `setTimeout(..., 1)` in handleOpenChange is the standard 'wait one frame for the popover's open animation to start, then measure' trick. `IconsColumnSkeleton` uses 40 fixed-size tiles because at width 256px (w-64 popover) and grid-cols-5, 8 rows = 40 icons is a reasonable full-page skeleton. `displayName = 'IconPicker'` is set on the forwardRef for React DevTools.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/icon.tsx
nodes.summary: Lazy icon-component bridge from the project's 31 react-icons libraries to a name-keyed render. `Icon({ nameIcon, propsIcon })` uses useState to hold the resolved component, and a useEffect that calls `resolveIcon(nameIcon)` and stores the result. `resolveIcon(nameIcon)` derives the library prefix by `nameIcon.replace(/([a-z0-9])([A-Z])/g, '$1 $2').split(' ')[0].toLocaleLowerCase()` (e.g. 'FaHome' → 'fa', 'LiaHome' → 'lia', 'MdHome' → 'md'), then uses a module-scoped `iconComponentCache: Map<string, IconType>` keyed by `${lib}:${nameIcon}`. Cache miss triggers `allIconsPromise` (a module-scoped single-flight Promise) that `Promise.all([import('./icons/group-01'), ..., import('./icons/group-15')])`, then flattens each group's `iconLibraries` (a Record<lib, Record<name, IconType>>) into a single `Record<name, IconType>` map. The component returns `null` while the resolution is in flight (avoids a layout shift on first render). The vite.config.ts plugin `iconGroupsSSRStub()` stubs out the icon group imports in the SSR environment to keep the Worker bundle small (the picker's loadIcons is client-only).
nodes.languageNotes: The `allIconsPromise` module-scoped Promise is the single-flight pattern — concurrent calls share the same in-flight import (so two components that both render 'FaHome' on mount only trigger one set of 15 dynamic imports). The library prefix extraction by CamelCase split is necessary because react-icons exports 31+ libraries and each one is a separate npm import — the icon name carries the library as its prefix (Fa, Lia, Md, Hi, etc.). The `iconComponentCache: Map<string, IconType>` keys on `${lib}:${nameIcon}` rather than just `nameIcon` to handle the rare case where the same name exists in multiple libraries (e.g. a 'Home' icon in several sets). `useEffect` with the `cancelled` flag is the safe pattern for setting state on async resolution — when the component unmounts mid-fetch, the resolution result is discarded. Returning `null` while loading means there's no flash of the wrong icon — the consumer should reserve space (e.g. with a same-size skeleton or aspect-ratio container). The `as IconBaseProps` from `react-icons/lib` is the type the actual icon components accept (size, color, etc.).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/icons-data.ts
nodes.summary: Static catalogue of 921 react-icons icon names with their categories and search tags. Exports `iconsData: Array<{ name: string; categories: string[]; tags: string[] }>`. Each entry is a curated subset of the 31 react-icons libraries bundled by the icon.tsx dynamic-import system. Categories: 31 distinct values (accessibility, account, actions, animals, arrows, communication, connectivity, contact, design, dev, dev-stacks, emoji, files, finance, food, gaming, home, maps, media, medical, notifications, science, security, shapes, shopping, sports, stack, text, transportation, travel, ui, weather). Each icon typically belongs to 1-3 categories and has 2-6 search tags. The data is loaded on demand by icon-picker.tsx via `import('./icons-data')` (the dynamic import + the vite.config.ts iconGroupsSSRStub together keep the icon libraries out of the SSR bundle).
nodes.languageNotes: The categories are deliberately the consumer-facing groups (not the library prefixes) — so 'FaHome', 'FiHome', 'HiHome' are all under 'home' and the picker shows them as one bucket. The `tags` array is the fuzzy-search seed for Fuse.js in icon-picker.tsx — common synonyms (e.g. 'house' for 'home', 'shopping' for 'store') make the search more forgiving. The file is intentionally hand-curated rather than generated from the full react-icons metadata because: (1) the project only uses a subset, (2) categories map to product concepts not the upstream library's organization, and (3) the curated set stays small enough to keep the dynamic import cheap. The 4896-line size is the cost of 921 entries × ~5 lines each; the file is otherwise unremarkable.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/icons/group-01.ts
nodes.summary: Icon group file for the @/shared/ui/icon lazy-load system. Imports the two react-icons submodules react-icons/ai and react-icons/bi as namespace imports, then re-exports them as `export const iconLibraries: IconLibraries = { ai: ai as unknown as IconLibraries[string], bi: bi as unknown as IconLibraries[string] };`. Ant Icons (ai) + Bootstrap Icons (bi) — the foundational icon sets covering UI patterns (arrows, actions, media) and a few dev/social glyphs. Consumed by the `Promise.all([import('./icons/group-01'), ..., import('./icons/group-15')])` in @/shared/ui/icon — the vite.config.ts `iconGroupsSSRStub` plugin replaces these imports with empty stubs in the SSR environment to keep the Cloudflare Worker bundle under the per-module size limit.
nodes.languageNotes: The `as unknown as IconLibraries[string]` double-cast is needed because react-icons exports a flat Record<string, IconType> for each library but the IconLibraries[string] type expects that exact shape — the unknown hop is the only way to tell TypeScript the upstream type is structurally compatible (since react-icons' types haven't been published with the project's IconType import). The 2-library grouping is a Vite/Rollup dynamic-import chunking decision (each group becomes its own chunk so concurrent first-renders don't all pay the cost of the same set of files). In SSR the stub returns `export const iconLibraries = {};` so iconLibraries[name] is undefined and the icon resolver short-circuits.

nodes.summary: Icon group file for the @/shared/ui/icon lazy-load system. Imports the two react-icons submodules react-icons/fa and react-icons/fa6 as namespace imports, then re-exports them as `export const iconLibraries: IconLibraries = { fa: fa as unknown as IconLibraries[string], fa6: fa6 as unknown as IconLibraries[string] };`.
