nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/icons/types.ts
nodes.summary: Type aliases for the icon-bridge system. Re-exports `IconType` from `react-icons/lib` and declares `IconLibrary = Record<string, IconType>` and `IconLibraries = Record<string, IconLibrary>`. Consumed by the 15 group-*.ts files (the `iconLibraries: IconLibraries` cast) and transitively by @/shared/ui/icon.
nodes.languageNotes: The two-step `Record<string, IconType>` then `Record<string, IconLibrary>` shape mirrors the actual data: the outer map is library-name → icon-map, the inner map is icon-name → component. Re-exporting IconType from `react-icons/lib` (not `react-icons`) keeps the public surface tied to a single type-import path — `react-icons/lib` is the published type-only entrypoint that avoids pulling all 31 libraries into a consumer's type-check graph.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/image.tsx
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper around @tsu-stack/ui's Image component that injects the site + imgproxy base URLs from env. `Image(props: WrapperImageProps)` spreads the props onto the raw Image and adds `siteBaseUrl={ENV_WEB_ISOMORPHIC.VITE_WEB_URL}` and `imgProxyBaseUrl={ENV_WEB_ISOMORPHIC.VITE_IMGPROXY_URL}`. The wrapper exists so app-level imports use the local `@/shared/ui/image` path (consistent with the rest of the shared/ui surface) and so the two base URLs are set in one place rather than at every call site.
nodes.languageNotes: Spreading the env URLs at the wrapper layer rather than the call site means the imgproxy deployment is a single-point-of-change — if the URL ever rotates, only image.tsx needs to be updated. `WrapperImageProps` is the @tsu-stack/ui type that accepts the same shape as Image but allows the wrapper to add the two base URL fields. The wrapper does not add any additional behaviour (no lazy loading toggling, no fallback srcset) — it's a pure env-injection shim.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/list-item-action-buttons.tsx
nodes.summary: Polymorphic action button row for a list item: view / edit / toggle-portfolio / delete. `ListItemActionButtons({ view, edit, togglePortfolio, delete, classNames })` — each action is an optional ActionButtonConfig (`{ onAction, isLoading? }`) or TogglePortfolioConfig (`{ onAction, isLoading?, initialValue }`). `hasMenu = !!togglePortfolio || !!deleteConfig`; `menuLoading = togglePortfolio?.isLoading ?? deleteConfig?.isLoading`. The render branches on what was provided: (1) when both (view || edit) and hasMenu are true, the buttons go in a Group with a GroupSeparator before the menu; (2) when only view is provided, render a single icon-only 'View' button; (3) when only edit, single icon-only 'Edit' button; (4) menu-only, render the dropdown directly. The dropdown is a Menu/MenuTrigger/MenuPopup from @tsu-stack/ui with a Switch in the toggle-portfolio item (read-only Switch with checked={initialValue} + pointer-events-none) and a destructive-styled Delete item separated by MenuSeparator. All onClick handlers call `event.stopPropagation()` so clicks on the action buttons don't bubble up to the parent Card's onSelect.
nodes.languageNotes: The 'menuLoading = togglePortfolio?.isLoading ?? deleteConfig?.isLoading' precedence means toggle-portfolio's loading state wins when both are loading — important UX because the toggle is the more frequent action and shouldn't be blocked by a delete. The Switch in the toggle-portfolio item has `pointer-events-none` because the surrounding MenuItem is the actual click target (the Switch is purely visual — the user clicks 'In portfolio' text and the row's onClick fires). `event.stopPropagation()` is critical here: the ListItem wraps the whole row in a Card with `onClick={onSelect}` (to open the item), so without stopPropagation every action button would also trigger the row's open behaviour. The (view || edit) && hasMenu branch is the 'split button' pattern: the primary action is a regular Button and the secondary actions collapse into a dropdown — this is the design pattern from the 2026-07-04 design spec in docs/superpowers/specs.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/list-item.tsx
nodes.summary:
Generic list-item card wrapper for the dashboard pages (experiences, projects, stacks, etc.). `ListItem({ selected, onSelect, className, dragHandleProps, isSort=false, isBatchSelected, onToggleSelect, onMouseEnter, onView, onEdit, onDelete, isDeleting, onTogglePortfolio, isTogglingPortfolio, inPortfolio, deleteTitle, deleteDescription, children|title, ... })` — the props form a discriminated union: either `children: ReactNode` OR `title + titleStart + titleEnd + meta`. Internally: `bodyContent = children ?? ...

{title}

...{titleEnd} + {meta}`. Renders a Card with `role='button'`, `aria-pressed={selected}`, Enter/Space keyboard activation, the conditional onToggleSelect Checkbox, the conditional drag handle (GripVertical wrapped in a button), the bodyContent, and the ListItemActionButtons. The delete confirmation Dialog opens via `setDeleteDialogOpen(true)` when the action-button's delete is clicked. The `inPortfolio` indicator dot pulses (animate-pulse) — green for in-portfolio, red for not.
nodes.languageNotes: The `role='button'` on a Card is the project's pattern for making the whole card click-to-open — `oxlint-disable-next-line jsx-a11y/prefer-tag-over-role` is the standard acknowledgement (the alternative is wrapping the Card in a `<button>` which breaks the card's content layout). The prop union (`children | (title + meta)`) is the project pattern for letting the caller pick between 'I render my own body' and 'just give me a title and I'll render the default' — using a discriminated union rather than optional props prevents the caller from accidentally passing both. The inPortfolio dot indicator (green/red pulse) is the project's at-a-glance status badge for items that have been added to the user's portfolio — the colour switches based on inPortfolio, the pulse draws the eye to recent changes. The `data-selected={selected}` attribute is used by the parent ItemsList to style selected rows without an additional className round-trip. The drag handle (dragHandleProps from sortable-list.tsx) is mounted only when isSort is true — otherwise the slot collapses.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/logo.tsx
nodes.summary: Two brand-marks using the project's D-mono SVG path. `LogoIcon(props)` renders the raw SVG (378x387 viewBox, two path elements in #EC4E02 and #93370A forming the stylized 'D' mark) and forwards all SVG props plus a className. `LogoWordmark({ className, ...divProps })` renders the icon next to `appConfig.site.shortName` (from @/config/app.config) in a flex row — used in the topbar as the brand link. The wordmark is annotated `fallow-ignore-next-line unused-export` because in practice the topbar uses the @tsu-stack/ui TextAnimate on the username rather than the wordmark — the wordmark is kept exported for use on the public-facing portfolio page or for testing.
nodes.languageNotes: The two-colour scheme (#EC4E02 + #93370A) is the project's brand identity — the lighter orange is the primary, the darker shade is the shadow/depth layer. `fallow-ignore-next-line unused-export` is the project linter-suppression marker for intentionally-unused exports. The wordmark's top-0.5 nudge on the SVG (`relative top-0.5 size-8`) aligns the mark with the text baseline — a tiny but important detail for visual balance. The LogoIcon is used directly by the contact-button (via the @/shared/ui/icon bridge) and the LogoWordmark is the canonical full-brand wrapper.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/markdown.tsx
nodes.summary: Tailwind-styled react-markdown wrapper with shiki code highlighting and a content-asset URL resolver. `Markdown({ children, className, resolveAssetUrl })` provides a MarkdownAssetUrlResolverContext that child nodes can read via `useResolvedAssetUrl(url)` — the resolver is opt-in (returns the original url when no resolver is provided, or when the url is undefined). The `components` map (Record<string, React.FC<any>>) provides project-specific renderers for h1-h4, p, a (opens in new tab with rel=noopener), ul/ol/li, blockquote, code/pre (the `code` component extracts the language from the className and routes to ShikiCode), hr, img/video/source (the source handler resolves srcset entries individually), table/thead/th/td (with a wrapping div with rounded border), input[type=checkbox] (read-only), strong/em/del, and details/summary (with a custom rotating chevron svg). `ShikiCode({ code, lang })` wraps `ShikiCodeInner` in a Suspense fallback (a plain muted-background pre) — `ShikiCodeInner` uses `use(highlightCode(code, lang))` to read the highlightCode promise (the use-hook suspends if the WASM isn't loaded yet). `CopyButton({ code })` is an absolute-positioned button that appears on group-hover and shows a 1.5s 'copied' indicator (Check icon). `useResolvedAssetUrl` reads the context, returns the original url if not configured. `resolveAssetSrcSet` splits a srcset string on commas, resolves each URL (skipping data: URLs), and re-joins.
nodes.languageNotes: The `use(highlightCode(code, lang))` is the React 19 use-hook pattern for unwrapping a promise during render — it suspends if the promise is pending (which is why ShikiCodeInner is wrapped in a Suspense boundary). rehype-raw enables raw HTML in markdown (used for the alert plugin's <blockquote class='alert'> markup), remark-gfm enables GitHub-flavoured markdown (tables, task lists, strikethrough), remark-github-blockquote-alert enables the > [!NOTE] / > [!WARNING] alert syntax. The `useResolvedAssetUrl` hook returns the original url when no resolver is in the context — this is the 'safe no-op' pattern so child components don't have to null-check. `resolveAssetSrcSet` is the multi-URL variant for responsive images — the `match(/^(\S+)(\s+.+)?$/)` captures the URL and the descriptor (e.g. '2x') separately so the descriptor isn't mangled by URL resolution. The custom <pre> renderer inspects the code child and short-circuits when the inner code has a language className (so the ShikiCode component owns the pre entirely — no nested-pre bug). `oxlint-disable-next-line jsx-a11y/media-has-caption` is the project acknowledgement that video elements in markdown don't always have captions.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/repo-commit-sparkline-lazy.tsx
nodes.summary: IntersectionObserver-based deferred-mount wrapper for the repo commit sparkline. `LazyRepoCommitSparkline({ repo, placeholderClassName })` uses a containerRef and useState `showChart` (initially false). On mount, a useEffect creates an IntersectionObserver with `rootMargin: '240px 0px'` — when the element becomes visible (or is within 240px of the viewport), `setShowChart(true)` and the observer disconnects. Once visible, renders `<Suspense fallback={placeholder}><RepoCommitSparkline repo={repo} /></Suspense>`. The placeholder is a 13x42 muted div (DEFAULT_PLACEHOLDER_CLASSES = 'h-13 w-42 shrink-0 rounded-sm bg-muted/15') or a custom placeholderClassName. The 240px rootMargin pre-fetches slightly before the user scrolls the row into view so the chart appears without a delay.
nodes.languageNotes: The 240px rootMargin is the canonical 'prefetch before visible' distance for infinite lists — at ~600px row height the chart will mount one row before the user scrolls the row into view, hiding the network latency. The observer disconnects after the first hit (no need to keep watching once the chart is mounted), which also avoids the perf cost of observer callbacks firing as the chart scrolls around. The Suspense boundary inside the chart branch is a belt-and-braces against the recharts library triggering a synchronous render that suspends on first mount. `h-13` and `w-42` are the placeholder dimensions — they match the rendered chart's 168x52px box (with a few extra pixels for line-height rounding) so there's no layout shift when the chart appears.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/repo-commit-sparkline.tsx
nodes.summary: Recharts area chart of 52-week commit activity per repo. `RepoCommitSparkline({ repo })` — uses `useId().replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, '')` to generate a unique gradient ID (the regex strip is necessary because React 19's useId can include ':' which is invalid in a CSS URL fragment), `useIsClient()` to gate SSR, and `useGetGithubRepoCommitSparklineQuery(repo)` for the data. While not client-mounted or loading, renders the muted placeholder div. `weekly = query.data?.weeklyCommits ?? []`; `hasActivity = weekly.some(n => n > 0)`. The stroke colour is #60C679 (active) or var(--foreground) (inactive), strokeOpacity 1 / 0.5, with a 3-stop linear gradient fill (52% → 20% → 0% opacity for active, 44% → 14% → 0% for inactive). `chartData` is the weekly array mapped to `{ i, commits }` (52 padded with zero entries if empty). Renders a Recharts AreaChart (168x52, 5-side margins) with one Area (`type='monotone'`, `dataKey='commits'`, `dot={false}`, `isAnimationActive={false}`, `connectNulls`). The chart's `aria-label` is the activity summary.
nodes.languageNotes: The `useId` regex strip is the React 19 fix — useId's output starts with `:r0:` and the colon is illegal in a `url(#...)` reference. `useIsClient` is the SSR gate so the chart never tries to render on the server (recharts depends on browser-only APIs like ResizeObserver). The two gradient-stop presets (active=52%→20%→0%, inactive=44%→14%→0%) are tuned so the active chart has a slightly more saturated fill — this is the visual cue that the repo is actively being worked on. `isAnimationActive={false}` is important: animated chart mount on a 50-row list would create a visible waterfall of animations. The 52-week padding (Array.from({length: 52}, (_, i) => ({i, commits: 0}))) is for repos with no activity — the chart renders an empty baseline rather than collapsing to 0 width.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/repository-row.tsx
nodes.summary: Single-row component for the repo overview list. `RepositoryRow({ repo, isAdmin, ...divProps })` is memoized. Renders a Card wrapping a TanStack Router Link (`to='/repos/$repo'`, `params={repo.name}`) with a 4-column grid layout (name, description, meta, sparkline). Meta entries (built up in `metaEntries: { key, node }[]`): language (with a 2px dot using `repo.languageColor ?? languageColors[repo.language] ?? 'var(--muted)'` — the lookup table has 11 hand-curated GitHub-language colours for languages that don't have a built-in colour), updatedAt (via formatRelativeTime), stars (with Star icon and formatCompactCount), forks (with GitFork icon and formatCompactCount). Each entry is separated by a · dot. If isAdmin, prepends a VisibilityBadge (EyeIcon for public, EyeOffIcon for private/internal). The LazyRepoCommitSparkline is mounted in the rightmost column with the repo name as the query key. Description line-clamp-2 with a placeholder '-' for empty.
nodes.languageNotes: The 11-entry languageColors lookup table is the curated complement to GitHub's automatic language colours — the upstream GitHub API doesn't always return a `languageColor` (especially for private repos), so the table provides a sensible fallback for the most common languages. The pattern `?? languageColors[repo.language] ?? 'var(--muted)'` is the project's three-tier fallback (API → curated → theme muted). `isAdmin` controls whether the visibility badge appears — public viewers (e.g. unauthenticated users browsing the public portfolio) shouldn't see whether a repo is private. `formatCompactCount` is from @tsu-stack/core — turns 1500 into '1.5K'. The `metaEntries` array-with-FRAGMENT-key pattern is the canonical 'build the meta column dynamically' approach — entries are added conditionally and the separator (·) is inserted between them via the Fragment children.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/shared/ui/sortable-list.tsx
nodes.summary: Generic @dnd-kit-based sortable list wrapper. `SortableList<T extends { id: string }>({ items, onReorder, disabled=false, siblingsDimOnHover=false, children })` — children is a render prop `(item, dragHandleProps, isDragging) => ReactNode`. The `useSensors` call configures a single PointerSensor with `activationConstraint: { distance: 4 }, axis: 'y'` (4px movement before drag starts — prevents accidental drags on click; y-axis only — no horizontal drag). `handleDragEnd({ active, over })` finds the old/new index in `items` and calls `onReorder(arrayMove(items, oldIndex, newIndex))` if the move is valid. The DndContext is wrapped with a SortableContext (verticalListSortingStrategy) and renders each item in a SortableRow. `SortableRow({ id, disabled, children })` calls `useSortable({ id, disabled })`, builds a style with `transform: translate3d(0, ${transform.y}px, 0)` (only y) and `opacity: 0.6` while dragging. The dragHandleProps it returns includes attributes + listeners (only when not disabled), a className with cursor-grab/touch-none/active:grabbing, and pointer-events-none + cursor-not-allowed + opacity-50 when disabled.
nodes.languageNotes: The 4px activation distance is the standard 'click vs drag' disambiguation threshold — clicks within 4px register as clicks on the underlying button (e.g. edit/delete) rather than initiating a drag. `axis: 'y'` is the constraint that prevents vertical lists from having their rows drag horizontally (which would conflict with the row's internal layout). The `translate3d(0, ...)` (only y) is the project pattern for vertical-only sortable lists — recharts and other DOM measurement libraries misbehave on horizontal transforms. `siblingsDimOnHover` toggles the `group` class on the container so child items can use `group-hover:opacity-60` (and the hovered item gets a hover scale-up override) — this is the design pattern from the items-page list where hovered items get full opacity and siblings dim. The render-prop children pattern (vs JSX children) is the only way to pass per-item drag state to the consumer without forcing the consumer to write a wrapping component.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/start.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack Start createStart factory that wires the project's logger middleware into the server-function and request pipelines. The vite.config.ts injects two build-time constants via `define`: `__BUILD_NODE_ENV__` (from ENV_WEB_SERVER.NODE_ENV) and `__BUILD_SOURCE_COMMIT__` (from ENV_WEB_SERVER.SOURCE_COMMIT). The file `declare const __BUILD_SOURCE_COMMIT__: string; declare const __BUILD_NODE_ENV__: string;` to satisfy TypeScript. `initLogger({ env: { environment, service: LOG_SERVICES.WEB_SERVER, version: __BUILD_SOURCE_COMMIT__ }, sampling: { keep: [{status: 400}, {duration: 1000}], rates: { info: 100 } } })` initializes the @tsu-stack/logger/server with the web service identity and the project's keep-and-rate sampling rules (always keep 4xx responses and operations longer than 1s; sample info at 100% — i.e. keep everything). `export const startInstance = createStart(() => ({ functionMiddleware: [tanstackStartServerFnLoggerMiddleware({ context: { environment, version } })], requestMiddleware: [createCsrfMiddleware({ filter: (ctx) => ctx.handlerType === 'serverFn' }), tanstackStartRequestLoggerMiddleware({ context: { environment, version }, excludePaths: ['**/_api/health/**'] })] }))` — CSRF is applied only to serverFn handlers (so cross-origin server-function POSTs are protected but plain API routes are not, since the API uses bearer auth not cookies), the request logger excludes the health check path to avoid filling logs with k8s probes.
nodes.languageNotes: The `__BUILD_NODE_ENV__` and `__BUILD_SOURCE_COMMIT__` define-injected constants are how the build pipeline propagates runtime-evaluated server env into the client bundle (where the env vars aren't available) — TypeScript needs the `declare const` to accept the undefined-at-typecheck but defined-at-buildtime values. The `createCsrfMiddleware({ filter: (ctx) => ctx.handlerType === 'serverFn' })` is a scoped CSRF: only server functions get the CSRF check, because they accept user-submitted mutations; regular API routes are session/bearer-authenticated and don't need a CSRF token. The log-sampling `keep: [{status: 400}, {duration: 1000}]` rule keeps all 4xx responses and all slow (>1s) operations regardless of the rate — these are the 'always interesting' log lines. The `rates: { info: 100 }` keeps every info-level log (the project doesn't sample info — only debug if that were ever added). The `excludePaths: ['**/_api/health/**']` pattern matches the wildcard glob syntax for TanStack Router's path matcher — keeps the health check probe from spamming the request log.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/items-page/index.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel re-export of the items-page widget surface. Re-exports `createItemsUIStore` and `isAnyOpened` from lib/, the ItemsNavProvider + useItemsNavContext from lib/items-nav-context, the three items-ui types (ItemsUIConfig, ItemsUIState, ItemsUIStore), useItemsNavigation, useItemsTabUrlSync, the two skeleton components (GridSkeleton, ListSkeleton), the four UI primitives (ItemsEmpty, ItemsFilterButton + its ItemsFilterOption type, ItemInfoPanel, ItemsInfoFooter, ItemsInfoSheet, ItemsList, PageHeader, PageLayout). The barrel lets feature pages (experiences, projects, stacks) import everything they need from a single `@/widgets/items-page` path.
nodes.languageNotes: The barrel pattern here is the project's standard for widget surfaces — a feature imports `@/widgets/items-page` and gets the full public surface in one go, without needing to know the internal lib/ui split. The internal `import '@/widgets/items-page/lib/...'` paths are still used by the files within the widget (so the barrel is a one-way valve — internal code never imports from the barrel). `ItemsFilterOption` is exported as a type-only re-export (the `export type` syntax) because it's only used as a generic constraint in feature code.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/items-page/lib/create-items-ui-store.ts
nodes.summary: Generic factory for the per-feature items-page UI store (tab/filter/selection/opened-item state). `createItemsUIStore<T extends {id: string}, Tab extends string, Filter extends string>(config: ItemsUIConfig<T, Tab, Filter>)` returns a useStore hook. The store uses the project's standard module-scoped listener pattern: a `let state` closure, a `Set<() => void>` of listeners, `getState`/`setState(partial)`/`subscribe` triple. The `useStore` hook calls `useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getState, getState)` (server snapshot = client snapshot — same value, no hydration mismatch) and useMemo's the snapshot + the stable action methods into a new object reference on every state change. Action methods: `setActiveTab(tab)` (resets selection; validates via config.isValidTab), `setFilter(filter)` (resets selection), `setOpenedItem(item)`, `setIsItemOpen(open)`, `openItem(id, item)` (toggles; sets openedItem to the item or null), `closePanel()` (resets both openedItem and isItemOpen), `toggleSelect(id)`, `selectAll(ids)` (Object.fromEntries over the id array), `clearSelection()`, and `setTabAndFilter(tab)` (composes setActiveTab + the optional config.tabToFilter mapper). All actions are module-scoped per-store-instance closures — their identity is stable across renders so consumers can include them in dependency arrays safely.
nodes.languageNotes: The `useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getState, getState)` (third arg = getState) is the project's 'server snapshot is same as client' pattern — avoids the hydration mismatch that would happen if the server returned a different initial value. The useMemo([snapshot]) is the key to referential stability: the returned object's identity changes ONLY when the snapshot changes, not on every render. The `Object.fromEntries(ids.map(id => [id, true]))` for selectAll is the canonical 'set of all selected ids' initialization. The `if (config.isValidTab && !config.isValidTab(tab)) return;` guard at the top of setActiveTab/setTabAndFilter lets the consumer plug in runtime tab validation (e.g. a tab the user isn't authorised to see) without a separate validation layer. The `wasOpen = state.isItemOpen?.[id] ?? false` check in openItem means the same call can either open (if closed) or close (if open) the item — a click on an open item closes the panel. The factory pattern is the project's standard for 'one-store-per-feature' — the same factory is used by experience.slice.ts, project.slice.ts, stack.slice.ts to instantiate their respective stores with their own T/Tab/Filter types.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/items-page/lib/is-any-item-open.ts
nodes.summary: Tiny utility that returns true if any id in the open dict is open. `isAnyOpened(isItemOpen: Record<string, boolean> | null | undefined): boolean` — safe for null and empty dicts (returns false in both cases). The `for (const key in isItemOpen)` loop short-circuits on the first true value. Used by useItemsNavigation to decide whether to reset selection to the first item or to move to the next/prev item.
nodes.languageNotes: The function is intentionally a plain function (not a hook) so it can be called from useMemo/useCallback dependency arrays or from non-React code (e.g. server-side rendering helpers). The `null | undefined` union type is the input shape from the store — `isItemOpen` starts as null (no item open), transitions to a Record when an item is opened, and returns to null when closed. The for-in loop is faster than Object.values(...).some for the typical case (≤10 items) and is the project pattern for boolean aggregation over a small dict.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/items-page/lib/items-nav-context.tsx
nodes.summary: Context that distributes the keyboard-navigation handlers + container ref to the items-list children. Types: `ItemsNavContainerRef = React.RefObject<HTMLUListElement | null>`; `ItemsNavContextValue = { handleNext, handlePrev, containerRef }`. The default context value is null. `useItemsNavContext()` reads the context and throws 'must be used inside <ItemsNavProvider>' if the context is null. `ItemsNavProvider({ children, value: { handleNext, handlePrev, containerRef? } })` — creates a local useRef<HTMLUListElement>(null) as the fallback, picks `value.containerRef ?? localRef`, and useMemo's `{ handleNext: value.handleNext, handlePrev: value.handlePrev, containerRef }` into the context value (useMemo on [handleNext, handlePrev, containerRef] keeps the context value referentially stable so consumer re-renders are minimised).
nodes.languageNotes: The throw-on-missing-provider pattern (vs returning a default value) is the project convention for component-must-be-wrapped situations — it surfaces the misuse immediately during development rather than letting the consumer silently fail with the default value. The local `useRef<HTMLUListElement | null>(null)` as fallback handles the case where the parent doesn't have a container ref to pass in (e.g. a list that doesn't need scroll-into-view navigation). The useMemo dep array `[handleNext, handlePrev, containerRef]` is the right minimal set: the actions are stable across renders (they come from useItemsNavigation's useCallback) and the containerRef is either the parent's ref object (referentially stable) or the local ref (also stable).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/items-page/lib/items-ui.types.ts
nodes.summary: Type definitions for the items-page store factory. `ItemsUIConfig<T, Tab, Filter>`: `{ initialTab, initialFilter, tabToFilter?: (tab) => Filter, isValidTab?: (tab) => boolean }` — the two optional hooks let a feature plug in tab-validation and tab-to-filter mapping without subclassing. `ItemsUIState<T, Tab, Filter>`: `{ activeTab, filter, openedItem: T | null, isItemOpen: Record<string, boolean> | null, selectedIds: Record<string, boolean> | null }` — the three Record-or-null fields encode 'no value' as null (semantically distinct from an empty map, though functionally equivalent for `isAnyOpened`-style checks). `ItemsUIStore<T, Tab, Filter>`: `() => ItemsUIState & { setActiveTab, setFilter, setOpenedItem, setIsItemOpen, openItem (toggles: open if closed, close if open), closePanel, toggleSelect, selectAll, clearSelection, setTabAndFilter (composes setActiveTab + config.tabToFilter) }`.
nodes.languageNotes: The `Record<string, boolean> | null` for isItemOpen and selectedIds is the 'explicit no-value' encoding — `null` means 'no item/selection active', `{}` means 'user has actively cleared all items' (functionally the same in many checks, but semantically distinct for the 'show select-all' UI). The two optional config hooks (`tabToFilter`, `isValidTab`) keep the factory generic without a strategy-pattern ceremony — feature code can pass them inline. The use of `_T` (leading underscore) in `ItemsUIConfig<_T, Tab, Filter>` is to suppress the unused-type-parameter warning when the config doesn't reference T directly (only the state/store types do).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/items-page/lib/use-items-navigation.ts
nodes.summary: Hook that wires ArrowLeft/ArrowRight keyboard nav across a list of items. `useItemsNavigation<T extends {id: string}>({ items, openedItem, isItemOpen, setOpenedItem, setIsItemOpen, containerRef? })` returns `{ handleNext, handlePrev }`. Internal: `isEditableTarget(target)` returns true if the keydown target is an INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT or has isContentEditable — the global keydown listener ignores those. `setSelectionById(id)` finds the item by id and calls both setOpenedItem and setIsItemOpen({[id]: true}). `resetSelection(last?)` opens the first or last item. `handleNext()` — if no item is open, reset to the first; if at the end, reset to the first; otherwise advance. `handlePrev()` — symmetric (no open → last; at start → last; otherwise go back). The keydown listener is on `window` and only fires for ArrowLeft/ArrowRight without any modifier; calls preventDefault. The scroll-into-view useEffect: when openedItem changes, finds `[data-item-id='${id}']` inside containerRef.current (using CSS.escape for special characters) and calls scrollIntoView({block: 'nearest', behavior: 'smooth'}); a `lastScrolledId` ref prevents re-scrolling on the same id.
nodes.languageNotes: The `isEditableTarget` check is the canonical 'don't capture arrow keys when the user is typing' pattern — using isContentEditable covers rich-text editors, Slate, Tiptap, etc. The CSS.escape on the id is critical for ids that contain special characters (colons, slashes — common in TanStack Router splat params). The lastScrolledId ref is the project's standard 'only scroll when the target actually changed' guard — without it, a re-render that re-assigns openedItem to the same object would re-trigger the scroll (and potentially fight the user mid-scroll). The cyclic behaviour (end → first, start → last) is the project pattern for arrow-nav in lists — feels more natural than dead-ending at the bounds. The `if (!items?.length) return;` guards in handleNext/handlePrev are the no-op-when-empty case. `pathname triggers scroll-into-view on route change` style comments in adjacent code don't apply here (no pathname dep) — the scroll effect's only dep is openedItem (via the lastScrolledId comparison).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/items-page/lib/use-items-tab-url-sync.ts
nodes.summary: Two-way sync between `?tab=...` in the URL and the items-page's active tab. `useItemsTabUrlSync<Tab extends string>({ paramName='tab', defaultTab, isValidTab })` returns `{ tab, setTab }`. Uses nuqs's `useQueryState` with `parseAsString.withDefault(defaultTab)`. `tabFromUrl: Tab` is the validated value — returns defaultTab if the URL value fails the isValidTab type-guard. `safeSetTab(next: string)` no-ops if `next === tab` or `!isValidTab(next)`, otherwise calls setTab (voided). The setTab return value from nuqs is `Promise<URLSearchParams>` — the void cast is intentional since the caller doesn't need to await the URL update.
nodes.languageNotes: The `tabFromUrl = isValidTab(tab) ? tab : defaultTab` is the project's 'URL is just a hint' pattern — if the URL has an invalid value (e.g. user hand-edited the URL to a tab they don't have access to), the page renders the default rather than crashing. The safeSetTab pattern (validate before writing) means a race where the user types a fast invalid value never pollutes the URL. The `void` on the setTab call is because nuqs's setTab returns a Promise that the caller can await to read the updated URL params — the items-page doesn't need that, so the promise is voided. `paramName: 'tab'` is the default but a feature can override (e.g. for nested pages that use a different param name).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/items-page/ui/item-info-panel.tsx
nodes.summary: Frame-style detail panel for the items-page side-panel slot. `ItemInfoPanel({ title, description, children, updatedAt, createdAt, className })` renders a CardFrame with max-height = calc(100dvh - var(--navbar-height) - 10px) (the -10px is for the bottom padding in the root layout). Inside: a CardFrameHeader with the title (FrameTitle) and description (FrameDescription) — both accept ReactNode so the caller can pass a custom node, but if the title is a string it gets the default text-lg styling. A ScrollArea with className `max-h-[calc(100dvh-var(--navbar-height)-200px)]` wraps the children, render-prop'd to a FramePanel. The ItemsInfoFooter is mounted at the bottom with the updatedAt/createdAt timestamps.
nodes.languageNotes: The `100dvh` (dynamic viewport height) unit is the modern replacement for 100vh — it accounts for mobile browser chrome (URL bar collapsing/expanding) and prevents the layout from shifting when the URL bar auto-hides. The -10px and -200px offsets are the hard-coded fudge factors for the root layout's bottom padding and the header+footer height — the project accepts these magic numbers as the cost of not having a layout engine measure the actual sizes. The title/description 'string-or-ReactNode' prop type is the project's pattern for letting the caller pass either plain text (gets default styling) or a custom node (for inline badges, links, etc.).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/items-page/ui/item-skeleton.tsx
nodes.summary: Two skeleton components for the items-page loading states. `ListSkeleton({ count=6 })` — a vertical `<ul>` of Card-wrapped list items, each with three Skeleton elements: a 10x10 rounded square (icon), a flex-1 column with h-4 w-1/3 and h-3 w-1/2 bars, and a 8x8 rounded square (action button). `aria-busy='true'` and `aria-live='polite'` on the ul for screen-reader announcement. `GridSkeleton({ count=6 })` — a 2/3/4/8-column responsive grid (mobile/tablet/laptop/desktop) of Card role='button' tabIndex=-1 elements, each filled with a size-full Skeleton. `aspect-square` keeps the cards square regardless of the column count.
nodes.languageNotes: The aria-busy + aria-live='polite' combination is the project pattern for screen-reader announcement of loading state — assistive tech announces the change without interrupting the current speech. tabIndex=-1 on the GridSkeleton role='button' cards is the focus-skip pattern — the cards look like buttons but shouldn't be focusable while loading. The 6 default count + the responsive grid (sm:3, lg:4, xl:8) gives a comfortable layout on every viewport without the skeleton feeling either empty (1 item) or overwhelming (50 items). The 'flex-1' on the text-column skeleton ensures the bars stretch with the available width regardless of the icon/action button widths.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/items-page/ui/items-empty.tsx
nodes.summary: Empty-state component for the items-page list. `ItemsEmpty({ title, description?, action? })` — renders the @tsu-stack/ui Empty primitive with a header (title + optional description) and an optional action slot (e.g. a 'Create your first experience' button). Used by the page-level feature code (experiences, projects, stacks) as the emptyState prop to ItemsList.
nodes.languageNotes: The `action` prop is intentionally `React.ReactNode` rather than a typed Button — the caller decides whether the action is a Button, a Link, a DropdownMenu trigger, etc. The optional description is hidden via the `description ? <EmptyDescription>...</EmptyDescription> : null` pattern rather than passing null to the component, because the Empty primitive renders an empty paragraph for nullish description values which can throw off the layout. This is the simplest possible wrapper — most of the design lives in the @tsu-stack/ui Empty primitive.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/items-page/ui/items-filter-button.tsx
nodes.summary: Filter combobox for the items-page header. `ItemsFilterButton<Filter extends string>({ options, value, onChange, label='Filter:', triggerClassName, emptyMessage='No matches', searchPlaceholder='Search...' })` — opens a Popover containing a Command (cmdk) with a CommandInput for fuzzy search, a CommandList, a CommandEmpty (renders the emptyMessage), and a CommandGroup with one CommandItem per option. Each item shows a Check icon at the right (opacity-100 for the current value, opacity-0 otherwise) so the user can see the active selection. The trigger is a buttonVariants({variant:'outline', size:'sm'}) with the Filter lucide icon, the label, and the current value's label.
nodes.languageNotes: The Command primitive from @tsu-stack/ui is a wrapper around cmdk (the same combobox library used by shadcn/ui Command) — the wrapper adds the project's tailwind theme. The 'Check' opacity-100/opacity-0 pattern (instead of conditionally rendering it) is the project convention for keeping the row width stable across selection changes. `aria-label={`${label} ${current?.label ?? ''}`.trim()` builds the screen-reader label by combining the prefix ('Filter:') with the current value, so a SR user hears 'Filter: All' / 'Filter: Draft' / 'Filter: Published'. The generic `<Filter extends string>` is the project pattern for type-safe filter values — feature code can use `const filter = ExperienceFilters.Published` and TypeScript narrows correctly.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/items-page/ui/items-info-footer.tsx
nodes.summary: Footer of the items-page info panel — the prev/next nav buttons + the updatedAt/createdAt timestamps. `ItemsInfoFooter({ updatedAt?, createdAt? })` — reads `handlePrev, handleNext` from useItemsNavContext (the consumer must be inside an ItemsNavProvider). Renders a FrameFooter (flex justify-between) with a KbdGroup of two icon-only ghost Buttons (ChevronLeft, ChevronRight) and, if updatedAt/createdAt are provided, two `<time>` elements formatted with toLocaleDateString — 'en-CA' locale for the updatedAt format (which gives 'July 9, 2026 14:30' style), 'en-GB' for createdAt (slightly different date conventions). 24-hour format (hour12=false).
nodes.languageNotes: The two different locales (en-CA for updated, en-GB for created) are a tiny design choice — en-CA's date format reads slightly more naturally as 'day month year' (e.g. '9 July 2026') while en-GB provides a complementary visual distinction between the two timestamps. `dateTime={new Date(...).toISOString()}` is the canonical accessible-time-element pattern: the visible text is localized, the machine-readable attribute is ISO. The ChevronLeft/ChevronRight lucide icons (rather than ArrowLeft/ArrowRight) match the carousel-style navigation convention. The 24-hour format (hour12=false) is consistent across the project's date displays.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/items-page/ui/items-info-sheet.tsx
nodes.summary: Mobile fallback for the items-page side panel — a centered Dialog. `ItemsInfoSheet<T>({ open, onOpenChange, item, title, description?, children: (item) => ReactNode })` — renders a Radix Dialog with max-height 90vh, no gap, no padding (children render inside a scrollable inner div). The DialogTitle/Description are sr-only (required by Radix for a11y but visually hidden). `children` is a render-prop that receives the item — only called when `open && item` (to avoid the consumer rendering nothing during the close animation). The docstring notes that this mirrors the cilas `CourseInfoModal` pattern and that a `<Sheet side='bottom'>` could be swapped in if a bottom drawer is preferred.
nodes.languageNotes: The sr-only DialogTitle/Description is the Radix-mandated accessibility pattern — the dialog must have an accessible name and description for screen readers, but the design often doesn't want a visible header. The `open && item ? children(item) : null` guard ensures the consumer's render-prop isn't called with a stale item during the close animation. Mounted-unconditionally-by-the-page is the project's pattern for letting the dialog's enter/exit animation run cleanly — the page wraps the sheet in a permanent mount and toggles the `open` prop.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/items-page/ui/items-list.tsx
nodes.summary:
Generic list shell for the items-page widget. `ItemsList({ items, isLoading, renderItem, showSkeletonOnRefetch=true, skeletonCount, emptyState, containerRef?, className })` — internally reads `useItemsNavContext().containerRef` and falls back to the prop. Tracks `hasLoadedOnce` in useState (set when items && items.length > 0) so the skeleton doesn't re-appear on every refetch after the first load. `showSkeleton = isLoading && (showSkeletonOnRefetch || !hasLoadedOnce)`. Renders ListSkeleton during loading, the emptyState when items is empty, or a `
    ` of `
  • {renderItem(item)}
    • ` children. The `data-item-id` attribute is the contract that useItemsNavigation's scroll-into-view effect looks up via `container.querySelector(`[data-item-id='${id}']`).
nodes.languageNotes: The `set-state-in-effect` oxlint-disable is required because `setHasLoadedOnce(true)` inside the items-effect is a legitimate 'derive state from props after first render' pattern (the alternative is to make the parent control the loading state, which would leak the cache-skip logic into every consumer). The `data-item-id` attribute on each li is the key contract — it lets useItemsNavigation's CSS-escape-aware querySelector find the right DOM element to scrollIntoView. `space-y-2 outline-none` is the default className — the outline-none is critical because the ul itself can be focused for keyboard nav and a default focus ring would be visually noisy.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/items-page/ui/page-header.tsx
nodes.summary: CardFrame-based page header for the items-page (and any dashboard sub-page). `PageHeader({ title, description?, actions? })` — renders a CardFrame with a flex row (me-5 = 20px right margin to align with the items list below) containing a CardFrameHeader (CardTitle + optional CardDescription) and an optional CardFrameAction on the right. The actions slot is the project convention for the right-aligned header buttons (typically the HeaderActions component from batch 32 in one of its three modes).
nodes.languageNotes: The `me-5` (margin-end) right padding is the alignment hack — the rightmost edge of the header lines up with the rightmost edge of the items list below (which has the same me-5 because of the side-panel spacing). Using logical margin-end means it flips correctly in RTL. The `actions` prop is ReactNode so the consumer can pass any action-button composition — typically a HeaderActions component (single add, sort mode, or batch mode). The CardFrame primitive from @tsu-stack/ui provides the styled container with proper rounded corners and border.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/items-page/ui/page-layout.tsx
nodes.summary: Generic page container for the items-page widget. `PageLayout(props: React.ComponentProps<'div'>)` — a flex column with gap-5 and p-5 padding, min-h-0 so the flex child can shrink (essential for the root layout's flex-1 + overflow-hidden chain). Spreads all div props (className override, children, etc.) onto a single div.
nodes.languageNotes: The `min-h-0` is critical and subtle — without it, the flex column would have min-height: auto (the content's natural height) and the page would overflow the viewport. With min-h-0, the flex column respects the parent's height and the child (typically a scrollable main) can scroll. The `gap-5` (20px) is the project standard gap between header, list, and other vertical sections.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/layout/index.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel re-export of the layout widget surface. Re-exports everything from `@/shared/lib/use-register-github-public-tab` (a hook for registering the github-public tab in the tab-store), the layout widget's items-info-panel (which renders into the SidePanelPortal), root-layout (the root page shell), and side-panel (the SidePanelProvider/Portal/Slot/Toggle + the public/dashboard width constants).
nodes.languageNotes: Note the re-export from @/shared/lib — the layout widget's barrel re-exports a shared hook because the hook is the canonical way to register the github-public tab from any page that wants the tab to appear in the topbar. The pattern is 'shared lib exposed via the widget barrel' — keeps the import path consistent for feature code that imports from @/widgets/layout.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/layout/ui/command-palette.tsx
nodes.summary: Topbar-mounted Cmd+K command palette. `CommandPalette()` reads `useCommandPalette()` for open/close, `useRouter()` for navigate, `useCommandItems()` for the registered commands, and groups them by `item.group` (Map → array of {label, items}). `handleItemClick(item)` — if `item.action.type === 'navigate'`, calls `router.navigate({ to, params })`; otherwise calls `item.action.fn()`; then closes the palette. The render is a CommandDialog (Radix Dialog wrapping the project's Command primitive) with a CommandInput, a CommandPanel containing CommandEmpty (a custom message: 'Type at least 2 characters to search.' for single-char queries, 'No results found.' otherwise), a CommandList that maps each group to a CommandGroup with label/separator/collection, and a CommandFooter with keyboard-hint Kbds (ArrowUp/Down for navigate, Enter for open, Esc for close).
nodes.languageNotes: The 2-char minimum for search is a small UX choice — single-character searches are too noisy and would match every command. The action discriminated union (`{ type: 'navigate', to, params } | { type: 'fn' }`) keeps the command-palette decoupled from any specific router — the registry can register either kind. `useCommandItems()` is the project's command-registry hook (from batch 30 — command-palette/registry.ts) — pages and features register their commands via the registry and they automatically appear in the palette. The footer Kbd hints are the canonical 'here are the keys you can press' UI for command palettes.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/layout/ui/dashboard-bottombar.tsx
nodes.summary: Bottom-of-page warning bar that surfaces all registered warnings + the extension install prompt. `DashboardBottomBar()` reads `useWarnings()` (from the warning-store external store) and renders a flex row with the ExtensionInstallPrompt and one warning tile per warning. Each tile has a colour scheme (red-500 for error, yellow-500 for warning) with an AlertCircle icon, the warning message, an optional action (link or button — discriminated by action.kind), and an optional dismiss button (X icon) that calls `removeWarning(warning.id)`. The container has `empty:hidden` so it collapses when there are no warnings and no install prompt.
nodes.languageNotes: The `empty:hidden` Tailwind variant collapses the entire container when it has no children — the parent root-layout renders the bar unconditionally but it visually disappears when nothing is registered. The action.kind discriminated union (action.kind === 'link' or 'action.kind === 'button'') lets the warning define which render path to use without the bar knowing the warning's specific semantics. The two colour schemes (red-500 for error, yellow-500 for warning) are the project's warning-vs-error visual convention. The dismiss button is only rendered if `warning.dismissible` — some warnings are mandatory and the user can't dismiss them (e.g. permission errors).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/layout/ui/dashboard-breadcrumbs.tsx
nodes.summary: Auto-generated breadcrumb from the current URL pathname. `DashboardBreadcrumbs()` uses `useRouterState({ select: s => s.location.pathname })` to subscribe to pathname changes. `KNOWN_SEGMENTS` (dashboard, resume, experiences, projects, stacks, new, github-config) and `SEGMENT_LABELS` map the URL segments to human-readable labels. Segments are split on '/', filtered (no empty, no TanStack-router virtual segments like `{-$param}` and `__layout`), then iterated: `isIdSegment(segment)` (any segment not in KNOWN_SEGMENTS) gets the label 'Edit' (convention for /dashboard/{kind}/{id}/edit URLs), segments in SEGMENT_LABELS get their mapped label. The breadcrumb is null if no crumbs were produced. Each crumb renders a BreadcrumbLink (TanStack Router Link, hidden on mobile) for non-last segments, and a BreadcrumbPage (non-link) for the last segment. Separators (BreadcrumbSeparator) are inserted between crumbs and hidden on mobile.
nodes.languageNotes: The `useRouterState({ select: s => s.location.pathname })` is the standard pattern for 'subscribe to the smallest possible piece of router state' — the component only re-renders when the pathname changes, not on every router state update. The pathname filter `!s.startsWith('{-') && !s.startsWith('__')` is the project's pattern for ignoring TanStack Router's virtual segment syntax (e.g. `{-$projectId}` for optional splat params, `__layout` for file-based layout markers) — these segments shouldn't appear in the breadcrumb. The 'Edit' label for unknown segments is a heuristic — if the URL is `/dashboard/experiences/abc123/edit`, the `abc123` segment is the id and the breadcrumb shows 'Edit' as the user-friendly action. The hidden-on-mobile pattern (`md:block` on the link + `hidden md:block` on the separator) is the project convention for mobile breadcrumb simplicity — on mobile, the breadcrumb shows just the current page (last segment), no back links.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/layout/ui/extension-install-prompt.tsx
nodes.summary: Placeholder for the browser-extension install prompt. `ExtensionInstallPrompt()` returns `null` — the prompt is currently not implemented (the file exists as the future mount point for an extension-prompt UI). The dashboard-bottombar imports it so when the prompt is implemented, only this file needs to change.
nodes.languageNotes: Returning null is the project's convention for 'intentionally not rendered' — the function still exists with a real name so the consumer can mount it without a null check. The 3-line file is the entire implementation; the import in dashboard-bottombar and the export in this file are the contracts that the future implementation will satisfy.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/layout/ui/github-access-dialog.tsx
nodes.summary: Dialog that prompts the user to configure their GitHub access (shown when a feature needs repo access the user hasn't granted). `GitHubAccessDialog()` reads `useGitHubAccessPrompt()` from the github-access-modal-store; the dialog is open when the prompt is non-null OR when the URL has `?show-org-setup=true` (the org-setup onboarding path). `useRefreshOnReturn({ enabled: isOpen })` invalidates the relevant queries when the user returns to the tab (e.g. from the GitHub install page). `handleOpenChange(nextOpen)` — on close, if showOrgSetup, removes the `show-org-setup` query param via `window.history.replaceState`; calls `closeGitHubAccessPrompt()`. The title/description are templated from the prompt's repo (if any). Renders a Dialog with the title/description header, a centered placeholder 'GitHub access is managed from the configuration page' with a Link to /dashboard/settings/github, and a footer with Close (ghost) + 'Configure access' (primary, renders a Link).
nodes.languageNotes: The dual-open condition (`showOrgSetup || prompt !== null`) lets two different code paths trigger the same dialog — the org-setup onboarding flag (set by the dashboard/settings/github page when the user lands there) and the runtime prompt (set by any feature that needs access and finds it missing). The `window.history.replaceState` (not push) is the right primitive because we don't want the back button to navigate back to the query-param version of the URL — replacing the URL silently is the correct UX. `useRefreshOnReturn` is the project's 'user returned to the tab' hook that re-runs the GitHub queries in case the user installed a new repo permission. The `render={<Link .../>}` on the Configure access button is the @tsu-stack/ui pattern for making a Button render as a Link (preserves the Button styling but provides the router navigation).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/layout/ui/github-public-mobile-nav.tsx
nodes.summary: Mobile-only bottom nav (md:hidden) for the public-facing pages. `MobileNav()` — uses useRouter, useQueryClient, useAuth, useGetGithubSetupStatusQuery, useTheme. `handleSignOut` calls authClient.signOut and on response invalidates getAuthUserQueryOptions + getGithubSetupStatusQueryOptions + router.invalidate (so the auth state is fresh on the next page). `displayName` falls back through user.name → user.email → 'GitHub'; `initials` is the first letter of up to 2 space-separated parts, uppercased. Renders a `<nav className='md:hidden'>` with three flex-1 items: (1) Home link (House icon, to='/'), (2) Repositories link (Archive icon, to='/repos'), (3) Avatar DropdownMenu trigger. The dropdown contains the user's name+email, an inline theme switcher (Sun/Moon/Monitor icon-only buttons), a Repositories link (disabled if no owner), a Settings link, and a Sign out menu item. The container has a `pb-[env(safe-area-inset-bottom)]` for iOS safe area.
nodes.languageNotes: The `md:hidden` (and `md:block` on the desktop topbar) is the project pattern for switching between the mobile nav and the desktop topbar at the md breakpoint (768px). The `pb-[env(safe-area-inset-bottom)]` accounts for the iOS home-indicator safe area — without it, the bottom edge of the nav would be covered by the home indicator. The inline theme switcher in the dropdown is more compact than the standard theme switcher — three small icon buttons rather than a single select. The avatar DropdownMenu trigger is itself a button (not a MenuTrigger asChild) because the trigger needs the custom border + size styling. The `disabled={!owner}` on the Repositories menu item prevents the user from navigating to /repos when their GitHub connection isn't configured (no point showing an empty repo list).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/layout/ui/github-public-tabs.tsx
nodes.summary: Scrollable tab bar for the topbar with drag-to-reorder, HTML5 drag-and-drop, scroll-into-view, and right-click context menu. `Tabs({ tabsReady, routerRef })` reads `useTabs()` (the open-tabs list), tracks `dragTabRef` (currently-dragged tab id) and `contextTab` (right-clicked tab for the context menu). `useScrollShadows(tabCount)` returns a `scrollRef`, `canScrollLeft`/`canScrollRight` booleans (driven by a ResizeObserver on the scroll container — the gradient overlays on each edge fade in/out as the user scrolls), and a `handleWheel` that maps vertical wheel to horizontal scroll. `handleDragStart/Over/End` manage the HTML5 drag reorder via `reorderTabs(next)`. `handleCloseTab(id, tabUrl)` removes the tab and navigates to the next/prev if the closed tab was active. `handleContextClose*` remove the current / others / tabs to the right. A right-click context menu (ContextMenu from @tsu-stack/ui) provides 'Close', 'Close other tabs', 'Close tabs to the right'. The tab list is a `<div ref={scrollRef}>` of `DetailTab` (memoized) elements — each renders a Link with the tab's icon, title, addition/deletion counts (for review/commit tabs) or number (for pr/issue), and a close button (mobile in-flow, desktop overlay-on-hover). `ScrollActiveTabIntoView` is an isolated sub-component that subscribes only to the pathname and scrollIntoViews the active tab.
nodes.languageNotes: `ScrollActiveTabIntoView` is extracted as a separate component specifically so the parent Tabs doesn't re-render on every navigation — the parent re-renders only on tab-list changes, the child re-renders on pathname changes. The pathname-driven scroll only triggers if the active tab is fully or partially off-screen (the `if (tLeft < cLeft || tRight > cRight)` guard). The `preload={false}` on the Link is important — tabs are links, not preloaded routes (they're already mounted). The onMouseEnter/onFocus/onTouchStart `preloadRouteOnce(routerRef.current, tab.url)` calls preload the route chunk when the user signals intent (hover/focus/touch) without leaving the current page. The two close buttons (mobile in-flow vs desktop overlay-on-hover) are the project's pattern for giving mobile users a usable touch target (≥44px) without bloating the desktop tab width. The HTML5 drag reorder uses `e.dataTransfer.effectAllowed = 'move'` and `dropEffect = 'move'` for the cursor indicator. The tabIconMap (pull/issue/review/repo/commit/actions) maps the tab.type to the lucide icon. The 'preload-only' tag means the tab data is loaded but not the route chunk (the Link itself is the click target).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/layout/ui/github-public-topbar.tsx
nodes.summary: The desktop topbar (the mobile counterpart is MobileNav). `Topbar()` — uses useRouter, useNavigate, useLocation (selecting pathname), useQueryClient, useAuthSuspense, useTabs, useIsClient. `navigateRef` and `routerRef` are useRef mirrors of the raw navigate and router (so the global-shortcut callbacks always see the latest values without re-firing the useEffect on every render). `queryClient.getQueryData(getGithubSetupStatusQueryOptions().queryKey)` reads the cached setup status synchronously (no refetch). `handleSignOut` invalidates the auth + setup queries and calls router.invalidate. `initials` is the first letter of up to 2 display-name parts. The mount effect pre-preloads the /, /repos, and /dashboard routes via preloadRouteOnce. `useGlobalShortcuts` registers: shift-Digit1..9 (jump to tab N, up to 9 tabs), 'g' then 'u' (g u = go to user profile), shift-W (close current tab and navigate to neighbor), shift-ArrowLeft/Right (cycle tabs). Renders a nav with the user avatar dropdown (only when admin and not on /dashboard) with Profile / Repositories / Dashboard links + Sign out, the LogoWordmark link to /, the Tabs component in the flex-1 middle slot, and a right-side cluster with ThemeSwitcher, Search button (opens command palette, shows Cmd+K kbd), and a More menu (View GitHub profile, Report an issue, login link).
nodes.languageNotes: The `navigateRef` + `routerRef` mirrors are the project pattern for capturing the latest closure values in callbacks that need referential stability — the useGlobalShortcuts effect depends on stable handlers, but the handlers need to call the current navigate and router, so the refs bridge the two requirements. The shift-Digit shortcuts are the 'press shift+1 to jump to tab 1' vim/emacs convention. The g-u chord is the vim-style 'g u' = 'go to user' command. `queryClient.getQueryData(...queryKey)` is the synchronous read pattern — for state that's known to be in the cache (the setup status was just fetched by the layout), this avoids a refetch round-trip. `getQueryData` returns the data or undefined — `setupStatus?.owner ?? null` is the null-safe derivation. The TextAnimate is the per-character slide-in animation on the brand name. The 'preload-only' approach (`preloadRouteOnce` rather than `router.preloadRoute`) ensures a route is loaded at most once across the app (subsequent calls are no-ops). The More menu's 'Report an issue' link points to the GitHub issues page (out-of-app deep link).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/layout/ui/items-info-panel.tsx
nodes.summary: Portal into the root-layout's side-panel slot. `ItemsInfoPanel<T>({ open, item, children: (item) => ReactNode })` — when `open` is true and item is non-null, renders `<SidePanelPortal>{children(item)}</SidePanelPortal>`; otherwise returns null. The SidePanelSlot uses a MutationObserver to detect when the slot's child list becomes empty and auto-collapses the side panel via the hasContent flag — so when the consumer sets open=false, the side panel visually disappears without an explicit close call.
nodes.languageNotes: The MutationObserver-driven auto-collapse is the project's elegant side-panel UX — the panel's hasContent is driven by the slot's child count, so any component that renders into the slot (and then unmounts) causes the panel to auto-collapse. The user doesn't need a close button on every content component — the panel's own width animation handles the transition. The `if (!open || !item) return null;` guard is the explicit check (the MutationObserver also handles it, but the explicit guard avoids mounting SidePanelPortal at all when there's nothing to render).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/layout/ui/root-layout.tsx
nodes.summary: Root layout for the entire app — the layout that wraps every page. `RootLayout({ children })` reads `useSidePanelSlot()` (the hook that owns the side-panel state — node, collapsed, hasContent, toggle, setters), `useMediaQuery('(min-width: 1280px)')` (xl breakpoint), and `useLocation().pathname.includes('dashboard')` (is the current page in the dashboard section). `showPanel = isXl && sidePanel.hasContent && !sidePanel.collapsed`. Renders: (1) Topbar at the top; (2) SidePanelProvider (passes the side-panel state through context to the children), inside which a flex row contains the PublicSidebar (hidden on non-xl), the main content area (with the page children inside a ScrollArea + scrollFade + clampContentMinWidth), the SidePanelToggle (the collapse arrow), and the motion-animated SidePanelSlot (its width animates to 0/DASHBOARD_SIDE_PANEL_WIDTH/PUBLIC_SIDE_PANEL_WIDTH based on showPanel + isDashboard); (3) DashboardBottomBar, MobileNav, GitHubAccessDialog, CommandPalette at the bottom (all portal-rendered into the page). The IntersectionProvider wraps the sidebar + main area so any IntersectionObserver-using component has a shared context.
nodes.languageNotes: The IntersectionProvider from @/shared/providers wraps the sidebar + main area so any IntersectionObserver-using component (e.g. the lazy sparkline mount) can register against a shared root observer — the context provides the root element + the intersection entries. The motion-animated width on the side panel uses `type: 'spring', stiffness: 400, damping: 35` — fast and crisp (no overshoot). The PUBLIC_SIDE_PANEL_WIDTH (320px) and DASHBOARD_SIDE_PANEL_WIDTH (530px) constants are exported from side-panel.tsx. The `bg-container selection:bg-[#C0E7C8] selection:text-primary!` is the brand selection highlight colour. The `not-dark:bg-clip-padding before:pointer-events-none before:absolute before:inset-0` adds a subtle inset shadow on light mode (the `dark:before:shadow-[0_-1px_--theme(--color-white/6%)]` provides the dark-mode equivalent).

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/layout/ui/side-panel.tsx
nodes.summary: Side-panel state + portal infrastructure. Constants: `PUBLIC_SIDE_PANEL_WIDTH = 320` (w-72 + pl-2), `DASHBOARD_SIDE_PANEL_WIDTH = 530`. `SidePanelState` type: `{ node, collapsed, hasContent, toggle }`. `SidePanelContext` default value: `{ node: null, collapsed: false, hasContent: false, toggle: () => {} }`. `useSidePanelSlot()` hook — owns the state (useState for node/collapsed/hasContent) and a toggle callback (useCallback wrapping a setCollapsed invert). Returns `{ node, setNode, collapsed, hasContent, setHasContent, toggle } as const`. `SidePanelProvider({ value, children })` is a thin context provider (uses `<SidePanelContext value={value}>` rather than the standard Provider component — this is the React 19 context-as-element pattern). `SidePanelPortal({ children })` reads the context, returns null if no node, otherwise `createPortal(children, node)`. `SidePanelSlot({ slotRef, collapsed, onHasContent })` renders the visible slot — uses a refCallback to set both innerRef.current and call the slotRef prop, a MutationObserver on the inner element to detect childList changes (when the slot empties, the removed children are cloned into a ghostRef for the exit animation; when it fills, the ghost is cleared), a custom 'sidepanel-content' event for imperative hasContent updates, and a setTimeout cleanup for the ghost (clears after 500ms). The motion-animated opacity reveals/hides the slot. `SidePanelToggle` is a floating arrow button (ChevronLeft when collapsed, ChevronRight when expanded) that only renders when hasContent is true.
nodes.languageNotes: The context-as-element pattern (`<SidePanelContext value={value}>` rather than `<SidePanelContext.Provider value={value}>`) is the React 19 simplification — contexts can be used as Provider elements directly. The MutationObserver + ghost-ref pattern is the project pattern for animating exit when content is removed — the ghost is a clone of the removed children, positioned in a pointer-events-none sibling, that fades out via the parent's motion opacity transition while the real slot is empty. The custom 'sidepanel-content' event lets imperative code force a hasContent check (e.g. when async content loads and the childList hasn't changed but the rendered state has). The 500ms ghost cleanup is the motion duration + a small buffer; the timer is cleared on every mutation so a fast add/remove cycle doesn't leave a stale ghost. The 'hidden xl:block' on the outer div means the side panel is desktop-only (xl ≥ 1280px) — on mobile, the items-info-sheet takes over. The SidePanelToggle is positioned absolutely at top-14 right-0 (just below the navbar) and overlaps the side panel's edge for a polished collapse arrow.

nodes.name: apps/web/src/widgets/layout/ui/sidebar.tsx
nodes.summary: Desktop public sidebar with portfolio + dashboard navigation + contact links in the footer. `PublicSidebar()` — uses useAuthSuspense (so user is guaranteed to be present — the sidebar only renders for authenticated users, or a redirect happens upstream), useLocation for the active path matching, and useGetPortfolioListQuery for the contact list. `PublicItems` (Portfolio, Repositories) and `DashboardItems` (Overview, Experiences, Projects, Stack, Resumes, Profile, Account, Github — all grouped under 'Dashboard') are static lists; `groupBySection` splits items by their `group` field into Section[] arrays (ungrouped items first, then alphabetical grouped sections). The rendered sections are PublicItems followed by DashboardItems (only when isAdmin = !!user). Each Sidebar001Item is keyed by href, with label and isActive={'isExternal' in item ? false : pathname === item.href}. The footer renders one ContactButton per contact from the portfolio query.
nodes.languageNotes: `useAuthSuspense` (not useAuth) means the component assumes the auth query is in cache and won't show a loading state — the parent route guard is responsible for the redirect. `'isExternal' in item` is a type-guard — the static item lists don't currently have external items, but the type is `'isExternal' in item ? false : ...` so a future external link (with the isExternal discriminator) can opt out of the active-match logic. The grouped section order (`ungrouped` first, then alphabetical) is the project's standard sidebar order — Portfolio + Repositories at the top, then the dashboard group. The contact footer uses `contact.createdAt.toISOString()` as the React key — contacts are immutable per-portfolio so the createdAt is a stable unique key.

nodes.name: apps/web/vite.config.ts
nodes.summary: Vite + Plus build configuration for the web app. Imports: node:path resolve, @cloudflare/vite-plugin, @lonik/oh-image/plugin, @mdx-js/rollup, @rolldown/plugin-babel, @tailwindcss/vite, @tanstack/devtools-vite, @tanstack/react-start/plugin/vite, @vitejs/plugin-react with reactCompilerPreset, vite-plus defineConfig. Env imports: ENV_WEB_ISOMORPHIC and ENV_WEB_SERVER from @tsu-stack/env. `ROUTES_TO_PRERENDER = ['/sitemap.xml', '/robots.txt']` with the type-narrowed PAGES_PRERENDER_CONFIG array. `shikiSSRStub()` is a Vite plugin (name='shiki-ssr-stub', enforce='pre') that intercepts all shiki imports in the SSR environment and replaces them with empty stubs — the DEFAULT_STUB replaces the main shiki export with `bundledLanguages = {}; createHighlighter = () => Promise.resolve({}); codeToHtml = () => ''` etc.; the CORE_STUB mocks the fine-grained @shikijs/core for the rehype integration; LANG_STUB and THEME_STUB are 'export default []' / 'export default Object.freeze({})'. `iconGroupsSSRStub()` is a similar Vite plugin that matches `^./icons/group-\d{2}$` in SSR and replaces it with `export const iconLibraries = {};` — prevents the 31 react-icons re-exports (~40 MiB of SSR chunks) from being deployed as Worker modules. The plugins array wires devtools, cloudflare (viteEnvironment: ssr), tanstackStart (with prerender enabled, autoStaticPathsDiscovery: false, crawlLinks: false, concurrency: 2 — Cloudflare Pages build env has ~256 PID limit so high concurrency hits EAGAIN), the two SSR stubs, mdx, viteReact, babel with reactCompilerPreset, tailwindcss, and ohImage (pl_show: true, webp/quality 80). The exported config: `run.tasks.build` is a cross-env + dotenvx command with the env vars NODE_ENV, VITE_SERVER_URL, VITE_WEB_URL, VITE_IMGPROXY_URL, SOURCE_COMMIT, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, DATABASE_URL; preview host 127.0.0.1 (workaround for TanStack Router issue 6275 in Docker); base = new URL(VITE_WEB_URL).pathname; build reportCompressedSize: false (PID limit); rollupOptions.manualChunks splits server-auth, server-content (marked/prismjs), server-db (drizzle-orm) to stay under the 3 MiB Worker per-module limit; onwarn swallows the 'evlog externalized for browser compatibility' warning; external marks @aws-sdk/* packages as external (the r2 binding adapter means the S3 chunk is never loaded); envDir points to packages/env/; define __BUILD_NODE_ENV__ and __BUILD_SOURCE_COMMIT__; server port 3000.
nodes.languageNotes: The two SSR-stub plugins (shiki + iconGroups) are the critical perf decisions for the Cloudflare Worker bundle — without them, the shiki WASM (~1.5MB) and the 31 react-icons libraries (~40 MiB) would be bundled into the Worker. The manualChunks split is the other key Worker constraint — Cloudflare Workers have a 3 MiB per-module limit, so large server-only deps (better-auth, marked/prismjs, drizzle-orm) are split into separate chunks. `staticNodeEnv: true` prevents process.env.NODE_ENV from being changed at runtime (a security/correctness constraint for the Worker). `autoStaticPathsDiscovery: false` + `crawlLinks: false` + `concurrency: 2` are the three Cloudflare Pages build-env workarounds — auto-discovery would spawn too many processes, crawlLinks would hit external links, concurrency: 2 stays under the 256-PID limit. The ohImage plugin (from @lonik/oh-image) is the project's image-optimizer — it processes images at build time and produces webp variants. `define: { __BUILD_NODE_ENV__, __BUILD_SOURCE_COMMIT__ }` is the build-time constant injection that start.ts reads. `envDir: ../../packages/env` lets Vite watch the env files in the shared env package.

nodes.name: apps/web/worker-configuration.d.ts
nodes.summary: Auto-generated Cloudflare Worker env type declarations (generated by `wrangler types`, hash 5024c97136c044eb43b81f2204cfe0e3, workerd 1.20260617.1, nodejs_compat). The file declares the `__BaseEnv_Env` interface (which includes `MEDIA_BUCKET: R2Bucket` — the R2 binding for media storage — plus all the worker-specific env vars) and the union of all bindings, plus the Cloudflare-specific runtime types. The file is regenerated by running `wrangler types` in the apps/web directory; it's committed to the repo so editors and the TypeScript compiler can see the env types without running wrangler at build time.
nodes.languageNotes: Auto-generated by `wrangler types` from the wrangler.toml / wrangler.jsonc config — never edit by hand. The `// Generated by Wrangler by running `wrangler types` (hash: 5024c97136c044eb43b81f2204cfe0e3)` comment is the regeneration hint. The runtime types match the workerd version (1.20260617.1 from 2026-06-01) — the `nodejs_compat` flag enables the Node.js API compatibility shim. The 14515-line size is typical for the full Cloudflare runtime type bundle (Durable Objects, R2, KV, D1, Queues, etc. — most of which this app doesn't use but the types are all there).

Lists the props (ActionButtonConfig, TogglePortfolioConfig, ListItemActionButtonsProps), the render branches (view+menu, view-only, edit-only, menu-only), the design rationale, and the acceptance criteria.

nodes.summary: Design spec for multi-select and batch actions on the items-page. Adds checkbox-based multi-select to the dashboard pages (experiences, projects, stacks) with batch actions in the page header. Documents the motivation (the rename of `itemInfo`/`isItemSelected` → `openedItem`/`isItemOpen` freed the 'select' vocabulary for its intended use), the state additions to ItemsUIState (`selectedIds: Record<string, boolean> | null`), the new actions (toggleSelect, selectAll, clearSelection), the batch actions in HeaderActions (Delete + optional Add to portfolio), the UI behaviour (show checkboxes on hover, select-all toggle, batch action disabled state), and the acceptance criteria.
