nodes.name: packages/api/package.json
nodes.summary: Package manifest for @tsu-stack/api. Name: @tsu-stack/api, type: module. Imports: `#@/*` → `./src/*.ts` (the #@/* subpath pattern for in-package imports, mapped to src/). Exports: `./*` → `./src/*.ts` (wildcard re-export — every file in src/ is a public subpath of the package). Scripts: `check` (vp check), `fix` (vp check --fix). Dependencies: @orpc/client, @orpc/server, @orpc/tanstack-query, @tanstack/react-start, @tsu-stack/auth, @tsu-stack/core, @tsu-stack/db, @tsu-stack/env, @tsu-stack/github, @tsu-stack/logger, drizzle-orm, files-sdk, pdfnative, zod (all with catalog: or workspace:* references). Dev dependencies: @cloudflare/workers-types, @tsu-stack/tsconfig, @types/node, hono, typescript.
nodes.languageNotes: The wildcard exports pattern (`./*: ./src/*.ts`) means every file in src/ is automatically a public subpath of the package — `#@/routers/index` and `#@/lib/agent/worker` are the two non-relative import paths the package exposes (used in orpc.ts: `import { appRouter } from '#@/routers/index'`). The `catalog:` protocol means the dependency is resolved from the workspace root's pnpm-workspace.yaml catalog (pnpm's central version-management feature). `workspace:*` resolves to the local workspace package. hono is a dev dependency because it's only used in test/dev tooling (the server package uses the Cloudflare Workers native router, not hono).

nodes.name: packages/api/src/client/tanstack-start/orpc.ts
nodes.summary: Isomorphic oRPC client factory for the TanStack Start app. `getORPCClient = createIsomorphicFn().server(() => createRouterClient(appRouter, { context: ..., interceptors: [(options) => runWithDb(createDb(), () => options.next())] })).client(() => { const link = new RPCLink({ fetch: (url, options) => fetch(url, { ...options, credentials: 'include' }).catch((error) => { console.error('[rpc-fetch-failed]', { url, error }); throw error; }), url: `${VITE_SERVER_URL}/rpc` }); return createORPCClient(link); })`. The server context (the oRPC procedure's request context) does: runWithDb(createDb(), async () => { session = await auth.api.getSession({ headers: getRequestHeaders() }); githubSource = await resolvePublicGitHubSource(); agentWorker = (env.AGENT_WORKER ?? env.AGENT_WORKER_URL) ? createAgentWorker(env) : { fetch: () => { throw new Error('Agent worker is not configured. Set AGENT_WORKER_URL or add a service binding.'); } }; return { github: { binding, privateOctokit, publicOctokit, source }, logger: createLogger({ operation: 'web__client__orpc' }), session, mediaBucket: env.MEDIA_BUCKET, agentWorker }; }). The interceptor ensures the procedure's handler also runs inside a runWithDb scope (the oRPC server calls the context function BEFORE invoking the interceptors that wrap the procedure's main call — both layers need their own runWithDb scope). Exports: `orpcClient = getORPCClient()` (the singleton instance), `orpcQueryClient = createTanstackQueryUtils(orpcClient)` (the TanStack Query wrapper), and re-exports `eventIteratorToUnproxiedDataStream` from @orpc/client. `orpcQueryClient` is what every query-options builder in apps/web uses as `orpcClient.github.publicGetRepoCommitSparkline` etc.
nodes.languageNotes: The `createIsomorphicFn` from @tanstack/react-start is the project's pattern for 'this code runs on the server when called from the server, runs on the client when called from the client'. The .server branch is a tree-shakeable server-only bundle; the .client branch is the only one that runs in the browser. The lazy-throw fallback for the agent worker is a key design point: in development, the agent worker may not be configured (no AGENT_WORKER_URL, no service binding), but the SSR should still start up. The fallback's fetch() throws only if a procedure actually tries to call it, so the SSR startup is unaffected. The two runWithDb scopes (context + interceptor) are the project's pattern for keeping Drizzle sessions request-scoped: the context function (called by the oRPC server before the interceptors) needs its own scope (for resolvePublicGitHubSource → findPublicGithubSourceSettings that reads github_config), and the interceptor needs its own scope (for the procedure's handler calls). The 'credentials: include' is required for the session cookie to be sent with cross-origin requests. The rpc-fetch-failed log line is the catch-all for debugging SSR → server RPC failures.

nodes.name: packages/api/src/lib/agent/worker.ts
nodes.summary: Agent worker client adapter. Exports `AgentWorkerEnv` (optional `AGENT_WORKER` Fetcher binding or `AGENT_WORKER_URL` string) and `createAgentWorker(env)` which returns an `OrpcContextAgentWorker`. The returned object has a single `fetch(input, init)` that prefers the service binding (zero-hop in-process) and falls back to plain `fetch()` with a new `Request(input, init)` resolved against `stripTrailingSlashes(baseUrl)`. The fallback path sets `duplex: 'half'` (with a ts-expect-error on the non-standard fetch option) so streaming request bodies forward correctly to the agent Worker.
nodes.languageNotes: Two exports, one function. The fallback throws if neither binding nor URL is configured. Imports `stripTrailingSlashes` from @tsu-stack/core and `OrpcContextAgentWorker` from the local context/types.

nodes.name: createAgentWorker
nodes.summary: Factory: returns an `OrpcContextAgentWorker` whose `fetch` proxies to the `AGENT_WORKER` service binding or, when missing, to a worker URL via global `fetch` with `duplex: 'half'`.

nodes.name: packages/api/src/lib/context/hono/create-context.ts
nodes.summary: Per-request oRPC context builder for Hono. `createContext<TEnv>({ context, logger })` resolves the Better Auth session from the incoming headers, pulls the GitHub runtime bindings (KV + signal relay Durable Object), reads the MEDIA_BUCKET R2 binding, builds a per-user `privateOctokit` (preferring the user's fresh OAuth token from `betterAuthAccountRepository.findGitHubAccessTokenForUser`, falling back to the static PAT in `github_config`), constructs a `publicOctokit` (always anonymous), and returns the full `OrpcContext` (github, logger, session, mediaBucket, agentWorker). Includes a `TEMP debug` console.log that traces which token source the private octokit is built with and the resolved scope.
nodes.languageNotes: Single exported function plus the `OrpcContextBindings` type. Calls `auth.api.getSession` to get the user session. Uses `runWithDb(createDb(), ...)` to scope the Better Auth account lookups to a per-request Neon pool.

nodes.name: createContext
nodes.summary: Builds the OrpcContext for one Hono request: session, github octokits, mediaBucket, agentWorker.

nodes.languageNotes: One export statement. The file exists so existing `import { type OrpcContext } from '@tsu-stack/api/lib/context/types'` callers keep working while the structural definitions live in @tsu-stack/core.

nodes.name: packages/api/src/lib/procedures/factory.ts
nodes.summary: oRPC procedure factory. Defines three reusable base procedures from a single `o = os.$context<OrpcContext>()` instance: `publicProcedure` (no middleware), `protectedProcedure` (authMiddleware + OpenAPI `authCookie` security) and `ownerProcedure` (authMiddleware + requireOwner that loads `github_config` and asserts `session.user.id === ownerUserId`, with a typed `FORBIDDEN` 403 error). The `requireAuth` and `requireOwner` middlewares both narrow the context shape to `{ github, logger, session }` so downstream handlers don't have to re-check the auth state.
nodes.languageNotes: Three exports, two private middlewares. The owner check is the only place that reads the GitHub config repo for a per-request authz decision.

nodes.summary: oRPC agent router. Two public procedures: `chat` (POST, non-streaming — posts to /agents/{agentId}/generate, returns `{ content: text ?? JSON.stringify(object) ?? '' }`) and `chatStream` (POST, streaming — posts to /agents/{agentId}/stream/ui and pipes the byte body through oRPC's `streamToEventIterator` so the client's `eventIteratorToUnproxiedDataStream` can turn it into a `ReadableStream<UIMessageChunk>` for `useChat`). The `agentIdSchema` defaults to 'weather-agent'; the messages schema is a typed role+content array, while `chatStream` uses `z.array(z.any())` so the AI SDK UIMessage shape doesn't leak into the input contract.
nodes.languageNotes: Default agent id is 'weather-agent'. Uses /stream/ui (not /stream) because /stream returns Mastra's own chunk format and /stream/ui returns SSE-encoded AI SDK UIMessage chunks.

Each handler delegates to `experienceRepository` and maps the rows through `toExperienceOutput`.

Two protectedProcedure routes: `get` (returns `{ githubToken, githubUsername, hasGithubToken, updatedAt }` where the token is replaced with the `GITHUB_TOKEN_MASK` constant when present) and `update` (upserts via `githubConfigRepository.upsert`, replacing the masked token with `undefined` so it isn't clobbered). Includes a private `toGithubConfigOutput` mapper.
nodes.languageNotes: Token mask pattern: client never sees the real token, only the mask or null. The mask sentinel '••••••••••••••••' is checked on update and replaced with undefined before being passed to the repo.

nodes.name: packages/api/src/routers/github.router.ts
nodes.summary: Monolithic GitHub router with 40+ procedures, each exposed twice (`public*` on publicProcedure and `private*` on ownerProcedure). Endpoints: getRevalidationSignals, getSetupStatus, refreshInstallationAccess, clearViewerCache, publicGetProfileRepos / privateGetProfileRepos, publicGetRepoBranchComparison / privateGetRepoBranchComparison, publicGetRepoPulls / privateGetRepoPulls, publicGetRepoIssues / privateGetRepoIssues, publicGetRepoWorkflowRuns / privateGetRepoWorkflowRuns, publicGetRepoDiscussions / privateGetRepoDiscussions, publicGetRepoBranches / privateGetRepoBranches, publicGetRepoContributors / privateGetRepoContributors, publicGetRepoCommitSparkline / privateGetRepoCommitSparkline, publicGetRepoFileContent / privateGetRepoFileContent, publicGetRefCommit / privateGetRefCommit, publicGetRepoOverview / privateGetRepoOverview, publicGetRepoTree / privateGetRepoTree, publicGetTreeEntryCommits / privateGetTreeEntryCommits, publicGetUserActivity / privateGetUserActivity, publicGetUserContributions / privateGetUserContributions, publicGetUserPinnedRepos / privateGetUserPinnedRepos, publicGetUserProfile / privateGetUserProfile. All public procedures delegate to the matching `getXxx(input, context)` function in @tsu-stack/github; the private variants delegate to `getPrivateXxx`. The router also defines small input/output zod schemas (RepoInputSchema, RepoBranchComparisonInputSchema, RepoTreeInputSchema, RepoFileContentInputSchema, RepoRefCommitInputSchema, RepoTreeEntryCommitsInputSchema, RepoListStateSchema, RepoPullsSortSchema, RepoListDirectionSchema, RepoIssuesSortSchema, RepoPullsInputSchema, RepoIssuesInputSchema, RepoWorkflowRunsInputSchema, RepoDiscussionsInputSchema, RevalidationSignalsOutputSchema, RevalidationResultSchema, PublicGitHubStatusOutputSchema, UserActivityInputSchema).
nodes.languageNotes: Pairs of public/private procedures share the same input/output schemas. The private procedures use the owner's per-user `privateOctokit`; the public ones use `publicOctokit` (always anonymous). The router imports a long list of helper functions from @tsu-stack/github (all 38 getters, plus bumpGitHubCacheNamespaces, markGitHubRevalidationSignals) and 17 schema shapes from @tsu-stack/github/schemas.

nodes.summary: The exported oRPC router with 40+ procedures (mostly public/private pairs).

nodes.name: packages/api/src/routers/health.router.ts
nodes.summary: Server health router. Two publicProcedure routes: `live` (always returns 200 with `{ status: 'healthy', buildSha, environment, timestamp, uptimeMs, url }`; `spec.security` is wiped to `[]` so it shows up in OpenAPI as unauthenticated) and `ready` (runs every entry in the `serviceChecks` object via `runCheck`, which wraps each check in a 1.5s timeout and returns `{ status, latencyMs, error? }`; throws a typed `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` 503 error with the per-check data when any service is unhealthy). Helpers: `getErrorMessage`, `withTimeout`, `runCheck`, `buildBaseHealth`, `checkDatabase`. The `serviceChecks` map is the single extension point — `database: checkDatabase` is the only one today.
nodes.languageNotes: Five region markers with #region/#endregion comments. The `runCheck` helper always times out at 1.5s (`HEALTHCHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`).

nodes.summary: Exported oRPC router with the `live` and `ready` procedures.

Imports every sub-router (agent, contact, experiences, github-config, github, health, portfolio, profile, projects, resume, stacks) and assembles them into the single `appRouter` object. Also exports the `AppRouter` type (typeof appRouter) and the `AppRouterClient = RouterClient<typeof appRouter>` for client-side consumers.
nodes.languageNotes: Eleven router sub-objects composed into one. The keys are the public oRPC client namespaces (agent, github, githubConfig, health, experiences, projects, stacks, contact, portfolio, profile, resume).

nodes.summary: Portfolio row → output mappers. Four row types (`StackRow`, `ProjectStackJoin`, `ProjectRow`, `ExperienceRow`) plus four mappers (`toStackOutput`, `toProjectOutput`, `toExperienceOutput`, `toContactOutput`) that translate Drizzle-shaped rows (with `portfolioEntryId: string | null`) into the core `*Output` types (with the derived `includedInPortfolio: boolean = !!portfolioEntryId` and coalesced `updatedAt`/`createdAt` defaults of `new Date()`).
nodes.languageNotes: Pure data transformation — no I/O. `toProjectOutput` recursively maps each `ProjectStackJoin.stack` through `toStackOutput` and filters out nulls. The contact mapper copies the contact's type/value/icon verbatim and adds the `includedInPortfolio` flag.

nodes.name: packages/api/src/routers/portfolio.queries.ts
nodes.summary: RSQL filter parser for the portfolio list endpoint. Self-contained: tokenizer (Tokenize), recursive-descent parser (Parser with parseOr/parseAnd/parseGroup/parseComparison), AST-to-Drizzle SQL adapter (astToSql), public entry `parseRsql(input)` and `buildPortfolioEntityFilter(filter, type)`. Supports the standard RSQL operators: ==/=, !=, >=, >, <=, <, =in=, =out=, =like=, =ilike=, plus `;` for AND and the keyword `or`. The supported selectors per entity type are encoded in `ENTITY_COLUMNS` (title, year, name, type, id, sortOrder) and the four supported entity types are encoded in `PORTFOLIO_ENTITY_TYPES` ('experience', 'project', 'stack', 'contact'). Throws `RsqlFilterError` (status 400) on bad input.
nodes.languageNotes: Includes its own AST type (comparison | and | or), Token union, and the `isEntityType` type guard. `ENTITY_COLUMNS` maps each entity to the physical column name it uses for the 'title' selector (e.g. stack uses 'name' as its title column).

nodes.name: packages/api/src/routers/portfolio.router.ts
nodes.summary: Public portfolio router. Two procedures: `list` (publicProcedure, GET, takes `PortfolioListInputSchema` with an optional RSQL `filter` string, returns experiences + projects + stacks + contacts + nextCursor — wraps the rsql parse in a try/catch and re-throws as `ORPCError('BAD_REQUEST')`), and `toggle` (protectedProcedure, POST, takes type+entityId+included, asserts entity exists in the matching repo, finds-or-creates a `portfolioEntry`, then `syncPortfolioFK` updates the entity's `portfolioEntryId` column to point at the entry or null). Three private helpers: `syncPortfolioFK`, `assertEntityExists`, `listAllOptedIn`.
nodes.languageNotes: The `syncPortfolioFK` helper handles all four entity types (experience, project, stack, contact) with one branch each; the contact branch uses `userRepository.findFirst()` to find the admin and updates by `(userId, type)`. `assertEntityExists` does the same and throws `ORPCError('NOT_FOUND')` when missing.

nodes.name: packages/api/src/routers/profile.router.ts

Three procedures: `get` (protected, GET, returns the current user's profile + contacts — accepts an optional `disableContacts` boolean to drop contacts from the response), `getContacts` (public, GET, returns the admin's contacts via `contactRepository.getAdminContact`), and `update` (protected, POST, takes `ProfileUpdateInputSchema`, performs an email-collision check that throws the typed `EMAIL_TAKEN` 409 error, clears `emailVerified` when the email changes, updates the user, and upserts the contact list). Includes a private `toProfileOutput` mapper that runs the result through `ProfileOutputSchema.parse`.
nodes.languageNotes: Single-user portfolio: profile endpoints always operate on `context.session.user.id`. `EMAIL_TAKEN` is a typed oRPC error (409) so the dashboard form can render the message verbatim.

nodes.summary: Projects CRUD router. Six protectedProcedure routes: list (GET all + stacks), get (by id, nullable), create, update (id + data), reorder, delete — plus `toggleArchived` (POST id → returns the updated project, throws `NOT_FOUND` if missing). All handlers delegate to `projectRepository` and map through `toProjectOutput`.

Exports `ResumeBuilderData` (the `{ portfolio: { experiences, projects, stacks, contacts }, profile: { name, email } }` shape consumed by the resume generate handler) and `buildResumeDocument(data)` (returns `{ params: DocumentParams, layout: { tagged: true, margins: 52/52/52/52 } }` for pdfnative). The builder filters the portfolio to opted-in items only (excluding archived projects) and assembles DocumentBlocks for the heading, contacts, EXPERIENCE/PROJECTS/SKILLS sections. Two private constants (SPACING, COLORS) and four helpers (stripHtml, extractBullets, displayContact, toContactMap, formatDateRange).

Block assembly is hand-coded. Bullets are pulled from
  • ...
    • spans in the experience description with a fallback to plain stripped text. Contact display strips http(s):// and leading www. for resume use.

nodes.name: packages/api/src/routers/resume.router.ts
nodes.summary: Resume CRUD + generate router. Six procedures: `list` (public, GET all resumes), `get` (public, by id), `getDefault` (public), `setDefault` (protected, POST id), `generate` (protected, POST — fetches portfolio + profile, builds the PDF via `buildResumeDocument` + `buildDocumentPDFBytes`, uploads to the R2 mediaBucket at `resumes/SalahMohsen_Resume_YYYY-MM-DD.pdf`, and persists the resume row), `delete` (protected, accepts `DeleteInputSchema` of ids, deletes the matching R2 objects and DB rows). Includes `fetchPortfolioData` (loads opted-in experiences/projects/stacks/contacts through the portfolio repos) and `formatFilename` (today's date in YYYY-MM-DD).

nodes.name: packages/api/src/routers/stacks.router.ts
nodes.summary: Tech-stacks CRUD router. Five protectedProcedure routes (list, create, update, reorder, delete) plus one publicProcedure route (`get` by id, nullable). `create` and `update` both check for an existing stack with the same name and throw `ORPCError('CONFLICT', ...)` if so. `create` auto-assigns the next sortOrder by `max(all.sortOrder) + 1` (or 0 for the first row).

nodes.summary: Package manifest for @tsu-stack/auth. Name is private, ESM, with the `#@/*` -> ./src/*.ts subpath alias and four exports (`.`, `./index`, `./react`, `./react/*`). Runtime deps: @better-auth/drizzle-adapter (the relations-v2 unstable build), @better-auth/passkey, @tsu-stack/email + @tsu-stack/env (workspace), better-auth. Peer deps: @tanstack/react-query + @tanstack/react-start + @tsu-stack/db.

nodes.name: packages/auth/src/auth.ts
nodes.summary: Better Auth server config. Constructs the `auth` instance with: pg drizzle adapter (relations-v2), openAPI plugin (deepSpace theme) + passkey plugin, 5-minute cookie cache, joins experimental, registration-closed `databaseHooks.user.create.before` that throws `APIError('FORBIDDEN', { code: 'REGISTRATION_CLOSED' })` once any user exists (single-portfolio site), email verification + change-email with the @tsu-stack/email `VerifyEmail` template, `user.additionalFields.summary` + `phone`, and a GitHub social provider that is only mounted when `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` and `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` are present (otherwise it throws at runtime if not in build mode). The GitHub scope list enumerates all 30+ standard OAuth scopes so the access token can read private repos. Exports `AuthSession = typeof auth.$Infer.Session`.
nodes.languageNotes: The GitHub scope list is the full set per GitHub's docs (comment cites the OAuth apps scopes page). `trustedOrigins` is derived from VITE_WEB_URL. `basePath` is the VITE_SERVER_URL pathname joined with 'auth' via node:path/posix.

Exports `$getUser` (the GET server function that wraps `_getUser` — used by the auth query factory) and the server-only `_getUser(query?)` helper that calls `auth.api.getSession({ headers, query, returnHeaders: true })` and forwards any Set-Cookie headers to the client response via `setResponseHeader('Set-Cookie', cookies)`. Returns the user or null.
nodes.languageNotes: The `GetUserServerQuery` shape is private to the file (used by both middlewares + the server function). `createServerOnlyFn` keeps `_getUser` from being bundled into the client.

nodes.name: $getUser
nodes.summary: TanStack Start GET server function — returns the current user (or null).

nodes.name: _getUser
nodes.summary: Server-only utility — calls auth.api.getSession and forwards Set-Cookie headers. Used by $getUser and the middlewares.

nodes.name: packages/auth/src/react/tanstack-start/hooks.ts
nodes.summary: React hooks for the auth user query. `useAuth()` returns `{ isPending, user }` from `useQuery(getAuthUserQueryOptions())`. `useAuthSuspense()` returns `{ user }` from `useSuspenseQuery(getAuthUserQueryOptions())`.
nodes.languageNotes: Two hook functions. The suspense variant is the canonical hook to use in protected layouts since the auth query is preloaded by the _auth layout's beforeLoad.

nodes.name: useAuth
nodes.summary: Read the current user from the React Query cache (pending + user).

nodes.name: useAuthSuspense
nodes.summary: Read the current user (suspense-flavor, throws until resolved).

nodes.name: packages/auth/src/react/tanstack-start/middleware.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack Start auth middlewares. Two exports: `authMiddleware` (creates middleware that calls `_getUser()` — i.e. honors the cookie cache, sets 401 + throws if no user, adds the user to the next context) and `freshAuthMiddleware` (same but calls `_getUser({ disableCookieCache: true })` so the session is always re-read from the DB; recommended for sensitive/destructive mutations).
nodes.languageNotes: Both middlewares are typed via `createMiddleware().server(...)`. The 401 is set via `setResponseStatus(401)` before throwing.

nodes.name: authMiddleware
nodes.summary: Auth middleware that respects the cookie cache (5 min default).

nodes.name: freshAuthMiddleware
nodes.summary: Auth middleware that bypasses the cookie cache (always reads from DB).

nodes.name: packages/auth/src/react/tanstack-start/queries.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack Query factory for the auth user. Exports `authQueryKeys = { user: ['user'], currentToken: ['user', 'current-token'] }`, the `getAuthUserQueryOptions()` factory (5 min staleTime, 10 min gcTime, refetchOnReconnect/windowFocus 'always', refetchOnMount false, queryKey authQueryKeys.user, queryFn calls $getUser, retry 3 with exponential backoff capped at 3s), and the `AuthQueryResult` type alias.
nodes.languageNotes: The staleTime (5 min) matches the cookie cache TTL in auth.ts — intentional alignment so React Query and the auth cookie cache expire together. The factory returns the result wrapped in `?? null` so the hook is total.

nodes.summary: Query key namespace for auth queries (user + current-token).

nodes.name: getAuthUserQueryOptions
nodes.summary: Query options factory — 5 min staleTime, 10 min gcTime, always-refetch on focus/reconnect.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/index.ts
nodes.summary: Public entry for @tsu-stack/db. Wires up two Drizzle instances: (1) a module-level HTTP Drizzle singleton (used by Better Auth's drizzle adapter and module-load wiring); (2) a per-request WebSocket Drizzle created by `createDb()` and stored in AsyncLocalStorage via `runWithDb(...)`. `getDb()` reads the per-request WS instance or falls back to the HTTP singleton (logs once). Re-exports the repositories barrel and `drizzle-orm/sql`. `checkIsDbReady()` runs `SELECT 1`.
nodes.languageNotes: See ADR-0009 for why the WS pool is per-request instead of closed eagerly. The HTTP fallback is no longer a hard 500 for missed `runWithDb` calls but transactions still require a real WS scope.

nodes.summary: Composite relations object merging appRelationPart (hand-written app relations) and authRelations (auto-generated by `npx auth generate`). Passed to both Drizzle instances.

nodes.name: db
nodes.summary: Module-level HTTP Drizzle singleton. Stateless and safe to share across requests in Cloudflare Workers.

nodes.name: WsDb
nodes.summary: Per-request WebSocket Drizzle instance type. Supports transactions; required for repositories that need prepared-statement reuse.

nodes.name: createDb
nodes.summary: Builds a fresh Neon Pool + drizzleWs(relations) for a single request scope.

nodes.name: runWithDb
nodes.summary: Run `fn` with the per-request WS Drizzle instance available via getDb() inside the AsyncLocalStorage scope.

nodes.name: getDb
nodes.summary: Returns the per-request WS Drizzle from AsyncLocalStorage; falls back to the HTTP singleton (and logs once) if no scope is active. Transaction calls still require a real WS scope.

nodes.name: checkIsDbReady
nodes.summary: Liveness probe — runs SELECT 1 via the HTTP singleton and returns true on success.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/migrate.ts
nodes.summary: Subpath export ./migrate. `migrateDatabase()` wraps `drizzle-orm/neon-http/migrator.migrate(db, { migrationsFolder: ./migrations })` against the HTTP singleton. Used by the deploy pipeline.

nodes.name: migrateDatabase
nodes.summary: Apply pending migrations from ./migrations against the HTTP Drizzle singleton.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/repositories/index.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel for the repositories subpackage. Re-exports every named repository plus two extra type-only exports: `DbExecutor` (from github-cache) and `PortfolioEntryEntity` (from portfolio-entry).

nodes.name: packages/db/src/repositories/better-auth-account.repository.ts
nodes.summary: Read access to Better Auth's `account` table for the per-request GitHub OAuth access token. `findGitHubAccessTokenForUser(userId)` reads `account.accessToken` where `providerId = "github"`; `findGithubScopesForUser(userId)` reads the space-separated `scope` column. The token is used to build `privateOctokit` with whatever scopes the user actually granted at sign-in time (e.g. `repo`), instead of the static PAT in `github_config`.
nodes.languageNotes: Composite key: (userId, providerId). The `scope` check is what prompts the UI to ask the user to re-authorize when their token lacks `repo`.

nodes.name: betterAuthAccountRepository
nodes.summary: Repository object exposing two query methods (findGitHubAccessTokenForUser, findGithubScopesForUser).

nodes.name: findGitHubAccessTokenForUser
nodes.summary: Return the access_token from the user's GitHub account row, or null if no GitHub account is linked.

nodes.name: findGithubScopesForUser
nodes.summary: Return the space-separated scope string from the user's GitHub account row, or null.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/repositories/contact.repository.ts
nodes.summary: CRUD for the `contact` table. Exports `ContactEntity` (InferSelectModel), `UpsertContactItem` (form input). Methods: `findByUserId`, `findOptedInByUserId(userId, extraWhere?)` (filters to rows with a non-null portfolioEntryId for the public portfolio), `getAdminContact` (all rows), `upsert(userId, input)` (diffs by type, creates portfolio_entry rows in the same transaction when `includedInPortfolio` is set, leaves untouched rows in place).
nodes.languageNotes: Dedup-by-type happens before the transaction so the unique (user_id, type) constraint cannot be violated by the form's "Add contact" button producing duplicates.

nodes.name: ContactEntity
nodes.summary: InferSelectModel<typeof contact> — a single contact row.

nodes.name: ContactSchemaSelect
nodes.summary: Inferred from the contact Drizzle schema (defined in #@/types/contact.schema.ts and re-imported here for the return type of getAdminContact).

nodes.name: UpsertContactItem
nodes.summary: Form input shape — id is optional, type is the contactTypeEnum union, value/icon are strings, includedInPortfolio is optional.

nodes.name: contactRepository
nodes.summary: Repository object for the contact table.

nodes.name: findByUserId
nodes.summary: Drizzle relational query for all contact rows belonging to a user.

nodes.name: findOptedInByUserId
nodes.summary: Find contacts that are opted into the public portfolio (portfolioEntryId is not null), with an optional extraWhere SQL fragment for additional filtering.

nodes.name: getAdminContact
nodes.summary: Return all contact rows (admin view — no userId filter).

nodes.name: upsert
nodes.summary: Sync a user's contacts from a form payload. Dedupes by type, patches rows with an `id` (preserving portfolioEntryId), inserts rows without. For items where `includedInPortfolio` is set, creates or removes the matching portfolioEntry in the same transaction.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/repositories/experience.repository.ts
nodes.summary: CRUD for the `experience` table. Exports `ExperienceEntity`, `CreateExperienceData` (Omit id+createdAt+updatedAt), `UpdateExperienceData = Partial<CreateExperienceData>`, `ReorderExperienceItem = {id, sortOrder}`. `findAll/findById` eager-load projects → stacks. `findOptedIn(extraWhere?)` filters to non-null portfolioEntryId. `create` auto-assigns the next sortOrder (max+1) and a uuid, optionally creating a portfolioEntry. `update` syncs the portfolioEntry inside the same transaction. `reorder` validates the ids and updates sortOrder per item in a transaction. `delete` returns the deleted id or null.
nodes.languageNotes: The auto-sortOrder-on-create only looks at the experience table (not joined tables), so inserting two experiences back-to-back will give them the same sortOrder if findAll runs in between. Acceptable for the dashboard's "Add new" button which always precedes a manual reorder.

nodes.name: ReorderExperienceItem
nodes.summary: Id + sortOrder pair used by the reorder endpoint.

nodes.name: experienceRepository
nodes.summary: Repository object for the experience table.

nodes.name: findAll
nodes.summary: Return all experiences with their projects (eager-loaded) and each project's stacks, ordered by sortOrder then title.

nodes.name: findOptedIn
nodes.summary: Find experiences opted into the public portfolio, with an optional extraWhere SQL fragment.

nodes.name: findById
nodes.summary: Find one experience by id (eager-loads projects → stacks) or undefined if not found.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Insert a new experience with auto-incremented sortOrder; optionally create a portfolioEntry in the same transaction. Returns the created row via findById.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Patch an experience; sync the portfolioEntry membership inside the same transaction when `options.includedInPortfolio` is explicitly set. Returns null when not found.

nodes.name: reorder
nodes.summary: Bulk-update sortOrder for the given id+sortOrder pairs in a single transaction. Throws if any id is missing.

nodes.name: delete
nodes.summary: Delete an experience by id; return the deleted id or null.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/repositories/github-cache.repository.ts
nodes.summary: CRUD for the four GitHub-side tables: `github_response_cache` (cached GitHub HTTP responses with etag + namespace version), `github_revalidation_signal` (per-signal-key invalidation timestamps), `github_cache_namespace` (per-namespace version counter), `github_webhook_event` (idempotency log). Every method takes an optional `executor: DbExecutor = getDb()` so callers can run inside a transaction. Also re-exports the `DbExecutor` type = WsDb | NeonTransaction<typeof relations>.
nodes.languageNotes: The `executor` parameter is the standard repository seam — repositories always take one so callers can drop the call inside a tx without re-implementing the query.

nodes.name: DbExecutor
nodes.summary: Union: WsDb | NeonTransaction<typeof relations>. Lets repositories run inside or outside a transaction.

nodes.name: UpsertGitHubResponseCacheInput
nodes.summary: Input shape for upsertResponseCacheEntry — cacheKey, namespace, namespaceVersion, owner, status, etag/lastModified, payload, staleAt/expiresAt.

nodes.name: RecordGitHubWebhookDeliveryInput
nodes.summary: Input for recordWebhookDelivery — deliveryId, event, action/scope/payload (all optional).

nodes.name: githubCacheRepository
nodes.summary: Repository object for the four GitHub cache tables.

nodes.name: clearAll
nodes.summary: Wipe the response cache, revalidation signals, and namespace versions (used by tests + admin reset).

nodes.name: findNamespaceVersion
nodes.summary: Look up the version row for a namespace, or null.

nodes.name: findResponseCacheEntry
nodes.summary: Look up a cached GitHub response by cache key.

nodes.name: findRevalidationSignals
nodes.summary: Return all revalidation-signal rows for the given signal keys, newest first.

nodes.name: findLatestRevalidationSignalAt
nodes.summary: Return the most recent updatedAt across the given signal keys, or null if none exist.

nodes.name: markWebhookDeliveryProcessed
nodes.summary: Stamp the webhook_event row's processedAt to now(); returns the updated row or null.

nodes.name: markRevalidationSignals
nodes.summary: Upsert revalidation-signal rows for each signal key — on conflict, refresh updatedAt to now().

nodes.name: bumpNamespaceVersion
nodes.summary: Upsert a namespace row with version=1 (or version+1 on conflict) and updatedAt=now().

nodes.name: recordWebhookDelivery
nodes.summary: Insert a webhook_event row keyed by deliveryId; on conflict do nothing (idempotency log).

nodes.name: upsertResponseCacheEntry
nodes.summary: Upsert a github_response_cache row; on conflict, refresh every field plus updatedAt.

nodes.name: clearByOwner
nodes.summary: Delete all response-cache rows for an owner.

nodes.name: deleteResponseCacheEntry
nodes.summary: Delete a single response-cache row by (cacheKey, owner).

nodes.name: packages/db/src/repositories/github-config.repository.ts
nodes.summary: CRUD for the `github_config` table (PAT + public username). Methods: `findPublicGithubSourceSettings()` — most-recently-updated row with non-null token or username (the source the public site should read from); `findByUserId(userId)` — the dashboard's per-user config; `upsert(userId, {githubToken?, clearGithubToken?, githubUsername})` — preserves the existing token unless `clearGithubToken` is set.

nodes.name: UpdateGithubConfigData
nodes.summary: Update payload — githubToken (optional new value), clearGithubToken (boolean, set null even if not provided), githubUsername (required).

nodes.name: findPublicGithubSourceSettings
nodes.summary: Return the most-recently-updated github_config row with a non-null token or username, or null.

nodes.name: findByUserId
nodes.summary: Return the github_config row for a user, or undefined.

nodes.name: upsert
nodes.summary: Insert or update a github_config row. Trims the token, applies `clearGithubToken` semantics, and preserves the existing token when no new value is given.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/repositories/portfolio-entry.repository.ts
nodes.summary: CRUD for the `portfolio_entry` table. `PortfolioEntryEntity = InferSelectModel`, `CreatePortfolioEntryData = Omit id+createdAt+updatedAt`. Methods: `findByTypeAndEntityId`, `findById`, `create` (assigns a uuid), `deleteByTypeAndEntityId`, `deleteById` — each returning the deleted/created row or null.
nodes.languageNotes: The unique index on (type, entity_id) means a given entity can be in the portfolio at most once; the repositories that own the entity (experience, project, stack, contact) manage the portfolioEntryId FK on their own rows so the toggle endpoint updates both sides in one transaction.

nodes.name: portfolioEntryRepository
nodes.summary: Repository object for the portfolio_entry join table.

nodes.name: findByTypeAndEntityId
nodes.summary: Look up a portfolio_entry by its (type, entityId) key, or undefined.

nodes.name: findById
nodes.summary: Look up a portfolio_entry by id.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Insert a new portfolio_entry with a generated uuid; return the row or null.

nodes.name: deleteByTypeAndEntityId
nodes.summary: Delete a portfolio_entry by (type, entityId); return the deleted id or null.

nodes.name: deleteById
nodes.summary: Delete a portfolio_entry by id; return the deleted id or null.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/repositories/project.repository.ts
nodes.summary: CRUD for the `project` + `project_stack` join table. Exports `ProjectEntity`, `CreateProjectData` (with optional `stackIds: string[]`), `UpdateProjectData = Partial<CreateProjectData>`, `ReorderProjectItem = {id, sortOrder}`. `findAll/findById` eager-loads `stacks.stack`. `create` accepts `stackIds`; the transaction validates they exist, then inserts project + projectStack rows in one go. `update` rebuilds the projectStack set when `stackIds` is provided. `reorder` validates ids. `toggleArchived` flips the boolean. `delete` returns the deleted id or null.
nodes.languageNotes: The update path intentionally spreads each `projectFields.*` into `updateData` only if defined — `null` clears the column, `undefined` leaves it alone. Avoids clobbering fields the form didn't touch.

nodes.name: CreateProjectData
nodes.summary: Insert shape — Omit id+createdAt+updatedAt, plus optional stackIds.

nodes.name: UpdateProjectData
nodes.summary: Partial of CreateProjectData, but the non-undefined-only update semantics live in the `update` function.

nodes.name: findAll
nodes.summary: Find all projects with their stacks (eager-loaded), ordered by sortOrder then title.

nodes.name: findOptedIn
nodes.summary: Find projects opted into the public portfolio with optional extraWhere.

nodes.name: findById
nodes.summary: Find one project by id with its stacks, or undefined.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Insert a project, optionally with a portfolioEntry and a set of projectStack rows. Throws if any stackId is missing. Returns the new row via findById.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Patch a project (only-defined fields, nulls clear, undefined leaves alone). Rebuilds the projectStack set when `stackIds` is provided. Syncs portfolioEntry inside the same transaction when `options.includedInPortfolio` is explicitly set.

nodes.name: reorder
nodes.summary: Bulk-update sortOrder in a transaction; throws if any id is missing.

nodes.name: toggleArchived
nodes.summary: Flip the project.isArchived boolean. Returns the updated project, or null when missing.

nodes.name: delete
nodes.summary: Delete a project by id; returns the deleted id or null.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/repositories/resume.repository.ts
nodes.summary: CRUD for the `resume` table. Exports `ResumeEntity`, `CreateResumeData` (Omit id+createdAt+updatedAt+default), `UpdateResumeData = Partial<CreateResumeData>`. `findAll` orders by createdAt desc. `findDefault` returns the row with `default=true`. `create` always sets `default=false` (the admin must explicitly promote). `setDefault(id)` runs a transaction that flips the existing default off and the new one on. `deleteMany(ids)` returns the deleted id+r2Key pairs (so the caller can clean up the R2 object).

nodes.name: findAll
nodes.summary: Return all resume rows ordered by createdAt desc.

nodes.name: findById
nodes.summary: Find one resume by id, or undefined.

nodes.name: findDefault
nodes.summary: Return the resume row with `default=true`, or undefined.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Insert a resume row; default=false (no implicit default on create).

nodes.name: setDefault
nodes.summary: Transactionally clear the existing default and promote the given row.

nodes.name: deleteMany
nodes.summary: Delete many resumes by id; return deleted id+r2Key pairs so the caller can clean R2.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/repositories/stack.repository.ts
nodes.summary: CRUD for the `stack` table. Exports `StackEntity`, `CreateStackData` (Omit id+createdAt+updatedAt), `UpdateStackData = Partial<CreateStackData>`, `ReorderStackItem = {id, sortOrder}`. `findAll/findById/findByName` for reads; `findOptedIn(extraWhere?)` for the public portfolio. `create` optionally creates a portfolioEntry in the same transaction. `update` patches fields and syncs portfolioEntry membership. `reorder` validates ids. `delete` returns the deleted id or null.

nodes.name: findAll
nodes.summary: Return all stacks ordered by sortOrder then name.

nodes.name: findOptedIn
nodes.summary: Find stacks opted into the public portfolio with optional extraWhere.

nodes.name: findById
nodes.summary: Find one stack by id, or undefined.

nodes.name: findByName
nodes.summary: Find one stack by its unique name, or undefined.

nodes.name: create
nodes.summary: Insert a stack; optionally create a portfolioEntry in the same transaction.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Patch a stack and sync the portfolioEntry membership inside the same transaction when `options.includedInPortfolio` is explicitly set.

nodes.name: reorder
nodes.summary: Bulk-update sortOrder for the given pairs in a transaction; throws if any id is missing.

nodes.name: delete
nodes.summary: Delete a stack by id; returns the deleted id or null.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/repositories/user.repository.ts
nodes.summary: Read/update access to the Better Auth `user` table for the API profile surface. `findById`, `findFirst` (single-user app), `findByEmail`, `update(id, input: UserSchemaInsert)`. Writes here bypass Better Auth — used for dashboard-triggered name/email changes and the profile endpoint round-trip.
nodes.languageNotes: The `user` table is owned by Better Auth for the auth lifecycle; this repo is for the profile surface (name + email changes) that Better Auth's API does not own.

nodes.name: findById
nodes.summary: Return a user row by id, or null.

nodes.name: findFirst
nodes.summary: Return the first user row (single-user portfolio app).

nodes.name: findByEmail
nodes.summary: Return the user row matching an email, or null.

nodes.name: update
nodes.summary: Patch a user row (name/email via dashboard). Returns the refreshed row or null.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/schema/auth.schema.ts
nodes.summary: Better Auth tables: user (id, name, email, emailVerified, image, createdAt, updatedAt, summary, phone), session (token, userId, ipAddress, userAgent, expiresAt, indexes on userId), account (OAuth + password), verification (identifier, value, expiresAt, indexes on identifier), passkey (credentialID, publicKey, counter, deviceType, backedUp, transports, aaguid). `authRelations = defineRelationsPart(...)` declares user↔sessions, user↔accounts, user↔passkeys, plus each .user back-relation. Auto-generated by `pnpm auth:generate`; do not hand-edit.
nodes.languageNotes: `.defaultNow()` sets the timestamp on insert; `.$onUpdate(() => new Date())` auto-bumps on every update. The relations use the new `defineRelationsPart` API (Drizzle 1.0 alpha).

nodes.name: packages/db/src/schema/contact.schema.ts
nodes.summary: `contactTypeEnum` (website, email, phone, location, linkedin, github, x, youtube) and the `contact` table (id, userId, type, value, icon, portfolioEntryId, createdAt, updatedAt) with a composite primary key on (userId, type). The `id` column is a stable uuid text column added by the 20260705102604 migration.
nodes.languageNotes: Composite PK on (userId, type) preserves the original uniqueness guarantee; the new id column is a stable addressable key for the API.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/schema/experience.schema.ts
nodes.summary: `experience` table (id, title, organization, description, fromDate, toDate, sortOrder, isPresent, portfolioEntryId, createdAt, updatedAt) with indexes on sortOrder and portfolioEntryId. `fromDate`/`toDate` are text (ISO 8601) — preserved as strings so the date format is portable across Postgres versions.
nodes.languageNotes: Timestamps use `withTimezone: true` so the date arithmetic in the API is timezone-aware.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/schema/github-cache.schema.ts
nodes.summary: Four tables that back the GitHub local-first cache: `github_response_cache` (cacheKey, namespace, owner, namespaceVersion, status, etag, lastModified, payload jsonb, fetchedAt, staleAt, expiresAt, createdAt, updatedAt) with indexes on namespace and owner; `github_revalidation_signal` (signalKey, updatedAt — PK on signalKey, no FK); `github_cache_namespace` (namespace, version, updatedAt); `github_webhook_event` (deliveryId PK, event, action, scope, payload, receivedAt, processedAt — webhook idempotency log).
nodes.languageNotes: The unique signalKey is the cache-invalidation primitive — bumping a signal row's updatedAt invalidates every entry subscribed to it. See ADR-0011 for signal vs namespace invalidation.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/schema/github-config.schema.ts
nodes.summary: `github_config` table (userId PK + FK to user ON DELETE CASCADE, githubToken text nullable, githubUsername text nullable, createdAt, updatedAt) with an index on githubUsername. One row per user.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/schema/index.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel for the schema subpackage. Re-exports all pgTable/pgEnum/enum values from auth, contact, experience, github-cache, github-config, portfolio-entry, project, resume, and stack schemas.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/schema/portfolio-entry.schema.ts
nodes.summary: `portfolioEntryTypeEnum` (experience, project, stack, contact) and the `portfolio_entry` table (id text PK, type enum, entityId text, createdAt, updatedAt — both withTimezone) with a unique index on (type, entityId). Also exports `PortfolioEntryType` = (typeof portfolioEntryTypeEnum.enumValues)[number].
nodes.languageNotes: The unique (type, entity_id) means each entity can be in the portfolio at most once — the entity repositories manage the portfolioEntryId FK in lockstep.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/schema/project.schema.ts
nodes.summary: Two tables: `project` (id text PK, logo text, repos text[] (array of repo strings), demoUrl text, year integer not null, title, summary, description, sortOrder, isArchived, experienceId FK to experience ON DELETE SET NULL, isPresent, portfolioEntryId FK to portfolio_entry ON DELETE SET NULL, createdAt/updatedAt with timezone) with indexes on sortOrder, experienceId, portfolioEntryId; `project_stack` (id text PK, projectId FK to project ON DELETE CASCADE, stackId FK to stack ON DELETE CASCADE) with indexes on projectId, stackId, and a unique index on (projectId, stackId) preventing duplicate links.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/schema/relations.ts
nodes.summary: `appRelationPart = defineRelationsPart(schema, ...)` — the hand-written half of the relations composition. Declares: githubConfig→user (1:1), contact→user (n:1) + contact→portfolioEntry (n:1, optional), experience→projects (1:n) + experience→portfolioEntry (n:1, optional), project→experience (n:1, optional) + project→stacks via projectStack (1:n) + project→portfolioEntry (n:1, optional), projectStack→project + projectStack→stack (n:1 each), stack→projects via projectStack (1:n) + stack→portfolioEntry (n:1, optional), plus empty relation blocks for portfolioEntry and resume.
nodes.languageNotes: Merged with `authRelations` (from auth.schema.ts) in #@/index via `{ ...appRelationPart, ...authRelations }`. The new `defineRelationsPart` API lets you split a relations graph across files.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/schema/resume.schema.ts
nodes.summary: `resumeAuthorEnum` (admin, agent) and the `resume` table (id text PK, prompt text nullable, author enum, filename, r2Key, default boolean default false, createdAt, updatedAt — both with timezone). Also exports `ResumeAuthor` = (typeof resumeAuthorEnum.enumValues)[number].

nodes.name: packages/db/src/schema/stack.schema.ts
nodes.summary: `stack` table (id text PK, name text not null with unique index, description text, icon text, sortOrder integer, portfolioEntryId FK to portfolio_entry ON DELETE SET NULL, createdAt, updatedAt — both with timezone) with a unique index on name and indexes on sortOrder and portfolioEntryId.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/types/auth.schema.ts
nodes.summary: Inferred Drizzle insert/select types for the auth tables (user, session, account, verification, passkey). Exports 10 types: `UserSchemaInsert` (Omit createdAt+updatedAt+emailVerified+id — the dashboard-safe subset), `UserSchemaSelect`, plus the 4-session/account/verification/passkey Insert/Select pairs.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/types/contact.schema.ts
nodes.summary: Inferred Drizzle Insert/Select types for the contact table: `ContactSchemaInsert = typeof contact.$inferInsert`, `ContactSchemaSelect = typeof contact.$inferSelect`.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/types/experience.schema.ts
nodes.summary: Inferred Drizzle Insert/Select types for the experience table: `ExperienceSchemaInsert`, `ExperienceSchemaSelect`.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/types/github-cache.schema.ts
nodes.summary: Inferred Drizzle Insert/Select types for the four GitHub cache tables. Exports 8 types: `GithubResponseCacheSchemaInsert/Select`, `GithubRevalidationSignalSchemaInsert/Select`, `GithubCacheNamespaceSchemaInsert/Select`, `GithubWebhookEventSchemaInsert/Select`.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/types/github-config.schema.ts
nodes.summary: Inferred Drizzle Insert/Select types for github_config: `GithubConfigSchemaInsert`, `GithubConfigSchemaSelect`.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/types/index.ts
nodes.summary: Type-only barrel for the inferred Drizzle types. `export type *` from every per-table types module so consumers can import all of them from `@tsu-stack/db/types`.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/types/portfolio-entry.schema.ts
nodes.summary: Inferred Drizzle Insert/Select types for portfolio_entry: `PortfolioEntrySchemaInsert`, `PortfolioEntrySchemaSelect`.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/types/project.schema.ts
nodes.summary: Inferred Drizzle Insert/Select types for both project tables: `ProjectSchemaInsert/Select`, `ProjectStackSchemaInsert/Select`.

nodes.name: packages/db/src/types/resume.schema.ts
nodes.summary: `ResumeSchemaSelect = InferSelectModel<typeof resume>`, `ResumeSchemaInsert = InferInsertModel<typeof resume>` (uses the explicit generic instead of `$inferSelect` because the import is a `type` import).

nodes.name: packages/db/src/types/stack.schema.ts
nodes.summary: Inferred Drizzle Insert/Select types for stack: `StackSchemaInsert`, `StackSchemaSelect`.

nodes.name: packages/db/tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: Tsconfig for @tsu-stack/db. Extends @tsu-stack/tsconfig/tsconfig.base.json, includes all .ts/.tsx files in the package, excludes node_modules. No compiler overrides — the Drizzle tables use plain TS, not JSX.

nodes.name: packages/email/package.json
nodes.summary: Workspace manifest for @tsu-stack/email (v0.0.0, private, ESM). #@/* import alias → ./src/*.tsx. Single subpath export `.` → ./src/index.ts. Script `email:dev` runs the react-email dev server on port 3010 against src/templates. Deps: react-email, resend, react, react-dom, @tanstack/react-start, @tsu-stack/env. Dev deps: @react-email/ui, @tsu-stack/tsconfig, @types/{node,react}, typescript.

nodes.name: packages/email/src/index.ts
nodes.summary: Public entry for @tsu-stack/email. Re-exports `sendEmail` (the Resend-backed send function) and the five default-exported React Email templates: ResetPasswordEmail, SendMagicLinkEmail, SendVerificationOTP, VerifyEmail, WelcomeEmail.

nodes.name: packages/email/src/react-email-jsx.d.ts
nodes.summary: Ambient .d.ts that widens the global JSX.Element type to `ReactElement<unknown, unknown> | null | undefined`. Required so React Email components (which can return `JSX.Element | undefined` under React 19) typecheck in JSX positions. Also re-exports `ReactNode`. See resend/react-email#1432.

nodes.name: packages/email/src/resend.ts
nodes.summary: `sendEmail({subject, template: ReactNode, to})` — Renders the React Email template to HTML via `react-email.render`, then posts to Resend. Reads `EMAIL_FROM` (defaults to `contact@salahmohsen.com`) and `RESEND_API_KEY` from ENV_SERVER. Skips delivery (with a console.debug) when RESEND_API_KEY is unset; throws the Resend error if the send fails.
nodes.languageNotes: `template: ReactNode` (not ReactElement) so the Hono JSX `Element` type used by apps/server is assignable — `react-email.render` accepts ReactNode anyway.

nodes.name: packages/email/src/templates/layout-email.tsx
nodes.summary: `EmailLayout` — the shared visual shell for every transactional email. Wraps children in `<Html>` → `<Head>`/`<Preview>` → `<Tailwind>` → `<Body>` → `<Container>` → `<Section>` (rounded border + shadow). Used by every template in src/templates/.

nodes.name: packages/email/src/templates/reset-password-email.tsx
nodes.summary: Default-exported `ResetPasswordEmail({resetLink, username})` template. Renders a heading, "Hi {username}", instructions, and a blue Button (Tailwind class) linking to `resetLink`. Stamps `ResetPasswordEmail.PreviewProps` for the react-email dev server.

nodes.name: packages/email/src/templates/send-magic-link-email.tsx
nodes.summary: Default-exported `SendMagicLinkEmail({username, url, token})` template. Concatenates `url + "?token=" + token` into a single link, shows the Button + a copy-paste-friendly Text block. PreviewProps set to "https://example.com/magic-link" / "123456".
