nodes.name: packages/env/src/server/env.ts
nodes.summary: `ENV_SERVER` — the server-side environment singleton built via @t3-oss/env-core. `skipValidation: true` (Zod validation is bypassed for the 1s Cloudflare Workers startup budget; see ADR-0014). `emptyStringAsUndefined: true`. Schema declares DATABASE_URL, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET (min 32), NODE_ENV, WORKERS_CI_COMMIT_SHA, ENABLE_OPEN_API_DOCS, IS_BUILD, GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET, GITHUB_CLIENT_ID/SECRET, RESEND_API_KEY, EMAIL_FROM, OPENCODE_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, OLLAMA_BASE_URL (default https://ollama.salahmohsen.com), EMBEDDING_MODEL (default mxbai-embed-large, max 1536-d for Vectorize), AGENT_WORKER_URL. VITE_SERVER_URL + VITE_WEB_URL are normalized URL strings with dev defaults. `runtimeRequired()` helper makes a schema optional at build time (`IS_BUILD=true`) and required at runtime so the build can run without runtime-only secrets.
nodes.languageNotes: `process.env` is spread first, then the VITE_* URL defaults are applied so explicit defaults can backfill. ADR-0014 explains why validation is skipped and how the build pipeline keeps the secrets.

nodes.name: packages/env/src/utils/url.ts
nodes.summary: `normalizeUrlString(value)` — trims the input, prepends `http://` in dev / `https://` in production if the value has no scheme. `normalizedUrlSchema = z.preprocess(normalizeUrlString, z.url())` — the zod schema used by VITE_SERVER_URL / VITE_WEB_URL.

nodes.name: packages/env/src/web/env.isomorphic.ts
nodes.summary: `ENV_WEB_ISOMORPHIC` — the browser-safe env singleton (available in both client and SSR). Declares VITE_IMGPROXY_URL, VITE_SERVER_URL, VITE_WEB_URL via the same dev-default / production-required pattern. `clientPrefix: "VITE_"` enforces the Vite naming convention. `runtimeEnv: import.meta.env ?? process.env` so it works in both Vite (browser/SSR) and Workers (server) build modes.

nodes.name: packages/env/src/web/env.server.ts
nodes.summary: `ENV_WEB_SERVER` — the web-server-only env singleton (apps/web). Schema: NODE_ENV, SOURCE_COMMIT (default "unknown", Coolify autogenerates), IS_BUILD (stringbool), R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL (default placeholder during build, required at runtime), FILES_API_SECRET (default "dev-only-secret-do-not-use-in-production"). `runtimeEnv: process.env`.

nodes.name: packages/github/package.json
nodes.summary: Workspace manifest for @tsu-stack/github (private, ESM). #@/* → ./src/*.ts. Many subpath exports: cache (cache-policy, revalidation), infrastructure (octokit, cache), repo, runtime (bindings), shared (public-github-source), schemas, types, user, webhooks. Deps: @tsu-stack/{core,db,env}, octokit, zod. Dev deps: @tsu-stack/tsconfig, @types/node, typescript.

nodes.name: packages/github/src/index.ts
nodes.summary: Public entry for @tsu-stack/github. Re-exports the entire surface: all 17 repo-domain getter modules, cache, revalidation, octokit, runtime bindings, public-github-source, types, user getters, webhooks, and the `CommandPaletteSearchResult`/`MyIssuesResult`/`MyPullsResult` types (from repo/shared.types). Plus 7 type aliases that map schemas.ts names to shorter API names (DiscussionsResult, DiscussionSummary, IssueSummary, PullSummary, WorkflowRun, WorkflowRunPullRequestRef).

nodes.name: packages/github/src/infrastructure/cache/get-github-resource-local-first.ts
nodes.summary: One-line barrel that re-exports `getCachedGitHubRequest` from github-cache under the shorter name. Lets repo-domain modules import via the local-first path.

nodes.name: packages/github/src/infrastructure/cache/github-cache-policy.ts
nodes.summary: `githubCachePolicy` — the central `staleTimeMs`/`gcTimeMs` table for every GitHub resource family. Keys: viewer (5m/24h), reposList (2m/12h), list (30s/1h), mine (10s/15m), detail (5s/10m), activity (5s/10m), userActivity (1m/30m), status (5s/5m), workflowRun (5s/5m), contributions (15m/24h), repoMeta (1h/24h), repoParticipation (15m/24h), installationAccess (5m/24h), repoProtection (5m/24h).
nodes.languageNotes: `as const` so callers can narrow to literal values. Names match the resource family used by the repo-domain getters — `getRepoOverview` uses `policy.detail`, `getUserContributions` uses `policy.contributions`, etc.

nodes.name: packages/github/src/infrastructure/cache/github-cache.ts
nodes.summary: The local-first GitHub cache engine. Exports `bumpGitHubCacheNamespaces`, `markGitHubRevalidationSignals`, `getGitHubRevalidationSignals`, `getCachedGitHubRequest<TData>`, `getOrRevalidateGitHubResource`. The core path: read KV (fast) → fallback DB → if stale (namespace version mismatch, signal updated after fetchedAt, or past staleAt) call fetcher with conditional headers → on 304 refresh row → on 200 upsert + write to KV via `executionContext.waitUntil`. Stale-on-error / rate-limited responses return the cached payload with a different `source` field. `buildCacheKey` = `${owner}::${resource}::${stableSerialize(params)}`; `buildNamespaceKey` sorts+dupes. `stableSerialize` walks Date → ISO string, arrays, sorted-object keys.
nodes.languageNotes: DEFAULT_KV_EXPIRATION_SECONDS = 7 days. STALE_IF_RATE_LIMITED_FALLBACK_MS = 60s. The "fresh window" is `getFreshWindowMs(baseFreshForMs, metadata)` which forces a 60s minimum when rate-limit-remaining is 0.

nodes.name: packages/github/src/infrastructure/cache/github-revalidation.ts
nodes.summary: The cache-invalidation signal registry. Exports `githubRevalidationSignalKeys` (30+ factory functions for owner-scoped, repo-scoped, and entity-scoped signal keys — e.g. `pullEntity({owner, repo, pullNumber})`), `getGitHubWebhookRevalidationSignalKeys(event, payload)` (the big switch: pull_request, issues, push, check_run, workflow_run, status, etc. each fan out to the right signal keys), and `getGitHubRevalidationSignalKeysForTab(tab)` (maps an open tab type to its signal subscription).
nodes.languageNotes: The signalKeys registry + the event-payload extractors (`getRepositoryIdentity`, `getPullRequestNumber`, `getIssueIdentity`, `getWorkflowRunId`, `getWorkflowJobId`, `getCheckRunPullSignals`, `getCheckSuitePullSignals`, `getWorkflowRunPullSignals`) are all internal — only the three exported functions are used by callers.

nodes.name: packages/github/src/infrastructure/octokit/client.ts
nodes.summary: Octokit + Cloudflare Workers shim. Exports types `GitHubClient`, `GitHubContext`, `GitHubConditionalHeaders`, `GitHubResponseMetadata`; functions `createGitHubOctokit(source)`, `createGitHubResponseMetadata(statusCode, headers)`, `executeGitHubGraphQL(octokit, label, query, variables)`, `getErrorStatusCode(error)`. Wraps `globalThis.fetch` with `createRequestScopedFetch` that drains the body (via `response.clone().arrayBuffer()`) so an aborted request cannot leak its body stream to a sibling request. `executeGitHubGraphQL` runs the query through `withGitHubOperationTimeout` (15s default) which races the task against an abort-triggered timeout and ensures the AbortController fires in `finally`.

nodes.name: packages/github/src/repo/repo-activity-cards/get-repo-activity-cards.ts
nodes.summary: `getRepoActivityCards` and `getPrivateRepoActivityCards` — both delegate to `_fetchRepoActivityCards(input, context, octokit)`. The fetcher runs a single cached request (resource = "repo.activityCards.v1") that fans out to (a) a GraphQL query for the 5 newest OPEN pull requests and the 5 newest OPEN issues with comment counts, and (b) a REST `actions.listWorkflowRunsForRepo` (per_page=5) wrapped in a 404/403 → empty-list fallback. 404 outside the fanout also returns `emptyActivityCards()`. Logger calls set context/outcome/local-first outcome.

nodes.name: packages/github/src/repo/repo-activity-cards/repo-activity-cards.types.ts
nodes.summary: Two raw GraphQL/Rest response types. `GitHubGraphQLRepoActivityCardsResponse` — the response shape for the activity-cards GraphQL query (repository.{pullRequests, issues} + rateLimit). `GitHubWorkflowRunListItem` — the raw shape returned by `actions.listWorkflowRunsForRepo` (with all fields optional except `id`).

nodes.name: packages/github/src/repo/repo-activity-cards/repo-activity-cards.utils.ts
nodes.summary: `emptyActivityCards()` (all empty arrays + 0 counts), `mapWorkflowRuns(items)` (maps to the canonical GitHubRepoActivityCardAction shape with display_title fallback to name), `mapGraphQLRepoActivityCards(repository, actions)` (merges graph nodes into the final GitHubRepoActivityCards; the mergedAt-vs-state → open/closed/merged logic lives here; uses `hashIdToNumber` for the client-side `id` field), `createRepoActivityCardsMetadata(rateLimit, headers)` (builds a `GitHubResponseMetadata` with x-ratelimit-remaining + x-ratelimit-reset derived from the GraphQL rateLimit block).

nodes.name: packages/github/src/repo/repo-branch-comparison/get-repo-branch-comparison.ts
nodes.summary: `getRepoBranchComparison` and `getPrivateRepoBranchComparison` — both delegate to `_fetchRepoBranchComparison(input, context, octokit)`. Cached request (resource = "repo.branch-comparison.v1") calls `octokit.rest.repos.compareCommits({base, head, headers: buildGitHubConditionalHeaders(conditionals)})`. 404 → null. Uses signalKey `repoCode({owner, repo})`.

nodes.name: packages/github/src/repo/repo-branch-comparison/repo-branch-comparison.types.ts
nodes.summary: `GitHubRepoBranchComparisonData` — raw REST shape: `{ ahead_by: number, behind_by: number }`.

nodes.name: packages/github/src/repo/repo-branches/get-repo-branches.ts
nodes.summary: `getRepoBranches` and `getPrivateRepoBranches`. Cached request (resource = "repo.branches.v1") runs a GraphQL query for `repository.defaultBranchRef.name` + the first 100 refs ordered by TAG_COMMIT_DATE DESC. 404 → []. signalKey = `repoCode({owner, repo})`.

nodes.name: packages/github/src/repo/repo-branches/repo-branches.types.ts
nodes.summary: `GitHubGraphQLRepoBranchesResponse` — raw response shape (repository.{defaultBranchRef, refs.nodes[].target.{committedDate, oid, url?}} + rateLimit).

nodes.name: packages/github/src/repo/repo-branches/repo-branches.utils.ts
nodes.summary: `mapGraphQLRepoBranches(repository)` — flattens the refs nodes into GitHubRepoBranch[] (committedAt, isDefault computed against the default branch ref, name, sha, url).

nodes.name: packages/github/src/repo/repo-commit-sparkline/get-repo-commit-sparkline.ts
nodes.summary: `getRepoCommitSparkline` and `getPrivateRepoCommitSparkline`. Cached request (resource = "repo.commitSparkline.v1") calls `octokit.rest.repos.listCommits({per_page: 100, since})` where `since` is computed by `getRepoCommitSparklineSince()` (16 weeks ago). 404 → empty sparkline. signalKey = `repoCode({owner, repo})`.

nodes.name: packages/github/src/repo/repo-commit-sparkline/repo-commit-sparkline.types.ts
nodes.summary: `GitHubRepoCommitListItem` — the raw shape used by the sparkline mapper (commit.{author, committer}.date are both optional).

edges.description: installer stage extends the base stage (FROM base AS installer) to install the vite-plus CLI and pnpm dependencies on top of the slim Node image.
The Dockerfile file defines the server container service, including its build and production stages.
installer stage extends the base stage (FROM base AS installer) to install the vite-plus CLI and pnpm dependencies on top of the slim Node image.
The Dockerfile file defines the web container service, including its build and production stages.

The `check` job runs `vp install` and `vp check`, both routed through the root vite.config.ts via the Vite Plus CLI which wraps pnpm and bundles lint/typecheck/test config. The pipeline definition is co-located in this same workflow file.

The build job materializes packages/env/.env (truncating it with `: >` and writing VITE_SERVER_URL, VITE_WEB_URL, VITE_IMGPROXY_URL, SOURCE_COMMIT, DATABASE_URL, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, GITHUB_CLIENT_ID, GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET, and GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET via `printf '%q\n'`) inside the same workflow file's job steps, so the web build can `dotenvx run -f ../../packages/env/.env` at build time.
The CI workflow file defines the `CI` GitHub Actions pipeline (jobs check and build, with triggers, permissions, and concurrency).

The API fetching patterns doc is a focused sub-policy of tanstack-patterns.md — it covers the data layer (TanStack Query + oRPC) while tanstack-patterns.md covers route structure and beforeLoad. They are intended to be read together.
Instructs readers to import shared enums/filters/categories from packages/core rather than redefining literal unions locally, deferring to core.md for the propagation rule.

Auth.md pairs with api-fetching-patterns.md to cover the full auth data flow: auth.md owns server (Hono /auth/*), middleware, and route guards while api-fetching-patterns.md owns the slice-local query wrappers (getAuthUserQueryOptions) that the auth routes preload.
References the (guest) and __protected/ pathless layout groups which are also documented in tanstack-patterns.md under Route Hierarchy.

Defines shared domain contracts in packages/core; typescript.md defines the same constants.ts/types.ts/utils.ts/index.ts folder shape and schema-placement policy that core.md's Default Folder Shape prescribes.
Step 1 Database defers to workflow.md for migration generation, Neon-backed DATABASE_URL safety, and migration application.
Step 2 Shared Domain Contract defers to core.md for shared Zod schemas, enums, and defaults; the workflow file only sequences the steps.
Step 3 API Contract and Step 5 Client Error Handling defer to orpc.md for procedure factories, typed errors, and the isDefinedError client pattern.
Step 4 Web Data Layer defers to api-fetching-patterns.md for slice-local *.query.ts/*.mutation.ts file structure.
Step 6 Routes And UI defers to tanstack-patterns.md for route placement, thin beforeLoad, and page composition.
Step 6 Routes And UI defers to ui.md for app-level component composition.
The vp build pipeline reads IS_BUILD=true via cross-env in apps/web/vite.config.ts; the env policy builds on Vite Plus conventions documented in vite-plus.md.

Logging.md is the upstream policy for the request-scoped evlog-backed @tsu-stack/logger facade (wide events, post-emit warnings, Hono onError + parseError). Orpc.md's Logging section implements the handler side of the same policy via context.logger.

The oRPC handler logger contract (context.logger, .set/.emit) described in orpc.md is part of the wider logging policy; orpc.md's Logging section points back to logging.md for event shape and emit lifecycle.
Media-storage media_asset shape lives in packages/core/src/media-asset/types.ts following the core.md folder shape (constants.ts, types.ts, utils.ts, index.ts).
Lists preferred env names (MINIO_ENDPOINT, MINIO_BUCKET, MINIO_ACCESS_KEY_ID, etc.) and defers to environment-variables.md for the full six-place propagation checklist.
Storage oRPC procedures must live in the owning slice router per orpc.md; storage helper functions go in packages/api/src/lib/storage/media-asset/ rather than a dedicated storage router.
Implementation order defers to workflow.md for the migration generation + apply cycle (db:generate, db:migrate, DATABASE_URL safety).
Orpc.md's Client Error Handling section defers to api-fetching-patterns.md for query/mutation file structure, with oRPC adding the isDefinedError narrowing pattern.
Orpc.md's Logging section defers to logging.md for event shape, emit lifecycle, redaction, and global error handling; oRPC handlers only consume the request-scoped context.logger.
Seo.md uses TanStack Start route head() objects which are part of the file-based routing surface described in tanstack-patterns.md.
Tanstack-patterns.md defers all data-layer concerns to api-fetching-patterns.md and explicitly keeps route file wiring rules in its own scope.
Route Hierarchy in tanstack-patterns.md references the (guest) and __protected/ layout groups, which auth.md documents as the canonical auth-guard mechanism.
Testing policy mandates Vite+/Vitest setup with config in vite.config.ts; canonical commands `vp run test:unit:run` and `vp run test:e2e:run` rely on the Vite Plus CLI described in vite-plus.md.
Both docs prescribe the same constants.ts/types.ts/utils.ts/index.ts folder shape; typescript.md's Schema Placement rule defers to core.md for cross-package promotion.
Ui.md defers to tanstack-patterns.md for route/file placement and FSD layer mapping; ui.md only owns the packages/ui boundary and extraction rules.
Workflow.md defers all end-to-end feature implementation order to end-to-end-features.md, keeping itself focused on validation timing, commands, and migration safety.
Workflow.md defers UI component selection, shadcn install decisions, and visual coherence rules to ui.md.
Workflow.md defers the testing decision (when to add tests, test commands, test locations) to testing.md; the default policy is no auto-add tests.
Step 6 Routes And UI adds auth patterns when the feature touches auth-protected or guest-only surfaces.
Step 6 Routes And UI adds seo patterns (route head(), @tsu-stack/seo) when the feature needs page-level SEO.
Validation section defers to workflow.md for validation timing and to testing.md only when tests are explicitly requested or the task is test-specific.

Logging.md's Identity And Better Auth section documents evlog's Better Auth integration for request identity (Hono c.get('log'), TanStack Start/oRPC context), stable allowlisted fields, and client identity sync via setIdentity/clearIdentity. Auth.md owns the architectural side of the same integration.
The component registry index points readers at `npx shadcn@latest add @coss/<component>` commands documented in cli.md; the registry is the catalog, cli.md is the install procedure.
The component registry index points to portal-props.md for the `portalProps` forwarding pattern on composed `*Popup` and toast surfaces.
cli.md directs users to the component registry index when picking which primitive to add; the registry names the components and the CLI installs them.
dialog.md says "use AlertDialog for destructive confirmation"; alert-dialog.md says "use Dialog for non-destructive flows". They are paired by use case.

Both are searchable text-input overlays. Combobox constrains to a known item set; Autocomplete accepts free text with suggestions. The two refs cross-reference each other for pick-the-right-primitive decisions.
Both have search. Command is an unconstrained action dispatcher (no value commitment); Combobox commits to a value from its item set. Command is for "do thing X", Combobox is for "pick value V".
Checkbox is the single boolean primitive; CheckboxGroup composes multiple Checkboxes for multi-selection. They share the same underlying Checkbox node.
field.md documents the label/description/error spine and points to autocomplete.md as one of the form-control primitives that composes inside Field.
field.md documents the label/description/error spine and points to combobox.md as one of the form-control primitives that composes inside Field.
field.md documents the label/description/error spine and points to checkbox.md as one of the form-control primitives that composes inside Field.
field.md documents the label/description/error spine and points to checkbox-group.md as one of the form-control primitives that composes inside Field.
Fieldset provides the legend/group shell that RadioGroup is commonly rendered inside. The two refs cross-reference for grouped-radio patterns.
Form composes Fieldset for grouped form sections. fieldset.md is referenced from form.md for that integration.
Form uses Label as the accessible label primitive for inputs. label.md is referenced from form.md for that integration.
InputGroup wraps Input with addons; the inner control is the base Input primitive. input.md is the leaf, input-group.md is the wrapped composition.
NumberField is a typed Input with stepper controls. number-field.md references input.md as the underlying text-entry primitive it extends.
Both are specialized text inputs with constrained value types. NumberField constrains to a numeric range; OTPField constrains to a fixed-length passcode. They are sibling typed-input primitives.
Popover is the general anchored overlay; PreviewCard is a special hover-triggered preview. PreviewCard is essentially a popover with hover affordance + rich content layout.
Both render a horizontal bar with a fill. Progress is unbounded-until-done (loading, upload); Meter is bounded (battery, capacity). progress.md references meter.md for the bounded alternative.
Both pick a single value from a set. RadioGroup is always-visible; Select is a collapsed dropdown. radio-group.md references select.md for the dropdown alternative.
Separator is the standard divider primitive used between MenuItems and MenuGroups. separator.md references menu.md as the most common consumer.
Sheet and Dialog are sibling overlay primitives. Sheet is for side-panel workflows; Dialog is centered and focused. sheet.md references dialog.md as the centered alternative.
Drawer is the mobile-bottom-panel sibling of Sheet. sheet.md references drawer.md as the mobile-only bottom panel alternative.
Sheet handles side workflows; AlertDialog handles destructive confirmations. sheet.md references alert-dialog.md for the confirmation flow alternative.
Sidebar and Toolbar are complementary app-shell primitives. sidebar.md references p-toolbar-1 for command-bar context next to navigation.
Sidebar and Tabs both structure primary navigation regions. sidebar.md references p-tabs-1 for related app-shell patterns.
SidebarMenu uses Menu-style grouping primitives for items. sidebar.md references p-menu-1 as a related navigation pattern.
Both signal loading state. Skeleton reserves layout geometry for content; Spinner shows indeterminate progress. skeleton.md references spinner for short-op alternatives.
Spinner is commonly rendered inside disabled Button. spinner.md advises preferring button built-in loading UI over ad-hoc wrappers, and references p-button-18.
Spinner and Toast are both pending-state surfaces. Spinner is in-place; Toast is a notification (p-toast-3 loading toast). spinner.md references toast for cross-primitive pending states.
Switch and Toggle are sibling two-state controls. Switch is for binary preferences in settings; Toggle is for pressable commands. switch.md references toggle for the command-flow alternative.
Switch handles a single binary preference; ToggleGroup handles multiple grouped toggles. switch.md references toggle-group for grouped-selection alternatives.
Switch is for immediate preferences; Checkbox is for form agreements (terms/conditions). switch.md references checkbox for form-value flows.
Table variants compose with Frame for app-surface framing (p-table-2). table.md references frame.md for the bordered-surface shell pattern.
Table is composed with CardFrame for static tables in a card shell (p-table-7). table.md references card primitives for the card-shell variant.
Tabs and Toolbar are app-shell peers. tabs.md references p-toolbar-1 as a related shell primitive.
Textarea is meant to be wrapped with Field + FieldLabel + FieldError for accessible form integration. textarea.md is largely a specialization of field.md.
Textarea is the multi-line sibling of Input. Use Input for single-line; Textarea for variable-length multi-line. textarea.md references input for the single-line alternative.
Toast is non-acknowledgment feedback; AlertDialog requires user acknowledgment. toast.md references alert-dialog for acknowledgment-required flows.
Toast is temporary; Alert is inline and persistent. toast.md references alert for inline persistent feedback.
Anchored toasts (with anchor element) overlap with Tooltip use cases. toast.md points to tooltip/popover when no toastManager is configured.
ToggleGroup is the multi-control wrapper around individual Toggle items. toggle-group.md is the container; toggle.md is the leaf control.
Toggle is the single control; ToggleGroup is for mutually exclusive or shared-state sets. toggle.md references toggle-group for grouped behavior.
Toggle is a command; Switch is a binary preference. toggle.md references switch for the settings-preference alternative.
ToolbarButton is composed over ToggleGroupItem via render. toolbar.md heavily uses toggle-group as the underlying pressed-state primitive.
ToolbarGroup clusters commands; Group is the lower-level control-cluster primitive. toolbar.md references p-group-1 as a related composition reference.
Icon-only toolbar buttons need Tooltip for discoverability (aria-label still required). toolbar.md references tooltip for label patterns.
Tooltip is for short informational hints; Popover is for interactive or persistent content. tooltip.md references popover as the interactive-content alternative.
Tooltip is for short non-blocking hints; Dialog is for focused blocking content. tooltip.md references dialog as the long-form/acknowledgment alternative.
Slider patterns in coss particles pair Slider with Label + SliderValue. slider.md references label for accessible labelling of slider controls.
Slider is for continuous/ranged numeric input; Select is for discrete option labels. slider.md references select as the discrete-option alternative.
Tabs are often embedded inside Card layouts. tabs.md references p-card-1 as a related composition pattern.
Composition rules describe when optional `portalProps` is allowed and point to portal-props.md for the allowlist of composed popups and toast providers.
The Trigger + Popup pattern in composition.md is illustrated with Dialog/DialogTrigger/DialogPopup/DialogHeader/DialogTitle/DialogPanel. Dialog is the canonical trigger+popup example.
The Grouped Controls pattern in composition.md uses Group + GroupSeparator. group.md is the underlying primitive the composition rule is built on.
The first core rule in forms.md defaults to Field composition (Field, FieldLabel, FieldDescription, FieldError). forms.md is largely a usage contract over field.md.
forms.md codifies the InputGroup DOM-order invariant (InputGroupAddon after InputGroupInput/InputGroupTextarea). The rule is enforced by the input-group.md pattern.
forms.md includes the OTP length-sync rule (root `length` must match rendered OTPFieldInput count). otp-field.md is the underlying primitive this rule governs.
forms.md codifies the Textarea rule: use Textarea directly inside Field and avoid manual FieldControl render wiring. textarea.md is the primitive the rule applies to.
forms.md's Do/Don't snippets use Input with `type="email"`/`type="text"` to enforce the explicit-type rule. input.md is the underlying primitive the rule applies to.
forms.md's accessible-labelling rule mentions Label as the visible-label primitive. label.md is the underlying primitive the rule applies to.
migration.md's per-component notes point to ../component-registry.md for the full coss component registry and the canonical path to each primitive's ref.
migration.md documents the ToggleGroup `type="single"` -> multiple-default coss mapping. The rule applies to toggle-group.md.
migration.md documents the Slider array-defaultValue ([50]) -> scalar (50) coss mapping. The rule applies to slider.md.
migration.md documents the Select children-only -> items-first coss mapping with SelectValue placeholder pattern. The rule applies to select.md.
migration.md documents the input-otp package -> @coss/otp-field migration (rename components, length/onValueChange, drop InputOTPGroup and slot index). The rule applies to otp-field.md.
migration.md's primary composition example migrates shadcn DialogTrigger asChild+Button to coss DialogTrigger render+Button. dialog.md is the canonical primitive for the trigger+popup migration.
migration.md documents the Menu onSelect -> onClick mapping. The rule applies to menu.md.
styling.md reserves variant="ghost" for cancel/close buttons in Dialog footers. The styling rule applies to dialog.md footer composition.
styling.md reserves variant="ghost" for cancel/close buttons in AlertDialog footers. The styling rule applies to alert-dialog.md footer composition.
styling.md reserves variant="ghost" for cancel/close buttons in Sheet footers. The styling rule applies to sheet.md footer composition.
styling.md reserves variant="ghost" for cancel/close buttons in Drawer footers. The styling rule applies to drawer.md footer composition.
styling.md's recommended font setup uses `npx shadcn@latest init @coss/style`. cli.md is the install reference that backs that command.
composition.md singles out ToastProvider and AnchoredToastProvider as accepting optional `portalProps` alongside composed `*Popup` wrappers. The composition rule applies to toast.md.
forms.md's explicit-type rule applies to Button (`type="button"|"submit"|"reset"`). The rule governs button.md usage in forms.

common-errors.md repeatedly directs readers to embedded-docs.md and SOURCE_MAP.json lookup for the 'Property X does not exist on type Y' error and the debugging tips section. Embedded docs are the version-accurate source of truth for fixing import errors.

.dockerignore explicitly excludes **/.env.docker (line 45) — the populated version of .env.docker.example. The example file is the template; .dockerignore ensures the real one never lands in a build context.

CONTRIBUTING.md then defines how to contribute to that project (Conventional Commits, two-stage PR process). copilot-instructions.md's Key Commands table is the Copilot/CI-facing surface; README.md's Getting started/Install sections are the human-facing surface of the same commands. They are alternative presentations of the same toolchain (vp/vpx, pnpm scripts, Cloudflare Workers, Neon, Drizzle).

apps/web/components.json is a slimmed-down copy: it uses the same `style: base-maia` + baseColor=stone + coss/`@tsu-stack/ui/*` aliases but swaps @dotmatrix for @files-sdk. Both files share the css path `../../packages/ui/styles/shadcn.css` (apps/web) and `styles/shadcn.css` (this file).
The `exports: "./components/*": "./components/*"` map makes `packages/ui/components/button.tsx` importable as `@tsu-stack/ui/components/button` (the canonical coss/Base-UI Button primitive).

The `exports: "./styles/globals.css": "./styles/globals.css"` map makes the main CSS entry importable as `@tsu-stack/ui/styles/globals.css` — apps/web/src/shared/styles/app.css `@import`s it as the base of its cascade.

Peer dep on react + react-dom (catalog-pinned). The `ui` script also exercises the icon registry via apps/web/src/shared/ui/icon-picker.tsx (which lives in apps/web and consumes the icons/* + icons/types.ts modules in this package).
Explicit include of `../../apps/web/src/shared/ui/icon-picker.tsx` — a file in apps/web that composes @tsu-stack/ui primitives and therefore needs to be in the UI package's compilation graph.
globals.css `@import "./animations.css"` — loads the spinner-leaf-fade keyframes + .animate-spinner-leaf-fade utility into the cascade before shadcn.css so its references to the utility are valid.

globals.css `@import "./shadcn.css"` — the coss/Base-UI theme layer with @theme inline, @custom-variant, :root/.dark tokens, and the @layer base resets. Must load before base-theme.css (which references its neutral-* colors) and before prose.css (which references var(--color-base-N)).

globals.css `@import "./base-theme.css"` — loads after shadcn.css so the backward-compat aliases (--color-base-N -> var(--color-neutral-N), --color-white-4, --color-surface-N, --color-night, --color-night-faded, --color-light) can resolve the neutral-* palette declared by shadcn.css.
globals.css `@import "./scrollbar.css"` — loads the custom-scrollbar rules + .no-scrollbar utility into the cascade.

globals.css `@import "./prose.css"` — loads the @utility prose typography block (the Tailwind 4 port of tailwindcss-typography). Must load after shadcn.css and base-theme.css because the `--tw-prose-*` variables reference `var(--color-base-N)` and `var(--color-primary)`.

prose.css's `--tw-prose-*` theme tokens reference `var(--color-primary)` (from shadcn.css's --color-primary theme inline) and `var(--color-base-N)` (from base-theme.css's @theme inline aliases, which themselves reference shadcn's neutral-* palette).

base-theme.css's 11 `--color-base-N` aliases reference `var(--color-neutral-N)` which is provided by the coss neutral palette in shadcn.css (the only file in the package that actually declares the base palette).
scrollbar.css's `--scrollbar-thumb: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-foreground) 20%, transparent)` references the `--color-foreground` token declared in shadcn.css's :root block.

globals.css is the package-level CSS entry — apps/web/src/shared/styles/app.css `@import "@tsu-stack/ui/styles/globals.css"` (via the package's `exports: "./styles/globals.css"` map) at the top of its cascade, then loads the local fonts.css + theme.css on top.
shadcn.css is the `tailwind.css` target in packages/ui/components.json ("css: \"styles/shadcn.css\"") — the file the shadcn CLI rewrites when a new component is installed.

apps/web/components.json `tailwind.css: "../../packages/ui/styles/shadcn.css"` points at shadcn.css (a child of globals.css), not at globals.css directly — apps/web's app.css does the @import of globals.css.
The `animate-spinner-leaf-fade` utility from animations.css is consumed by the coss Spinner primitive in packages/ui/components/spinner.tsx (spinner-leaf per-leaf fade pattern).

Both coss skills live under .agents/skills/coss*/. The coss skill provides the primitive import / composition rules; the coss-particles skill provides the copy-paste-ready examples built on those primitives. coss-particles references particle files at apps/ui/registry/default/particles/ which the coss skill's workflow step 4 ('check at least one particle') points users to consume.

SKILL.md's 'Scripts' subsection explicitly lists scripts/provider-registry.mjs as the tool to 'Look up current providers and models available in the model router. Always run this before using a model to verify provider keys and model names.' The model-selection.md reference echoes the same rule.

Summary's 'Important Files' list explicitly names apps/web/src/pages/github-repo/ui/github-repo-page.tsx as the public repo overview page, alongside branch-comparison-banner.tsx, repo-explorer-layout.tsx, and the page-local api/ directory.

Two sibling issue templates with matching frontmatter shape (name/about/title/labels/assignees), matching Platform/OS -> Additional Context structure (reframed for features), and the same commented-out 'Would I like to work on this?' opt-in block at the bottom.

Two halves of the Vite Plus git-hooks pipeline. pre-commit runs `vp staged` to lint+typecheck+test changed packages before the commit is created; commit-msg then runs `commitlint --edit` on the message. Both live in .vite-hooks/ (tracked in git) rather than .git/hooks/.

mastra/index.ts instantiates `new Mastra({ agents: { weatherAgent }, ... })` and imports `weatherAgent` from #@/mastra/agents/weather-agent. The AGENTS.md rule 'Register all agents, tools, workflows, and scorers in src/mastra/index.ts' makes this the canonical registration surface.
weather-tool.ts's `weatherTool` is wired into `weatherAgent.tools: { weatherTool }` in agents/weather-agent.ts, which is in turn registered in mastra/index.ts via the agents map.

mastra/index.ts imports the three individual scorers (toolCallAppropriatenessScorer, completenessScorer, translationScorer) from #@/mastra/scorers/weather-scorer and registers them in the Mastra instance's `scorers` field. The same scorers are also attached to the weatherAgent via its `scorers` map.

mastra/index.ts imports `weatherWorkflow` from #@/mastra/workflows/weather-workflow and registers it via `workflows: { weatherWorkflow }`. The workflow internally calls `mastra.getAgent('weatherAgent')` in its planActivities step.
weatherAgent imports `weatherTool` and attaches it to `tools: { weatherTool }` — the agent's only tool.

weatherAgent imports the `scorers` object and destructures toolCallAppropriatenessScorer / completenessScorer / translationScorer into the agent's scorers map, each with `{ scorer, sampling: { type: 'ratio', rate: 1 } }`.
weather-workflow.ts's planActivities step calls `mastra?.getAgent('weatherAgent')` to invoke the registered agent for activity suggestions from the forecast.

worker.ts is the Workers runtime entry. Its default `fetch` export either routes the WS path to the GitHubSignalRelay DO or delegates to `app.fetch(request, env, executionContext)`. app.ts's Hono app holds all routing logic.

worker.ts re-exports the `GitHubSignalRelay` class so Wrangler's `new_classes` migration registers the DO. The default fetch also forwards the WS upgrade to `env.GITHUB_SIGNAL_RELAY.idFromName('global').fetch('https://internal/connect', request)` — github-signal-relay.ts's handleConnect picks that up.

index.ts is a one-liner that re-exports the `app` symbol from app.ts. Per apps/server/package.json, `main: src/index.ts` is the package entry — so any external consumer (or the worker's default fetch) imports `app` from here.
app.ts has `import '#@/shared/lib/logger';` near the top — the bare-module import triggers logger init at module load so the HonoLoggerMiddleware never sees an uninitialized log service.

vite.config.ts's `cloudflare({ configPath: process.env.IS_BUILD === 'true' ? 'wrangler.jsonc' : 'wrangler.dev.jsonc' })` decides which wrangler config the build/dev reads. The `run.tasks.build.command` sets IS_BUILD=true before vp build, which causes wrangler.jsonc (with the real production routes and bindings) to be used. The 'main' field in both wrangler configs points at `src/worker.ts`, so this is the entry the bundle targets.

vite.config.ts's `cross-env IS_BUILD=true vp build` workflow depends on `wrangler types --config wrangler.dev.jsonc` (the cf-typegen package.json script) being run first to generate the worker-configuration.d.ts the app code reads as the typed `Cloudflare.Env`.

Barrel re-exports CreateAnAccountForm from the ui folder.
Barrel re-exports SignInForm from the ui folder. Sign-in + create-account are the only two auth forms in this slice.

Barrel re-exports GitHubRepoCombobox (single-select) from the ui folder.
Barrel re-exports GitHubRepoMultiCombobox (multi-select) from the ui folder.

project.slice imports ProjectTabs, ProjectFilters, ProjectFilter, ProjectTab from the sibling types file.

ResumesPage calls useResumeStore() for opened/selected state.

settings-layout.tsx renders the <Outlet /> from @tanstack/react-router, and the matching /dashboard/settings/account route file imports AccountSettings as its component — so layout is the parent of account-settings in the route tree.
settings-layout.tsx's <Outlet /> renders the /dashboard/settings/github route's component, which imports GithubSettings (also re-exported from the dashboard index.ts barrel).
settings-layout.tsx's <Outlet /> renders the /dashboard/settings/profile route's component, which imports ProfileSettings. Layout's default tab is 'profile'.
GithubSettingsForm imports useUpdateGithubConfigMutation from the dashboard api/ folder. Also calls orpcQueryClient.githubConfig.update.mutationOptions directly for the 'Clear token' flow.

stack.slice imports StackTabs, StackFilters, StackTab, StackFilter from the sibling types file.
StacksPage calls useStackStore() for opened/selected state.
StacksPage mounts the StackForm dialog with editingStackId + open/onOpenChange, keyed to reset between rows.

stack-form's updateMutation invalidates projects.list (and projects.list.queryKey) so that changes to a stack's name/icon propagate to every project that uses it. Cross-entity cache invalidation between the two dashboard domains.
Page barrel re-exports StacksPage for the stacks route file.
DashboardHomePage renders the top 3 experiences with their projects as Badges, mirroring the per-row data on ExperiencesPage. Both pages consume the same experiences.list query.

DashboardHomePage computes the unique-stack count and renders 'All Tech Stacks' as de-duped Badges — same data as StacksPage. Both pages consume the projects.list query (which embeds the stacks) and the stacks list query.
StackItem is rendered by StacksPage (the parent page file) — indirect relationship via the page composition. Same parent-import chain as experience-item and project-item.
BranchComparisonBanner imports useGetGithubRepoBranchComparisonQuery from this query file. The query is the data source for the banner's aheadBy/behindBy UI.
CodeExplorerToolbar's BranchSelector consumes getGithubRepoBranchesQueryOptions to power its Command palette (and the branchCount/tagCount footer).
RepoSidebar's ContributorsSection uses githubRepoContributorsQueryOptions to fetch and render the per-repo contributor avatars + tooltip with commit counts.
CodeFileView uses getGithubRepoFileContentQueryOptions to fetch the actual blob content. Also used by RepoMarkdownFiles for the README/License tabs.
GithubRepoPage reads useGetGithubRepoOverviewQuery for the page header (owner/name/description/stars/forks) and to drive the BranchComparisonBanner + RepoSidebar + RepoHeader composition.

LatestCommitBar (defined in batch 27) uses getGithubRepoRefCommitQueryOptions to render the per-branch tip commit bar with the avatar/login/message/SHA. The query is also wired into the signal-stream list in GithubRepoPage.
FileTree (the row-list view) is fed the tree query's data via props. CodeFileView also uses the same options to read the parent directory's tree (for the file size).
FolderView (in the explorer split-pane) is fed the same tree query's data. RepoExplorerLayout (defined in batch 27) gates the query on hasMounted + viewMode === 'tree'.
FileTree fires useGetGithubTreeEntryCommitsQuery once per directory render to populate the commit-message + relative-date columns. Same hook used by FolderView.

The REPO_ACTIVITY_CARDS_PER_PAGE constant is consumed by the discussions, issues, pulls, and workflow-runs query options as the default perPage/first. Discriminated discussion query: it uses 'first' (GraphQL) instead of perPage (REST) but reads the same constant.

RepoExplorerLayout (batch 27) renders CodeExplorerToolbar inside its ExplorerToolbar (memoized). The toolbar's onBranchChange callback comes from RepoExplorerLayout's useCallback that navigates via TanStack Router to /repos/$repo, /repos/$repo/tree/$, or /repos/$repo/blob/$ based on the current explorer path.
RepoExplorerLayout (batch 27) renders <CodeFileView> as the contentPane for viewMode === 'blob'. CodeFileView handles its own queries (file content, tree-entry commit, parent tree).

LatestCommitBar consumes getGithubRepoRefCommitQueryOptions to render the per-branch tip commit bar with the avatar/login/message/SHA. The query is also wired into the signal-stream list in GithubRepoPage (batch 26).
RepoActivityCards fires useGetGithubRepoDiscussionsQuery (and pulls/issues/workflow-runs) and renders the ActivityCards list. Also wires the per-entity signal-stream targets.
RepoExplorerLayout fires the root + current-path tree queries (both getGithubRepoTreeQueryOptions) and feeds root data to usePrefetchTree. The data is then passed to RepoFileTreeSidebar + FolderView.

RepoFileTreeSidebar reads every cached tree query (via getQueriesData on the githubRepoTreeQueryKeys prefix) for the global fuzzy file-search card, and fires per-directory tree queries when a DirectoryNode expands.
RepoMarkdownFiles prefetches and re-fetches file content per known-md-file tab using getGithubRepoFileContentQueryOptions. Same query consumed by CodeFileView (batch 26).
RepoSidebar's ContributorsSection uses githubRepoContributorsQueryOptions (the options-only builder) wrapped in its own useQuery so it can layer the hasMounted enabled gate.
RepoExplorerLayout calls usePrefetchTree({repo, ref}, rootTreeQuery.data, isPrivate) to BFS-walk the repo tree and progressively prefetch subdirectories (3 every 150ms).
githubReposHubQueryOptions uses buildReposHubResult in its select transform to compute the {totals, matchingCount, repos} shape from the raw GitHubUserRepoSummary[] and the ReposHubInput.
RepositoriesPage imports the ReposHubInput type to type its derived hub-input memo. The actual computation lives in the query's select.

RepositoriesPage calls useListFilters({ pageId: 'repos', initialStore: filterStore, ... }) to derive its search/filter/sort state. The hook is generic over FilterableItem and persists to the diffkit-filters cookie.
RepositoriesPage renders <FilterBar state={filterState} searchPlaceholder='Search by title...' /> to surface the search/sort/filter UI.
RepositoriesPage accepts filterStore as a prop (populated by the route loader calling getFilterCookie server-side). The hook + FilterBar write back to the same cookie via writeFilterCookie.

FilterBar imports the FilterableItem / ActiveFilter / FilterOption / ListFilterState / SortOption / FilterDefinition types from use-list-filters — it's a generic renderer of the state shape produced by the hook.
Indirect: both ExperienceSection and UserActivityFeed consume the GitHub data layer on the home page, but ExperienceSection uses the portfolio query for experiences, not the activity query.
HomePage fires useGetGithubProfileQuery and wires the profile queryKey to the githubRevalidationSignalKeys.ownerProfile(owner) signal target.
HomePage fires useGetGithubContributionsQuery, wires it to ownerContributions signal, and passes the calendar data to the lazy-imported ContributionGraph.
HomePage fires useGetGithubPinnedReposQuery and wires the queryKey to ownerPinnedRepos signal; renders the result as a grid of PinnedRepoCard.
HomePage fires useGetGithubActivityQuery(1) (page 1 only). The events list isn't directly rendered in HomePage but is used downstream by the UserActivityFeed component when included via a tab.

HomePage lazy-imports ContributionGraph and renders it inside a Suspense boundary (with a matching gradient fallback). The graph is gated on useIsClient() because it uses createPortal to document.body.
HomePage renders GithubProfileUnavailableState in 3 error/empty cases: !setupStatusQuery.data.isConfigured, any of profile/pinnedRepos/contributions/activity isError, and !profile.
HomePage maps pinnedReposQuery.data to <PinnedRepoCard key={repo.owner/repo.name} repo={repo} /> in the 'Pinned' section (only when non-empty).
HomePage renders <ProjectsSection /> in the #projects section. The projects list comes from useGetPortfolioListQuery (consumed inside ProjectsSection).
HomePage renders <Experience /> in the #experience section. Same portfolio-query source for the experiences list as ProjectsSection.
HomeNav renders <Contact contacts={portfolioQuery.data.contacts} /> at the bottom of the right-rail nav.
PrivacyPolicyPage imports the MDX content file as the default Content component and renders it inside a <Container className='prose not-dark:prose-invert'>.
TermsOfServicePage imports the MDX content file as the default Content component and renders it inside a <Container className='prose not-dark:prose-invert'>.

router.tsx imports routeTree from '@/routeTree.gen' (which includes __root.tsx's Route as the root) and sets defaultErrorComponent / defaultNotFoundComponent / defaultPendingComponent / Wrap that match what __root.tsx expects. The createRootRouteWithContext in __root.tsx is what makes context.queryClient and context.user available to every child route's loader.

Layout route (route.tsx) is the parent of the index route (index.tsx) in the TanStack Router file-based routing tree. The layout's Outlet renders the index route's component when no deeper sub-route matches.
Route imports ProjectsPage directly (not via the page barrel) and prefetches projects.list in the loader. 'use client' directive on the route file (only project route in this batch).
Layout route (route.tsx) is the parent of the index route (index.tsx). Outlet pattern matches the experiences layout.

Route loader calls authClient.listSessions() + getSession() and returns a parsed-session array. The page reads it via useLoaderData({ from: '/(root-layout)/__protected/dashboard/settings/account/' }) and passes it to the coss AuthSessionManager.
Route imports ProfileSettings and prefetches profile.get in the loader. The page composes a tanstack-form with onChange zod validation against ProfileUpdateInputSchema.
Route head() calls generateAppSeo() for the default home page title/description. generateAppSeo is the shared helper that wraps @tsu-stack/seo with the appConfig-derived site identity.
Health route is served by the TanStack Start server entry exported in server.ts. The handler runs inside the per-request requestLog scope so probe failures are logged structurally.
Route forwards GET/POST/PUT to filesRouter (the createFilesRouter instance from files-gateway). The gateway wires the R2 binding, the auth.authorize check, and the allowedOrigins CORS list.
filesRouter is consumed by the /api/files route handlers (forwarding to filesRouter.handle(request) for each verb).
server.ts imports handler from @tanstack/react-start/server-entry (which is generated from the routeTree at build time). The handler is the catch-all router for the apps/web app.

Sitemap handler imports routeTree from @/routeTree.gen and walks its children to extract every fullPath. The walk is structural (recurses on the children array) so changes to the generated shape don't break the handler.
form.ts imports fieldContext and formContext from form-contexts.ts to wire them into the createFormHook call (the contexts are the keys for the field/form context binding).
CalendarField imports useFieldContext to bind the coss CalendarDropdown's selected/handleChange/handleBlur to the typed TanStack form field.
CheckboxField imports useFieldContext<boolean>() to bind the raw <input type='checkbox'> to a boolean TanStack form field.
ComboboxField imports useFieldContext<string>() to bridge the coss Combobox's nullable value/change contract to a string form field.
ComboboxMultipleField imports useFieldContext<string[]>() to bridge the coss Combobox's multiple-value/change contract to a string-array form field. Also re-exports the ComboboxItemType type.

DropdownField imports useFieldContext<string>() to bind the coss Select's value/onValueChange to a string form field. The two items-shape conversions (props.items[] → itemsMap + a per-render itemToStringLabel) live in the component.
IconPickerField imports useFieldContext<string>() to bind the IconPicker's onValueChange/onBlur/value to a string form field.
ImageField imports useFieldContext<string>() and uses TanStack's useStore to read the current form value (the public URL) from the form's store. Wires files-sdk upload to the field's handleChange.

InputField imports useFieldContext<string>() to bridge the coss Input's value/onChange/onBlur to a string form field. The value ?? '' coercion is what makes the controlled <input> happy when the field is un-set.
InputGroupField imports useFieldContext<string>() to bridge the coss InputGroup+InputGroupInput to a string form field. Children become right-side addons inside the InputGroup.
NumberFieldForm imports useFieldContext<number>() to bridge the coss NumberField's onValueChange contract (null when empty) to a number form field (defaults to 0 on null).
PasswordInputField imports useFieldContext<string>() to bridge the coss PasswordInput to a string form field. Used by the SignInForm + CreateAnAccountForm in apps/web/src/features/auth/ui.

RichTextField imports useFieldContext<string>() to bridge the coss RichTextEditor's HTML-string output to a string form field. The Omit<> on RichTextEditorProps strips value/onChange/onBlur from the consumer's prop shape.

StackSelector imports useFieldContext<string[]>() to bridge a list of stack IDs to a string-array form field. The Popover+Command+Dialog UI is bespoke; the coss primitives are used for the individual Command/CommandItem, Dialog, Popover, Field primitives.
SubmitButton imports useFormContext() (not useFieldContext) because it subscribes to the form's overall state, not a field's. It's registered as formComponents.SubmitButton in form.ts.
SwitchField imports useFieldContext<boolean>() to bridge the coss Switch's checked/onCheckedChange/onBlur to a boolean form field. The right-side label/description uses coss FieldContent+FieldTitle.

YearField imports useFieldContext<number>() to bridge the coss Select (year options as itemsMap) to a number form field. The year range is module-scoped (1980..currentYear) and pre-built as a Record for the coss Select items prop.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start here to understand the monorepo structure, tooling (Vite Plus), and development workflow. The root package.json, AGENTS.md, and vite.config.ts define the entire build pipeline.

tour.title: Database & Schema Layer
tour.description: Drizzle ORM schemas in packages/db define the data model — users, experiences, projects, stacks, contacts, GitHub cache, and auth tables. This is the foundation everything else builds on.

tour.title: Shared Domain Core
tour.description: packages/core holds Zod schemas, enums, and domain contracts shared between API and web. This single source of truth prevents duplicated type definitions across the monorepo.

tour.title: oRPC API Layer
tour.description: packages/api defines typed API routers using oRPC with public/protected/owner procedures. Each router maps directly to a domain entity with full end-to-end type safety from DB to client.

tour.title: Auth, Email & Infrastructure Packages
tour.description: Better Auth integration, Resend email templates, environment validation via @t3-oss/env-core, and the logger package form the infrastructure backbone. Understanding env scoping (server vs isomorphic vs web) is critical.

tour.title: Web Application & UI
tour.description: apps/web uses TanStack Start with FSD architecture — routes preload data via beforeLoad, pages compose widgets and features, and packages/ui provides app-agnostic shadcn-based primitives.

tour.title: End-to-End Feature Workflow & Extension
tour.description: When adding a new feature, follow the prescribed order: DB schema first, then core contracts, then oRPC router, then TanStack Query wrappers, then route preloading and UI. This doc is the checklist for extending the system.
